naughtypip,

Where the candles form, how they close and the time frame they represent is the key. Higher time frame signals are powerful and you counter trend them at your peril on lower time frames and always keeping in mind this this can turn and bite you hard.

When you see the setup as I mentioned, look for the obvious signs, is pro money buying or selling? They cant hide billions of dollars for very long and it is unfortunate trading books and many forums all say that tails are rejection of lower price and wicks are rejection of higher price. That is only half the picture and it programs your brain incorrectly, it more importantly should state tails are buyers and wicks are sellers. It couples into price action nicely too and this is where I know a lot of people are getting confused because it means a bear candle is now suddenly a bull candle and a bull candle is a bear candle.

At the time of typing this, the eur/usd wants to go higher, we know this for over head supply where anxious sellers are waiting, but the bulls need more orders to help them push some more, there is little pro money support below price now and the only way they will run with it is when price drops to the next support area and this is where you may see some tails. The other alternative is let price drop away, pro money spike it up, take out stops, this now gives pro money more orders and up it goes.

I have heard many are curious about the Doctor. There is much I cannot say, but of what I can say I will offer you this.

If there was a trading book I have not read, it has not been written. Virtually all books once forensically examined (as I have done) and the message in the text put into practice, it shows you where the book steers you in the wrong direction. Proving this is a simple matter but very time consuming because it takes a lot of testing on historic price and on many time frames. The same applies to DVD systems, methods, indicators and seminars. Please dont waste your money on those. The print and TV media is full of cleverly worded statements to push you along into making a decision, usually the wrong one. Contrary to a certain business TV channel's adverts, I do not know any traders who manage their money on the basis of what the TV channel says, all their news is old news, too late then.

Also consider some of the most basic phrases which are thrown around since the early 1900's.

The trend is your friend.......in order for a trend to be in place you must have two points where your trend line is drawn, all sounds good to most. But to form a trend you need for example in an up trend two higher highs and two higher lows. If you wait for that type of trend analysis you miss most of the move, try it on historic data and you will see how much profit is lost. Do you think there is any advantage in professional money telling you how they take a trade?....of course not!

Here is another classic. Buy dips in rallies....yeah sure, we missed the start of the move and now you want us to buy when there is clearly no target and no way of knowing where the move may end, eventually all dips turn into bearish moves. A real smart way to loose money.

Everyone person I meet who has not met me before or know I trade, says same the same thing when the subject of trading or investing crops up. They say, I would like to throw in a few hundred bucks into a stock or fund for a year or so and see who it does. Why?....they know nothing about the stock or fund and yet hand money over blindly to some fat cat who will gladly take it. It has to be the lure of easy money in their eyes, but of course in here we all know better.

It is a gambling attitude and they dont treat their money seriously enough to ever be a success. Would you honestly see yourself giving money to somebody you dont know and say here....make me money. This is how retail traders treat the markets every day, as if it is a game and making a few bucks gives them enough pleasure to try another trade. I could write pages on the amount of times I see people seeking revenge on a loosing trade and doubling up or trying to force money out of the markets looking for smaller moves, but using higher lot size.

Like it or not, trading is a business and if any new trader is really serious you will treat it as a business and not a place in which to gamble. All professionals in business need plenty education/training before they are considered a pro. You are taking the right attitude and now aware it will take years from you before this will pay you even a penny each week. All professional traders had to start somewhere and there is no school for this work and the only way to learn is right at the coal face and on a DEMO account. Some however will never make money in trading, it just does not click with them, this is the majority of people who try it. There I said it, I just made a lot of people upset over their trading future, but they wont know until they try.

Everyone should do the following until they are making virtual money every month and every quarter.

Only trade a demo account using the same amount of money in that demo account as you would invest as a real trader. Treat the account and if it is real and take no chances, treat all new trades as vital. Use money and risk management to suit your style of trading and pocket. Any wins or losses must NOT see you become happy/sad/annoyed etc. Your emotions must be completely flat, cold and you are more of a machine where the monetary losses and gains mean nothing. Your only goal is to grow an account every month/quarter. Get your enjoyment and kicks not from the joy of trading, but from some other topic. Distance yourself from trading when not sitting at your computer and dont think about open positions or trades setting up, this will eat you alive mentally if you let it. Place a trade and as you do, know where your stop and target(s) are and hard set all of them.

A good test is this, can you take a pile of money that you would consider as your maximum risk on any trade, pile it on the ground in cash notes....and burn it. IF you can detach yourself from the sight of money going up in flames you are well on your way.

To follow up on this I am shortly going to post a chart for paragon about professional people trading and show the risk reward/element.

paragon, here is a chart for you and some insight into what la ahead for trading off the 4hr and higher time frames. I choose the daily chart here in my example as it is the most traded time frame world wide among professionals.

First item I must mention is that this is not a valid trade nor a means to enter one, but it does go along with the kind of trading talked about in this website.

You will see an entry off the move back into demand, a good place to look for buys. If a standard lot is traded, this is 10 dollars per point, decide how much money you want to put on the trade and how much risk you wish to accept. Considering this is a longer term trade and most who trade longer time frames have more capital than day traders to work with, lets say 10 lots are traded, this is 100 dollars down on the trade. Still sounds cheap right?

Look at the first move up in your favor, approx 410 points. That is 44,110 dollars profit so far. Sounds nice?

Now look at the pull back which came back down into your entry, you just took 44 grand in heat and no way to know it will stop, does it still look nice?....what if price were to break below your entry and now you are in negative equity, how far will you let it run?...remember, here we are talking 100 dollars per point. Measure a few wicks on some daily candles and you will get a feel for an average fake move. Just dont take that number as scientific. I measure about 50 points, 50 x 100 - 5000 dollars, and still no way to know if it will stop or break through and continue.

Consider the target way up on top, that is 900 or so points away. Look how long capital has been tied up and the target still nowhere near being reached. Look at all the other pullbacks even if you held your nerve. Ask yourself a very serious question, am I willing to wait months to get a return and am I willing to sit through deep pull backs as price winds up?

Another thing to consider are the amount of entries on any given time frame. In the chart below we only see about three good long entries, and the one I picked is taking much longer than the others to reach its target. We have about 9 months and three trades. Does that suit you?

I would steer you away from using the 4hr unless you can see each 4hr candle close. It is common to see one 4hr candle wipe out the previous, today was a classic example of this on several currency pairs. The daily time frame is safer...but not the safest, there is no such thing as safest.

To sum up, long term trading means plenty capital, willingness to take extra heat and also willing to wait months for profit and losses to occur.

Hope this gives some food for thought.

Here is why Box A are sellers and Box B are buyers.

My hint earlier was where this is counter intuitive. The trading books, courses and media all steer you into trading in a herd like mentality and my answer to you know will at first sound wrong. Engage the logical part of your brain and see how the sense in this shows itself to you.

When you enter the market in Box A, you 'buy' into the market. You do not make any money until you close your position in profit, and profits are not gained unless there is a willing buyer of your position when you close it. He buys from you, (price is still going up) but your position is sold to him, therefore its a sell. Before you enter the market you must ask yourself some simple questions.

If I enter at price x, who am I likely buying from and who am I likely trading alongside. Is it the right place and I am not buying blind or where there is high volume. All moves by professional money begin when there is little volume, they slowly filter orders into the market so that the large amount of money they have to trade (orders) will not cause price to move much from where it is now. Remember, even a few points the wrong way is critical for them and hurts profitability and can tie up funds too long for intraday trades.

Assuming you picked your entry price and you place an order and now you get a fill.

Now what?

You were a buyer, now you are a seller. Another question you ask is, where do I exit with profit? (price level) You identify your exit before you place your order and also your stop. Counter intuitive is allowing yourself to think ahead where you must get out, and this is best done into the willingness of weak hands who all jump at the market when its moving hard in case they miss the move. They always buying at the top, right where your target is and they 'buy' your 'sell' (close position) which on the most common forex trading platform MT4 is called 'close'.

The Box B is the inverse of this.

It gels with the concept of buying when prices are low and selling when prices are high and where most wont see why the price at those areas is where you should be placing a trade. But nothing is earned unless the trade is completed in profit and at the right place. If you dont get a fill when you wish to close, you get slippage, requotes etc. This all points to a narrow price range where there is a great deal of activity.

There is some insight into how all this works behind the scenes. Any sign of slow processing of orders mean there is a large volume of trading going on at the level. You will also see spreads widen because the broker does not want you to get away totally with the upper hand. Those guys always get their profit from you.

Does this make sense to you yet?

Think of you being in the minority of traders (the successful ones) when entering the market and getting out when the herd are still willing to buy, you must see from their perspective what you no longer look for i,e buy dips on rallys, head and shoulder neck break, double top etc etc. Knowing where the herd will probably place a trade that fits perfectly with your exit is essential, trade toward them when they will be happy to take your order when you close it.

The hunt for liquidity is far more subtle than that. In fact last weeks close on one currency pair in particular was a superb example of forcing liquidity in the form of taking out short stops, getting new longs filled and yet, any sensible trader would have seen this as a false bullish break when it closed perfectly at resistance and at an area where sellers were waiting, text book!

posts.text:
i was recently asked to look over a topic in the school room part of the forum and rather than push the posters thread in a new direction, I decided to put some digital ink here and help you make sense of what order flow is and how it works.

The London close and any other session close is of no significance in the greater scheme of things. What most of you see will typically break down into two common moves, the next session will reverse the previous session, or it will work price to where the next batch of major orders lay. Many times London will close with lots of positioning going on. Some of you will see positioning as the term compression. But it has no defined shape or pattern, it is simply a slow price grind to an entry price area.

Never forget the fundamentals behind price movement, it will only break in the direction where more orders have been placed and the break will leave pending orders behind at the breaking price and these price levels are future targets on all time frames. The higher time frames give the greatest reaction as more of the professional money will be targeting those. Intraday targets are less dramatic in movement unless they happen upon a 4hr+ area of old movement. We know there will always be pending orders remaining to be filled at those now old prices, because the banks and institutions will have been given instructions from their customers to sell currency x and a particular price. The banks and institutions cannot get all the orders into the market at the desired price because it will cause the price to move too far from the desired order price.

Asia tends to have a subdued trading session and only when the EU and London sessions get under way will you get movement, the majority of the worlds money is traded in the London session and a great deal of the good moves happen in that session.

it is better if you dont beat yourself up looking for some secret to any session in particular, because there are no secrets to trading, no special or hidden signals. It is all plain Jane and in your face if you constantly refer to the big picture i.e higher time frame and then drop down for a closer view. I see too many people trying to conduct an of over analysis of what is very simple in reality. There are no banks or institutions that know what way price will break, they know as much as we do and its all right there on the charts. They look for the same things we do and their only edge, and it is a very slight edge, is the bigger players will have custom orders that tell them where their customers want to deal. In the overall picture this information has little validity because it can only be proven accurate after a move. Therefore historical price now becomes an asset to them and all other traders once they know where to look. This is what we do here in case the penny has not yet dropped.

There is also talk going on in this forum about liquidity and there is a very obvious fact which is easily over looked. Books and those who quote from them often state price can only do one of three things, price goes up, price goes down, and price goes sideways. Nonsense!

Price cannot go sideways, price is not a vector and can only rise or fall.

Order flow in the market determines how long it takes for price to move with more vigor than it does when in a period of consolidation. The amount of money traded to make any move happen is not a set amount or even a minimum amount of orders, in the end price will only move where there are more orders placed of a particular type i.e long or short. Nobody knows how many orders of each type there are in the forex market, there is no central exchange and no way to get the order information. Dont waste your time trying to find a way, countless others before you tried ways and all failed.

When price moves, those who were wrong are stopped out, new orders come in from those who are reversing their position and retail traders jump in as price is moving and those who were first stopped out also add momentum to the move with market orders in the direction of the break, mainly retail traders.

All we can do at best is look for historical reasons and apply this to a level or price area for possible future moves. Trading is neither science or art, it is a reflection of what value humans place on a particular financial instrument at a given point in time.

Supply is normally resistance and demand normally suport. Where it changes is when the level is broken, then you take the opposite view. Broken supply is now new support which is also new demand and the price rises. Some people call this a flip zone or S/R flip etc. The names and terms mean little, the main thing is to train your brain to be aware this can happen.

Take a current pair. eur/usd just broke resistance which means no sellers were willing to take it down and the buyers ran with it. If price makes it back to the break out area it will show support once price action confirms this. The time it takes for support to hold cannot be defined, it can take a single 5min candle or an hourly candle close etc. This ties into your risk appetite.

A clue is often gained on higher time frames where cleaner price action is displayed. Given today is a friday I still hold the view that I said some days back when I was looking for euro longs up to an important resistance/decision area. This area will be watched very closely by pro money for signs of major buying coming into the euro.

If you look on the daily chart this area should immediately stand out to you, if it doesnt. You must engage your logical brain and think like a guy with deep pockets and where do I see the most obvious place to put my money.

Now the current time is 2pm London and I see an hourly candle close with a spike on top. Some people have taken profit on the move and New York open is not far off. We also have a 4hr candle close at 3pm local and then we wait to see what will come about. There is a possibility of selling because we hit an old supply/decision area. Both long or short are options at current time, but I wont short this. I take the longer term view which is still bullish for about another typical days trading, a strong push will not surprise me either with an over head target and only strong bullish candles on the 4hr chart since July 25th.

I mentioned it many times before, this is counter intuitive and the rules change to most peoples eyes which is why I say there are no rules.

A new trading month is about to begin and here is what to do at the beginning of every month, and each week, day etc.

View and conduct your analysis on...

monthly chart weekly chart daily chart 4hr chart

On each new week

View and conduct your analysis on....

weekly chart daily chart 4hr chart

On each new day

View and conduct your analysis on....

daily chart 4hr chart 1hr chart + lower time frames of interest you with considering your risk and capital funding.

Lets get stuck into what I see on the monthly chart for eur/usd.

The blue purple lines represents support and resistance denoted with an S an R. I know, I spoil you lot rotten. The blue line has more touches and becomes the main line of interest. I will come back to these lines shortly and for the moment cast your eyes on the lower Box B. This is the last place where clean buyers entered the market, I call it clean because we have not had any attempt to come back into that box. Given the time frame being what it is and the support gained later in time and at higher prices, it would take incredibly bad news politically, financially and a war etc to pull price down that far. Given we are in recession the Euro is proving highly immune to lower prices contrary to the media telling us the sky is falling.

Above the blue line I have Box A, my script writer is off for the weekend so excuse the poor dramatic effects in my text. Box A is where few sellers remain, why?....price took most if not all of the sellers with it as it wound lower, therefore any future target we look for on this time frame is much higher and the top of the chart the most obvious place. Can we get there?....possibly, we need Europe to extract the digit and find a way to create virtual money to pay for real debts.

The present state of play on the monthly chart shows a bullish close and pinned support and also gave a nice false break to the down side. Given the world and their granny are short the Euro this move would have made sense to a lot of traders because the move until this monthly close was bearish.

Pay attention to the spike left of current price, see how it pinned the lower purple line? That was perfection to grab the last of the demand (buyers) to its left. Very nice move indeed and would have been seen by pro money as a nice covert long when everyone else was shorting the Euro, you only need to see that red candles close with a long tail which can only mean one thing, major buying was going on and right off support.

Who would have guessed? (c) The Doctor 2012.....there, glad I worked that in this early:)

Now onto the weekly chart, and you do the same at the beginning of ever new week. I dont wish to sound like a broken record but please get this into your heads if you want to get the over all picture. It is far to easy to just look at the daily and lower.

Ok, what have we got here. The lower purple line is a carry over from the monthly and the blue line is also carried over. You can see a better view of price reacting at these lines. Always treat a line more of an area and not a hard fixed line. Price wont always pin the line, but most of the time it gets very close. Markets are far from the chaos most see in a price chart.

I marked off the support and resistance levels and held Box A above to show you where most of the sellers got consumed. If we get up there, pushing through may not be too difficult, just want price action as it reaches the box.

Box C, a new box. Last of the newest seller in the market, but look how far they got and look at the reation, why?....the likely cause is there was already heavy shorting well above those traders and those short sellers shorted into support not far below, not a very bright move on any time frame. What you want it plenty room for price to move and a very obvious target. This will net you more profit in the long term even when trading off low time frame charts. Look for the room for price to move and the target before you pull the trigger.

The last candle is our weekly candle close, what do you see? Well considering I made it easy for you there is no problem is seeing a bullish close and pinning over head resistance. And this tells you what for the new week?....expect a pull back first, but there where?....look down and to the left for an area where you can see the last buyer comes in, or where there is good support. Would the blue line suit you?...or maybe the purple line?...lets look deeper again.

Here is the daily chart.

Box A carried over from the higher time frames and while its a good distance away, always keep it in mind as over head resistance as well as a target if longs look good. The blue line is also carried over and the purple too far down to see it on this time frame. The blue line now shows some order to the chaos, note the support it provided in the past, many hits, therefore it is of significance.

About the blue line is a black line, a lesser line of importance but still price has reacted here with both support and resistance coming in. It was the precursor to the last bullish move last week. Practically pixel perfect. Marked are two D candles, even though more exist, these are the most important that immediately jump out. These are decision candles where price decided it was time to make a move, note how it happens to also be at last Friday's close too, another decision area. Who would have guessed?

Last chart is the 4hr and I have this here just to concentrate your mind as you would on every new week day while trading from here and lower. We get many good signals off this time frame.

The blue line is once again carried over and is seen here to provide strong support. It also have clean and untested demand (buyers) remaining. Above the blue line we have a black line showing resistance at first, then price pushes through strongly and it forms support with a sweet single candle than pinned it nicely. Not going long on that close with such a strong signal would mean trading is not for you, it rarely gets to be much better than that entry.

Above this black line we could draw another horizontal line and you would see price was contained in a range. My upper black line is the top of the price range, but can you see where the lower line would be?.....approx 1.24850 on that chart.

We closed off the week with a bullish candle with no conviction in it at all and this does not surprise me. The end of each day and end of each week will very often show profit taking and this tends to negate the value to us as technical traders in reading that final candle.

A hint prior to the last candle close was a bearish engulfing candle, but there was no follow through and the closed candle sealed the deal for possible shorts. No takers.

We end the week with one candle pinning the upper green line which is resistance and next week I would expect a pull back into support/demand/false break and see can we muster some bulls and new orders with deep pockets would can push price up and through resistance. We will sit/wait and let those guys fight it out and we wont trade until we see at least price at an area of support and price action showing us buying is going on. A counter trend trade may be possible on lower time frames. Exercise caution with going against the tide of pro money.

I prefer to not use much in the way of buzz words or terms in my trading because it is not needed and only makes it more difficult for others to learn that is going on. I stick to the most basic and universal language used by professional money. Only economists like to use the BS terms, it helps them to sound as if they know what is going on, when in reality there is no way to know until it has happened.

You will not see me use trend lines or moving averages, fibonacci etc. None of these influence price and price will never react to them either. Price is a fixed and hard value and an indicator is a math function based on some guys idea of what the indicator is meant to display. My usual reply about indicators is this.....if I take the 200 period moving average off your chart, has price still moved without it?

Keeping this trading business simple is the key to success. My live charts have zero items drawn on them, totally blank and just candles on it. I use the cross hair to walk around the charts during the trading session to help me find areas as time marches on. The charts I post on here are a reflection of what I saw at the time, but not everything I saw. It would clutter a chart too much if I were to note all the meaning of every candle and area of interest. In time all successful traders develop a mental knack to immediately filter out the noise on a chart and only the important areas jump out at them. fxgangstah, my stop losses for the most part are mental and I do sit and watch my trades as they progress. Once price has moved away from my entry to where I consider it difficult for it to return to my entry price, only then will I place a hard stop. There are other times when price action looks 'settled' and I will place a hard stop. Much of this is in the eye of the trader and there are no hard and fast rules of using x point stops. If your entries are accurate you will often find your hard stops are rather small intraday. I had thought about posting a trade I took on the South Africa Rand last week where I had a hard stop, but I decided not to post up the trade because the wide stop with the Rand's character with major spikes would cause many here to have a heart attack with the draw down and sometimes violent price action.

I never use trailing stops, they are a good way to give points back to the market and cut your trade short. Broker like you to use them, I wonder why?

All my entries happen around support and resistance, supply and demand and decision areas. Anyone who places money in the market away from those area will ultimately fail and become part of the 95+% of ex traders. Once you enter at the correct area you have little draw down and lowest risk. The hardest part of trading is finding the entry, all else is child's play.

My targets are hard set. If the target is a clear old top I will hold the entire trade until it hits that level. If the move looks really nice and a few stroke moments come up, such as a fast spike in the opposite direction, I will look for price action to give me another entry if it coincides with an old area where the same thing happened in the opposite direction, a decision area. Then I will load up more. In the case of monthly and weekly trade signals I will scale in a touch early (low time frame price action) with really small lots and as it starts to move I will load up heavily. My targets for those are intraday and when they close I will again look for more trades in the direction of the bigger picture and only load up on those. The intraday counter trend trades will have lower point targets and hard stops due to the potential of the major players pushing it again. Remember, the pro money does not need price action for the most part, they are the market makers, they make the moves happen and they have the price levels of where they scale in and where the start to close out, and both cannot be done with a single click, they do it slow in the vast majority of trades otherwise the markets move away from them and they loose client money, thats worse than loosing your own in their eyes.

fxfury, the 200ma or ema is often used by the media as a way to guide you. They will say some load of tripe such as price has broken below the 200 ma and the market must be weak. I do not know of a single professional trader who uses any ma as a trade signal. All it means is over time price has come down, but we know that price has come down with supply making it happen and from the highs. You will never hear any person in the media saying price is on yearly highs (say a stock price) and how far can it go down?....we know in forex this is a good place to look for shorts. Stock traders are a different animal and trade often will blind ambition. There are companies out there who are trading on all time highs and their stock prices are still pushing higher. Why would I want to tie up say 300 to 2000 bucks per share on maybe 20 shares for about a year or more and make perhaps 10 to 50k profit, when I can take the same captial and make the same money in a month?

All indicators are FALSE and INCORRECT interpretation of REAL price. Write that on your monitors!

Given professional money know the most likely areas where they will filter in and out of their positions, this is where we also look based upon price action in these areas and where others say price is getting support of the x moving average. Over many years I have people show me the multi thousand dollar DVD systems/methods and the live courses they attended. Ask one very simple question here........

Trading is price in an area of interest, realised profit is price in an area of interest. (c) The Doctor 2012:)

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
I cant suggest a risk size, that is a problem only you the trader can answer given your capital and risk appetite. Obviously it is easier to do this with higher funding. From past experience I had taken a new trader's 3k account to average 1k per week profit while he was learning. Risk was.5 lots per trade and all trades taken off the 5min chart. If you look at an established chart where the London session is open for at least and hour and no terrible price action was going on as we saw toward the end of last week, only then can you see clarity and where entries can be pin pointed.

You can also see the average pull back amount and where buyers and sellers came in and left candles with wicks and tails. By all means measure all of these and determine what you feel is an amount of points you consider to be within your funds. I take every trade on the basis that it will fail, and I know before I take the trade how much money I will loose. More importantly, how much money I am prepared to loose. When I win there are no emotions of joy, just get on with the next trade and none of this.....well I would double up cos I done well last time. Money management works for both wins and losses.

I hope this gets you some way towards a risk appetite plan. Taking small bites with a few euro or dollars per trade will build an account in a surprisingly fast period of time. Getting more wins that losses will also grow your confidence and in time you can then go from say placing a 2 to 4 dollar order and work from a 6 to 10 dollar (1 lot) order. The hits when they come wont hurt as bad when you start low. Starting with small amount of real money is always wise and losses are low. In the virtual world you need to make virtual money on a demo account for at least six months before going live. Trade it the same as real money with tiny partial lots and the same risk plan. It does teach valuable lessons without risking a penny. A few will experience losses when going from demo to live, only because their emotions have caught up with them now that the money is real, and theirs.

posts.author: MitchWorse
posts.text:
Price Action => the action of price => How does price behave.

It means pretty much everything price does and has done. Is it making new highs, new lows, lower highs, higher lows, compressing, engulfing, rally, base / range, drop.

As IF likes to say: Past, Approach, Reaction, Thank You (P.A.R.T.Y): Past => Mark the decision points/supply demand/support resistance Approach => How does price move towards your levels => Price Action Reaction => How does price move away from your levels => Price Action Thank You => The reward from looking at past and present Price Action

Hope this helps. If not, keep on asking:)

A few questions came up by PM and throughout the forums and I thought I would answer these on some charts to aid clarity.

Here is a monthly chart of GBP/USD.

WE have come from a high price on this chart and rapidly down to a low price where the fall stopped. Why stop there?....look left and look at the spot I named buyers, this is history repeating itself in an reas which has not been tested before and where pro money know it is a good place to go long. The tell tale signs of pro money are all those long tails.

To create a tail of that magnitude it takes a large pool of money, certainly more than all money combined in this forum. Given we know this is a good place for buying, we would wait until we reach A, in fact two entries if you if saw how to profit from the first A....how?

Assume you took the first A, where is the target?.....follow price up, see that red candle with a wick on top?....that pinned a resistance area. I have left off much detail on this chart just to get your eye used to looking where it should. I will follow up with more detail later in this post.

Where are we now?....we know we came of lows where pro money came in and they are now in for a second time to the long side. Ask your logical brain a question, if I were long here, where is my target?....you will of course know this before you hit the buy button, right?!

On the larger scale there is only one obvious target. Well two if you wish to split hairs. We are so far from B that there is a whole lot noise to get through first and all the noise is nowhere near enough profit for pro money to justify taking the trade. There are 100's of billions looking you in the face, this is a powerful force and will eat you alive if you dont trade with them. They want profit and want as much as they can push the market toward the obvious target. There are two traders active in this chart, both bulls and bears. Look at the price action, which do you see is the stronger hand?

Also note on B, the left most candle is end of the bull run and the right most B is there to serve two purposes. It gets short term traders long because they never think the party is over, and when price pins the tail of the first B candle it retraces and takes out all the stops and feeds the bears easy money. From that candle you should have been short and wait for the break. It is virtually the same as what happened at A. A second shot with a false move to get more orders for the reversal is very common.

The same monthly chart here again, but with much more info drawn in. The lower grey box is demand/buyers. Looks very obvious to you now I hope with the second touch of the area. Look left for D. The left most D is a decision area and one of the questions asked of me and why some other trader says we must not trade decision areas. Look closely at the first D, where has it formed?...right on top of an S/R box, therefore the decision area is also support and we go long at support once we are coming off lows. Did we come off lows?...yep.

Look at the right D, see the same thing?...it was also a retest of a clean area of proven demand. Price action even confirmed that for a further wake up call. Look into the middle of the chart, see decision 1 & 2. These are also decision areas, both show up in the correct area and both have price action as a bonus. Do you think I am wrong to trade off these decision points?....I am not saying the other named trader is wrong, it could be the person has not looked at price as I do. If something is proven to work over time, then it works and cannot be said to be otherwise.

Look at the upper S/R area in the thin band and please excuse my poor drawing, I got a belting head ache all weekend and typing this is not helping either. I missed out of placing R1 on the bottom of that S/R area. But note now R1 pinned the box, this box is now resistance, look left, see how the box formed S1?....look left again, see how the box was resistance?

Now look at the top. I left B on there to concentrate your minds. What does E suggest to you? The E area was an area used to collect nothing but more orders to allow price to fall, it contains weeks of very serious buy backs of short orders, just look at the money at play in there, thats big player flexing their financial muscle. The last B told us already we are looking for shorts, there is nothing in the E area to say different and we wait and hold. All the tails in E are not in the right place for long entries because pro money will not get enough profit going long at those prices, the target is just too close.

At C the market just fell, and was pushed very very hard by pro money. note the over all length of the candle body in the first bear candle and the close very much solid right to the end, not even a hint of a pull back. The firs target at S1 was blown through and the next was at the lower box and the origin of the move up. If price doesnt show at least some profit taking on the way down in an area where historically we saw reactions, then expect the big picture to play out and ride it if you have the patience.

At the moment price is showing bullish strength and a target you can all see by now is the upper S/R box. But along the way we have some bumps. Lets focus in a little.

Here is the weekly chart. I have zoomed out a little so it looks a touch like the monthly and I done this so you can see more of levels rather than candle stick price action. We came off two levels of support, the lower grey box and recently the lower gold box. There is potential for a retracement down to collect orders, but where is the easiest place for price to go?...how about E for a near term target?....how about E and D given they are so close together and for all purposes an over lapped target area. But realistically the obvious target is the bottom of the upper S/R box which was pinned just above C. A grind up is possible as this helps get intraday orders, or a big shake out and form a nice long tail on a false bearish break. We have to wait for price action to show us. I am not in this pair, but if I wanted to get in, I would wait for a pull back into old demand and look for longs, I see not reason why pro money would want to short this longer term.

If we hit the upper S/R box and push through, all I want to see if a fall back on top of the box, maybe a nice tail into the box with a close above, and then load the boat long up to A. I put B on there for you to determine if it would make sense in your mind to target it. I cant spoon feed you everything:)

And the last significant candle?.....it is whats known (in some circles) as a high wave candle. Supposed to be a 'nothing much' candle. I dont use that language, all candles have a meaning. What the candle done was break long and break short and the majority of trading was conducted within the body which is about 1/3 of the price value of the entire candle. It gave you a false long, stopped you out if you were gone long, it gave you a false short and stopped you out if you went short. So who won?....pro money won, because previous price action off support told us the price was going higher and you focused on one and most current candle to take a trading decision. It was clear all along we came off support we came with buyers on board and we have an over head target which has not yet been hit and its about as obvious as you get, the target is the purple line and if you look left.......is the base of a decision area....and if you drop lower in time frames you will see nice price action in there. Simon,

I dont know who Same Seiden is or his/her background etc. So it is not a trading style or technique I am familiar with and can comment upon. All my charts here are based upon what I have found and proven over time for myself. If it doesnt work for other people, then it is only down to them not being able to see what I can see and I post the proof of my work in live charts where the trade is ongoing. Other traders be they professional and retail all have their own take on where to place a trade and when to exit. All traders have their own methods and mine is just but one, and not necessarily the correct one, it works for me. Take what you can from it and make it your own, change, add, remove as you need to in order to see results.

There is so much information about trading online that it is causing confusion among all those who are trying to make a go of this. Many will spend years looking for a system, and jump from one to another, they will do the same with indicators and jump from one to another. All this does is waste years and isolate them from the most important part of trading, which is the price.

I could put you all into a room for a day and go through live charts and still find people are confused. The contradictory comments I make will just not make sense. A candle stick of the same visual formation can mean different things depending on where it formed in time. Time and experience will eventually make sense of this for you, there are no short cuts.

Many factors determine the time frame you choose to trade off of and this is also your risk appetite. I always take my lead from very high times and drop down into smaller and smaller time frames looking for an entry and an exit. I can take a 5min entry as I have done with the dozens of trades in my euro trades posted yesterday, play them off the 1 and 4hr longer term and as price reaches overhead resistance, which can become supply/sellers can be my target. I then have a decision to make, do I close all positions, or close some and hold others in case we see new support, which is then new demand/buyers and follow the continued move up. Even the pro money do not know if price will hold or break at these levels and it is why you see a fight between the bulls and bears around those levels. The creation of new demand is not classic supply and demand theory. I do not take supply and demand as the absolute only way to look at the markets. My charts show newly created trading areas all the time.

I know some of my trades will appear odd to many and why they were taken where they were. All you need to do is check where the pro money was active and when its setting up for the next move. They cannot hide all their cash for very long. Where the most difficult trades are hidden are in the longer periods of consolidation, those can break either way because the longer it continues the more money both the pro bulls and bears have in the market and when it breaks it moves hard and fast, never take those break outs, wait.

Pro money has to feed money into the market all the time and what looks a quiet period is still active and subtle signs, some are what many see as spinning top candles. I will see if I can get some candle stick close up charts in over the weekend.

Supply and demand is not 'the' method, there is no one method. There are times when classic supply and demand doesnt fit very good. One of the best things you could do is to work on one entry that you can see improvement on, and see how many you can spot it historically. When you have this working all the old entries will come to you in a split second and that is your proof of having that entry type correct. Then move onto the next. Master one, the rest will follow in time and you may find new ways of getting other entries that others dont talk about or say not to take. If it works for you, then it works!

i believe in MT4 it has a feature to allow you step through a time frame candle by candle. Just take a common currency pair, scroll way back in time and then hit the step button and mark where you think are the setups and then see are you correct. Turn off the auto scroll if you are doing this in the live market.

If you go back through my posts you will see I talked about a bullish euro weeks ago, long before this move. If the trading books, or system, or method or some guru says there is nothing to trade there, then you just lost of the best move of the year. The early signs of a move come only off high time frames no matter if all you can afford is a 5min time frame trade. Pro money has been active to the long side for a while now. Go back in time on the charts and find where it started coming in. Those people wont bail early and want profit and will get it. We follow them.

Forget about indicators no matter what its function is, all they do is draw attention away from your price eye onto the indicator where it should not be. You must learn to read a chart in your own head in seconds and decide do you go long, short or wait. Most times, I wait and its boring as hell.

Before you take any trade, know the target and know where the safest place is for a stop and set all of these. As you improve you can use mental stops if you are watching the charts and only have one of two trades in there. I have a ton of trades still live and all have hard stops because there is too much to give back if I let it go. Earlier today my stop was moved above the last trade placed and there is a few thousand points profit combined in all of the trades. The entries off the 5min are the same as pro money do on a daily basis even when taking the long term view, if the capital is there and the opportunity for a trade comes they take it. I loaded up heavily on the euro and its paying back nicely now. I would not have loaded up so heavy unless I saw early signs of bullish activity weeks ago. Setups like these come only a few times per year. Get good at even catching one and the money made even on a small account will make you several times the account size back in profit. Patience, take your time and let your brain soak in the charts. Screen time is your friend.

The longer time frames are where the money comes in and once you drop down lower, look for the small areas where you see the first one of two pull backs, this will form support or resistance for the main move. Price has to be slowed and and reversed and only pro money can do this. Once price has stopped its move and gained support or resistance (depending on the direction) then look for price action for your entry off these new lower time frame levels.

My comments I hope do not confuse you.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
Some light candle reading for you all. The pun's come early on today.

First chart is monthly chart, the pair involved is meaningless and I removed as much from the chart to concentrate your eye and brain.

Look at where price is now and can you determine the reason for the current candle, and lets assume it is a closed candle.

Here is the same chart with a little detail, and just enough to show whats going on. We again assume a closed candle and we see a reaction of support and old demand, the price goes up. The likely target?....the box above. All simple, no fuss and nothing difficult to understand.

Lets really get into the details now.

Here is a zoomed in view of the last leg down in price. To help guide your eye here, candle 1 was a race to grab old demand and is also taken at support.

2 the bulls have already got their work done and the follow through buy intraday bears is weak the close well off the lows.

3 the bulls intent is obvious here with a very large body and close with very little wick on top. On the other chart you will see this candle hit old supply.

4 considering we just hit old supply this candle close showed such weak bullish momentum that it was plain to see we need to fall back down, or collect more orders to break above.

5 a weak bearish candle, note how it closed well inside the previous candles low, note the long tail, a sign of buying.

6 a very strong bull candle with strong close above support, so we long this puppy to the moon now right?

7 no, we wait for a pull back and see does support hold. And 7 is a perfect bearish engulfing candle and proves candle 6 was a false bullish break.

8 unfortunately the market timing for the previous move was not very good and we are now stuck between close in old supply and demand. When this happens we need to keep the big picture in mind, we are still below supply. This candle attempts to grab more orders from the bulls by the tail showing buying, however the weak close tells is its going nowhere.

9 we have a break below near term candle 5 and old demand from candle 3. But hitting candle 3's demand hard means we have to see a reaction higher.

10 this is the reaction from candle 9, it has setup up pro money for the main bearish move.

11 this is interesting, the candle pushed lower than the previous candles wick and closed within the body of candle 3 which is still the most significant candle we need to break.

12 finally a strong break and strong close. Of note here is the candle got into the tail of candle 1. There were a lot of buyers here and even though it is not the first time price has been in that area, there is validity given to this area given its likely hood to act as resistance once broken and retested.

13 no interest in taking price lower yet and no progress made by bulls or bears. The very slight tail below the tiny body means we wait.

14 this is the start of the pro bears selling. See how the wick pulls in supply from candle 12 and closes as a bullish looking candle but with a very low close on the candle 12 body. Books will tell you this is a bullish engulfing candle because it had contained the previous candle, correct, but, the books fail to tell you the reason for the wick and where it went.

15 Something to look at on this candle is the fact that the body is both bearish and closed within the previous candle, but no takers higher considering candle 14 is what is considered bullish. Pro money know better.

16 This is the bug push to get the market running and all the work prior to this candle was done in candle 14 and a lot of bears waited for this move whereas candle 14 would have got day traders long and now candle 16 would have stopped them out adding fuel to the bearish orders. Also note candles 12, 13, 14, 15 are all at S/R.

17 not much to say, we are moving down at a nice clip and money being made by the bears, dont stand in front of this freight train, be on it.

18 The line at the bottom of my chart is old demand taken from the chart earlier up. So why has price suddenly stopped and gone bullish?....two reasons, not all pro money has the same take profit target and some will bail before the ultimate target. This candle shows profit taking, which in itself has pinned the last of the bears who entered at the close of 16 which is 17's open. Who would have guessed it setup one final small move down. But on this time frame is enough to buy a nice lunch:)

19 old demand pinned to the pixel and also the first sign of the market slowing down. The tail tells us this. When the market is running hard it will not stop on a dime and the tails and wicks you see at major old price level on higher time frames has to be traded against in the opposite direction by pro money to first stop the current move and setup the next. This is never a cheap exercise and costs a lot of money. We see the wicks and tails and look for our entries.

20. Given pro money reached their target it was of no surprise we will at least see one small leg up and possibly a retest of the newly created low.

21 so far we are no longer bearish and now bullish, but a retest of the low is still on the cards unless we see a test of new support coming along and this may look like a decision point. Possible places for a sensible decision are candle 18, 13 thru 15 cluster.

The time frame for this doesnt matter because price which is plotted in time is a fractal of itself and keeping all the old support and demand areas from higher time frames for use on lower time frame charts is essential for success. An example would be a 1 or 5 min trader taking a short at candle 19 because it was a break of 18, but not understanding that he was shorting into a major higher time frame of buyers.

The other horizontal lines on the chart are a partial guide to help train your eye and logical side of your brain. There are more places to find support and resistance and I will let you look for those.

If you are willing to wait price will always show you a clear direction and when its turned. There are times when even a 5min trade wont come around for a day or so. This chart is primarily for a trader in the US who made a nice gesture to me and I am returning both his appreciation and letting him know there is more value in money alone. Everyone else has some more material to study, so thank our US friend for coming up with this idea of a numbered candle stick chart.

Have a good weekend everyone.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
A follow up on the last post.

This chart is a closer in view of current price and where we will likely see changes. Some of what I will say here will make what you have read earlier be contradictory. But, lets get stuck in and see what happens.

First off we have a purple line at the bottom of the chart. This is near term a minor support and resistance. This follows on from the bullish signal on a previous chart. 'A' shows where pro money have done their restest to see will the bears come in and if not, give the bulls another place to enter long with a safer margin for profit. Close of A was the entry long.

Above the purple line is a black line, this is placed at the origin of the sellers where I also indicated it wont be respected....eventually, how long we spend in that price area will say a lot for the move. Where you need to turn your brain upside down is that we are no longer bearish, but bullish and old supply is no longer valid to us on this chart and our primary lead comes off the higher time frame and watch how it helps setup new demand on this chart.

Above the black line is a 'D'. This is a decision to take price down further. It was so close to higher time frame demand that shorting there was not an option. It is from this old supply area where the major change in the market will come about. Once the new bullish order becomes established the additional newly created demand further up the chart and on lower time frames will become more reliable as pro money are happy to hold through all the daily pull backs.

The next black line up is very obvious S/R, w will expect a reaction from price up into this area and we once again look for price action to tell us how strong the market is. At that point we will start taking out a lot more of the long term bearish stops. There are longer term traders who do hold for too long and get taken out.

Finally on the very top we have three old supply areas all of which will become areas to watch for as price approaches. Getting the right order flow prior to these areas will mean a push through immediately. The timing needs to be correct for each move or it will allow price fall back down until it reaches support and where prices will be cheaper for the bulls to take in more long orders as the weak bulls bail out. There will also be further orders develop as price climbs and the new comer bears get stopped out. All this adds fuel to the continuing move up.

The transitional areas when day traders forget about the monthly and weekly is where most get chopped up badly and all could have been avoided if the bigger picture is examined each day. Even though this is a weekly chart and most here dont have the capital to trade this kind of move, you can still achieve the approx 230 point move from candle A to where price is now, by dropping down to a 5min and placing fractional lots. In fact scaling in like this on longer term moves is how I work my way through the daily chart and will keep putting in small lot sizes are prices moves. At worst I will loose the last order placed and get profit on all the previous trades. Look at my euro trade for all the trades placed and one of those is in excess of 230 points shown here and all my combined orders are several thousand points already and when the trade is closed it might break 10,000 points with all orders total, price action next week will tell me when to close some, or all. The idea is to reduce risk and hold through the deeper pull backs to realise the profit. Its still a lower risk means of getting larger profits without placing large lot trades in one or two places.

An example would be, if I were taking a day trade off the 5min for a typical move in one day and I liked the area I was placing the trade. I might put on between 2 and 10 lots. If the same 5min entry was to be used for a longer term hold, I will reduce down to.5 to 2 lots per trade and scale in as the subsequent entries come around. But each new entry will have the previous orders safe with stop above and in a safe place against normal price action and profit in the bank. My risk is now lower than placing large lots in one or two places and profit margin much higher than day trading.

The point I want to drive home is to never be fixated on the market is bullish or bearish and learn to recognise the high time frame supply and demand turns. If they look choppy lower down, just wait for a few days and price action will start to look much cleaner.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
What looks like a pivot point on a higher time frame is of interest to me because it will be a decision area on a lower time frame and if taken with S/R and price action, I will trade it. A pivot point in a low time frame is rather rare and taking that on say a 1min time frame is not for me.

Pro money only gets value when it is in first and can shake you out and take your money and your order and turn it into profit for them and help feed the machine further along. The smartest money in the world is in cash, if this makes sense.

A break out/pull back and support/resistance is the back bone of my trades.

I omitted to comment on C-12's trend lines and channels. Any line other than horizontal is in my opinion, useless. Price is not a vector and for anyone to convince me otherwise will need to state why price doesnt always follow a trend line or trend channel, thus making the use of such a line pointless. All trend lines and trend channels fail, they have to. Price only responds to old price level and once they are hit, pro money comes in and then current price moves.

The most you will see on a pro's charts will be the odd horizontal line. On my own charts they are virtually free of everything other than candles and I walk around the chart with the cross hair tool when I need to get more detail. But most of the time, I eye ball everything.

All this other junk with macd, rsi, fibonacci is all complete nonsense. I do not know one pro trader who uses any of those things when a trade is planned taken and exited.

12 moving into 11 was the inevitable move down after the earlier work was done by the bears. That candle was where pro money was already sitting inside when it broke.

18 took the last of the late to market sellers in and they didnt get much profit out before monthly demand was hit. Unless there is good room for profit and an obvious target, let the setup go, even if it is a perfect setup. Pro money wont sell hard from a level like 18, at best you will see light orders just to get price down to the target and the last reaction was an immediate reversal.

On longer legs moves often end with many long tailed candles. It costs a bundle to stop price like that and you can be sure once taken off the monthly especially, the pro's will not want that amount of capital tied up in the market to be against them for long. Pro money buys into a short market as it nears the target and it sells in a bullish market as it nears the target. All the other orders they place are being attempted to hide in decision areas and at S & R. There is no way anyone here can get in right at the end of a run, the money to ride out the chop for a few weeks while the market changes direction would break us all.

Price will react at those 11, 12 and 17, 18 candles on the way back up. How much of a reaction is unknown and all we can do is what price action into and out of those areas. Once you see the market direction, trading in that direction is the safest.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
Floor trader pivots or any other functions that are calculated on price are to me of no interest. Why distance yourself from actual price, historical price with a set of fictional future prices?

All they are in my mind are another indicator, and indicators have no place on my charts. If they work for others that fine, let them run with it. I want to see a means of getting the best data on where the likely reaction places will be based upon known past price levels. Its a rather basic and simplistic way of looking at markets, but there are a lot more than me out there trading like this for a long time.

I guess you need to feel comfortable with what you can find will work for you, prove it over time, and use it.

Most session closes will see profit taking and this will show up as price either drifting off, or hitting a previous old level. On your chart the close pinned an old decision area which further back in history was and still is a major support and resistance level. A long off that was a high probability. There is also what is known as positioning that pro money does around price levels of interest, but you wont see much talk of it in public due to it being aimed and used by pro money with deep pockets.

Intraday charts will burn you easy and that NY close you show will have got some traders short. I have stated it many time before and maybe its worth stating it again. If you take any trade, who are you trading with, who are you trading against, is there enough room for profit, is there an obvious target, is there an safe place for my stop. If you can get in on the coat tails of pro money most of the time, you will grow an account in a period of time that will make it appear you are robbing a bank. Even say 5 euro on a 60 point typical daily range is 300 euro profit. In the same 60 points pro money are into 7 figs even for the same move. If you can keep in mind that there must be a sensible entry and exit, it will be rare you loose.

There is so much noise on the internet and opinions offered that it is easy for anyone to get confused and jump from one thing to the next. The best advice I can offer anyone in trading new or old, is keep your charts ultra clean with no indicators, only horizontal lines (fewer is better) and only trade off a closed candle.

Just because there is a large candle, or large spike doesnt mean the market is changing direction or that it has to be like this because NY or London has closed. Price will move according to the direction given on higher time frames, because the real market movers operate only up that high and a daily spike of 100 points or more is meaningless unless its reach their new entry point, or exit point. Make sense?

Another basic and simple fact to keep in mind is at any market open or close is, if you are not in the market, wait and allow it settle. If you are already and want out, want for it to settle, false moves are very common around those times. If you find yourself getting stopped out, where was your stop and is there a trend in getting stopped out you can see?....there is always a reason. You can also scale in and out of trades to spread your risk thinner. This works well when you want to hold for longer periods of time. Loose the pivot points if you can and concentrate on price levels. The longer you have used any form of indicators means the longer it will take for you to reprogram your brain and delete all the old lies they told you.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
Seeing the setups after the fact means you are learning and this being similar to learning a new language, there will be a lot of time in the early days when you hear someone speak some basic words, but your brain is not used to them, so it has to make you wait while it processes the sound and then decide if it is a sound that has been associated with a meaning. Over time, the waiting time reduces and eventually this will all happen in real time and be smooth, fluid and no guessing, a trade setup will be good or not so good. The bad ones you let go.

I deliberately said not so good, because there are trade setups I see that are not the really nice type I like to take, but if the levels make sense and there is room for profit I will take it with a smaller lot size to reduce my risk in case it goes bad.

I personally do not use limit orders, I pull the trigger live. This my style and others will have pending orders waiting for price to come to them and then see what happens. The problem I have with that, is that while price is coming to your order, the newest price action might not look so good now as it did when you first spotted the trade. I will place automatic take profit targets and unless its from lower than a 4hr I tend to keep a piece on, just in case it breaks the target area. At worst I give back a few points and that is of no concern to me as most months I have made plenty points.

The limit order thing is a personal choice, there is no right or wrong. Trade with your risk and capital in mind and build a style that is yours.

Another quick follow up.

Here is a 30min chart and the blue lines have changed from their previous green because it was not very clear for support and resistance outlining the price range formed by today's price action.

posts.text:
On lower time frames I still use 4hr+ as my guide. Even though I am now out of the euro trade I will still consider scaling in long. The higher time frames are still bullish and helping now is the lower time frame action showing bullish activity too. I will pull the trigger when it looks good to my eye.

Look for multiple reasons to take any trade, all must be obvious and pro money must show signs of activity for lower time frame entries to work.

The time frame you choose to enter must gel with your risk appetite and capital. Also be aware that when trading intraday you do not have the luxury of time. That is, waiting for a 1hr candle can miss out on a lot of trade entries. You have to decide what kind of move you want i.e how many points. Using a 1hr will net you more per trade, but you wont get many of those in a day. Where the 1hr candle shines (pun) is when it closes nicely at a good time during the trading day and there is resistance or support along with it. If price action on the 5 and 15min look good, then I will take it and know before hand if I am playing it to the next supply or demand area or if I will close some at that area and leave a portion on to run.

Where you place your entries, exits and how you manage the trades is a personal thing and there is no right or wrong, it is done to suit your pocket and style as a trader. Try developing a trading style on a time frame you feel comfortable with and take it from there. It will evolve over time into something that feels comfortable, and once you reach that, stop changing it and hone it down to become second nature. It may not be there yet, but when you see the right setup for your style, light bulbs go off and you are all set.

Screen time is the best educator there is.

It has been a while since I posted a trade, so here is a live one. This is Brent crude on the daily time frame.

Overhead we have a gray box that is an old supply area, we touched the bottom of this box four days ago and I waited for a deeper push into the box. Clearly we didnt get a deeper push in and I had to sit and wait for the next area to be hit lower down and where some S/R and price action would bring a trade.

If you look at candle A, you will see it pinned old supply and the market rose as expected. But what does the close of that candle tell you?....look at its close in context to what history is around it, it is at the same price as the previous bullish move up. Pure fluke you say, yeah sure!

The following day we see a false bullish move which on the intraday charts would have had day traders going long. I had no intention of going long when pro money had already signaled their intentions. It was the break of the 2nd last candle today that got me in short. The entry was taken off the 15min chart as it tends to be a little easier to get entries with oil, rather than the 5min which can easily mess you about. If you look at your own 4hr chart you will see a large spike down, this was the candle that got my attention, note it pinned old supply. On the 1hr the same area has two candles with long tails and no bullish follow through, if you saw that and went long. Bad move, it was not a supply demand play at all. The overall market picture must be in your mind at all times and not focus purely on supply and demand intra day. The higher time frame price action and their supply and demand areas take priority.

Walking down from where I entered I have a number of choices for a target. I can go for the last demand area which is pretty much hit now, or go lower to my blue line which is the most significant S/R on the chart and an obvious place as I like to see. Or I can sit through the pain of the ugly decision area which is a real messy price action area, but if broken there is only place left to go ad that is 90usd or less. Do keep in mind my blue S/R line did see strong bullish move off back in Dec 2011. A reaction there is highly likely, but equally likely not to turn the market back above 118 unless the bulls manage to get a ton of orders.

There is the possibility we are at the beginning of a bear oil market. We need a lot more information before taking longer term bearish trades. first up is a 4hr chart of the euro/usd.

The two upper black lines are here to show you how the candle tails removed quickly old demand, a nice trick if you can spot this in real time and is an S/R play when you break it down. Marker E shows the clean price action and the desire of the bulls to get price higher.

Even in the very recent past, only the previous two candles showed strength to the bears. Given we have a wall of buyers that were left by the side of the road at E, would you short this?....all those buyers need to be absorbed if the market is going to turn and a show of strength by the bears.

Now down to the 1hr where it gets interesting, or perhaps more interesting from an intra day perspective.

Lower box is a consolidation of price and so too is the box above, look at your own 1hr chart with nothing but candles on there, can you see this by eye?....if you can, you have developed a good edge over other traders who look for breaks rather than how and where the move developed etc. Now look at C, again can you see these candles touch the top of old resistance/new support/new demand and in doing so they quickly fill new demand and race off, none of us would have caught these moves even on the 1hr. Again, the bulls wanted price higher, fast!

At the top of the chart we have a minor S/R level. This was the area I was looking at for the past few days while putting my comments in this part of the forum. We have broken below it and retested old support, which at A was bullish activity rejected and the bears ran with it, no surprise there as it was classic S/R at work, but no way would I take it. This is still short term bearish trading and not for me, too risky.

Again we try to test old support a second time which has already once before proved to be resistance and the remaining bulls didnt have the necessary $$ to push price above and only one thing then will happen, price falls off.

The last attempts by the bulls are both candles marked at B. Note the bearish move down is rather weak looking on the 1hr, but strong on the 4hr. Now note the time, this happened in the Asian session where it is typically quiet.

Now what?......we wait for a reaction off an area where we can see old bulls active, or you trade it lower with the greatest of care because we have strong bullish history not far from where price is at the moment. Market sentiment doesnt change direction on a dime.

D is one place I will carefully watch, after that it would be my blue line on the 4hr chart.

You cant force a trade, so let the price come to your pre planned area and where you have a better opportunity of reducing your risk and getting points in the bank. The daily is starting to suggest me fall to my 4hr blue line, we wait for a close before taking that decision. If this means a failure for bullish activity around D, I will skip the euro and look at something else until next week. Why?....because if no bullish activity happens soon, we will likely close on a strong bearish weekly candle and I wont stand in the way of a raging bear!

C-12, this may seem like I am picking on you, but I assure you I am not. Think logically about what you wrote.

"I mark off trend lines and sometimes fibs. Its helpful for me to see what the majority are doing and helps me spot potential traps."

1. Logical question, does a trend line touch or a fib touch change the direction of price?

2. Logical question, if I remove a trend line and/or fib, does it effect how price HAS moved?

3. Are the majority of traders correct if this is what you are looking for?

4. How do you differentiate from the majority to the winner?....given we know the majority of traders fail. This is well documented for nearly 100 years.

Look at the area you circled in red. Ask another logical question, would pro money buy there?...if so why, if not why?

When you find the answers which are all easy to arrive at, it will greatly simplify your approach. And like I said at the top of this post, I am not picking on you and just want you to break the market down to very basic and simple analysis, every technical pro trader does the same.

beebolbod, pro money are large banks, institutions and money given to both by the wealthy to trade and it is done so along side the banks and institutions own funds. All the market liquidity you see getting spiked all over the charts is coming from these people. Retail cannot get a look in, it is not organised to get enough money in the market at the same time and it doesnt have the reserve to absorb price movement.

When price moves it does so with more orders in the market when compared to the opposite position holders. When it leaves a price and heads away, it will leave some orders left behind and given time it will get back to or close to the origin at some time in the future. This can take years.

The euro when viewed from long term charts is showing a turn. Grab a monthly and have a look. For this to play out we will go through weeks when it may appear bearish, this is all part of how the market works because you have all sorts of capital in the market and some hold for longer periods than others and this all adds to the way in which the market moves in relation to higher value orders being opened and closed.

My trading style is mine alone and not everything here is what the other guys in AG do. I have been trading a long time and developed what I know from years of research and talking with people in the industry. How the other AG guys trade is what they found works for them and it is good to see people no matter who they are, find something that works and they prove it over and over again. As I said before, take what you can from my posts and also from other places and people and make it something you can build upon and make your own unique style. Given time and interest you may well surprise yourself.

C-12, good, looking for demand is what you should have been doing and also noting what is going on in the higher time frames. Most retail trades do what the books, course material and other armchair experts tell them, which is typically place a stop above a previous high or below a previous low, depending in the direction you are trading.

Spiking these areas and even spiking supply and demand areas is very common. All those tricks gets cheap money entries for the pro's. They want a cheap price to enter and will do all they can with the funds available to make it happen. At times you will see incredible moves and this is a number of pro money funds entering at the same time and that is also common in highly visible places in their eyes, we are talking about price levels of note in the 4hr+ for this and it will show up intraday as a bullet out of nowhere.

Good trade by the way, now be careful with the time of day and it also being end of week.
