posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
Simon, I dont think there any candle stick books that show candle sticks as they approach and leave areas of supply and demand. Most of the text will be candles alone, and then candles in context, but not in the context of supply and demand. Have you ever noticed how the majority of traders get excited with a pin bar which is really called a hanging man, or a reverse pin bar which is a shooting star?...same goes with a doji. They mean little to us unless they form in the right place because we want to be in the move before all the retail traders where the various schools of though with moving averages must cross, or a pull into a certain value moving average. All those approaches are much later than where I want to be, which is before the howling mob.

I want to take money from retail traders because I cant take it from the pro's. Good fortune means this tends to work the vast majority of the time:)

The most useful thing to do first is get the accepted meaning of a candle in your head first and then look at historic supply and demand areas and look for candle sticks that make sense of the move into and out of the area.

There are no set patterns or formations because the market will not show the same path twice. In time you will find some common things to look for and then build around those where some subtle signs come in. All that has to be done with the higher time frames in mind and watch as they give signals for their supply and demand areas. The market has may faces and wont show the same one very often, pro money want to hide what they are doing for as long as possible, or at least until they filter in as many orders they possibly can. After that, all it takes is one little push and off it goes.

Time for a refresher on some principles and to help you focus on what I hope is becoming obvious for you all. I wont continue to post charts like these as it must be rather boring for many of you and I do not wish to labour the point either.

First chart is eur/gbp on the daily.

Blue lines are support and resistance and the lower most s/r line is only there to help highlight a particular candle.

Starting in reverse order we see candle C. I have noted this in the context of current price action. We have fallen off the highs after piercing old supply. Note how weak the sell off looks, very little in the way of conviction from the bears so far. We have our middle s/r line next which could be a good near term target and then we have the candle marked C, which is the origin of the push up through resistance. Demand did not come into the market at that point, it was in there all along which is seen from the reaction at candle B which came off real support. Its support may not appear obvious, but it gained this from the pin bar off the top of the box where candle A is marked. See how candle A quickly took buyers with it, now look at the candle prior to B. It was simply a false move and not only took pro money with it, the day trader bears and those who got stopped out all fed the bulls for the real move. Nice. After a time you will see stacked orders happen where they dont appear to be coming off areas of support and resistance / supply and demand, but the very fact that they are stacked originally off those areas gives them credibility.

On to the 4hr chart.

The blue lines remain so that you can get your eyes tuned to the over all picture taken from the daily and transposed here. Its gets interesting on this chart too. Starting at the bottom we also see the top of the box from the daily sitting there with a nice move of the top of it, which you will recognise by now as......support/demand.

The black line above this box is an interesting area due to its history, it is still acting beneficial and we pinned the line which took more demand upward. At candle B is the first move off support which has been setup since the move off the top of the box. Is this making sense yet?.....you ought to be building plenty mental images around this.

Above candle B we have another minor s/r line and proves an old decision area to be important, we always mark these are time passes because they will become useful at some time in the future. Note candle C. I have two marked. The black line from candle C is off the daily and looks obvious there, but lower down on this 4hr we can see the move setup for black C came about by orange C, which is taken off support/demand. Who would have guessed?.....been a while since I got that in:)

Our middle S/R line was blown through and price was determined to break resistance, this is a clear sign pro money are active and now want to set the stage for the real move and the major money maker. I have three candles marked at D. Note all the long tails showing buying, but as you should be asking yourself now, why are the bulls buying off fresh air?

If you look on the daily chart you will see the bulls are in fact buying off old support from the 16th of May. This was a major turn and always expect a reaction at such places even if your chart doesnt show you. This is a good example of why I keep going on about keeping the higher time frames in mind and know whats going on up there.

Once pro money cleared out the weak holders with three deep bearish candles they had all the free orders they wanted and price could only go one way and to a very obvious target, daily supply. Perfection.

And now your mission, if you choose to accept it, is to determine where price is likely to go next and where is a sensible price to enter and where is a sensible target where there is room for profit.

Hey guys

I was recruited over here from the FF forums by Turtle man and I have been perusing the forums all weekend. Very very good stuff. S/D based PA trading is really where great traders are built.

The recent posts by Doc about the PA on the EUR/GBP pair. I have been following this exact pair since the Break and close over the.7955 level. This level has yet to be properly retested as support.

We all have different strategies to assess if price will bounce or break at a critical area of S/R such as this one. I will share mine.

1. Determine smaller trends/channels/critical numbers and zones for scaling into the trade. (I personally use Monthly/weekly/Daily levels to find critical S/D, then I will scale in those zones using PA on the 5min/15min/1hr tf's to mitigate risk) 2. Determine market timing. Typically currency pairs move most when the related equity markets are open. Ill have alarms set for these levels and look to trade them during the European session. 3. Observe PA and play each subsequent channel( break/pullback/fake/break w/momentum/close/retest/ lock in position/next channel) 4. Keep an eye on correlating markets and news wires for aberrations.

I keep my trading itself very simple.

I look forward to when price gets to some of these zones and then we can get into detail on how to trade them:)

Wulf

Greetings all.

A lot has happened since my last trade posts and while I still do not have much free time to come in here, I will describe a GBP/USD trade that I took earlier today and still letting it run.

First chart and in reverse order (the opposite of what I used tell you) is of the 1hr.

Blue line shows support and resistance and has been proved over time to be and price where moves happen. On the top of the chart is a yellow box which indicates 1hr supply and today we got well into this area which is what I prefer to see happen, it is better to see a deep punch into the old areas where moves originated, rather than see a weak touch.

My stop as shown is above a nice bearish candle which removed the last of the weak holders i.e intra day bullish scalpers. The trade did not setup until we got back into this supply area earlier today and since I took and commented on these charts, the move down is slow and expected given it was getting late in the day and now just starting the Asian session. In time I do expect to see my lower target hit. I choose an old decision point as a near term target. Although at the time of writing I have moved my target lower of most of the trades.

Next chart is the 4hr. Again the blue line is from the 1hr chart as support and resistance and it is still making sense here, but not as clean as could be. We need some amount of artistic license when it comes to trading levels/areas. Note the last 4hr candle, when this candle closed shortly after I took this chart grab, it closed as a weak bullish candle with no signs of pro money being active. The next 4hr candle closed as a strong bearish engulfing candle. Using the logical side of your brain, if price fails to make new highs and is at old supply and is previously untested supply, the price has only one way to go.....unless there are reason(s) on higher time frames to continue the push up. But look at how much effort went in to reaching the price on this 4hr chart and look at where it stopped. On the bottom of the chart you will see my comment on fresh ground, eventually these prices get hit.

Final chart is of the daily. The yellow box is what is at first a confused looking support and resistance area and a single line does not show it up properly. I did put a line on the top of the box to show the most interesting area for support and one we may hit in the future. Remember, for prices to rise they must first fall. Why?.....unless pro money can get you stopped out, trading in the wrong direction etc they will not have enough profit margin to start the move and make it pay. Even on this chart we see two strong bullish days and this too is into 1hr, 4hr and daily supply. Does it make sense to be buying here?....that is a question only you can answer and you should have little hesitation in answering it.

While nothing is written in stone with trading you need to exercise caution to preserve capital and not be fixated in one direction and let a loosing trade burn you, Set a stop in case some unforeseen event tears up a perfect setup.

I had a nice Brent crude trade today but didnt get time to draw up a chart. In time I will get you all a few more trades as they happen rather than after the fact trades as seen on the experts on youtube when price has already moved.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
I have been watching the GBP/USD pair all day waiting for failure. And its very slowly starting to unwind. Making this chart possible is my shiny new monitor and i feel one with the markets again:)

This is a 5min chart and not to be taken as trading advice or a reason to place a trade. What I want to show you here is how a market direction changes and what signs to look for. There is no 100% certainty that the market is changing now, but rather what signs tend to show up and what gives us reason to pay attention.

First off the blue line is support and resistance. I omitted by typical S/R comment as I see a lot of new people in here and its helpful to new people to get to terms with the buzz words us old farts throw around and not considering there are others who look at the screen and say....what?

Note the bullish break from the support line which is one of the most powerful things you can look for in trading. If you take longs off support and shorts off resistance you will do yourself a huge favor. What ties nicely into that is when support forms along side historic buying and resistance forming along side historic selling. Either one is a powerful combination and I have depended on this proven fact for a long time. Master one, then the other.

enough waffle, onto more charting. The bullish move off support has reached 4hr supply and we expect some reaction given it is the first test of this price area. What you cannot tell for sure is if there is enough reason for pro money to push up through old supply and absorb all the sellers, or just satisfy themselves they have enough profit to the long side and unwind their positions and look for the next move. Market timing for intraday trading like this is crucial for you to understand how it works. If you see a nice setup and its close to the market close, let it go. You only want to trade in an active market where pro money is also active.

Now that the 4hjr supply has been hit and the 4hr candle has closed on it lows, this is a good indication for further bearish activity, tomorrow, not now. You dont have the capital to trade this over night and have such a wide stop that any market spikes wont take you out. Make good use of your capital by trading it wisely and putting it to best use where you get profit within a reasonable period of time.

As price came back down it bounced off our blue line, pure price action. The move back up went nowhere and a sign of the bulls are about done. When price came down to the support line again, it blew right through and didnt look back for a long time. When it eventually came back it bounced back down proving to us that this area is an area of historic support and resistance and its giving us a trade entry....at some point in the future, or now if you have a trade plan in mind that works this early in.

A little more recent we got another small move up to the S/R line and off we bounce again.

Look at other time frames and note as price moved up all the little pull backs you see are a combination of profit taking and new orders, and the small fish bailing out. Always keep the over all market direction and its timing in the front of your mind so that you can at least recognise where the likely true reactions will be and not get suckered by all the low time frame noise and fake moves.

Tomorrow is Friday and a good day for a sell off. We have more room for margin/profit to the bearish side than we do for any bullish move. One thing I often ask of you is to use the logical side of your brain. If you had a billion dollars, would you be taking a long or short order around here?

The amount of capital you have is of no consequence, you treat the value of your money equal to those who have a lot more than you do. As you see the signs of active pro money at the areas I mentioned and with higher time frame support/demand and supply/resistance, you want to ride on the coat tails of the pro's.

For the moment I will continue to watch this pair and pull the bearish trigger when I feel the right opportunity presents itself and the lucky rabbits foot indicator is kicking me in the shins. Keep in mind, this is very early analysis, the market changes and we change with it and we are not blindly trading in a surprise direction.

posts.text:
The daily and 4hr time frames are the more reliable times from which you ought to get price areas from. There is a lot of money changing hands around these 4hr + daily areas and it takes time for the pro money to close out all their positions and not move the market too much against themselves and eat into their profit, and potentially hurt the margin on a reverse i.e bearish sentiment taking over.

All sorts of tricks will come to play out in the form of false moves and even multi hour bullish moves that look strong. But pro money only enters the market when it has the best price and best position within the big picture. It is easy to loose sight of that when trading intra day.

Look at each area you see thats of interest being an 'area' and not a line, price wont always turn on a dime. The biggest reason for me not to short this yet is on the daily you will see we are hovering above a major bearish sell off area. If the bulls want to retain control they have a lot of buying to do and not much in the way of a clear over head target. fxfury, I look at each pair on their own rather than seek confluence or agreement from one other pair. The concept of confluence falls over just as sloping lines do, eventually all fail because price is not always going to adhere strictly to what a human reads into both confluence and price vectors. Neither has been proven to be reliable over time.....and the most important thing you will read today is....price is not a vector!.....it does not have any clue what an indicator or a sloping line means. Pro money trade to price areas and a price area is not something you can find reliably with any indicator.

Take each pair on their own and if you are looking to short the Euro, by all means make sure it is indeed weak by looking at ALL the other pairs traded against it. The same principle applies to all currencies.

@mel, I like your charts and analysis very tight and concise. If we pull back the bullish move will come to an end because we would be getting too far against pro money's acceptable price areas from where they are positioned. Since my last post I have been scaling into the GBP/USD pair and have been holding for a few days now.

As you should all be aware by now, we start from the high time frames and work our way down to the time frame where you see your entry and where your capital will allow you take the risk and have sufficient reserve for your stop.

Here is the monthly chart. Upper and lower boxes are supply on top and demand below. Because the last most significant move was from bullish to bearish, we now look for a reversal. On the monthly chart here you can see a retest of the lower box where pro bullish lunch money was hiding out. The retest was as efficient and precise as you will become keenly aware of as you progress. From a professionals point of view, there is little to be gained from spending more money than you need trading against the position you wish to be in, but are not yet. Make sense?

In english, pro money will push price around where it is feasible in order to get the most profit they can from the real move, and in order to do that, they have to trade against themselves. If this is not clear now, it will be at some point in the future. It is one of those principles of trading that never changes, because it cannot change or the markets will fail to work.

Moving on. The blue line is major support and resistance and you can see the touches we have had to help us see this indeed is a price area we need to look out for in the future. I have drawn it in as a line so as to not clutter up the chart too much, and my hollywood graphics guy is on leave.

The lower black line I have indicated as positioning. Pro money once in an agreed direction will often conduct additional smaller counter moves to shake out weaker hands. That my friends, is you!

The classic trading books telling you to place a stop under the last low, last swing low etc and this is what is often targeted. Unless you look for the larger time frame move you wont see this coming. Now that you know about it, use it to your advantage and wait for them, they are ideal entries as on lower time frames they will setup into smaller support/resistance and also decision areas.

Now on to the weekly chart.

The blue line is our major support and resistance taken from the monthly and still making sense here. The lower box is also the area where pro money bulls came in and we now see how the move up has been rather slow and price has formed a trading range which has tightened in recent weeks.

Our lower black positioning line can now be seen with a lot more clarity and how its been used initially off a decision area and then formed as support. To date, it is clear any pro bulls are holding. It is not yet the end of the week, but it is possible we could see a bullish engulfing candle which would be excellent for a bigger move next week.

The daily chart is next up. The lower box is much nearer term demand but does not in any way have the significance of the higher time frames. This is about as low as most day traders look. The close of each daily candle is what those people want to see and where is on the over all scheme of things.

The awkward price action up shows bullish orders been taken out rather quickly. This is a double edged sword as any failure to push into higher prices will mean there is little to stop price falling rapidly. Look higher in the chart and you will see my comment which is the inverse of my last sentence. The supply was taken out on the way down also in double quick time, this makes it much easier for price to rise once there are no surprises higher up.

You can see from my entries they were all taken off newly formed support and where historic demand was evident and where the move away was clean. There are several targets for profit depending on how aggressive a trader you are.

On to the 4hr chart. On the bottom of the chart we see a real mess with price action here and this was plenty reason why many day traders couldnt see any entries. They were there but it takes a keen eye and getting the timing of market activity correct. There was places in here where price was at the right place, but it was not there at the right time. And so I passed on many text book entries, but not text book in my mind where both price and time were not ideal.

Once again the blus line is now major support and resistance on the 4hr chart. A near term target is pointed out along with some over head retests of old supply which were weak and hence a poor sell off. There is potential that we will blow through old supply in the top box. The higher time frames are showing signs of bullish activity and you need to exercise caution if you are counter trading pro money because what you think is an area of old supply coming as a day trader will get blown away and now becomes new deamand...but its new demand on the time frame you are looking at, but was well planned and executed pro bullish positions from way back. Most traders who focus purely on supply and demand will always get burned when the larger time frame market turns happen.

Finally, here is a 1hr chart for what is worth. Maybe not a whole lot, but lets have a look.

The blue line is major support and resistance taken from our 4hr chart. You can see it has been behaving itself well enough here to also be useful. The upper box is old supply and its got nothing but air between it and current price, this I like to see on all time frames, but you wont always get it. My text in the chart about price being in a young area means, we need to see this retested as another visit back down ideally. Price rarely shoots from one price level to another in a straight line. It is good to see some pull backs and retests you help feed the machine as it climbs in price. A fast push is not healthy, it just wont have the legs and we risk falling off or going into a trading range.

You can see my entries were all but one taken near the start of the move. This is pure voodoo black magic you see. I jest, it is lower time frame entries (5min) taken after 4hr price and 4hr retests were completed where both made sense to me. The last and highest up entry was taken on the 5min chart as well and after a 30min candle closed with much bullish activity and was also 1hr into a new 4hr candle. So I at least had some security behind this for another 3 hours and also had support below it. All this makes sense if you follow the logic.

What now you ask?

Now I will continue to hold partly due to insufficient time to come in here and lay out charts and I still have family business keeping me busy. I will watch this on higher time frames and see what plays out. Price action on lower time frames is likely to get much cleaner once we get a restest and then you day traders can get involved. If price action looks nasty to you, let it go and look at some other pair.

Look at the daily chart. The daily takes priority over lower time frames and it should have been obvious to anyone trading this pair that the lower price target for pro money bullish activity was where this was going. Further guidance was given from there being an old decision area to the left, proven bullish orders to the left which we were about to enter for the first time since that move, and we also were gaining support from those old bullish orders too.

There was little to be gained by pro money to take this lower, look where all the buying and selling took place below the last few days. Who would want to sell into that with the world and their granny already in major bearish mode.

For their to be any downside we have to push price up first in order to get enough margin and cheapest price to enter. I saw neither for a bearish move a few days back and was not willing to take a bearish position no matter what time frame or position size it could have been.

Even looking at the chart now, we have more attractive targets above that are showing very good old price action as well.

You should keep the big picture in mind all the time, even if this is the monthly and daily.

People who trade with real money and who take positions for months see this picture better than most can. But if you keep the same picture in your head and know the direction, all you want is a few good opportunities on lower time frames to trade in the same direction as they do. GBP/USD has only had its 4th entry for longer term positional traders (investors in reality) this year. Average moves were 800 points.

I obtain the same points gain and a lot more most of the time on lower time frames by watching what they are doing and by scaling into positions as the market shows me the real direction and over all I gain the same points gained.

I mentioned this in the past and its worth mentioning again. If you trade sure supply and demand it is unlikely you will become successful as you could. The reason is when the market turns based on those who matter i.e longer term pro money, it will break everything you ever read about supply and demand trading.

You will eventually learn to spot this by making three observations:

1. Big Picture

2. Big Picture

3. Big Picture

There is also a fundamental reason why supply and demand trading fails in its classic description around these turning areas. Pro money cannot bail out of and get into a position in one hit. They have to scale in and out and this takes time. If they just jumped in and out all the time, what you would see is incredibly long wicks and tails on price action. The violence these create will break your account in minutes and destroy how the markets now move. What they do is filter money in and out of the market in smaller bites. These smaller bites are shown as periods of consolidation on lower time frames. You can rest assured pro money is active when the market appears dull, but it must be within a generally active market such as London or New York. We are dealing with the best financial brains on the planet and they know how the herd reacts. If too much money is placed or withdrawn from the market the price will move against the pro's too quickly and their investors will not be happy. They have price orders to fill and price is always king, and so is their fee if they get it right.

A safer way to trade is to wait a few days after the daily/weekly turn has established a new direction because people have spent a lift time trying to pick tops and bottoms.

I trust this has shown you that focusing on supply and demand on the lower time frame will throw you off the main market sentiment. Commit it to memory and look for it, it will be an eye opener and it will put you in the same place where the rich and even richer make their money.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
I will scale in early and also scale out early depending on how the price action looks. There are a number of ways you can look at the market depending on your capital, time in the trade and target(s).

The higher time frames generally spend more time to unwind the current direction and slow down the move, then start applying positions in the opposite direction, which means pro money will be buying all of the bearish orders in this example, if they buy enough of the sellers orders they stop the momentum going down and the market will consolidate for a time, this provides them with excellent long grass in which to load up in the direction they wish to go and not show their true intentions for some time, anything from hours, days and sometimes, weeks. The best you can hope for is to be aware of the price area where this is going on, and you will only see the effect after the fact. But that is good enough. Nobody can ever pin point the exact price where a market will turn.

There is no right way to scale in or out, my own approach is to slowly filter into the market the amount of capital I want to put into a move, but I break it down into smaller lot sizes and only apply new positions as I see entry signals on lower time frames. If I want to put in 10,000 euro, I could use 100 lots at one time, but its too risk. Instead I may put in 5 or 10 lots at a time, and over a period of time and eventually get the full amount of capital I have decided to use for the move into the market in a some what covert manner.

Another approach is to only add positions when the new direction is obvious to everyone and only take them when old demand i.e the first new new demand created out of what looks like it should have been supply, is tested and support proven. These areas I prefer to see tested after a 4hr candle close, this is a safer way than taking them off the 5min, 15min and 1 hr. There are cycles within a pull back and the deeper ones tend to bring more profit because it is a very low cost way for pro money to get you out, take your money and run back in the direction you had correctly chosen.

Before you take to scaling into and out of positions, master conventional entries and exists. There are plenty more trades out there and missing one is no big deal, in fact trades are like buses, there will be another coming along real soon.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
It brings a good feeling people are getting something out of this. We all know that the day will also come when this will be no more. Life is a strange game.

If you are in a loosing position and you hedge against it, you'd better have deep pockets. That is a technique used by the foolish traders to offset losses. It is done by weak hands and those who wont close out and want to save face. If I have a bad trade, I take the hit and move on and will not throw good money after bad by doing what is to the vast majority of traders to be a bad move.

What you will see happen is for a trade in the wrong direction closed, and immediately placed back on in the opposite direction. If you do the math with say 2 trades in the wrong direction and now two more in the correct direction, at all are equal value lots, there is no way you will offset a loss. You have to trade with more money against the first trades. That is plain silly in my book.

When I can sit and watch the market move and I place a trade, I will do so without a stop. If I cannot sit and manage the trade I will place a hard stop. But the mental stop I have in place NEVER moves and it is the end of a trade with no if/and or but.

If you dont have the capital to trade longer term but still want higher points made, you can trade with partial lots and sit there and watch it move enough to gain some safety as each successive time frame pulls back and gives you more space between your entry price and current price. My longer term trades will hide behind support in the case of a move up, and behind resistance on the way down. I wont put them a point behind it, but well behind it because a weekly open can produce a gap or a strong fast and fake move to stop you out. All this is designed by pro money, however the higher time frame picture will play out. It just needs for you to give it the time and space it needs to move.

I trade the London session and all my charts are based on data from London. Candles will look different from each broker. Every few months I will setup a demo account with many brokers based in the UK so I can compare the price action and order fill/close etc. If I get a better service then its time to move, remember brokers want to keep you regardless of you making or loosing money. They get paid each time you place a trade. Pro money does not trade through them so you are feeding these people and its best to look for quality service.

The time frame you trade will be down to your capital and risk appetite. A guy trading off a chart less than 1hr will for the most part have no interest in higher time frames. All who used come to me said I dont look at the 4hr daily etc cos I dont have that kind of money. But yet they throw money at a 1 or 5min candle that is shooting for the stars. Nuts.

It should be common sense and logic to anyone trading that each higher time frame candle that approaches supply or demand is of great importance. I choose the 4hr candle for intra day signals as it is the highest time frame candle we get within any session. That means we have two 4hr candle per session. This will cause you to miss entries on lower time frames, but those entries are not as good as those you get when looking at the bigger picture. The move will also be smaller, some people are happy with taking 20 or 30 points out of the market.

My charts during the London session close a 4hr candle at 11am and 3pm local time. Other traders will be shown a close an hour earlier due to being on central European time. Those in the US will be sleeping and only the hard core traders up and at it, such as one guy from North Dakota I know who trades off the 1min and 5min charts and on every session there is and cat naps in between each session. Dedication is an under statement. But he makes his living off it and thats all most want, others dream of millions but dont have what it takes to make it happen.

Pro money can be seen in many ways and they all try to hide what their true intentions are for as long as possible when the market hits supply and demand or major turning areas that are hard to see on all but a very much zoomed out view. Where nobody can see what pro money is doing is when we have longer periods of consolidation, this can skew the higher time frame at times. Look now at GBP/USD, there was long

consolidation and a break lower, now we see buy backs. This is the last chance for the bulls to make it happen today, any failure here will be pushed down to the last place where buying took place. Doctor:

AlterEgo, who is control is what your risk dictates. If you are trading partial lot sizes and can only hold through a small pull back, you are only trading with the trend on that time frame. If the trend of that time frame is with a higher time frame you will net more points because the continuation move is now with your chosen direction. All higher time frames have cycles of lower time frames within them. Looking for who is in control is taken either has a day trader, intra day trader or investor. As you climb to each level you will have money to put in the market and will look for signals on higher successive time frames.

It may take some time for this to make sense, but looking for historic price areas where there was a move is the most sensible thing to do, providing you also be aware of what is happening on higher time frames. There comes a time when a 5min, 15min, 1hr and 4hr line up, then watch the move from that. If you extend out this to more time frames you can see, or will be able to see, how powerful this information is.

You are correct in that at years end we will see all time frames roll over, everything from the 1min to the monthly fall into place. Would you expect to see a massive move then?....no. Supply and demand still has to play out and time and price are both crucial to successful trading. Both have to line up and price will then move, it WILL move.

End of year is significant in that investors are unwinding their long held positions if the time and price is right, others will be placing long term invested funds if price and time is right. You are welcome, you are all welcome!

There are some very basic principles that never change but getting them into peoples heads takes time, we all think different because we are unique, and we all behave the same when it comes to trading, which is the way pro money want it to remain.

The most simplistic way anyone can look at the markets is to grab a few monitors and get at least four time frames open at the same time. I have four large screen monitors that I cannot trade without, I peeled back from the eight I once had.

You need the next successive higher time frame on the next monitor to the time frame you wish to trade from. For intra day trading I have the 5min, 15min, 1hr and 4hr open. In my opinion it is impossible to trade with anything less than this, I have tried to get down to one monitor but I keep missing entries because I do not see the full picture. Flicking back and forth wont work either.

Lets assume it is the beginning of the week, you use the 4hr chart and set it to the weekly chart and you place a box on the most obvious supply and demand areas to where price is now. Drop the same chart down to the daily and do the same, and finally bring up the 4hr chart and leave it there.

Mark all other charts with obvious supply and demand to where price is now. What you should see are the price and time cycles I keep talking about. All these eventually play out and you can see why price has moved in the past and where future turning points are most probable....not factual....and cannot be so until it has happened.

Once you have programmed your brain to look for these areas, you now focus on price action. Screen time gets you the best education on this too. As a professor once told my class, I can teach you, but I cant make you learn it. A wise man.

Eventually all this will click and will become logical and obvious. I will continue to post charts as these tend to help more than text alone. A trap to be aware of is looking for repeating patterns. There are subtle signs rather than patterns that you can draw. Price and time is the pattern I base everything off of, both never fail once you start well away from the 10 or 100 or 1000 bucks you are putting in the market. I am talking about the big picture. Put your money down and ride on the coat tails of the pro's once you see they are active and in the correct direction and not the fake move.

Victor wrote: Hey. Thanks a lot for what you are doing. It is amazing. I have a question that is bothering me for a while. Why do the big money use fundamentals instead of technical analysis?

Doctor:

A chicken and egg question Victor. Some use technical analysis and others use fundamental analysis.

A few examples. High frequency trading is a technical analysis used by large firms. Larger banks use both types of analysis, investors tend to use fundamental analysis. There is no hard and fast rule used, but you will see fundamental analysis take data from technical analysis.

The longer term trades (investments) are for the most part are based on fundamental factors which come from the political world. Even technical traders can eliminate political influences on price once the choose a time frame high enough. Look at some old charts of the 1920's and 1930's and you will see how price went where it was going anyway. I use those two decades as good illustrations for past students to enable them see what happens even when the wealthy nations economies crash.

For the past 25 years there has been a huge uptake in technical analysis. It at least has some basis and history whereas a political decision is the great unknown and nobody will know its full effect for a long time. A good example is the printing of money and the virtual money such as derivatives, both of these are going to sting for some time.

If you do a little trick with candles as I do (yes another secret about to be gone) you can blend candle bodies to get more information about a given time frame. Check candles A on the 1hr and you will see a strong bullish candle with a close on its high and a long tail. This is the most significant candle on the 1hr chart inside the price range. Drop back to the 30min again, if you look at both A candles again you will see the candle with the most movement was the second bullish candle and given we just came off support you can now subtract the previous bearish candle from the bullish candle and the result is a strong bullish candle with a long tail on the 30min, even though it is not printed as such. Make sense?

Moving on. We now know there is activity in the range and something will break at some point in the future. Cast an eye on candle B, here I also have two candles marked as B and note the first bearish candle pushed deep into the origin of the last minor move up. This now removes waiting bullish orders and typical of how a market wants to move. The second candle in B is a bullish candle showing a long wick but closing near its lows. It suggests weakness, but not so fast. Its purpose was to remove sellers higher up (supply) and this clears the way from price to move above the top of the wick easily as price approaches it the next time.

It was after candles B had closed I pulled my chair in closer and waited on a lower time frame. Candles C formed and my entries were buried within the first C candle. What it shows is a bearish candle that tested the candle B action, closed above the first B low and all I wanted was an entry anywhere quickly after this and I didnt fuss too much with 5min price action because I know when the break comes it wont give me a second chance.

The best I could do was to take two entries off the 5min where each entry was taken on a small candle body with little movement other than wicks and tails. There was no decent price action on the 5min to get an entry, it had to be taken from a higher time frames lead and with the knowledge of a price range holding so long at supply. Normal market movement would have seen it fall off.

posts.text:
blacky, a number of things you need to look at closer. After you have satisfied yourself to the longer term direction of the market be sure to check the next lower time frame is ending its period of correction. Price action will often show it drifting off with little interest and once it hits old supply or demand you then drop down through lower time frames to the one you feel most comfortable trading and have the capital to take the draw down.

ideally you want to see a deep push back to the origin of a move which sets up the bias for pro money entering on that time frame. This all hinges on the higher time frames all lining up with their counter trend moves ending. The pull backs seem to be whats taking you out. You can use a wider stop, or wait for a later entry rather than try and pick a bottom or top which few people can do in the real world. Look for price to come back to where you now think is a good place, it is better to miss the odd entry while learning. Perhaps rather than take trades for a few days, just mark on screen where you would have entered with your current method. Mark every entry you think looks good and also mark your take profit. See how many 1st, 2nd and 3rd entries work out best. In time you will find where your eye can immediately spot the wise entries and not the emotional ones.

It is easy to post a chart and say enter here, and here etc. it is much more difficult on a live chart. Your targets look reasonable as you have planned them out well. Try the method for marking trades and post back here next week and let me know how its working out. Dont waste real money doing this, all you need is to train your eye and have a little more patience.

Mel, all trades are taken with at least the 4hr chart in mind where possible. I want to have the minimum time frame with me when London opens. There are times when a setup comes after the first 4r period has elapsed after the London open. A pull back into the origin is common for my entries, at times I will take them early and scale in as the setup gets more orders in the market. Once I like what I see there is no hesitation and enter on the next closed candle. Pro money rarely gives a second shot an entry. If you have doubts, dont take it.

My check list is all mental these days, but in the early days I did have a checklist taped to my monitors. My journal is my trading posted into excel. Anyone starting off is wise to jot down all trades and any losers need careful analysis to see why it failed. There are trades which will fail even with the perfect setup, there is no such thing as a sure thing in trading.

Always maintain the longer time frames in your mind and know where each one is in the cycle.

This is the basis of being properly prepared.

Les_p, pro money wont do the same thing twice. They will do all possible to hide their movements and only show their true intentions after false moves and pain for the retail trader. This is the single most difficult part to figure out in trading. The changes only have a few set 'shapes' people look for, such as long wicks and tails. Some trade what they call pin bars only and design trading systems around them, but this is only a tiny part of the puzzle. The only way to see what pro money is doing is to spend a lot of time looking at charts. Good formations from candles form around support and resistance areas, which turn into supply and demand.

Castus, I dont place much emphasis on correlations because these will change over time and you cannot put much importance into them. At the moment look at the S&P500 and the AUD, over the past few months both are diverging. In my view too many traders look at too many other factors which are meant to have influence on a certain pair. I trade what I see on the chart of the pair I am interested, no external factors influence me unless price is at an important area and major news is due. Trading at a time like that will result in the price movement we saw last Friday in eur/usd which messed up a nice long setup and drove price down on nothing but emotion and the overwhelming new supply will have given pro money a lot of pain. There are times when the pro's cant hold an area.

posts.text:
blacky, the german open often pushes prices into false breaks and the London open an hour later reverses it. The majority of the worlds finance is traded through London and it makes sense to trade in that session. I dont trade the Yen or AUD very often, but if I do take it then its on the London session. Last year I may have taken a trade during the Asian session perhaps 4 or 5 times. Practically all trades are done in the London session.

Risk reward is highly individualistic. I trade between supply and demand and only adjust if I see the move weakening. I have no interest in risk reward in the typical fashion most see it. I trade for the major portion of a move and not become blinded with needing a risk reward. If risk reward is used, then it becomes an indicator and by now you will know my opinion on indicators. Position sizing has a huge effect on how far you wish to take the move and how long you stay in it. I can load up heavy and take the nearest support or resistance area as a target, or hold longer and look for the full move. If I am unwilling to wait for the entire move to end, I will have larger position sizes and hold them for a shorter period of time. My stop while I watch the trade is mental, and I use a hard stop when away from my trading station. As yet I am unable to stay awake for 24hrs and trade all the markets:)

And to take your first question last. When I started I wrote down trades and this was a bad way to keep track. You need to take screen shots of all time frames when you enter and mark them up where the entry, stop and target is. Along with that you type out the reasons why you took that trade. Trading is a visual thing and numbers wont help in getting the full story across. You need visual input. using more than one monitor is also essential in my view. As your trading evolves a pattern of what will eventually turn into a method will develop from your efforts. We are all different and learn at different speeds and in different ways. Dont take my way and the only way or best way. It is one of many ways. But there are principles to my trading that is applicable to all tastes. Take what you can from it and build upon it.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
blacky, there was a lot of news out of Europe last Friday and this was used by pro money to send price down to the last area of demand, but it fell so so hard that the wall of retail sellers and opportunistic bears means is not always possible to hold price back by the bulls and it means the pro money had to adjust positions and the tracks are all over the chart. Pro money has to soak up all selling orders if they want price to hold, but not all pro money will hold at the same area and they start a war between each other to see who can inflict as much pain on the other side and take out their limits. Times such as last Friday are opposing firms at work and when areas fail that we expect to have held start to fall through near term support. Opportunistic bears will also have seen this and taken shorter term orders to push it down to areas they want i.e the type who were holding draw down when the bullish move originally came. There is more than just bulls in the market and when price comes close to old areas where somebody got it wrong, they can hold and pounce later on.

Pro money will have hedged and others lightened up on positions. Pro money does not always win and their losses are based on their capital reserves which allow them hold through the draw down if they are big enough. Some can hold on for weeks or months if its viable and if the reserve funds are available for such times. Each firm will have their own rules internally. If the invested funds are from private investors, the call of what to do comes from the investor and not the firm.

High frequency trading is totally different to the way humans trade and you will not spot it unless you have inside knowledge of how it works. And the how it works is a closely guarded secret of the software algorithm. Each firm has their own and they protect this closely because the cost to produce it costs a hefty price tag. High frequency trading by nature is in and out fast, it will not cause price to drop or rise so dramatically.

Once you look back on the chart you can see the news was the reason for the price drop and as it was unable to hold levels, price was only going in one direction and will continue until the bulls either see value, or the bears pull it lower to their price area. A lot of traders will have been burned badly and the market has to settle from the big shake out. But that is trading, there is no defined set of rules where price will reach in a given time, other than it will get there eventually with all the twists and turns it takes.

There are two seasons in trading and it holds true for forex and stocks. In December postions for major players close early. I mentioned this last year and mid December is the time when most close out. It is a big time of the year for all banks and firms. In spring there tends to be a lot of volume placed in the market by longer term traders. This is mostly applicable to stock traders. Some traders are of the old guard where the start of the trading year is spring time and not January. In mid December I am closed out fully. If I happen to see a setup after that it will be short lived and wont push my luck, the volume tends to be gone and hitting a target is harder. Currencies are far more liquid than stocks and more opportunities to trade all year round.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
A brief reply and I am caught up in a few non trading days at the moment.

Your second entry was the only logical place to go long. The first entry was nothing but price leaving the bottom of a narrow price range and could at any time have fallen through the range and the momentum caused by stops being taken and new short orders come in cost you a lot of money. It is better to wait for price to break through the range in the original direction favored by pro money and wait for it to come back down to the origin and then look for an entry with price action. For price to fall back inside the range it means no interested buyers where we would expect to see support/demand. That is about as pure price action and candle reading as it gets. Others will take it on a candle close and not wait for price action. You need more capital for the entry on close alone.

I have not been in front of any charts for the past two days and have no idea where the euro is at present and cant comment further.

I find risk vs reward to be a misused and understood term. Pro money will go for open space between current price and an obvious target. It wont be based on risk vs reward but purely on enough room for price to move where it enables them to get their orders into the market. If you think logically about this it makes sense, you want to be where pro money is active and not scalping between 5 or 15min price areas. Of course this is considering you are willing to hold. The spread will be the same no matter how you trade but the profit is better when running with an active market. An example of holding in a trade over a day or two was my average 66 point stop last year on the euro. I was willing to take that based on an average 800 point win. Small change in the greater picture. For day trading the pull backs below the 1hr chart will be places to look for continuation. As you drop below the 1hr time frame the targets become much smaller and the false moves can then become a higher percentage of potential profit and risk reward then is of little benefit as it is a more scalpers scene. Taking trades in the same direction as pro money on lower time frames is possible but the pull backs are where it takes out a lot of day traders.

It is counter intuitive to go long in a falling market, but if this is done into support and with price action on your side and timing is correct i.e major market is open and at least the 4hr chart is also at support you can expect to see some action. The only unknown then is if a news release is due and its effect. But I think its being said enough times to wait until the ripples from the news have gone past their sell by date. And usually selling covertly planted cerebral non truths. That is about as nice I can be with the media today.

Your target for the second entry is ideal.

I am inclined to use horizontal lines only. The logic is price is a number that can only rise or fall and is not treated as a vector such as you get when using slanted lines. The other factor is use of slanted lines will not allow your eye focus on origins of a move which are of critical importance to us. On many of my charts you will see boxes or lines indicating reaction areas. This is the best way to tune into when to look real close and watch for price action.

Your chart otherwise is fine and its clean and easy to read. Dont put much emphasis on round numbers because and entry and a target happen in a range and not to the precise point, although some will hit with amazing accuracy. This is trading, not science:)

On your chart you have a weekly close (?) where buyers came in off old supply and old resistance, an ideal place to be long. The risk was low and there will be a battle a little about where price is now. This is partially due to old supply still being in the market with a few areas showing active selling and this must be absorbed on the way up in order for a bullish move to continue. There is also resistance a little above your TG line. Note the history from the left of the chart and all the way to the bearish candle that is intersected by your TG line 10 candles back. Profit taking there is likely and possible pull back. Making the long position more appealing is also the two areas where pro money came in around your RN line in the past.

If you draw horizontal lines you will see more detail and get a better handle on old supply/sellers/resistance, demand/buyers/support than you do now. This is just a tip for you.

posts.text:
Michael, trading is not a complex business, traders make it complicated for themselves. And the question you ask is very difficult to answer so that it is understandable. Getting words to fit what I look for is not a formula or science. It is looking back through history where professional money was active, and why they were active there. This means starting from high time frames and working down to the time frame you feel most comfortable with and can afford.

There are principles that apply to all currencies and indices more than stocks. Stocks in my view are manipulated due to the volume of the stock and other shall we say knowledge, and leave it at that.

The principles are:

Support Resistance Demand (buyers) Supply (sellers) Decision areas Price action

Then the lesser areas of importance such as round numbers and price patterns. Price doesnt make a pattern, humans make a pattern out of it. And round numbers are just on the way to the next number, but used to good effect by the media etc.

Support which forms with demand is good. Resistance which forms with supply is good.

Both when formed on higher time frames where all the lower time frames have had their opportunity to cycle or phase through, is really good. Decision areas when formed at historic areas where price stalled are good, but traded only after some time in the market i.e screen time. king of all is price action, this is where pro money can no longer hide their orders and the market reacts to the heave of orders.

Most people will get the principles of support/resistance, demand/buyers, decision areas, but most will fail on price action. There is no short cut to reading price action because you must learn to read it on the fly and as it unfolds live. When price action happens with any of the above principles you must be ready to act. What will throw most traders is they are trading counter intuitive to the markets direction. If the trade was so easy to see there would in effect be no trade to take because the flood of orders would make the move happen to quickly. Real trades behave to what the herd calls trending. Trends are pro money at work and it wont stop until their target is hit, and then they mostly try and create a false impression at the end of their move of it continuing forever and the herd responds as they do with an easy way for pro money to trade against and take their vast profits.

Charts posted of trades will help you more than any book or course ever can. I am not surprised that the past month has been difficult for you, I took off a month in December for the same reason you were confused, I know the markets get choppy at years end and start of the next, so there is no reason to trade. In fact there was only the last two weeks of February where there was good trades. The drift down we had is not worth taking and we are now in a range. Dont expect the charts to make sense when you see such choppy conditions. Wait for them to recover and give direction, then wait for an entry when an obvious target is hit and be on the side of pro money always, it is after all where the real money is.

Have you seen the videos made by IF (hippy guy with long hair and magic mushrooms behind his ear) they are worth watching. They will help get a feel for a market as he steps through the moves.

For the current point in time on eur/usd we are at the top of a trading range with price bound in about a 40 point range. I am still bullish the euro and will post some charts when there is action to report and some trades.

posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
Hi Blacky,

There is a mind set out there that sees all candle with long tails and wicks as reasons to place an entry. These are not always entries and unless they happen at longer time frames I rarely take them. The exceptions are for day trading where I look at lower time frames for a continuation move after a pull back from the higher time/missed entry took place. But what is common and always must be shown is taking it with support/demand for buying, or resistance/supply for selling.

At present we are just into a new month, I wonder how many people here have looked at the monthly closed candle this week?....it is easy to forget this.

Your loosing trade should be very obvious why it is loosing. Look on your 4hr chart, you went long off a 30min pull back and expected that to hold. The 4hr time frame has much more weight over a 30min chart and given price was also just finished with hitting resistance you were standing in the way of a raging bear. Not a good place to be. If you drew your 4hr upper blue line higher and where real supply came in historically you would have been getting better intel. It is apparent that the line was the cause of your wrong entry and the 30min chart where you saw support was pre mature. If you can, allow at least the 4hr chart to unwind before placing a trade, it will be safer and have more weight in the direction of price. Then drop down to your 30min, 15min etc and get a finer view on price action and take an entry on a pull back on that lower time frame where you see price ending the counter trend move.

I am aware that this is not always easy to do and teaching your brain to accept price must rise before pro money shorts it, and price must fall before pro money takes it long is not logical.....yet!

These pull backs are where I enter most times, and it is rather boring in fact because it is the same trick played over and over and dressed up with a different candle formation. But price, actual price, cannot be hidden in their games because we know there are narrow bands of price where a move must take place in order for targets be met. If this makes no sense now, it will in time.

Hope this helps you Blacky, feel free to post any time you wish here and I will help where I can.

Doctor wrote: Some light candle reading for you all. The pun's come early on today.

First chart is monthly chart, the pair involved is meaningless and I removed as much from the chart to concentrate your eye and brain.

Look at where price is now and can you determine the reason for the current candle, and lets assume it is a closed candle.

Here is the same chart with a little detail, and just enough to show whats going on. We again assume a closed candle and we see a reaction of support and old demand, the price goes up. The likely target?....the box above. All simple, no fuss and nothing difficult to understand.

Lets really get into the details now.

Here is a zoomed in view of the last leg down in price. To help guide your eye here, candle 1 was a race to grab old demand and is also taken at support.

2 the bulls have already got their work done and the follow through buy intraday bears is weak the close well off the lows.

3 the bulls intent is obvious here with a very large body and close with very little wick on top. On the other chart you will see this candle hit old supply.

4 considering we just hit old supply this candle close showed such weak bullish momentum that it was plain to see we need to fall back down, or collect more orders to break above.

5 a weak bearish candle, note how it closed well inside the previous candles low, note the long tail, a sign of buying.

6 a very strong bull candle with strong close above support, so we long this puppy to the moon now right?

7 no, we wait for a pull back and see does support hold. And 7 is a perfect bearish engulfing candle and proves candle 6 was a false bullish break.

8 unfortunately the market timing for the previous move was not very good and we are now stuck between close in old supply and demand. When this happens we need to keep the big picture in mind, we are still below supply. This candle attempts to grab more orders from the bulls by the tail showing buying, however the weak close tells is its going nowhere.

9 we have a break below near term candle 5 and old demand from candle 3. But hitting candle 3's demand hard means we have to see a reaction higher.

10 this is the reaction from candle 9, it has setup up pro money for the main bearish move.

11 this is interesting, the candle pushed lower than the previous candles wick and closed within the body of candle 3 which is still the most significant candle we need to break.

12 finally a strong break and strong close. Of note here is the candle got into the tail of candle 1. There were a lot of buyers here and even though it is not the first time price has been in that area, there is validity given to this area given its likely hood to act as resistance once broken and retested.

13 no interest in taking price lower yet and no progress made by bulls or bears. The very slight tail below the tiny body means we wait.

14 this is the start of the pro bears selling. See how the wick pulls in supply from candle 12 and closes as a bullish looking candle but with a very low close on the candle 12 body. Books will tell you this is a bullish engulfing candle because it had contained the previous candle, correct, but, the books fail to tell you the reason for the wick and where it went.

15 Something to look at on this candle is the fact that the body is both bearish and closed within the previous candle, but no takers higher considering candle 14 is what is considered bullish. Pro money know better.

16 This is the bug push to get the market running and all the work prior to this candle was done in candle 14 and a lot of bears waited for this move whereas candle 14 would have got day traders long and now candle 16 would have stopped them out adding fuel to the bearish orders. Also note candles 12, 13, 14, 15 are all at S/R.

17 not much to say, we are moving down at a nice clip and money being made by the bears, dont stand in front of this freight train, be on it.

18 The line at the bottom of my chart is old demand taken from the chart earlier up. So why has price suddenly stopped and gone bullish?....two reasons, not all pro money has the same take profit target and some will bail before the ultimate target. This candle shows profit taking, which in itself has pinned the last of the bears who entered at the close of 16 which is 17's open. Who would have guessed it setup one final small move down. But on this time frame is enough to buy a nice lunch:)

19 old demand pinned to the pixel and also the first sign of the market slowing down. The tail tells us this. When the market is running hard it will not stop on a dime and the tails and wicks you see at major old price level on higher time frames has to be traded against in the opposite direction by pro money to first stop the current move and setup the next. This is never a cheap exercise and costs a lot of money. We see the wicks and tails and look for our entries.

20. Given pro money reached their target it was of no surprise we will at least see one small leg up and possibly a retest of the newly created low.

21 so far we are no longer bearish and now bullish, but a retest of the low is still on the cards unless we see a test of new support coming along and this may look like a decision point. Possible places for a sensible decision are candle 18, 13 thru 15 cluster.

The time frame for this doesnt matter because price which is plotted in time is a fractal of itself and keeping all the old support and demand areas from higher time frames for use on lower time frame charts is essential for success. An example would be a 1 or 5 min trader taking a short at candle 19 because it was a break of 18, but not understanding that he was shorting into a major higher time frame of buyers.

The other horizontal lines on the chart are a partial guide to help train your eye and logical side of your brain. There are more places to find support and resistance and I will let you look for those.

If you are willing to wait price will always show you a clear direction and when its turned. There are times when even a 5min trade wont come around for a day or so. This chart is primarily for a trader in the US who made a nice gesture to me and I am returning both his appreciation and letting him know there is more value in money alone. Everyone else has some more material to study, so thank our US friend for coming up with this idea of a numbered candle stick chart.

Have a good weekend everyone.

posts.text:
Hotochin,

Your first 60 hours will be multiplied by several years before this can click. Not everyone will 'get it'. But if you hold your patience and put in the effort, the day when this suddenly makes sense is truly a defining moment in your life. Only screen time and being disconnected from emotions will help you. Other than that the trade entries and exists are something that is determined in seconds.

I wish I could shorten your journey, but my posts here are as good as I can do for you. Learn what you can from my posts and others too, I type in my explanations of price movement with my charts and detail what I can. I said this before, and will repeat it again. My way is not THE correct, or only way to trade. It works for me and I pass along what I know for anyone to use and are welcome to tweak it in any way they wish.

There has only been one person in many years who picked up trading as a novice in six months. The guys brain was just wired right to being with whereas all others try to force a call when there is nothing to trade off of.

Your comment of getting the higher time frames marked off is a lot more significant than you give yourself credit for. The markets and their time frames we trade within are all fractals of each other. If you remove the time factor from your higher time frame analysis, the chart now could be any time frame. Therefore it is logical that your higher time frame analysis is also correct on a lower time frame. What you must do is learn to stitch them together so that the higher time frame supply/demand reactions are witnesses by you in real time on lower time frames. i.e the lower time frame will move first and you will see perhaps a 1hr and 4hr candle close with noticeable price action present. The price action can sometimes be hidden on the higher time frames and it then presents itself as a false move on the 1 and 5min charts.

I could also put it this way, there are trading methods sold online that have you trade off pin bars on the 4hr and daily. Thats all well and good, but not all 4hr and daily supply and demand areas will form pin bars and you must look at lower time frames to see what price action is doing there.

Make sense?

FX1,

If you are getting stopped out could it be you are still in herd mode?.....taking break outs rather than wait for price to come back to the break and then pick up left over orders where we know pro money was active?

It is all very logical if you think about this for a while. If price moves away cleanly from an area it means pro money had to have been active, the less time they spend at an area doing this tends to make for better entries on the return back to this area where the pro's know more orders 'must' be waiting to be filled. When you see a move away, do not chase it. Let price go, and then return. On a day trading chart this could take all day or more than one day, but eventually it will return. You will get filled faster on a 1 and 5 min time frame than you will on higher time frames. If you are a day trader thats what most will look for, but it is also harder to trade off the lower time frames than it is the higher time frames. Ironic that the more money you have to trade, the easier it can be:)

Price is often ramped in one direction to make it appear to day traders that this is the move of the day, and of course the media latch onto this and sell it to you. The trading books will tell you to wait for trend line/channels confirmation where you have two touches on one line and at least one touch of the other side. This is complete nonsense and could not be further from the truth as we know it. All that does is get you further from the source of the move with less profit and higher risk.

A quick example right now at 1100GMT on the S&P500 is price has been ramped up, it is now at the high price for most time frames. Who was buying here, pro's?.......you must get good value in price before you take a trade and only where it is at historic clean areas of previous movement where pro money was active, and are likely to be active again. Your target will be also very clear in your mind and set it as a hard order close while you learn.

Hope that helps a little.

What should jump out at you after marking off historic supply and demand areas is that eventually all the boxes in their respective time frames will overlap. If you wait for this to happen the probability of a winning trade is much greater.

Hotochin's comment about price getting closer is one time when this way of trading is not going to give large results, you must look for room for profit and when price gets squeezed on higher time frames pro money wont leave orders in there keeping capital tied up. Price must move between supply and demand and when any factor effects the movement over a reasonable period of time, expect a squeeze to happen and plenty chop. posts.author: Doctor
posts.text:
Hotochin,

Waiting for price to hit supply or demand on the monthly and weekly is not something you or I can afford. But we must be aware than when it does hit these areas there is going to be a reaction and a likely change in direction. Once the new direction has been decided by pro money, we now drop down into daily and lower time frames to look for pull backs counter to the decided direction and look for those pull backs to be the restest of the origin of the move. The retest appears deeper on lower time frames whereas the daily generally will not pull back very much.

If you think about it logically, any low time frame within a day traders pocket is ripe for false moves and stop hunts. This is how most of the larger orders get filled. When you see the price turn against a break of even a few hours, think of this as the test of the strength of the bulls or bears. If they want to continue with the move they will close some of the positions because you are now taking the orders as the market is moving. The false sense of security plays out on all low time frames and all it does is hand a very low cost and low risk entry for pro money to reverse price back on the direction of the chosen direction.

When price is between lets say the 4hr or higher time frame supply and demand, my choice is only take a trade once a pull back has come and it is into an area where pro money was active. If the move fails my risk is small. Ideally you should not take a trade when mid range between supply and demand and take the easy trades, the type you can see from across the room!

As you get more screen under your belt you will see how price wants to come back to the origin of the move. It will give you one and sometimes a second shot at getting in. There are a few gotchas in day trading and what can mess up nice entries just waiting to be taken are the release of news and the time of day. When London in particular opens and closes price will not always react as you expect if it is approaching an area of historic price action and its best to stand aside and wait for the market to settle.

It boils down to lining up time frames and historic price action with current price action. However, it takes a long time to get your brain to work against what it sees on the hard right edge of the screen. Books tell you wait for confirmation, I say active pro money is confirmation, and pro money is its own confirmation.

posts.text:
Hotochin,

Nice charting, all well done and roughing it out on the higher time frames is ok, we dont look for precise scientific areas or something that can be measured to the nth degree.

Your comment on the arrows is close. What they show is that each time pushes higher, the source of the bullish orders is checked to see will it hold, of so filter on more orders because that small pullback is enough to get many day traders stopped out. Its a low cost entry. You can stair step those entries all the way up into old supply. But of course you need the capital to do it and the patience to wait for them. My old charts show some of my scaled entries where I take up most of the origin of the move with my entry lines:)

The origin of the move was tested when price came back and sat on top of the blue box and then bolted out of there. That was classic pro money false move and load up the boat. Note the test they took and where it was. Some of those test work out to point perfection. Who would ever have thought?....there, I had to work in my old copyrighted line as I havent used it in an age.

Keep in mind that when price wants to turn at the end of the move, it will react to old areas of price action. When ever there are deeper pull backs be very wary, if price can hit one during a turn there is unlikely to be any orders worthy enough of keeping the trend in tact and the market can turn very fast and move a long way. If there are no buyers and all historic bullish orders are taken and we are at old supply on a major time frame i.e 4hr and higher, watch out below.

The price range on 1hr+ time frames makes it hard for more traders to see clearly, this is why you must mark those area right down to the 5min with a box and look for price action inside the box. The deeper price works into the box the more I get interested to trade against it especially when 4hr + is with us.

All make sense?

When you get used to trading this way, wait for the 5min to pull away from the extreme edge of the box, then come back to test the origin of that break, once that retest is done and both market timing for a major market is not near close or news to effect the pair is not due, then I will get in. Again as you progress you will find it hard to trade against the market, this is the counter intuitive part messing with your head. If it helps and lets assume you want to trade a 3 euro trade....instead put in a 1 euro trade, wait for the price to move and form another pull back which now is a retest of the previous break, now add in another 1 euro trade. For my US friends your Dollar is still worth something, just.....keep the presses going Ben:)

Rather than take the full risk on one trade, spread your risk over a few smaller size lots. When you improve you can then determine yourself which entries you are good at and take those heavier.

I will trade in places that contradict what I say in here, but I assure you my trades are only taken with a good many years at this and you will get a feel for when a decision point or a sudden spike becomes a viable trade. For the moment stick to what you are doing, it looks to me you are doing great at this and you have no problems on the higher time frames and have a good grasp now of the pull back setups too.
