posts.text:
I had a trade last week (posted in my journal) where I got stopped out (faked out) by 5pips before price went in my direction. Price then just smashed back down without any retrace to allow me to re-enter the move. On post analysis I was happy with the setup and just put it down to a trade that didn't work, and moved on........... Or so I had thought, but I found myself thinking that this could happen again on my next swing, since I didn't have a reason as to why it had happened!! We are usually scared of things that we don't understand. Knowing that this would lead to indecision and hesitancy in my future shot making, I set about analysing FOs (fake outs).

Just for clarity, I'll be talking about:

S/D - Supply/Demand SUP - Supply D - Demand S/R - Support Resistance Swap - Suport becomes resistance and vice versa ENG - Engulf FTR - Failure To Return FTB - First Time Back FO - Fake Out

FL - Flag Limit

Using a Weekly chart of the AUD/USD I've marked one FO pattern in red and the other FO in blue

I've kept all markings on the chart to a minimum for clarity. Basically I'm

saying here that the area between an FTR and the price zone that it failed to returned to, is a potential FO zone. This FO zone needs to be narrow to have potential, as the pros have to be able to drive price beyond the FTR to the S/D level.

To me an FTR can relate to any important zone, whether it be S/D, S/R, Swap or FL. The red pattern has an S/R - FTR FO zone and the blue pattern has an S/D - FTR FO zone. FOs provide large liquidity for the pros to buy/sell into and so they can lead to a large move in price. Coast to coast type of thing.

Hey Doc excellent chart. It got me wondering why it started breaking down up there so I started digging.

I believe the opposing FTRs cause the highs (of price, not the drawn boxes) of the current PAZ, and if the current highs of the PAZ engulfed the opposing FTRs then price should have no problem jumping up to the next PAZ. Especially if price comes back down to a level/ftr smoothly without basing any, then it should be an easy ride up.

Its when price does things in extremes that makes all this hard. Like when supply and demand are close together the s/r lines are severly blurred (or you could say the PAZs are layered on top of each other), or like here when you have so much upward momentum the s/r lines are stretched far apart and barely visible. You have to go down to a smaller TF to see the effect. It all works exactly the same, it just makes it harder to pull the trigger. But if we can understand the extremes, then the middle ground should be cake.

DrSwing wrote: I had a trade last week (posted in my journal) where I got stopped out (faked out) by 5pips before price went in my direction. Price then just smashed back down without any retrace to allow me to re-enter the move. On post analysis I was happy with the setup and just put it down to a trade that didn't work, and moved on........... Or so I had thought, but I found myself thinking that this could happen again on my next swing, since I didn't have a reason as to why it had happened!! We are usually scared of things that we don't understand. Knowing that this would lead to indecision and hesitancy in my future shot making, I set about analysing FOs (fake outs).

Just for clarity, I'll be talking about:

S/D - Supply/Demand SUP - Supply D - Demand S/R - Support Resistance Swap - Suport becomes resistance and vice versa ENG - Engulf FTR - Failure To Return FTB - First Time Back FO - Fake Out FL - Flag Limit

Using a Weekly chart of the AUD/USD I've marked one FO pattern in red and the other FO in blue

I've kept all markings on the chart to a minimum for clarity.

Basically I'm saying here that the area between an FTR and the price zone that it failed to returned to, is a potential FO zone. This FO zone needs to be narrow to have potential, as the pros have to be able to drive price beyond the FTR to the S/D level.

To me an FTR can relate to any important zone, whether it be S/D, S/R, Swap or FL. The red pattern has an S/R - FTR FO zone and the blue pattern has an S/D -FTR FO zone. FOs provide large liquidity for the pros to buy/sell into and so they can lead to a large move in price. Coast to coast type of thing.

posts.author: DrSwing
posts.text:
H, In my view not all demand orders need to get removed in CP, just the larger pockets, to ease the move back down through it. Also you will notice that if you check A1 & A2 areas, marked on the chart below in a LTF, you can see more evidence of demand removal on the way up.

When price returns to the CP zone, these tiny pockets of demand still cause a reaction, but the small numbers of buyers here are easily overcome by the sellers from the flip area of B above. Unless B gets engulfed north the sellers are in control. Once the bottom edge of the PAZ is engulfed south we are free to move into the zone below.

Well guys and gals it's time for me to fess up!

I'll be a year here on RTM next week, and for months now I can smell and even touch the other side, but I just cant break through. Right now I find I am spinning my wheels, basically going around in circles, in frustration. So very often I have felt so close to being at one with the markets, only to awake the following day a stranger again. I am not learning anything new and not having any new aha moments, and this week in particular I just seem to have a mental block. Sure I can read the past PA all day and all night, but I just can't trade the hard right edge! Not even on Forextester!

When I first joined I posted quite a lot, but then I found that the more I learned the more difficult it became to post. This made it very difficult for me to make comments on posts or attempt to answer members questions. So I worked harder in silence, digging into the charts in order to be able to make posts that would add value to the forum.

Now heading into my second year, I feel something needs to change. My plan is to start posting regularly again with you all clearly knowing that I am just a mickey mouse trader who is still learning. Even if my posts don't help anyone maybe it will at least help shift my own mental block. Maybe I need the forum now more than it needs me. So please be aware that I am further from being a master trader than most of you posting here, and that everything I post is just my own probably misguided understanding.

Thank you If for your continued support and your patience with our silence.

God Bless all drswing

Dr Swing,

The last part of the Journey always seems the hardest. We are battle worn, tired and feel vulnerable.

That overwhelming urge to come "full circle" with any of our endeavours is what keeps us going. I know your frustration, It is like a splinter in your mind. The hardest thing is to accept is we may not be there yet, where others think we are. Being put on a pedestal is like being judged on every post you make. The most important thing you want to give to any reader is the correct information, this really exposes you in the raw. You are right or wrong, simple as that.

It is one thing for the market to prove you wrong, but it is another to make it public too.

As traders we must accept that until we master ourselves, we can not master the market.

you can be technically right 100% at chart reading. But what about your state of mind at that time, are there any life distractions, do you feel under pressure to perform. Have you had an argument with a loved one, is your boss winding you up.

The further up life's ladder you go, the more pressure to perform is on your shoulders.

All the professionals I have ever known, still spend countless hours going over the basics. EVEN those at the top of there game.

I have found the best way to deal with my demons is to face them FULL on. With more persistence and energy than before.

so, yes post in your journal, empty your thoughts in here. For our most vulnerable moments can be the most enlightening.

Regards

Warren

Hi Rex, sure, I will get to that in a following post, but first this:)

Something struck me in a post from Hotrod this morning about himself.

HotRod wrote:.................. I need to loosen up my thought process on price and FTRs. I am still wanting price to have defined rigid rules and then obey those rules.......................

My understanding is that price is not a monthly, weekly, or daily event that happens the same on each occasion. Price is a story that unfolds through time, and each event plays out differently on each occasion as price adapts to it's surroundings. This is why they say that understanding the markets is more of an art than a science. So once you understand all the elements of price reading (the science) that are thought here in RTM, you then use that science to decipher (the art) the unfolding story. The story is always about the ITs moving price from source to destination while playing tricks to hide the route they are taking from the reader. This is why the often double back and set traps to cover their tracks and confuse the tracker. They will not use the identical paths and identical tricks on each occasion.

What I am trying to put accross here, is that price events can be similar, but seldom the same. This is why Hotrod's statement is so important to grasp.

Ok, this post is an insight into one method of how I try to find my trade opps.

I read the charts to find zone engulfs rather than just DBR/RBD engulfs as this gives the desired R:R.

I see the charts in terms of Poles and Flags and I'm looking to the SR transition level between the PAZs. This trade level has to be an M1 SD zone 3-4 pips wide and providing an FO to the above/below FTR/FL. I then trade the return to this level, giving me a potentially massive R:R. I then draw the SR level.

posts.author: PASniper
posts.text:
milkeyway wrote: Hi Dr. Swing or any other expert. Can you please tell me why price did not respect this fresh supply? Thanks.

Hi MW, I am not any expert, but you need to remember:

“So here's what we look for on the charts:

General: HTF. Know where price is coming from and going to, and the PA past and present in all the TFs, from the Monthly down.

Specific: At the zones you want to trade, look to

Past. study the zone in all TFs, down to M1

ask yourself Where were the decisions made? Clean S/D? Mark these lines. No clean S/D? -compressed zone Did price really shoot away from the zone, or did it CP away? Did the zone itself react at the right place? Look beyond the zone further into the past. See what it reacted to. Was there a better S/D nearby that price wants to visit? This explains many fakeouts.

Present. Approach. How is price returning to the zone? Where's the nearest flag in the TF you want to trade? This is your tg1 in this TF. Flags in the LTFs? What does PA tell you? Has price tested the last flag on approach? (good sign) Has price compressed into the zone in this TF or LTFs? (good sign) Is there big news on the way? Has there just been big news?

Reaction In LTF, does price react violently to the first decision point? Does it quickly engulf the nearest S/D? (good sign) Does price simply CP away? Maybe it wants to go to the next decision point If the first decision point breaks, watch the signs on approach to the next, and, of course, reaction.

Chew this over for now. Apply it to your chart history. Apply it to as many failed setups as successful ones. Millions of them if possible! Capture and file them all. This will help make it instinctive.”

Supply and demand are not enough reasons to enter trades, watch how price arrives to a level (Compression, 3D...), if no PA - there is no trade; then wait for LTF PA (DM, QM, CanCan) to enter. Use TT only at DPs at levels where there is a high probability trade (previous QM level, FOs, ignored levels.

Introduction

Well RTM is up and running again and my fellow students and I have
recently finished undertaking the RTMA QM course. There is still a lot
of work to I need to do in regards to my trading but I have the
foundations on how I see price move and what to expect. Is that all that
 is required. NO. The psychological and aspects are more important.

I am using this new Journal take what I have learnt here and from RTMA
to put my thoughts on paper. These are my interpretations and may need
tweaking, so anything I write, please do not take as absolute. We have
had some great discussions over at RTMA and everyone has been amazing.
Thanks to the RTM (4) brothers: IF,Gil,Martin and Harry for RTM. Also
thank you to the RTMA students. Finally thank you to members here.

Purpose - The Blue Dot Community

Anyone who is not a part of the blue community, I suggest thinking about
 it. After all, it is my understanding this is why we are learning to
read price. Eventually the plan is to destroy the markets. My initial
motives years ago were not this and I only joined RTM with the aim to
quit my job and make money for me. I was motivated by greed. Now I am
not going to say that financial freedom is still not a goal, it is
however I am of the view we can only earn whilst the fund builds up and
serves the purpose of the blue dot community. My goal is simple to help
IF and others achieve
	www.theblue.community/
 . I will start by

1.	Finalise testing and trading (ongoing)

2.	Start to assist others with learning on areas I know (future goal)

3.	Also assist with the fund (future goal)

4.	Assist with THE BLUE COMMUNITY (end goal)

New Journal

My old journal was full of S/D rubbish especially the initial posts. I
hate S/D. I think it’s the new ploy to market it as institutional
trading. When I say S/D I mean the conventional way of trading S/D. In
fact one could say RTM methods are closer to S/R trading. But S/R is
also a terrible form of trading, especially the conventional methods.
The rest of the journal was jumping from one random thought to another
and chasing the shiny ball of a new RTM concept before understanding the
 basics of the previous concept.

Feel free to drop by and add anything or spark a conversation. I think I
 will start the next post with a summary of how I now see the market.
Let’s all get involved!

Regards, Clint

From what I have learnt, I.Ts move price from kink to kink (DPs) They
start as FTRs and once the TG is met the FL is confirmed. Price bounces

liquidity, all manufactured for manipulation purposes. Nothing like Fear
 or Greed to fill a long or short position.

something we don’t own. How can a market be framed legitimately. Simple,

and only visible on a tick chart. A tiny kink from the break of a LS or
into another Paz. The better the area is hidden, the better the trick is

****CAVEAT**** Only my view of the terminology to avoid confusion ***

Decision Points – Kink/Failure to Return (FTR)/Flag Limit (FL)

I see the decision point as the pièces de résistance in the RTM arsenal.
 Sometimes also referred to as a kink, FTR or Flag Limit, it represents
the decision made at a barrier in the past. For the sake of consistency
and to help alleviate any confusion I see it occurring in (3) stages
which are outlined below.

Stage One - The Kink

Price approaches a barrier such as minor Support/Resistance (S/R), Major
 S/R, Left Shoulder, Ignored barrier or break in/out of Compression (CP)
 Price pauses and begins a retrace or pull back once the barrier has
been broken. It is this hiccup that is now the kink.

Stage Two – The FTR

If price fails to retrace further and proceeds in the original direction
 it forms a FTR once price crosses past the origin of the retrace, it
has failed to return. At this point a decision has been made by the IT’s
 to absorb the remaining orders and likely set new orders to be used at a
 later point. However it is not a confirmed flag limit.

Stage Three – The Flag Limit

The Flag Limit (FL) is confirmed when an opposing one is hit. Until it
is hit the kink and FTR still form part of a flag’s body. This means the
 FTR and kink can retrace further prior to the opposing FL being hit.

Decision Points- Visibility

Its also important to understand the best DPs are those ones which are
invisible in the higher time frames. You have to remember that a DP
could form and be hidden within the range of a candle seconds after it
happens. Unless we are there to see it as it occurs we have to keep
digging until it is found. Sometimes we will unable to find it so in
that case we have to use the whole candle. My favourite is an invisible
DP that has a cap form as the first time back which price can fake out
to the real DP.

Well,first thing I like to do is to open the chart and have a look at
the highest scale. I do this in a informal sense. It helps me get in
tune with the market. Its not a mandatory step, but I find it helps
lubricate the cogs which turn inside my skull. I have a look to see what
 type of program they are running. This is simple. Its just looking at
the past to see where they have accumulated, marked up, distributed,
marked down. NOT THE WYCKOFF WAY. Many S/D traders love these
terms. I actually regret labelling them as the stages. In a simpler form
 its just ping pong between FLs.

We can see how they stack orders create highs and lows to FO past to get
 the BO traders and stops. This creates a big pool of liquidity for
them. How they move into a CP program swapping orders out and
positioning themselves which creates the liquidity spikes through a

posts.text:
2. Marking the DPs surrounding the PAZ’s which define the I.T order blocks

DPs are everywhere but we are best placed breaking them up into PAZ’s.
Everything I have read on RTM and over at the Academy and studied on a
chart suggests to me In its most simplest form that:

Price is either in space (an expanding Flag), Body of established
Flag OR its at the limit (FL). An Engulf means nothing if its returning
from an opposing FL.

Once we can master this and scale, I don’t think QMs DMs Can Cans etc
matter as they fall into place by the very nature of the before
mentioned statement.

Of course this all goes out the window if we do not correctly identify the FLs and Flags.

Other members here may notice that I tend to focus on areas which may
not be significant. Keep in mind I am marking it as possible
Conservative TG’s. I will not necessary look at it as a place to enter
or wait for further PA.

I follow these as a guideline. There may be times when I adjust the
rules. If we remain consistent in how we mark it up, it should all even
out in the end:

-	Mark All Highs/Lows/SR (The ones I see, some of us see things differently)

-	LS’s and Ignored LS’s

-	Break into and Post Compression (**N.B pre compression MPL is marked as TG only**)

-	CP must make a HH/LL than the last set of preceding orders.

-	Only the opposite swing point at the break in and out of CP can be used as S/R or L/S

-	Price must break the associated (FL) of the before mentioned areas. If not I don’t mark it up (more on this later)

-	Associated FTR has to have met an opposing TG before it’s a FL &
The barrier must have been in opposite direction (direction dictated by
EG’s)

Now I am in two minds regarding stacked zones. I know it can often be
used as a less aggressive form of Compression BUT in my opinion clean
orders can still reside between the stacked zones, so I treat them like
one of the before mentioned categories.

Please see below chart.

 I am not straying too far away from what I’m trying to achieve with
this plan. More reflection tomorrow

A member PMd me asking a question on how I choose the levels. They
referenced my last post. To me we all need to answer this by going back
to the PAR article. Its all there in half a page. I know that even the
masters are not carbon copies of each other. How Harry trades differs to
 Salivan which differs to Mertch who all even differ to even IF.

But you know what brings them all together? Its the foundations that can
 be witnessed in Price Approach Reaction. For me I look for a Big
picture, where price is going and come from. I find the LFL/UFL kinks I
want to trade, then I drill down and find all the order blocks and look
for confluence with a trick, PCP or SR kinks. LS being the most strong
**I NEED TO SEE CLEAN ORDERS**. I even drill further to find more kinks
and ensure its a UFL/LFL that has taken opposing area in its formation. I
 then decide where its come from and whether we have PA, or can I TT
based on the other factors and the approach. IE are retailers getting in
 early and being trapped.

I have been spending a lot of time with a few of my close friends
undertaking analysis and some trading, so I don't get to post as much in
 my journal as I would like.

What works for me, may not work for others, so take it with a grain of salt

posts.author: einrikr
posts.text:
Morning everybody,

I think I just had some sort of aha-moment.

For that reason, I wanted to post it here, so that I have had it written
 down, which makes me remember it more easiliy, and I can find it back.
That important of a memory is it, for me at least. For others, this may
be perfectly clear.

Little background information to start with:

Price moves in poles and flags. Poles exist either of simple poles, or
compression. Below, on top of, or somewhere in the middle of a pole, a
flag/cap forms. Flags are created by kinks, or Flag Limits, which in
their turn, are created by barriers such as PCP, LS, RS.

Now for the epiphany: Flags exist between 2 Flag Limits.

Easy as that. FL's have edges, and a flag sits right between FL1 for
example and FL2. This is stated in the article, I know, but somehow it
didn't make me really understand that. It is however, of major
importance in reading price.

I had a lot of trouble understanding the concept of Flag Limits,
although it didn't have anything to do with finding the darn things. I
do get when something is a FL but what I didn't seem to grasp, was when
they were of any use and how they would act in a chart. Sure, I've seen
price reacting the FL's but still. For some, this might seem really
silly, for me, it wasn't clear at all. Taking 3 days off off charting,
reading, commenting did it's job I guess, so there's a big lesson as
well. Learn stuff, go over it until you get it, and most importantly, let your mind process everything. It'll put together what needs to be put together and that's something you can't force.

Now, If someone doesn't agree with what's stated above, please feel free
 to elaborate on that. I'm still just a newbie and might be wrong about
things. I'm really eager to learn, so all feedback is very welcome.
Thank's IF, you've stated quite a few times that it's really important
to let stuff sink in, but experiencing it sometimes is the only way to
let that sink in. And thanks RTM, for being such an inspirational place!

posts.author: einrikr
posts.text:
The next post is sort of a addition to what was discussed recently, found in Salivan's journal.

In my opinion, it's a good way to read price on the way up, since it tells you lots!

Here goes:

1: Price broke through barrier, wants next.

2: Broke straight through, whats next.

3: Broken,

4: Broken immediately after, same with 5.

6: price touches it and retraces directly. This way, you'll know that
price is going down until it hits the next target, which you can find
the same way.

Not the quickest way to see live where price is bouncing but a fun exercise!

Now it's time to find out what makes that one a stronger level of
resistance, so that it's possible to anticipate on those levels.

posts.text:
After 3 days, I’ve closed my trade at 50R, be it by accident. Not the
most efficient trade but highly rewarding. Wanted to bank 50% but it
didn’t work, the action I performed close 100%.

However, what have I learned from this trade:

Targets

Setting a final TG for yourself is a good thing, so you know what you’re
 working up to. Watching it reaching your target helps building trust in
 your reads.

Do not however, neglect mid-range targets as they are very capable of
bouncing price. For example, price bounced off of 2 PCP points and got
as low as the cap of my point of entry.

It was a fun exercise though, getting in to a short, down to the PO I’ve
 set for a long and seeing price hit exactly that and turn around. There
 was 0.7 pip drawdown on this trade.

Expectations

50R (high of first day) or 70R (high of second day) is more than enough. Just be happy with it and take it.

I’ve been waiting for a bit higher R for 3 days now and it bugs me. It’s
 really annoying to see price going up and down and not hitting your TG.
 Sure, it didn’t hit my stop but the bit of extra R is not worth the
wait. Not for me it isn’t, not at this point in my trading career at
least. Maybe it’ll be later on. I’m not in a hurry, not in the need of
getting high R trades but the inconvenience of waiting and watching PA
all day long, sort of defeats the result for me. On the other hand, if
it turns out that I’m able to do this on regular bases, it gives me the
opportunity to do a lot of thing I like, rather than a day job. Future
goals, I guess ;-)

Patience is very important in this line of work but being satisfied with
 quite high R results is equally important. You have to be patient to
let price come up to the level you set as your TG and you have to have
faith in tour readings. You have to be realistic too, and not let your
final TG play with your mind.

All in all, this trade showed me the very basics, like caps working, CP,
 and some QM levels even. It has been good fun, watching price doing
it’s thing, at least for the first 2 days. Today, not so much for me but
 now I wanted to hold on to it and get the profit I predicted it to
give. It was a good experience, of which I’ve learned a lot. It works
wonders for me to witness price doing what it does at certain levels and
 I’m very happy with the result and especially of everything it taught
me.

On to the next! But I'm going to bed first, really tired after watching the screen for 3 days!

I'm having a not-so-wonderful trading week so far but that happens. I
decided to take the day off and do some manual labour and that was a
good thing.

Coming home, I decided to watch price a bit and marked up this, regarding the pinball nature of price:

(1) Price came, breaks QM level from the past so made LSK here. Currently holding price up.

(2) Price bounced from RSK in the past

(3) FTB of current FL. Important cap, that will hold price up until engulfed.

(4) Price hit PCP kink in the past. Still holding price down.

(5) Important cap (see 3) holds price up.

(6) FTB of newest LSK holding price down. Price goes to LFL.

(7) Price engulfs important cap (3) and gets back up.

( Price hits LTF QM level, price is now trapped between this lvl and the currently active LFL.

(9) Price hits MPL (i.e. QM Level) of LFL. Goes back up.

(10) Last LTF UFL engulfed

(11) Price comes down to last cap.

(12) Current UFL still active.

There are QM level bounces at 4, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 12. I actually think that 11 is a QM level bounce as well.

Now, I'm too tired to distill any more out of it at the moment but I
guess the main thing here is: price travels from QM to QM, in different
scales.

You can take a 1RR trade going from marker 7 to marker 8 for example, or
 take a 7RR trade from marker 9 to 12. I think this is all a matter of
scale, focus on the lower scales only, you get the lower R trades. Focus
 on larger scale ranges, combined with lower scale entry, and you're
getting the real high R trades.

Now, I haven't checked this on any other charts since the before made
statement of tiredness, but I'll keep diving in this matter the upcoming
 days. In the mean time, please feel free to comment. If I'm just
rambling nonsense, please just tell me too, so I won't focus on this any
 more

posts.author: Ifmyante
posts.text:
If you're not one to simply trade on the touch of a zone, but would rather wait for confirmation that price has rejected, there are some brilliant PA patterns you can look for before you enter a trade.

The best ones we'll cover involve an Engulf

Simply put, an engulf involves price making a lower low on reaction to Supply, or higher high from Demand This is a very powerful sign that price is on the turn. They say that a trend is a succession of LL's and HH's, or vice versa, so if you get a Lower Low from Supply, it's a great first sign that the uptrend may be over, and of course flip the scenario for an HH from Demand.

If you didn't have the patience to wait for that engulf, see the Lower timeframe for another lovely engulf showing the way much earlier!

The area below the PAZ is a FL, a small demand zone that temporary keeps the price inside the PAZ (flag). Then, when FL gets engulfed, we enter short at the first RT into the engulfing candle. posts.author: Andyfx
posts.text:
The Engulf - FTR combo is one of my favorite trade setup for a quick scalp.

If we are moving away from an HTF SD zone, I wait for an Engulf of previous high/low, then I take the trade if the FTR touch the SD pocket at the origin of the engulf. In fact it is trading SD pockets of a CP zone, subsequents Engulf and FTR to SD pocket at the origin of the Engulf. Like it is the FTB to previous FTR again and again after an engulf.

Just make sure of not buying near supply and selling near demand, and that the SD pocket is tight and clean with a strong move away making the engulf. Look to the left and take the trade only if there is free space or even better an engulf of previous opposite FTR SD pocket into a new PAZ, or wait for an Engulf of a FL and enter on the second FTR wich is FTBing the FTR SD pocket. The QM is also a powerfull Engulf-FTR setup.

Edit: an other option to trade ENG+ FTR combo: in strong momentum trends, price will often bounce at SR flip instead of origin-of-the-engulf-SD-pocket, if we are not sure we can split the position in 2: open one at SR flip and one if the price touch SD pocket, same stop loss above SD pocket for both.

Something like this FTR to FTR SD pocket

FTR to SRFlip

Hi all,

Year 2009 - AUD

Below is a 4hr chart, with the FTRs I have selected. I’ve numbered the FTRs 1-5 for referencing purposes. I will now go through the reasons why I think each zone qualifies to be an FTR on this 4hr TF.

FTR 1 failed to return to the blue demand area, plus look how powerful price was when leaving the zone, price engulfed some serious supply, If you look on the Daily this 4hr FTR is actually part of the Daily FTR, very powerful.

FTR 2 failed to return to the green SR which was prior resistance/supply, but now is Demand/support, also notice that the FTR had quite a powerful burst of momentum, and at the time I thought it may have been an engulf validating the FTR, I actually did take a look higher up and noticed on the weekly we were getting close to Major highs.

FTR 3 failed to return to the previous supply/high which is where I believed an engulf was present, notice also price engulfs FTR 2.

FTR 4 failed to return to FTR 2, remember above I said that price had engulfed FTR 2, once FTR was engulfed as demand, this now becomes supply, so FTR 4 was a failure to return to supply (FTR2)

FTR 5 failed to return to the blue demand area, which if you notice was also another FTR of off FTR 1, price also engulfed the high above, validating my FTR 5. I am not saying any of the above is correct, it is just what I see and something that is beginning to make sense. I have described why I think each zone is an FTR, now I will go through each zone separately investigating how one could have entered using various P.A concepts.

I will begin with FTR 1 (As per 4hr chart above), we already know price reacted well here, I went down to the hourly and this is what I saw, nothing much other than a clean pin.

I went down to the 15 minute TF as there was nothing much on the 30 min TF, I could see nothing here, so on to the 5 minute TF.

All I see on the 5 minute TF is this: a nice push from the big boys into the HTF FTR, price rallied back up and touched the supply, retraced a tad, and then engulfed the supply, what would have been nice is for price to come back to the small 5 min FTR below.

Now I will move on to FTR 2 (as per the 4hr chart above)

Straight on to the hourly I noticed a nice-looking QM set up 1-5 from which one may have entered long on.

The 30 min TF just shows a cleared view of the QM, so on the 15 minute TF. What I saw straight away on the 15 min was the prominent FTR above in blue where price reacted lovely, the lower FTR could have been a long entry as price engulfed the high (yellow) but as we know it reacted to the upper FTR.

Ok, now moving on to FTR 3 (again refer to the 4hr chart at the beginning of the post)

On the hourly, the first things I noticed was the clear and obvious FTRs present in and around the HTF FTR in blue look at the reaction from the very top one, beautiful.

Moving on to the 15 minute chart I saw what I think to be a 3-drive into the upper FTR, now I am not sure if it is one as I have only glanced through the 3-drive thread briefly, it may even be a 2-drive haha, if there is such a thing.

On to the 5 minute chart, I have written the details on.

Now on to FTR 4 (as per the 4hr chart above)

We know that this area did not hold price, so let’s try to see if we had the opportunity to short and lose, what this does for me is to see if I would have entered short and lost this trade.

There was nothing on the hourly, so I went straight to the 30 min TF, and what we see is price cannot break/engulf the demand in yellow, not a good sign if you’re looking to short.

The 15 minute chart shows a clearer view of price not being able to break this support in yellow, so definitely not any shorts for me on this TF.

For the 5 minute chart I would have at least needed price to break/engulf this green demand for me to consider a short somewhere, but as we see price did not, it respected the level, so no short here.

Now on to FTR 5 (as per the 4hr chart above)

As we know now, the level did get engulfed, so let’s try to enter long somewhere seeing if P.A will allow this.

Here is the 30 min TF, I see a nice FTR zone in green which I would have probably entered long on, the reason being as this area to me is also the base of the pole, price did react, and we may have got out with a small win or at worst a B.E.

Onto the 15 min chart, I have left the green FTR from the 30 min on, there was a nice entry short, I see straight away, but it is whether I would have had the ball to enter short in a HTF FTR. Price engulfed my green FTR, then RT to DP to enter short.

On to the 5 min chart, again I have left all prior zones on, I was still looking to go long, but if we look closely price was unable to engulf the upper highs and the supply above, which was essentially the DP to create the LL in the first place, which to makes these levels important to engulf. So no long for me using P.A on this TF.

If anyone sees something I am not, would be great to hear.

Cheers all

Here is a USDJPY H4 chart. As we approach W1 demand I want to analyze where my entries would be first in candle stick then in line chart. I would look to buy only after the engulf of the H4 FL and the swing high above it. The only entry that makes sense to me would be at the H1 FTB to FTR marked with a red tick, with stops below the H1/M30 FL zone and a target in the zone with price labels.

Now the fact that price had not made a LL coming from the FTB to FTR3 higher up into the long entry increased the probabilities that it could hit the FTR1 where target is, of course after engulfing the other ones on the way. I haven’t gone lower than H1 or M30 in this analysis but I quickly saw that on M15 there was an engulf of the last FL coming into the zone which also coincided with a very clear QM on M5.

Now for the last 2 charts… I read a post yesterday by a senior somewhere that said that it is not the engulf of the high or low that matters but the engulf of a FL that is important. Whoever, I have seen many traders here just taking the important high/low that created the last low/high. So after seeing the engulf of the high on H4 and the retrace to the origin of the move up on M5, possible entries are shown as tick marks.

I am sorry I too am still learning… but I thought maybe someone can comment on whether one can trade with a line chart or not.

Thanks again everyone and have a great weekend, Pucci

I didn't want the above in bold to confuse anyone.

I have sat here and wrote a few different explanations, but then erased them because they just don't reconcile what I have in my brain. Does a base have to engulf lows to be an FTR?

An FTR is created when a H/L or S/D zone gets engulfed and then price retraces. IF says the FTR is the deepest part of the retrace. So how do you have a deepest part of the retrace if a base never engulfs that last low (in this case) or zone? If it doesnt engulf the last low, then the only other alternative is it keeps retracing. Which means you still don't have an FTR.

So, yes I guess a base does have to engulf L/Hs or zones to be an FTR. Otherwise you don't have a "deepest part" yet. And if price never stops retracing, then you didn't have an engulf, you had a FO.

I need to clarify a few things on the following chart, and stop confusing everyone.

You still have to look at what an FTR engulfed, and what it didn't, to see how strong it is. But it does at least have to engulf that last L/H in the retrace to qualify as an FTR. If that is all that it engulfs then any trade taken should not be expected to go further than the retrace itself, and best planned on a lower TF. But look at that bottom yellow line, if FTR3 had engulfed that low, then the potential RR of any trade taken at FTR3 is much better. Of course then you need to look and see where any HTF demand might be.

Its relatively easy to see where price will react. Its the strength of the reaction that is so hard to judge. What an FTR engulfs, and the way price behaves on its way back to that FTR is all we have to judge that reaction. Look at the reaction after hitting demand, the break of that high, and the pockets of demand left behind on the way back to FTR3 is a lot to overcome for any short.

Sorry for any confusion I have created, and hopefully I cleared it up. Any seniors feel free to correct me.

Hi DT,

I have been watching your journal for a while now; I think 2014 is going to be a good year for you.

I had some comments on one of your trades. Hindsight trading has us all being superstars, but it helps to understand why something might have failed. Of course, take my comments as just comments, nothing more.

In the chart below, the real area to be engulfed was to the left - the FL. That wasnt engulfed until you were actually already long. Your long position was probably due to price stalling in that minor pullback, but that whole area is minor in

dM

movement to the wider price action. The FO that occurs a few bars later that pushes price through the true FL, would have been nice PA to get in on. Theres nice PA at the top there to reverse at the FL extent, and drop-base-drop that results in taking out the lows of this whole move. The base could have been one place to get in if you didnt want to miss the move, but then it should have been clear the best place to find sellers was really below the untested pivot to the left. If unsure, I would have placed part of my position at the base (though I wouldnt have traded the base in this image), and then look for PA to get long thereafter. Price sinks down to the lows, picks up those lovely sell orders and shoots to the moon. The push up from the lows was a signal to get in if you werent already in.

You had True FL broken -> price collapse->drop base drop->lows taken out, meaning buyers needed them, and this is the catalyst to the real major upswing. Theres clearly an SR in this initial push up that was also a means to get in on a lower timeframe too. No drawdown.

MF

Ok my take:

We've just come off the FTB to a H4 demand which is a base on the Daily i.e. Stronger demand vs the supply we'll find on the 15 min in this area currently. So where is price going to? I would think maybe the next H4 supply which I've marked in blue.

Now we look at the 15 min. This H4 is not fresh and worse we have stacked demand with wide bars which makes it a bit more difficult to work out targets and figure out which one will stop price.

Now we get an engulf on the 15 min before we hit the target but it could have been a bounce off that important FTR from engulfing the H4 demand to the left. So we expect a reaction there but I would think that it would remove supply for a push up into that H4 demand target as price sometimes fakes out stacked demand to get to the base.

So it engulfs the current FL after faking out below and then FO's again for a FTB to the base of the move. If we go to the hourly we get a possibility for a FTB with a move up to the 81.40's.

Not sure if this helps much as its after the fact and price has started to move as I write this.

The thing I'm trying to focus on is making sure I know where price is coming from and going to as I just got burned yesterday on a JPY trade very similar to this which I posted in my journal. I thought I saw a setup on the 15 min but missed a whole lot of higher TF information. Hope this helps. Cheers.

Hi! At the start I would like to emphasis, that my answer is only my point of view and please consider it rather as a seed for discussion than a correct answer.

It would be great if someone from senior members there could comment this post:) Especially my zones.

There are few things that we must take into account when looking for a trade opportunity: 1) HTF: where we are going to? In my opinion price wanted FTR above your trades (I have the zones drawn earlier, before answering your post, so I don't cheat:P). Personally I will wait for price reaction on this level, not earlier.

So according to charts price is going from one FTR to the one above, so at the time you take your trades it was in "midrange". Which is not good because price is very vulnerable for fakeouts. Additionally you taken the trades "counter trend" because price was going from demand to supply.

2) Some time ago I realize one very simple stuff: when price is at supply and I would like to take a short trade, then probably there are many other traders which want to do the same. So when there are so many traders shorting, then they are at big boys aim, because if they (big boys) also want to short at current supply level, then they must fill their big orders. So it is almost sure that the FO will happen near levels like that.

Generally we have two scenarios: If there is a CP to a given level we can place pending order. But if there is no CP at the approach, we must wait for flag engulf. I'm not good for the second one yet, so personally I often wait for engulf confirmation - I wait for FTB to FTR which was just created.

3) Sometimes diamonds happens:P And sometimes engulf happened before price reaches proper supply/demand, so you must be aware of levels above your supply/demand levels

So you see, there are many, many variables we must be aware of. In my opinion it is not only waiting for a break of the last low/high. We must learn to read the market: where the price is (HTF!!! LTF), where the price is probably going to, what is below/above a given level, is the level strong or it is tested? Maybe price just CP from your level not shot down with big momentum (very often hidden in the LTFs), we must take into account approach (demands/supplies tested on price's way? are there still fresh DPs?).

Hope this helps:)

Hey By!

This has frustrated me to no end as well. Sometimes they work and sometimes they don't but PA usually tells the tale. I have given up on TT any levels as I"m too retarded to pick them properly yet. I demand that price confirms there is supply at a fresh HTF level and if its a 2TB then it has to roll out the red carpet before I get interested. I get burned too easily otherwise.

So that being said here's my interpretation of the chart. My data does not match yours at all so I'll just work from your chart. It may not totally answer your question but most times we have to read the PA around the engulf and preface it with the HTF to surmise if its significant or not.

1: We start a leg down that manages to break your white line this will be our base. Its also a smaller ftr as it engulfed a local low but I can't see if it engulfed anything to the left. At any rate its our base.

2: We break the last flag and the one below it to form a small flag of our own, technically this is a ftr also. 3:There are two parts to this PA, the actual decision to break the low and then it retests back up making the FL=FTR and then engulfs the previous low confirming it is now supply. 4: Price tests up FTB and removes some supply 5: Price slices back up eating the FL and testing the first FTR before the origin. Les Pauls sweet FTR. Price has engulfed the FL for sure but it bounced off the sweet FTR and did not engulf it. I'm looking for a trade that has room to move and it has also not engulfed the origin (remember we like to see bases of poles engulfed for a heads up on a possible reversal). So as it stands now we have the FL engulfed but no room up to the next PAZ. It has instead bounced and is heading back down. We need more PA to figure out what nonsense the big guys are up to. 6: Buggers! They engulf what we thought should be demand. So now 5 is our FL right. But supply is cleared above it so the next fresh supply will be the origin. 7: Price flys up to the origin after acknowledging 5 with a slight kink. We then travel back down.

Since I don't know if the bottom of the chart is HTF demand H4 or higher can't decide if I would take a shot at that nice small doji long after the recent engulf higher on your chart. Price looks like it still aggressively wants to go down but there may be room for a scalp up and the R:R may work. It really depends on whether we engulfed anything to the left with the move down and what zone we are in.

I missed some of the PA here but hopefully you get the gist. In short I would wait until 1 and maybe the stacked demand above was just taken out before I would consider a long in this case. I will not take any level without a confirmation engulf and retest of the cap, or sweet FTR, or QM, compression after engulf etc. This engulf has to be the base of a pole with room up to the next flag in HTF S/D otherwise I'm just not interested.

I'm not 100% on weaving the proper engulfs together as we go up in TF. know that HTF engulfs will trump the lower action so I try to be aware of these as well. Does this help you any?

Hey By, Make a note of why certain FTRs are marked and others are not in KKB's chart. Then ask yourself why is that? I did a study regarding the engulf of previous H and L to the left to get the new more difficult to fake edges of the new PAZ zones. This is not a magic bullet but it gives you a heads up to which FTRS are better as not all are created the same. For instance if we have engulfed a previous PAZ edge as in the chart above, made a new FTR and are heading up we should expect most of the FTRs to break on the way up until we get to our target origin i.e. the next PAZ edge not the next 4H FTR. It has to be made after engulfing another zone to the left. Thats why IF speaks of engulfing the bottom of poles. finding compression etc on a chart. It makes us aware of the zones that price is coming from and going to. There are only extremes i.e. the edges of our PAZ all the rest is chop and prone to FOs. I would stick with HTF zones as if you try this on the Hourly or lower its a bit tricker to sort out and the big moves are coming off the HTFs anyways.

Now you bring up a good point that what is midrange on the weekly can provide whopper scalps or daily swing trades. We just have to be aware that if price is bouncing from 1H demand to 1H supply while its on its way to 4H demand we can only expect definite pips to the next flag in the 1H TF. it could fake us and then go the other way or continue on past the 1H target but we have to keep an eye on PA: compression into demand, where could comp LQ go to, is this demand truly fresh, is there an untested flag directly below our entry, are there any patterns etc. There is a quote that I remember and recite daily from IF: Something to the effect that we need PA to prove that there is still supply or demand at any given level. Now we see wild 100:1 R:R trades taken from perfect 5 pip 1M levels but either PA was given on a larger TF or we are watching the approach like a Hawk and manage the trade as it progresses. The seniors I'm sure have a better grasp of PAZs than we do so they can pinpoint untested S/D at the edge of zones with great precision. We will be able to do this one day too.

Sorry for my rambling hopefully this is helping. If you want to TT levels you have to weave all the TFs together to see if they are in sync. Then I have to have proof in the form of an engulf of a pole base with room to the next flag before I'll take a trade in a HTF zone. Yes I don't get 50 trades a week but I'm finding the ones I do get are much better quality. Cheers.

Hey Tor,

I really understand all the confusion you might be having without clearly understanding the basics or purpose behind the 'Engulf' price action. I was trying to figure out the same initially and had written a small post of my understandings here (might help you a little www.readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/jo...ve-bulbuli-s-journal(Post # 13)

To put it simply 'Engulf' signifies consumption of orders and thus to have important/significant engulf, we must have a zone (significant) marked where lot of pending orders are expected. But when this level is engulfed it shows that the orders have been consumed and thus price is free to go in the direction of engulf (After Retrace Of course!) Milkeyway had a line diagram drawn here: www.readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/tr...708-engulf?start=192

Some pointers which might stimulate your thought process a little:

This is something I have taken from 1st post of 'Engulf Or Fakeout' Thread

www.readthemarket.com/index.php/forum/ho...-engulf-or-a-fakeout

Thus to spot meaningful engulfs one must be able to spot significant PA zones/levels i.e. Significant FLs/ FTRs/ SD Zones first!

P.S: Newbie Alert!!

Hey By,

I hear your frustration. I am still very frustrated with my progress at times as well. I would say that PA is PA, and is TF independent. You should not be able to tell the difference between a 2 tick chart and a monthly chart. Its all the same reflection of manipulation of emotions. I put more weight on the higher Tfs PA vs the 15 min. I treat the Monthly as a countrie's money and the LTFs as pocket change. Who do you think is more comitted to reaching their target?

That being said you may be trying to use the engulf as an indicator (I know thats how I used it in the beginning and I was extremely frustrated as well; sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't arrrrrrgh!) If we simply used the engulf in isolation even the engulf of the previous FTR or pole base we might as well throw the old MACD back on maybe add some moon cycles in for good measure:).

We try to get around this by reading the market. We do this by looking to the engulf of certain important zones or use it as a "heads up" that price may want to relax and test the next fresh level of supply or demand. This does not always result in a useful trade and also doesn't result in a winning trade. Its information that we must weigh to make a decision on whether to be long short or out.

So I've attached one of your charts with some mark ups (next post) that may address the questions you will have to answer in order to use the engulf properly. Otherwise we're just dogs running after balls. This is exactly what the ITs want. To keep us jumping at shadows.

I'm posting the analysis for those who can't read yet (I'm only moderately good at it but I practice every day) or are just starting. I have left alot out on the chart as this took me a bit of time to write up and double check. Feel free to add to it. If you can do this already I appologise but I gained some good insight to doing this exercise and I encourage everyone else to do the same. Tear the charts apart. Why did this happen? Why did price stop here and not here? We'll suck at it for the first few but eventually light bulbs start to go on.

So the lesson to take away from this post for others that dont' have time to read it now, is that an engulf, QM, compression, cap, FTR, PAZ etc by themselves is meaningless without context. You might as well consult an astrologist or have your palm read. You can only draft if->then statments when you have conditions that are met again and again. i.e. If price compresses into HTF demand and there is room down to the next flag and I get an engulf and I get LTF confirmation on the retest then I'll take a trade. However, it is often way more fluid than this. You wil have to study further to understand when you can use discression on your entries if your ideal entry is not present. Hope this helps someone. Cheers.

posts.author: antraxia
posts.text:
Hindsight glasses fully on (do not discount this analysis as it trains your subconscious to react in realtime).

I've labeled 4 supplys and 2 demands on the left hand side of the chart as we progress down a-f. a:Current top cap b:Second FTR (depends on rather it engulfed anything to the left) c:Third Supply (this is the bottom of stacked supply and serves as the source/origin of the break down d:Fourth FTR/Flaglimit/supply/source of the final leg down (this is a 2TB reaction to a flag on the left) e:Demand source (we don't' know it is until we get and engulf up and start making new highs f:Final demand source

1: Before 1 we can see that price left the supply with good momentum it formed a base rallied up and created a FTB to this supply which may be weak but we've had an engulf so if we get lower TF action and can get good R:R I'll be game for a trade depending on whether that base is in HTF demand or not.

Now look at what happens when we touch the base, we get compression and then a burst of comp LQ away from the zone. Ask yourself: does this compression indicate that there are buyers or sellers in this base area? Should we use caution on the retest especially since we have had a FTB already.

Now we get the break of the supply (FL/FTR/Origin of the final down move) but we aren't all that surprised when it breaks. Why? Because this area isn't fresh. If this break is true then we're heading up to test the base or sweet FTR of this total leg down. All this has to be in the context of what the higher TF's are doing but lets assume there was HTF demand at the base but the area was wide and we have two distinct demand levels.

2: We flag just below the bottom of my stacked supply origin. We break out test the supply then go back into the flag. We then break out of the bottom of the flag. This is the engulf we make money off of. Look at the room down to the next fresh level. If price bounced before HTF demand we should be drooling and smacking our chops:). So if there was HTF demand before how would we know that it may be safe to go short here besides the engulf. Well the approach. It approached like a mack truck but then it stonewalled then made a weak assed attempt into supply. See those tails. We then reject strongly and then compress can-can like back through the previous bar. So does this compression mean there are buyers or sellers at this level. When we revisit will this still be the case?

3: Ok we've had our engulf so we're all ready for a long. I've got my lot size figured out, I'm planning my trip to OZ and polishing my pimp ring when I say wait a minute. Wasn't there untested compression away from this demand. What does that mean? Maybe I'll monitor PA on approach (yes if I set a TT here due to the engulf overnight I got burned). Well we see that price is coming on like a banshee with big bear bars just like the approach above but the difference is that this zone has been tested once and we have compression that hasn't vacuumed price back down yet. Our expectation is for price to possibly test the next fresh level of demand. So we wait for LTF PA on this one. The smart version of me (the one with out the pimp ring who drives a volvo) smiles in delight as price smashes through this demand engulfing it.

4: Ok so where is the next opportunity for a trade. Well that FL @ 4 looks nice and we sort of have a flaggy approach feel but without LTF signal I'm going to pass especially if we haven't engulfed HTF demand. I'm not good enough at these sorts of trades yet but thats ok. More around the corner.

5: Lets say this hits the secondary HTF demand. It is rejected and there is a small FL that led to the final push down. It gets eaten on its way to 4 again but I'm not sold on a trade here unless we get really close to the base low as the R:R is bad for the first target.

6: With this engulf 5 becomes the new base. 4 isn't a fresh zone and the DP to break the zone was only OK. It also creates a stacked flag so we could look for longs here on return depending on approach and PA. The last Flag before the engulf of the flag limit gets tested twice before the trip to the sweet FTR at 7. So we make a note of this.

7: We're expecting the move off this FTR as its fresh and its Les Paul's sweet one. i.e. The first one generated after an engulf of the last leg up. We're ping ponging (happens when we're trapped in a PAZ until one of the limits gets broken) so I'm only looking for nice PA confirmation trades as zones are getting used up fast.

8: We get a vicious bar down from 7 and even an engulf of a low but we fail to engulf that rotten flag that seems to be stubbornly holding price up. There is no room down as flags are stacked until 11. So I'm waiting.

9: Price wanders on up with some zeal to 9. This is 2TB to the original supply zone but FTB to 2 after an engulf which makes this the base of the last leg down and probably an origin on a HTF. Hey its 5:00 somewhere right so lets trade. Well what have we got. We've had an engulf down into HTF (assumption) so supply may have to be removed here before price can continue up. The approach is good (running out of steam slightly compressed). We have a QM from 2. My desired setup isn't really here on this TF. We have some of the pieces and after the spike down it gives us an opportunity to enter at the cap but it has met its target FL @10 and it didn't really engulf it so price may want higher (I'm not a senior yet so I can only read at my level). So I pass on this one.

10: I inform George Bush I was left behind. Price now eats this FL and compresses down to 8 where it is held up again. We are suspicious of longs as the next fresh level is still 11 below.

11: It spikes down to 11 and jonts up to the tip of our compression to test it. You could argue that 11 is the sweet FTR for this leg up and if PA is evident you could take a risk for a trade up to the top of compression. This is made trickier on further observation as it appears that we are compressed right down to the base if you include the stacked flags on the initial move up. We know that compression vacuums price so we haven't reached the target yet.

12: We race up to 12, flag just before it (which becomes the DP to break 12), break 12 and flag again (which becomes the DP to continue up to 13) Why did this move happen? Well it appears compressed down from 9 with only one real supply pocket which is acknowledged briefly on the way up.

13: We are coming off great strength but are showing weakness to the fresh supply @13. I can see my implied engulf cap retest trade here. We have a compressed move up, the big red doji eats the compression and misses our first target. Go short at the retest of the cap supply. Now we're aware that price may only want the next fresh (demand/flag/FTR/flag limit) but we have an ace up our sleeve. This move that confused us (well at least it confused me on my first attempt to explain it) may be trying to trick us as our compression target was not met. So that means this welfare 1:1 possibly 2:1 trade has the potential to be a spanking test of the origin of compression. If that doesn't make us sit up and take interest we are in the wrong gig:).

14: We hit our measly first flag and then compress up away from it (we suspect what this means given the current context weak buyers) and it then blows downward forming a flag @ 11 compressing nicely into a FTB to demand. We could look for longs here up to the next flag if we have PA confirmation but it is the 2TB to what I've assumed was HTF demand. However, the approach is good, our FL has already been tested once so it may be worth the risk to hold longer.

15:We've finished off our chart. We are traveling towards our HTF target and have eaten all the supplies in our way. posts.author: Eurotrash
posts.text:
Hey Hotochin,

PAZ's are for me a zone which when enetered price will want to get to the other side, be it compression, stacked supply/demand or a zone where price travelled through with very few hickups along the way.

I hope I was clear

Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

AAPL will hold a media event at the company's headquarters in Cupertino, Calif. on Tuesday, Sept. 10. At the highly anticipated event -- which will include breakfast and a presentation -- the latest versions of the iPhone will reportedly be unveiled. Specifically, attendees expect to see the iPhone 5S (the successor of the iPhone 5) with new fingerprint technology, and the iPhone 5C, a cheaper version featuring a plastic case that comes in a variety of colors. Overall, AAPL is focused on gaining more customers in Asia, where its rival Samsung Electronics Co Ltd and other Android manufacturers prevail.

On the charts, AAPL has suffered a 29.3% loss since hitting its record peak of $705.07 in late September 2012. Still, the brokerage bunch maintains an optimistic outlook. From the 38 analysts weighing in, AAPL has received 30 "buy" or better endorsements, compared to just eight "holds" and not a single "sell" or worse suggestion, leaving the door wide open for a potential round of downgrades, which could spur fresh selling pressure for the shares.

Furthermore, Apple Inc. -- perched at $498.22 -- continues to struggle to regain ground atop the psychologically significant $500 level, which is also the site of heavy call open interest in the front three-month series of options (most notably the November series). As such, this heavy accumulation of call open interest could end up translating into options-related resistance in the near term, as these bullish bets start to unwind.

Hi Merge, nice trades.

In my understanding, imbalance is where price go either way, where as
balance represent a a balance of buyers and sellers at a certain range.
thus, a doji would be a balance representing candle, or by it other name
 a none-decision candle, which may break either way.

The reason your trades are succeeding at these levels, is because of the
 decision that were taken prior to the doji/voodoo bar, were very
strong. So I would look at the decision itself, and how impulsive it is,
 rather then the form of candle of the un-decision bar/pattern....

Just my thoughts...

HI MG / thx for the compliments but trust me I am still learning
 regarding your questions about consumed , and supply filled , when a
zone is visited for the first time it will fill the remaining orders but
 if it is visited more than 2 or 3 times it will become weaker due to
the consumption of the remaining order and there is a chance to
breakthrought

Does "consumed" mean when a price touches more times the same level
without engulfing it? yes it is but when it breaks that level it means
no more orders are there so that consumed zone will become a buy zone or
 swap zone

What do they mean? Where can I find some informations? RTM is the place have a look
	www.readthemarket.com/index.php/education/markepedia

ok. fake-out: i'd like to share a note

Pedini wrote: Hey guys, thanks so much for the questions, they are great. At the moment, it is obvious that EU is in a trading range, and there have been some fake moves on either side and trapping people trading the range. I would personally choose to stay out till it resolves itself.

As for your questions, what I will do when I see an engulf is ask myself "does this engulf make sense?" By that I mean look at the history around where price engulfed. Did it engulf into a DP or a key level? Did it engulf into supply/demand. Also, look where the source of the engulf came from, was it coming from a HTF supply/demand level or has it failed yet to reach one? All these things should give you a heads up on a potential FO.

For example, if price is engulfing south, but price has yet to come off a significant level of supply, it makes sense to see a FO to help push price to higher levels. Something that looks like it may be currently happening on EU.

Anyway, I hope this gives some food for thought, it is past 2am, so excuse my lack of a detailed information/charts, I will try to find some example to post when I am well rested.

Peds

Points being: - An engulf must happen first and make sense (i.e. price engulfs a DP or keylevel, or "into" S/D) next: - The source of engulf. FO often happens when the source of engulf failed to reach the right zone (i.e. HTF S/D)

Logic: engulf first, then FO. I haven't seen any engulf that comes after FO.

Price regularly moves from decision point to decision point.

Take a look at this video to see what I mean

Homework:

This will be alot like the Read a Session Homework, except that I want you to do learn from it how to pinpoint in advance, turns in the market which will pay you very large rewards for minimal risk.

So Open a D1 chart on any pair Download as much LTF history as you can for it Start at the second price turn on the left Look to the left of it, in the lowest TF you can Work out why price reacted to that level Mark the reason on the LTF chart Take a little screenshot of that area - name it "name of pair"1 Mark the turning point on D1 with a 1 Move on to the next turning point, and repeat, and then the next. Do this for every turning point. When you're finished, you'll have a D1 chart with all the turning points numbered, and a gallery of thumbnails of the LTFs, each explaining the turns.

Do this for as many pairs as you possibly can

Believe me, it'll be well worth it!

posts.text:
Hi Oedipus,

Nice that you started this thread. DP are really important imo, I am sure that learning about it will help you a lot.

I took a look at your chart and marked a few thing. Actually I could keep on talking/writing about what happened but I do not want to confuse you. So let's start slowely...

I am trying to find the right words to explain what a decision point is to make it easy for you to understand...

So maybe this might help you a little bit:

What is a decision point: Well it's a price point on a chart where a decision has been made to take price either higher or lower

Where can I spot a decision point? You will see that new decision points take place at Unfresh Supply or Demand areas. Let's take a Supply area for example. New supply is created because of a new decision point. Now to take this supply away and break it, the big boys will need to make a decision and put lots of money in the market to take the supply out. So you will see that unfresh demand, eventually becomes Fresh Supply once it gets broken. This happens because all the demand was consumed (multiple retest of the area) and that there was finally a decision made to take price lower.

Hope this makes sence, if not let me know and I'll try to explain it beter. Best, Mel

posts.author: mettafort
posts.text:
OK here are some more breakdowns of the decisions. The realization already is that price is only ever moving from one decision point to another, and the invariant at any decision point (DP) is value. If price falls away from an area, its decided price is too expensive - this is the invariant at this level at this moment. The basis to that invariant is the amount of supply that such a DP attracts. After the decision is made, different market participants may then join in, not until, adding more supply and helping the invariant hold when price returns - RTM style trading does exactly that.

dM

The core move that we see is a move up into a space we can reason about, which is, if upwards, an DP area where it was previously decided price was too expensive. There will probably be resting limit orders, as well as active traders watching as price returns to the area. Everyone is waiting for some confluence depending on their trading modality, but at some point the supply/demand invariant holds or it breaks. So the move up happens, and the sign that price is too expensive is the engulf down. Some engulfs matter more than others it seems, and if a key DP is engulfed, price ascends in the winds of demand that it consumed, until those winds fade out and price returns to that last place where supply was overwhelming. This is the FTB trade down. And of course, the key to the DP is how the decision was made - was it timid, or was there conviction.

But the primary takeaway is that price is bouncing between decisions on value. One cannot say that its just some invariant that holds until price at a certain level in the book hits zero, because it is dropping as well as rising as the dynamics of the decisions about value play out.

MF

I probably completely botched this but here's my try at it. A lot of the turns in the weekly chart could be explained by weekly structures, but some of them needed LTF to explain it. Earlier was easiest to decipher, later on I ran into some areas I couldn't quite understand.

The big weekly picture, with explanations and inserts as I saw necessary:

1) Price hits the upper boundaries of a compression area and bounces. Price then decides to break into compression and makes it through the S/R flip.

2) Price starts to encounter demand below and bounces between demand and the S/R flip. Price then decides to break demand, with the important decision area outlined below.

3) The low here I don't really understand. To the left, there's an area of used demand but the move out of it wasn't very impressive to begin with so maybe this is one of those news driven turns?

4) Price rallies up to the decision point outlined in #2's chart and bounces, consuming the remaining orders. Price then creates new weekly demand before continuing higher.

5) Price bounces from our decision point to engulf the compression and forms weekly supply right below.

6) Bounce from demand.

7) Temporary rejection of price from supply. Price then moves up through supply. I didn't notice any specific decision points as to where it necessarily said "this supply is over with!", so maybe someone could help me out on this one.

8 & 9) Supply becomes demand, price re-tests our ignored supply and moves higher to fresh supply at 9.

Big consolidation area better explained on the daily charts with several caps on price forming. Eventually price breaks down and forms demand, rallying to form the FTR (?) in 10.

10) Somewhere in the wick to the left is our decision point to break the daily demand and go lower; upon returning here, price drops. A nice supply level is left here after failing to re-enter our previous price action zone.

11) Price ignores demand and makes a decision to go lower.

12) Price bounces from supply which wasn't consumed by the bounce at 6.

13) Price re-visits the decision point at 11 and drops.

14) Bounce from second-touch demand originating from March 8th.

15) Low of the swing turns before breaking the low of the last swing but the exact spot it moves from doesn't seem to have any significance.

16) Not sure about this one either. Price seems to be in the middle of a move where it turns exactly.

17) Price bounces from the base of our flag and forms demand.

18) Not really any specific PA to the left that would suggest a bounce here.

19 & 21) Bounces off of demand formed at 17.

20) Price bounces from the decision to go lower found on the H4 charts.

fxyogi wrote: Hi thanks.This method didnt work for me. Nobody seemed to be profitable in this. Looked like even ifmyante also not so profitable in this.I lost all my hope now.currently im thinking to give up this profession.

Harry's comment that I posted ended up in my journal because I was confused, so take heart because you are not alone. My (less than) 2 cents worth and suggestions for you: 1. Like Lupy said, treat this like an interest you're investigating right now, as if it were mountain biking, knitting, or photography, but DO NOT worry about what you do or do not understand right now or who is or is not making money - you wouldn't be worried about every detail, method, or maneuver if you were thinking about taking up biking, knitting, or photos, so the same applies here. 2. Forget terminology for now and just think of it this way: price can only go up or down, right? (It never truly goes sideways, so forget that for now.) Yes, price goes up or down. Before it goes up or down, the market makes a decision and that decision is what sends it up or down. Do not allow yourself to complicate it with terms for now! If price went up, the market made a decision. And if price went down, the market made the opposite decision. Nothing more, nothing less. 3. Perhaps you think I'm oversimplifying. OK, then disregard everything that I've said and watch this videoby If and read and reread the following words as many times as necessary until you believe it: "... decisions, that's all supply and demand is and that's all that support and resistance are. It's just decisions on the value of an asset." ~ Ifmyante in the video linked above 4. Once you've heard, read, and watched the video in #3 enough times to believe it like you believe the sun is hot, look at the charts below and keep everything simple and see if you follow as I try to "Find the Decisions" as this thread's title says. I'm trying to A. find an engulf; then B. mark where I think the decision was made to create that engulf; then C. watch what happens the first time back to the price where the decision was made. ABC - we've got this!

Post your questions, find the ABC's on your charts and know that the RTM community stands ready to help you learn but please: don't give up!

posts.author: fxdaytrader
posts.text:
There are decisions all over the chart - it does not make them tradeable or qualifies as a system.

Flips, fresh S/D. FL's, QM's, FTRs. tips of CP etc etc - yes, you will always find a reason why price turns (just keep looking left - a bit further, further...). Again, it still does not mean you will be consistently profitable identifying them.

Sometimes the decision will appear on a 1M and sometimes it will be "obvious" on a daily. Sometimes the "decision" will be 50 pips apart dependent upon the timeframe. Again - good luck making money with it. But after the event - you will look like a genius

FTB to a DP with CP on approach - yes - sounds good, but watch how many fail.

Suddenly, you realise this is a game of probabilities as much as this site and others seem to promote something far more certain. Suddenly you realise RR, trade management, HTF context, time of day, volatility, account size and other variables are much more important than this site and most give credit to.

Everyone can keep getting excited when price turns to the pip, because on a 1M there was a flip zone, but I guarantee you - it will just continue to perpetuate the retailer dream.

Just because anyone keeps posting pip precise trades (after the event of course) that just never lose, please accept that they are not showing their losers.

Of course there are many that do not have the experience to appreciate this reality and will dismiss this post, thinking I am just another frustrated losing trader. Maybe I am, maybe I am not.

But for all the losing traders here, I dare you to come back in 2 years and read this post again and tell me I am wrong.

This post is in no way directed to polymorph, and I am not suggesting that finding decisions is not part of the process, but the fascination with pip perfect entries will ultimately distract you from the real objective which is to consistently make $.

I love trading and really respect both new and experienced traders for having a go in the market, but eventually the insanity has to stop.

GL all.

Hi Nytewyre,. I noticed you sometimes marked the decision to break which is the base just before a barrier like S/R. I am giving you this information because I wasted so much time on conventional S/D trading which teaches these areas are true supply and demand. Erase that from your mind. You will even see how RTM has changed over time. What makes this place great is the fact that even IF and other Masters never sit idle with how they see the market. They adapt. You will love it here!!!

The true DPs occur seconds after the barrier is broken and it retraces. Its often hidden in the tick chart and makes for a great trap for those S/D traders who swear by peaks and valleys as true supply/demand. The less visible our DP kink the better, especially if it retraces and forms a high/low which makes for a great FO zone.
