posts.text:
In response to a pm I got this morning:

Lately I had a man-cold, and for a while during that time I'd open the chart and feel I had no idea what I was looking at.

I knew I knew the market, but there was still something inside me telling me that I wouldn't be able to read it

This wasn't upsetting at all , because I knew full well this malady would pass and I'd be back on top of it again.

This can happen to anybody, due to illness, fatigue, fear of failure, fear of success, or any number of other causes.

For a student this can be very distressing and debilitating.

But it need not be terminal. The problem is not that one's read has
gone. The loss of the read is just a manifestation of another problem in
 life.

That's why, when we lose it, we must step away from the charts, and look within ourselves to find the unresolved issues.

Once we've faced and fixed them, we can get straight back to work in a
better state than if we never had the problem in the first place

I remember when I was learning the market, I'd have these EUREKA moments, which were wonderful!

I'd think to myself "I've got it! I've got it!" and imagine that now everything I did would be perfect from then on.

But it wasn't. I'd still not be right all the time. Soon I'd get another eureka moment, and think I had it again. But no.

There are a number of lessons which need to be learned, and each helps.
After all these lessons are learned, it still takes time for them all to
 fit together.

Once they do all come together, we don't think "EUREKA". Instead we sigh, and say "I'm ready".

posts.author: Sean9henry
posts.text:
Hi IF,

After a lot of reading from this great site, I have come to a relatively
 clear thought of the concept behind the RTM way of trading. The only
thing is, I am not affirmative of it yet. I would really appreciate it
if you could help clear it up for me or comment on my thinking !

This is what I think ---

1. Use the s/d, s/r flip, ftr, etc. to identify the potential and high probability price reversal regions in a HTF.

2. As price returns to these identified zones, we switch to a LTF to
see how price reacts. In the selected LTF, after price trades to the
zone from Step 1, we wait for price to go back down or up to engulf a
significant demand or supply formed before price reached the zone, or
use the various other reaction price patterns discussed to confirm IT's
intention of taking price down or up.

3. Then, as price returns to a supply or demand formed at or near the
zone identified in Step 1, a touch trade or confirmed trade can be
taken.

4. Place the stop beyond the edge of the zone identified in Step 1;
target 1 is the next demand or supply in the LTF used, while the final
target is the original of the move to the zone identified in Step 1,
often the next demand or supply in that HTF used.

The reason you wanted us to put the puzzle pieces together instead of
handing over the golden keys is for us to accumulate the chart
experiences (screen hours), and figure out what HTF and LTF would work,
and to form the psychology to follow the plan.

Many many thanks!

Sean.

Guys,

FL is the two lines/zones that 'enclose' the flag area like a sandwich.
The bread is the limit, Not the egg inside. I remember that we must find
 setup on the edge, which in this case the 'Flag Limit' itself, not
inside the flag. The edge where the price break later become the new DP
point for price to return to. So I guess we must look at the limit, not
the flag area itself (which is mid range).

As for FTRs vs FLs, It's the same thing guys. what's become important is
 that not all FTR/FL is good for entry. It MUST break important key
levels before you can consider its value. That's my half cent.

Please kindly correct me if I'm wrong.

This is the way I see it. We have Flags, FTRs then the FL. A flag is
just a stop in momentum after an important area is broken. Our FTR is

continues in the direction of the engulf. Now our Flag Limit (FL) is
present in both the FTR and the Flag. The FL is simply exactly what its
name say it is; it's our Flag Limit. Price consolidates between the
limits. I've added a chart to show exactly what I'm saying. If I'm wrong
 on this matter, please correct me, because this subject is a very
important piece of the puzzle.

posts.author: smimon
posts.text:
Just to add my two cents. I only found RTM at the end of September.
For the first month, I was trying to "predict" what was going to happen,
 by analysing the charts down to the finest detail, and simple to say, I
 failed miserably, due to lack of experience in such things.

But does that mean I can't trade, and trade very successfully with the things taught on here? No, not at all.

My biggest strides forward came when I gave up trying to predict what
was going to happen, and just let the market show me its intentions.
Think you've spotted a level that price is going to turn at? Great, now
wait and see what happens. Got a significant engulf off the level you
want? Check again - was it really significant? Or has it just come down
to a SR flip level to continue in the way it was already going? How is
price moving? Has it shot up to your level with a single big candle? Has
 it compressed towards it? Has it proceeded up in a series of surges,
forming fresh demand levels every step of the way?

All we need to trade successfully is the ability to spot potential
turning points ahead of time, and then just wait and see what happens
when we get there. If we see things lining up in our favour, take the
trade, and set your target at the first point you can realistically
expect trouble from. Don't "expect" price to blow through several levels
 of strong supply or demand to some hollywood target.

There are plenty of pips out there, if one would just be patient, and let the market tell us what it wants to do.

Predicting huge moves, and setting POs ahead of time with pinpoint
accuracy is something I'm sure I will be able to do with 100s more hours
 of chart time, but right now, I've got more than enough tools in my kit
 with the things that are taught on here to be profitable.

Hi TinkerBelle,

I think IF's chart explained about "what's origin":

My thought is, If FTR formed after breaking key levels (not just recent
low/high), this FTR become Important. Price would respect it first,
before breaking it and aiming for the next important FTR above/below, or
 the origin.

As per Kovalenko's chart, you can see box1 is important because it break
 key SR level. Therefore, the last DP, which is the FL (red box 2) in an
 important one. When broken, the new FL/FTR (FTR 3) become significant
as well.

As for why not XYZ, instead of FTR3 in your chart, the FL/FTR3 is a
strong D zone that broke red box FL. the XYZ and B boxes you drew are CP
 zone if I'm not mistaken, as there is no clean D zone.

FTR 3 is (for me) exactly the edge of CPPAZ. If engulfed, it will slide
through even further down past your XYZ zone (I haven't check the left),
 right to the source of the move/FTR down below. But no, price can't
break the level because it's strong, and up she goes. I think it's also a
 FO because there is an engulf of the opposite FTR in box 1.

Happy weekend, everyone!

A line is not the answer.

Certainly, you may draw a line, but you must then go into the LTF to
find a DBR/RBD on the right side of the LL/HH swing which covers that

posts.author: geejay
posts.text:
Hi J9,

Sure. At point 1 on the down side, we have an engulf. The little flag on
 the left side is a decision, a decision to go higher and go back into
the M15 flag. On the way down, when this level marked by the red line in
 broken, we can say the demand was engulfed. Next price flags. It
bottoms, reverses back to the red line, then on the next wave down, it
makes a lower low. To me, that is a clear signal that price wants to go
lower. So, when price comes back to 3, to test the cap at 1, it is a
good place to go short.

And a point to clarify about QM. They do work in all timeframes, M1 up
to MON1. What I was referring to is their respective locations. We are
more interested in QM that form in historical S and D zones. So, the way
 you marked up your QM, was for a short. But I don't see any Supply zone
 there. There is supply for sure but the way I learned QM was to expect
them at higher TF supply zones (Daily Supply for example for shorts).
Perhaps the easiest is to go back to the QM article and read it again as
 that is probably clearer than my explanation.

GJ.

posts.text:
Shift the focus and importance away from trade results and focus on process.

Profit or Loss, if a trade is identified and setup properly, and
executed with proper risk management, thats a good trade. Even if it
loses money (shit happens?). But if it loses money, the focus should be
to dig deeper and see if a mistake was made or if it was a valid trade
as per the methodology taught in the program.

That will take away some of the trigger shyness. For every trader to
have 100+ winners in a row.... possible or not, the expectation can be
crippling. If you shift the focus to the process of trading,
irrespective of the results, it'll be easier for them to do what you've
taught them so well already.

Just my 2 cents

Cheers!

posts.author: Sean9henry
posts.text:
Hello Hans and aspiring fellow traders,

I have been through different trading classes, some free and some paid. I
 have also learned something out of some classes, at least when I
attended the class. I didn't become profitable after the class, but the
class sellers kept on offering additional and more advanced classes.

Most don't make money after taking the classes, but I have seen people
who honestly make money. So that is what kept me going forward. After
about 5 years in the market, looking at the chart almost everyday, not
saying reading the chart, that is IF's specialty, I can tell which
strategy makes money OVER TIME, and which won't. Of course there are
those boarder line strategies you have to have numbers to show if it
makes money. I honestly have been making some, but because after I have
made some, I become more risk tolerant and trade more aggressively by
betting bigger and taking more risky trades, I then give it back. This
is partial psychology and partial problem of using a variety of
strategies.

I can fairly say that IF's strategy works with my five years of
experience. By saying this I am not convincing you to pay for the class
or not to. Human nature determines that people to look for best return
on minimal to no "apparent" cost. So after people fully learned the
strategy and making money, they may shift their focus of life and not
visit this site any more, let alone keep on posting trades for no
return. Or their personal life doesn't allow that time commitment
anymore or any other reasons.

As I see it, IF has given the new people the most direct free approach
to be skillful (not saying profitable because of psychological barrier)
in trading, that is something very commendable! Try the internet, you
will see there are people selling indicator after indicators, among
those some make money in trading, and some don't. Some educators send
out free videos daily to say how many hundreds or thousands they make
that day in live trading, but from their occasional slips you find out
they are simulating. I suspect they record several and pick the winning
live videos to send out. Funny things is even from those videos I
learned quite a bit that helped me in trading.

If you are interested in seeing how the IF style trades work, please
visit my journal at
"readthemarket.com/~readthe3/index.php/forum/journals/2256-sean-s-journal#42927",
 I just started it and will try to put a trade out before it triggers
and then follow up to see how it turns out. I will track the overall win
 and loss based on my risk (R, can be any amount but needs to be a fixed
 % of account size between 0.5% and 2%). Keep in mind that this is
thoughts sharing not trade recommendations. To be fair to IF, I will
only put out the RTM style trades as best as I get it. Of course, if IF
doesn't mind, I can add a small amount of other traditional trading
style live trades that I look for and take with real money. I do this
because it helps me understand the human psychology behind the chart
better. I don't sell or preach anything. I just like this community that
 IF has built.

In order not to clog up IF's journal, maybe people can share in my
journal about their trading journey and experience, just for fun and for
 mutual enlightening.

Good luck!

Sean.

Hi If,

I think you theory about students "not being machines" was proven long
time ago with "The Turtles" experiment in stock trading. Where although
given strict step-by-step instructions how to trade profitably, by some
famous trader, majority of them was not able to follow it and really
trade profitably. Then the question WHY? comes to mind.

And the answer is rather simple, people have encoded in them various personality patterns and this is one of them.

So there are "procedure" people who have absolutely no problem following
 instructions and get things done and "options" people who just simply
cannot follow instructions and have to either create their own procedure
 or at least modify the one they have...which in trading with proven
system is rather fatal....On the other hand "procedure" folks have
terribly hard time creating procedures or they cannot create them at
all.. Just a small psychology lesson

Hi Smimon:

Here is my take on your diagram. When price engulfs your "more important
 FL" the logical expectation then would be a slide to the next demand
zone which is the "Less important FL" in your chart. So, for me, price
has reached its logical destination after the engulf or rather fakeout.

the price to reach the lower of the two stacked levels. The higher level
 is a prime case for faking-out. Whether you want to call the "Less
important FL" as a FL or DP is again up to you. Just nomenclature I
guess. Point is, there is pent-up demand in that area.

That area you point to was the FO level on the HTF, right before price
 fell away. On the HTF price hasnt been back here, so one thing you do
is look for the likely places where there was a clear turning point. If
 you look at IF's Nov chart you can clearly see the primary FO level
before price fell away. You want to remember that location when the HTF
 works its way out and the instrument heads back up.

Also keep in mind that IF used words like "on approach..." Thats gold.
 As price came up to that level there are some very good indicators that
 a trade was on the table. If your goal is to learn to make money, than
 I wouldnt be concerned with IF's to-the-pip entry; he's a grand master.
 For the journeymen, IMO the real focus was understanding the levels to
 be interested in when GU finally gets up to this major level, and then
be ready for any factors that are simple to monitor and identify. The
engulf was clear. the huge rally into the level was clear. A huge
rally into a major supply level. If you didnt manage to get in on
spike, the hesitation that IF mentions was absolutely worth jumping in
on in my view due to the engulf lower to the left. Added to this is
that the target was textbook....in fact I see a nice long up to supply
before taking the short back down, but thats just me.

Also pay attention to how IF got out...monitoring the moves/ reading
price. IF highlights the engulf, and the obvious question is why did it
 then make a lower low....but alas it still rises back to supply. Savvy
 trades will see there is at least 1:3 RR trade back up from this move
down, and worthy of the punt. That 1:3 actually turns into a 1:10 or so
 if the PA was being read well, back up to supply.

posts.text:
Hi Muffles, you make a very good point! Understanding this can give
us a massive leap forward in our learning curve, especially when paired
with a trained eye for spotting QM levels and important S/R. One thing I
 have noticed recently is the QM level flip, when a QM level fails it it
 actually turns in to a very well respected level on RT and even in the
future, and If we check I guarantee it will have been in the past. The
importance of how powerful S/R can been is shown in our QM levels, they
even give a tradable bounce most of the time, like in your chart. Like
you say, if the FO doesn't reach it's target then it's an engulf in to a
 new zone and we want the other side, this shows us what to expect from a
 QM level.

I am no expert but after many hours of looking at the charts I am seeing
 price for what it is, for me, there are levels of perceived value
running through the charts in every TF, these levels move up and down
but we can follow them with our flag limits and to be honest even just a
 good eye for perceived value flipping.

The more I look at the charts the more I think big money is lazy and
that is why this is so simple, I imagine big money goes like this, 'If
price is above X then it is worth Y, when it gets to Y I'll make a
decision, If Y is to expensive it is worth X, If Y is still to cheap, it
 is worth Z but no less than X'. And because big money is so lazy, these
 perceived levels of value are pretty evenly spaced, probably to the pip
 if we really wanted to take the time to find out.

I would like to take this opportunity to apologise to you IF and to be
honest the rest of the teachers and authors of the training material,
I'm not stubborn enough to not admit when I'm wrong, I went through a
period of mental turmoil, which I'm sure many of the members here have
at some point in trying to master this. The frustration was more with
myself and I didn't really have anywhere to direct it when I hit a wall,
 taking time away actually really helped me, I had to visualize the
charts in my head but I couldn't see the detail, this was the biggest
aha moment of them all and I was no where near a screen.

Anyway, I'm apologising for doubting what you have supplied here, I
would also like to give my admiration for how you have stuck with this
even through all of the grief you must receive from people. I don't
really know you but I do respect the fact you give so much, expecting
very little, if nothing in return.

I hope you manage to read this, along with every other member who may
have doubt. Trust what you see, I saw levels of perceived value and over
 layed the FTR, FL, diamond and QM on top of them, they all form on
perceived levels of value, this is how we can get out of a failed trade
at BE or better, by only trading these levels, I'm not saying it is easy
 but it works.

Thank you all for your time. I'll be getting back to my journal this week with a calm approach and self control.

Have a good Sunday all,

Robbie

I must vent my frustration, and what better place to do so than in my journal?

I started RTM for a number of reasons:

To help people become financially free

To make a group of traders who'll take over the World and give it to the people

The Blue Dot is also a part of this mission.

! had hoped that what I've done in RTM would inspire you to step out of
your comfort zone and help, in whatever way you can, to make this World a
 better place.

Only the tiniest percentage of you have been brave enough to get involved, and I take my hat off to you

The rest of you, however, have proven yourselves to be just takers.

As I see it, there are three types of person:

Takers

Givers

Sharers

The vast majority of the population seem to be takers. These people will
 forever make wonderful excuses to only look out for number one.

Then there are the givers. These poor people feel duty bound to actually take part in society.

I'd love to think there can actually be a type of person called a sharer. Someone who gives, but also gets.

But with the massive disparity between givers and takers, it seems unlikely that sharers can keep sharing without running dry!

Recently, I stated that maybe I should offer webinars and lessons as rewards for getting involved in the Blue Dot.

Since then I've had the most horrible experience:

Ono of our members is pestering me, saying that he's ready to start
bringing people to the Blue Dot once I assure him of the rewards he'll
get.

I started all this to be a part of a sharing community. Now, seeing how
little quid pro quo means to so many here, I think I'd be happy to close
 RTM to everybody but those who've proven themselves to be sharers.

To the sharers and givers reading this: You are the best people on this wonderful planet.

To the rest: Your excuses mean nothing

Have a great weekend everybody, and if you have a spare moment, ask
yourself if you're proud to hand this World to your children.

Hi Ifmyante

Many years ago I read a book by Harvey MacKay entitled "Beware the Naked Man Who Offers You His Shirt".

I lost that book, and I really don't remember much of it. But the thing I
 can't forget is the title. It makes sense to me. Everyone as individual
 must reach a level of understanding and results before trying to share
his/her ideas about something that is important.

This has been always the way I behave. I understand what Amit said
about growing first and then becoming someone who shares. Also I think
that at this moment you are asking for contributions in the form of
research and ideas.

Now, the thing is that I strongly believe each one of us must have a
personal and unique vision in life. What we must share is ethics and
values.

Also, in terms of colective knowledge and guidance, I've pictured many
times a leader as someone who is in the middle of the street, staring at
 something in the sky. Those who see him, become curious, and what they
do next is what defines the legacy of the leader: They stop watching
him, and begin to search in the sky the object that keeps that man
staring so firmly, and once they find it, they are able to evaluate what
 he was seing and why he was doing that. The fact that these people are
in the middle of the street is what make their actions evident to others
 and what inspires more people to do the same thing. But there can't be a
 permanent effect if there is nothing that attracts them to stay. Those
 who can't identify the target, will quit searching, and those who can
see it will stay as long as that object remains interesting for them.

The question now is: How can you make people stay?

At least, in my case I'm lost for the cause because in the frontpage I found this statement:Form a political party to become the government

I just can't make a commitment to follow a script that others write.
That's not me. And that is precisely what "political party" means to me.

I'm a stubborn man and I refuse to accept what I can't understand and
what I'm not ok with. So I also refuse to be "the blind guide leading
the blind."

This is the reason that I'm quiet in RTM. The discovering phase is just
for that. I'm discovering and I don't like to make others lose their
time because of my misreadings .

Anyway, I just want to thankyou for sharing your knowledge and your passion.

I hope you can achieve your goals in your project, even if I'm unable to follow that path.

posts.text:
And about the new course:

Up to now, I've taught all the complexities of the market from the very
start, so that after it's all been digested, one can easily see the
future of price.

Well, I've found that such complexity can be intimidating, and can
actually paralyse the student into not being able to understand any of
it for some time.

So, what I'll do this time is, at the very start of the course, teach
the students how to make profits without knowing all the minutiae of the
 market. Easy setups which will pay nearly every time they're taken.

I feel that if the students are making easy profits from the start, then
 the pressure to learn the finer points will be greatly reduced,
allowing them to digest it faster.

If their understanding of the market lies in the bottom dome of a
sand-timer, the worst thing they can do is try to press it down from the
 top. That just causes a blockage at the neck.

With the new method, they will hardly be paying attention to the timer at all, letting the sands fall as freely as they should.

That, at least, is my great hope for the new class

learned is

I strongly suggest that you stop trying to get more, and focus instead
on solving RTM. A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush

"engulf" the nearest opposing significant LTF FL - and then just turn in
 thin air and continue the move, and break through the HTF FL. Sure, if
you look back in chart history you will find some sort of swap - but
then you can do this ultimately for every single minor turn in the
market, and it's not exactly something you can predict.

It's making life extremely difficult - you don't know what you can
believe, and what you cannot. The best clue I have for whether it was a
real engulf or not, is how price behave afterwards.

There are 8 main currencies in the Forex market. It is possible to
calculate currency indexes for each one - but it's not a straight
average across each currency's crosspairs. Instead, the trade figures
for each currency are used, and the 5 most heavily traded opposing
currencies are used for the index weighting calculation. For example,
this is JPYX:

From these figures, you can calculate a correctly balanced currency
index for each currency. I have had these for some time now, I coded
them up in MT4 (AUDX/CADX/CHFX/EURX/GBPX/JPYX/NZDX/USDX). When correctly
 balanced, RTM style setups work exactly the same on these composite
charts - except it is an entire currency that is making a move.

Institutional money tends to flow from one currency into another, they
don't adopt a view on a single pair. For the best trades, you find
separate currencies forming opposing setups - when 2 currencies are
moving in opposite directions, the relevant crosspair totally flies.

Some brokers carry USDX and EURX, but the balancings are usually
incorrect or out of date. You can also find things like GBPX online on
some websites, but the calculation is a straight average across all
crosses. This is nonsense really, to attach the same weighting to GBPNZD
 as EURGBP when forming a GBPX index.

When used correctly, these are a massive odds enhancer. You get double
confluence by checking the 2 indexes for each cross, to see if it
supports your trade. It keeps me out of a lot of bad decisions. It also
helps keep you on the right side of the market if you always try to play
 strongest vs weakest. There's a good article here on ForexFactory about
 it
	www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=334165

In answer to your AUD question - if AUD is strong on the day, but JPY is
 stronger, the other AUD pairs will move up, but AJ will chop around at
its short zone. If JPY remains strong as AUD hits supply, then it will
drop. You quite often see this, one of the crosspairs "hanging around"
at supply or demand, waiting for the index to hit the appropriate level
before it moves off.

Here are the 8 currency indexes from today:

Yes that's spot on Gembel, that's exactly the way they should be used.
 Taking LTF trend continuations on pullbacks to FLs, based on the bigger
 picture strongest vs weakest currencies, as inferred from the indexes,
is the highest probability way to make easy pips, or even better,
getting in right at the top of the whole currency turn (although picking
 tops/bottoms is always going to be riskier somewhat).

Where a lot of currency strength indis fail, and we can do better with
them, is that in order to determine a currency's strength, they use some
 sort of moving average to determine the trend - simply "is it going up
right now, or going down right now?" We however, with our knowledge of
PA, could look at EURX and say "well, it's going up right now, but we've
 had a significant engulf south, and now we've pulled back to a QM
level, so in fact I don't think it's strong, I think it's about to
become very weak".

In this cases, we can actually hit the market on the correct crosspairs
at exactly the right moment that the crosspair is going to turn.

posts.author: Ifmyante
posts.text:
I'm way too disorganised to use limit orders!

I just open the charts from time to time, and if I see the ITs scaring
the retailers into closing good trades at a good level, I enter.

I'll take off some of the position at the first target, so if my stop
gets taken I can profit overall, then watch PA level by level. If price
doesn't get into a big zone quickly, I'll usually get bored and go flat,
 having made enough to cover my next week's expenses.

If I were truly meticulous, I'd treat my exits the same as my entries,
and trade up and down all day, but trading is usually way down on my
to-do list

ShadowPit wrote: bobyv - I think you need to upload the chart with your additional markups to make sense of what you're asking

The short answer to your question is Demand exceeded Supply at a level you have not drawn. My observations in black.

Some general feedback using the chart for illustration:

Be cautious with creating too higher expectation from one engulf or one observation
 you make. Trading requires consideration of multiple sources of
information which may come from other time frames as well.

Be careful not to expect price to make higher highs or lower lows, just
because you identified an engulf of a level (note obstacle 1 & 2).

Pay special attention to the QM level drawn on the chart, the level is
more than a singular horizontal line, if you want to use just a single
line, draw it under the lows of the "1" and "2".

The QM level held price up on 4 occasions! On the 2nd, 3rd and 4th
occasion it made a higher high on this timeframe. There was no engulf of
 this zone, therefore you cannot rely on your expectation that price
would go any lower than this zone at any stage of your analysis.

In fact if you look on from point "4" the simple observation that no
supply was holding price down and new demand was being created would
tell you that a sell off was highly unlikely.

Also last but not least, let's just say you did enter a touch trade
short based on your assertion that price engulfed the low you have
identified, you have obstacle #1 immediately below you, reducing your
probability of success.

Hope this helps.

posts.author: ShadowPit
posts.text:
boby,

First:

To me A&C have nuanced differences: C is a clean looking DBR, it
sits above a key level (resistance becomes support), it isn't
compressed, it moves cleanly away AFTER the break of a key level (strong
 imbalance). A doesn't have the same characteristics, it is a compressed
 move, it doesn't sit on top of a key level, it sits underneath a recent
 high, it is BEFORE the break of a key level, it does however have an ok
 move out of the level which eventually runs into the HTF supply
extremes without retracement to a demand level, which C does not have
this characteristic.

Onto the move up:

B is the supply (DBD) that caused the break of C (DEMAND) which sits at a
 key level. C could have just as easily bounced price back up, but it
didn't.

D does not have this same characteristic, it breaks nothing of
significance, it only extends the move lower into demand, and is very
promptly broken.

Having said that, strong imbalance of price is implied at both B and D
until price tells us otherwise and you cannot presume that price will
break either until it does.

In this case, D is broken without any retracement so we look to B if it
can hold price down, but it doesn't, which can only mean price has paved
 the way for higher prices.

As buyers flood the market, sellers are either trapped and wanting to
get out as close to their failed entries (at B and D) as possible or
face being stopped out. (this is the psychological makeup of the market)

Price will now look higher to find better supply, price will go higher
from most RECENT _fresh_ demand if it can, which happened to fall at the
 break of D (remember the imbalance has now been flipped). This is the
origin.

Remember, the break of D is the source of breaking D AND B, surely a
stronger imbalance of price compared to if it was only the source of
breaking D and NOT B.. Even better is that this origin is in CONFLUENCE
with the original KEY LEVEL (C) which is textbook perfect S/R which is
where you always want to be placing your trades.

Hope this helps.

Ifmyante wrote:

question about your thinking proces. Can you please tell me if this was
the reason for you?

Why you didn't marked end of CP where my blue line is?

And this is my answer. CP was ended there and price made a FL (the blue
one). After that price tested that FL (you see it tested the MPL of it)
it made another FL (the green one). Since the blue one was taken out,
the green one its the valid target for that PAZ. So, you can short the
source of the move down which is in the green FL. After price hit the
green FL (source of the move down) It made another FL (the brown one).
So the source of the brown FL can be shorted.

And now, the targets.

Thank you so much IF! :)

posts.author: Ifmyante
posts.text:
Whenever I post here, I get messages asking will we be opening the academy again.

I have no definitive answer to that, I'm afraid.

It seems that teaching everything I know has a great effect on some
students' trading in a short time, but for others it takes years, or may
 not happen at all.

We're all so different, that some make absolutely perfect entries and
exits, while others' trades seem utterly arbitrary, like they've never
been taught anything at all!

When I retell a lesson, it's often received as if I'd never told it before, and it seems to be soon forgotten again!

So far, I estimate that only between 20-30% of students have really
gotten it. I know the rest can get it too, but they'll need to exorcise
their demons in order to succeed.

So, to answer those messages:

You're welcome to apply for a place in the academy if

you're ready to put between six months and three years into transforming nurture into nature

you can usually retain lessons you've been taught

you can already adhere to strict money management rules

your loved ones will give you the time to do this, without putting pressure on you to succeed

I'll interview each applicant in due course, to assess (hopefully
correctly!) whether they have a good chance of success, and if we get
enough applicants with the right stuff, I may open the doors again. It'd
 be great to have some new voices in the trading room

posts.author: Ifmyante
posts.text:
I've just been reading Deenius' journal, where I found the answers to
pretty much every question I could ever be asked, so I'm stealing his
fine work and putting it here

deenius wrote: Ok, I would like to restart my journal with my favorite Ifmyante quotes. I think, it is really important stuff.

Ifmyante quotes

If the signal is given by the market mover (an engulf into a new
 zone), then price is very unlikely to break the extreme of the zone it
just came from. So, if you have the patience to wait at the last
remaining set of unfilled orders in the origin, you can be almost
certain that that price will be respected.

There is absolute order in the market. Nothing at all there happens
by chance. That's why it's so easy to read what's going to happen next.
There are rules which are strictly followed; so much so you'd imagine
it's all run by algorithms, up to the moment when the signal is decided
upon, and straight away thereafter. There is zero chaos in the market.
It's elegantly designed; a beauty to behold.

Fakeouts are extremely easy to predict. Most SD traders still look
directly left, which is the big shortcoming of Supply/Demand trading.
It's further left again we should be looking.

Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that
 supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the
extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell
short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders. Extremely
 simple stuff.

We always look to what S or D are reactions to, rather than just S or D themselves.

Look for tricks being played on approach to a place where a trick was played, and you'll find where price will turn.

If you can look beyond S/D, you'll see that the Flag Limit is the only true place to look for PA for a trade. Trade these levels and you're taking gambling out of your method.

All we can ever hope for is a bounce at these levels, unless we are
certain that this level is the deepest possible point of retrace after a
 previous engulf. Without that, we must watch PA as it develops, both
before and during the trade. Set and Forget trades can only be taken
once the signal is given and the target is clear.

Being patient is absolutely vital for making giant trades. We must
wait for the very best possible places before we enter; the places where
 you'd expect great PA to react.

If you're around to watch the PA unfold, it's rare your stop should
get hit. Price will so very often retrace enough for you to get out
without a loss. That's why I wait for the very best price to TT - it
tends to keep me in the black.

I'm not even a part time trader now, so I miss nearly every piece of
 action there is. If I ever open the charts and see a trade opp right in
 front of me, I take it. However, I usually get between 10R and 25R per
trade. If I lose, it's usually no more than the spread and commission.
There are between 5 and 20 such confirmed trades available every day.

First of all, we need to understand that time has no place in any
read of the market. The only way to be completely sure of where a FL is,
 is to be there when the break occurs, and mark the highs and lows as
they occur. Within a minute they can be obscured by a candle, but we'll
know exactly where they are. If we're not there to watch and mark, we
must use the full candle as a FL.

If we've had an engulf and are getting in on a RT, we must always be
 ready for a diamond to occur, especially if price hasn't yet hit MPL of
 the zone the original bounce was a reaction to. So, if we're not going
to be around to watch PA, our stop must be beyond the original FL.

Funny you should say that, as I teach to always and only trade
within a flag. Sometimes the flag will already have developed, and
sometimes the flag is to be made while you're in the trade. Either way, always trade within a flag.

Attune yourself to what the buggers are doing, and don't let them
fool you. Just know they've got orders to fill at a level, watch them
fill some on approach (CP), see the momentum, and watch them come back
to fill more orders 'til they've had their fill.

This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading: We're
 always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at significant
areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no trade. So,
 on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in the
market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their intentions
 - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn If we don't see
this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn immediately, as
there usually won't be enough orders against them to fill all the orders
 they must fill. This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move.

When we see decent CP coming into the base of a pole, we are very
often safe to touch trade the base. The safest thing to do however is to
 await the first engulf into the cp zone as confirmation.

Very often a zone will break strongly and price will retrace but
fail to retouch it. This is still the FTR - the confirmation of a new
trend (do a study of how price reacts and how far it goes after hitting
this spot). So an FTR can be first time back, but doesn't need to be.

During holidays, volume in the market is often greatly diminished.
This would lead some to imagine that price hardly moves. But. Say
someone decided to put a truckload of orders into the market. If there's
 nobody else in the market to oppose these orders, price can do nothing
but shoot away. So remember. Low Volume can = High Volatility.

Until now I have been so unfocused on the charts that my exits have
been very sloppy. My trade plan now has a couple of variables, but
essentially I'll let price travel back to the other edge of the last PAZ
 in the TF I'm trading. If it engulfs, I'll exit on a RT or a break of
the next LTF FL. If it rejects, I'll let the trade run and await exit
PA.

It's all about getting into the mind of the market makers and trading as they do. Nothing special.

Most of my analysis comes in after the trade is entered. Before
taking the trade, I do as you said - simple - it's really easy to find
pockets of orders which will bounce price, and if they happen to be at
great htf levels, even better - there's the highest chance of them
giving maximum pips. What I do certainly looks like touch trading -
picking tops and bottoms, but what you said belies that. These are not
tops and bottoms, but retraces to the best price to re enter. Once I'm
in though, I'm never guaranteed massive returns - sure price will bounce
 where I enter, but I'm never complacent until I've seen the engulf. In
fact, I'm never really complacent at all. If PA tells me to get out, I
must get out!

Many might misconstrue us as pattern recognition traders - we're
not. Certainly while learning we look for recurring patterns in the
market. But once we understand them, what becomes most important is WHY
the ITs made them. It's paramount to understand that it's not enough for
 the ITs to simply move price. They must also get massive amounts of
orders filled in order to make maximum gains. They must also refrain
from giving other ITs false signals, which could ultimately cause chaos
for everybody. Think of these things as you study, and you'll be able to
 get into the mind of the market mover.

Here are just a few targets for price, and the QM level is a big
one. Certainly we need to get PA for entry before or once it's hit.

If it breaks, then the same level can have the opposite effect on return.

Once price engulfs a level, all that's important is how far it
retraces before hitting its target. While the pockets of orders remain
in this RT, it remains strong. If price totally compresses (picking up
all orders) forward from the tip of the RT, then we will look primarily
for the orders at the entrance to said CP.

To the ITs, candle closes don't mean a damned thing, so please don't use them in your own analysis.

A line is not the answer. Certainly, you may draw a line, but you
must then go into the LTF to find a DBR/RBD on the right side of the
LL/HH swing which covers that line. That RBD/DBR will be your box. You
can scalp from each of these, knowing that it may only be a scalp. If
you're simply setting a PO, then you must set your stop beyond the FL
the HH/LL is a reaction to.

The usable engulf is the one which hasn't hit its target. Every engulf has a very specific target.

Apply that statement to your charts and eventually you'll see what I mean.

Being only a sporadic trader (I really couldn't sit and watch the
charts all day anymore!), I tend to open the charts from time to time
and ask myself what's coming up in the next few minutes for me to take.
If I'm lucky, I'll open the charts when we're at an HTF level. If not,
I'll gladly take whatever high R M1 or whatever is there for the
picking. 30 pips with a 3 pip stop is exactly the same as 150 pips with a
 15. If there's nothing decent to take, I shut the charts.

If I were asked where to trade, in one word, I'd say: Stops

I'm way too disorganised to use limit orders! I just open the charts
 from time to time, and if I see the ITs scaring the retailers into
closing good trades at a good level, I enter. I'll take off some of the
position at the first target, so if my stop gets taken I can profit
overall, then watch PA level by level. If price doesn't get into a big
zone quickly, I'll usually get bored and go flat, having made enough to
cover my next week's expenses. If I were truly meticulous, I'd treat my
exits the same as my entries, and trade up and down all day, but trading
 is usually way down on my to-do list.

Certainly there's an awful lot to learn here. But if I were to
summarise what I think is most important, I'd say look to an engulf into
 free space that hasn't yet hit the origin (tg). Very often it will
retrace deeply before advancing to the origin. Learn to spot these, and
you'll be better equipped than most other traders out there.

Price moves from PAZ to PAZ. The clear target for any trade after an
 engulf is the other end of the PAZ in that TF. If you zoom out to HTFs,
 you may find the TG is even further, but if not, stick to the TF you're
 in.

I just want to warn you though that watching candles is an absolute
waste of time. It distracts you from reading the story of price. The
chart is a page, and a candle is a word. A word in itself has little
meaning; it can be taken out of context. Sure, a sentence can be very
powerful, as can a group of candles. But to get a real sense of the
story, we need to view it all as a whole - be aware of how this
paragraph relates to one many chapters back, and get a sense of where
the story will lead in the future.

In essence, we know that if price engulfs South, it wants to move down to the last engulf North.

We want to read the story of price, and believe me, price has a
story! You'll need to go further left to get your analysis right. Yes,
you've marked levels well, but what are those levels a reaction to?
Without knowing this, you're just gambling. So, look left, read the
story, and be better equipped to predict what'll come next.

Ask yourself "Why did price shoot up from there?" You'll answer
"Because someone wanted to buy a lorryload, but there was nobody willing
 to sell at that price, so price shot up to find sellers." The next
question you'll ask yourself is "Will he have left orders to buy again
at that price?" The answer is usually "yes". Next question is "will
price reverse from there?" The answer is, "Well, it may well bounce form
 there, but we won't know if it'll reverse until an engulf tells us it's
 reversed"

Of course, the extremes in one TF can be midrange in another TF,
which is why it's vital to manage your adds in the lower TF until they
break into HTF trades.

Okay! One giant clue: If something which should have been important got ignored, then it will be given great import on return.

Personally, I love to dissect the HTF zone, in LTF, and look for a
DBR or RBD within it, where price had broken out of a box and failed to
get back in.

Whipsaw engulfing - a fakeout followed by a quick return breaking the last zone. It's great PA.

An excellent Supply or Demand zone is one where the future has
already been written. Having done some study of the markets, we know
that once we have an engulf of a zone, price will want to go to the
origin. So we look to where the trend change was confirmed - FTR.

You must study the zone which is being reacted to just as much as the reaction itself.

Just consider the manipulation of hope and fear at turning points, and you'll have a very valuable eureka moment.

When you begin to see the symmetry in the market, you're making one of the final steps in reading and predicting it.

High R is High R, and these trades happen with great frequency. I
applaud this easy way of making good money. If you're at the MPL of an
HTF level, however, think about taking enough at LTF tg1 to cover the
HTF stop, and letting the trade run.

A bit of simple advice, to avoid overtrading and impulse trading:
Draw up the most important looking zones, and look for trades only
there.

We absolutely must have an hard stop, always. But if we don't
 have an engulf before entry, we don't put it directly above the high or
 below the low, where all the retail stops lie. Instead, we find a
lovely LTF RBD/DBR just beyond, and put it on the other side of that, so
 that we have the best chance to get out at BE or in big profit from the
 usual RT.

There's no indication that a demand has been respected until the source above has been engulfed.

Flags/Poles

FTR (actualy the same as above)

Support/Resistance breaks (I hope you noticed by now that FTR is the precise science of this!)

PAZ (Same thing again!)

the unified theory of market dynamics, and you'll be astonished at how
simple the market is to read. You'll actually be able to boil it down
to; If X, then Y

off certain checklists for a trade in the right place.

What I've decided to do is teach exactly how to take these trades in a
very methodical fashion; where to enter, where to place stops, and where
 to take profit.

These courses will be far less expensive than the academy, but almost as valuable.

because they know how to get in at the tops and bottoms, long before the
 new crew enter.

In RTM, I've mostly focused on reading the market rather than trading it. Here's where that changes!

posts.author: akongb
posts.text:
This is the syllabus of RTM academy.After doing your homework you
should able do all the checklist below.Just for thought and thank you IF

The RTM FTTP syllabus

Price movement

Objectives:

Learn the simple ways ITs move price and the reasons behind why they do what they do

Learn the common mistakes retail traders make and how this is beneficial to ITs

Understand how stop hunting helps fill orders

Candles

Objectives:

Define commonly traded candles

Learn the common misconceptions about trading candle patters/individual candles

Learn how conventional stop placement on trading candle patters/individual candles can kill your account

Learn what candles mean depending where they form

Real Price Action 1

Objectives:

Define supply/demand and understand that SD traders are subjected to the same tricks as everyone else

Define support/resistance and learn how it can be such a powerful tool when used properly

Demonstrate your understanding of poles and flags. Define the strict rules on what makes a pole and what makes a flag (key)

Real Price Action 2

Objectives:

Demonstrate an understanding of the continuation engulf (key)

Demonstrate an understanding of the reversal engulf and where to look for it (key)

Identify and demonstrate an understanding of the FL and the circumstances in which they form (key)

Real Price Action 3

Objectives:

Critically evaluate the IF/Then rule and all its implication. Be able to identify it in a live market

Demonstrate an understanding of how different sized FL interact and how these interactions effect price movement (key)

Learn to use the multi-TF FL Compass to stay on the right side of the market at all times

Understand the max pain level in implied flags (key)

Investigate flag completion and evaluate how price can move in order to complete a yet to be completed flag (key)

Demonstrate the absolute essentials of Price Action

posts.author: Ifmyante
posts.text:
That's a really good and important question.

The issue you raised can be the difference between success and failure.

I've just finished a webinar with the Academy. We discussed the same
stuff we discuss in every webinar, yet the attendees still seemed to get
 a lot out of it.

This means that for many, learning comes from repetition.

Now, when we talk in the Academy, we can be talking about one topic, yet
 we remain mindful of all the other topics which have an influence on
price.

It can take years to be able to see it all at once. Some get it in a couple of months, sure, but for most it's a long journey.

The Academy Lite is made to be different.

Let's use a metaphor.

We want to make a cup of tea.

In the Academy, to do this, we teach about the electricity which powers
the kettle, the specific heat capacity of water and metal, the bimetalic
 strip which turns off the kettle, the latent heat of vapourisation of
water, how tea is grown, distributed, sold and stored, everything about
milk, sugar, etc.

In the Academy Lite, we'll teach how to fill a kettle, let it boil,
throw a teabag into a cup, pour water and add milk and sugar to taste.

Both can achieve exactly the same results. It's just that one gives a greater understanding of the process.

So, for the beginning of the lesson, all charts will be hand drawn. But we'll then move on to real chart based examples.

I've kept the drawing of levels as simple as possible, so that a trading system can easily be formed.

This means that students will have more losses than the Academy
students, sure, but our money management lesson will make sure that
overall profits can easily be made.

So, if you want to know the basics of how to make a perfect cup of tea, this is the place to go

Disclaimer: We will not be teaching how to make tea, but let me say that Earl Gray with milk and two sugars is absolutely lovely

Characteristics of Capitalism

Throughout its history, but especially during its ascendency in the 19th
 century, capitalism has had certain key characteristics. First, basic
production facilities—land and capital—are privately owned. Capital in
this sense means the buildings, mach ines, and other equipment used to
produce goods and services that are ultimately consumed. Second,
economic activity is organized and coordinated through the interaction
of buyers and sellers (or producers) in markets. Third, owners of land
and capit al as well as the workers they employ are free to pursue their
 own self-interests in seeking maximum gain from the use of their
resources and labor in production. Consumers are free to spend their
incomes in ways that they believe will yield the grea test satisfaction.
 This principle, called consumer sovereignty, reflects the idea that
under capitalism producers will be forced by competition to use their
resources in ways that will best satisfy the wants of consumers.
Self-interest and the pursuit of gain lead them to do this. Fourth,
under this system a minimum of government supervision is required; if
competition is present, economic activity will be self- regulating.
Government will be necessary only to protect society from foreign
attack, uphold the rights of private property, and guarantee contracts.
This 19th-century view of government’s role in the capitalist system has
 been significantly modified by ideas and events of the 20th century.

Hi guys, I'm posting this to Ifmyante journal because there is highest
 chance that most people will see it, especially newbies. And I feel
it's very important. Until now when studying I've always tryed to
analyse all charts multi TF, so I can see what zones did before, and in
lower TFs too.

Well, here's the problem. Data feed on demo accounts is so often
incomplete and misleading. I have demo accs on like 5-10 different
brokers and they mostly have same bullshit data. Then I tryed same
broker with real account(3 of those actually) and data is very often
vastly different, especially on LTF. I found out that on at about 20-40%
 of charts studyed on demo have misleading data.

I urge everyone using demo accounts for price analysis to do it on real
accounts, it will benefit you greatly and maybe save you some time
scratching your head as If once said.

Hope this will help someone.

PS dont use metaquotes also, bad data feed

IF

by Rudyard Kipling

If you can keep your head when all about you

Are losing theirs and blaming it on you,

If you can trust yourself when all men doubt you,

But make allowance for their doubting too;

If you can wait and not be tired by waiting,

Or being lied about, don’t deal in lies,

Or being hated, don’t give way to hating,

And yet don’t look too good, nor talk too wise:

If you can dream—and not make dreams your master;

If you can think—and not make thoughts your aim;

If you can meet with Triumph and Disaster

And treat those two impostors just the same;

If you can bear to hear the truth you’ve spoken

Twisted by knaves to make a trap for fools,

Or watch the things you gave your life to, broken,

And stoop and build ’em up with worn-out tools:

If you can make one heap of all your winnings

And risk it on one turn of pitch-and-toss,

And lose, and start again at your beginnings

And never breathe a word about your loss;

If you can force your heart and nerve and sinew

To serve your turn long after they are gone,

And so hold on when there is nothing in you

Except the Will which says to them: ‘Hold on!’

If you can talk with crowds and keep your virtue,

Or walk with Kings—nor lose the common touch,

If neither foes nor loving friends can hurt you,

If all men count with you, but none too much;

If you can fill the unforgiving minute

With sixty seconds’ worth of distance run,

Yours is the Earth and everything that’s in it,

And—which is more—you’ll be a Man, my son!

posts.author: jsr
posts.text:
This video is for those who think that struggling is a sign that you can't do this,

As someone implied, all what we need is a simple shift in our mindset.

These are some nuggets:

So how do we learn?

And why does some of us learn things more easily than others?

every time you learn a new fact or skill, you change your brain. It's something we call neuroplasticity.

So your brain can change in three very basic ways to support learning:
So neuroplasticity is supported by chemical, by structural, and by
functional changes, and these are happening across the whole brain. They
 can occur in isolation from one or another, but most often, they take
place in concert. Together, they support learning. And they're taking
place all the time.

all of our behaviors change our brain. these changes are not limited by age,

The primary driver of change in your brain is your behavior, so there is
 no neuroplasticity drug you can take. Nothing is more effective than
practice at helping you learn, and the bottom line is you have to do the
 work. And in fact, my research has shown increased difficulty,
increased struggle if you will, during practice, actually leads to both
more learning, and greater structural change in the brain.

You've had the experience of getting better and better within a single
session of practice, and thinking "I have got it." And then, maybe you
return the next day, and all those improvements from the day before are
lost. What happened? Well, in the short term, your brain was able to
increase the chemical signaling between your neurons. But for some
reason, those changes did not induce the structural changes that are
necessary to support long term memory.

Remember that long term memories take time. And what you see in the
short term does not reflect learning, It's these physical changes that
are now going to support ong term memories, and chemical changes that
support short term memories.

The uniqueness of your brain will affect you both as a learner and also
as a teacher. This idea helps us to understand why some children can
thrive in tradition ducation settings and others don't; why some of us
can learn languages easily and yet, others can pick up any sport and
excel.

So when you leave this room today, your brain will not be the same as
when you entered this morning. And I think that's pretty amazing. But
each of you is going to have changed your brain differently.
Understanding these differences, these individual patterns, these
variability and change is going to enable the next great advance in
neuroscience; it's going to allow us to develop new and more effective
interventions, and allow for matches between learners and teachers, and
patients and interventions. And this does not just apply the recovery
from stroke, it applies to each of us, as a parent, as a teacher, as a
manager, and also because you are at TEDx today, as a lifelong learner.
Study how and what you learn best. Repeat those behaviors that are
healthy for your brain, and break those behaviors and habits that are
not. Practice. Learning is about doing the work that your brain
requires. So the best strategies are going to vary between individuals.
You know what, they're even going to vary within individuals. So for

Who will not be able to understand the market?

The market is an herd, putting in cash.

The cash goes straight back to the people who created it out of nothing and loaned to them in the first place!

So, to understand the market is to understand the herd (of cash cows, in this case).

Can anybody in the herd understand the market?

People who understand the herd, leave the herd, so the answer is "yes, but only for a split second!"

So, if you want to know whether you'll be a great trader, simply ask yourself:

Do I believe in gods?

Do I believe in governments?

Do I believe in royalty?

Do I believe the news?

Do we have an emperor?

If the answer to more than one of these questions is "yes", then you're not ready to understand the market

IF, in answering your question, a FL limit can only be drawn after the
 TG has been hit. In this case TG (UFL) has been hit. Therefore, the
green box (LFL) is now an confirmed FL. The engulf downward is not
significant. It is just part of retracement in the creation of the LFL
(green box). The LFL (green box) is just the left shoulder, assuming
that price does not break above the UFL and decides to come down and
engulf the green box. So, we now have to wait for price to come down
from the TG (UFL) and engulf the LFL (green box) for PA. Otherwise, if
price continues going up and break above the UFL, the green box is just
another LFL.

Staurum, try to make it simple. For example, think about FL as a
retracement in price. How do you know when that retracement is over?
Answer, it is over when price hits the next FL to its left. That is
where orders are left waiting there to be filled (in the next FL).
After it hits the FL to its left (where orders are left waiting to be
filled), then you can say, the retracement (FL) is confirmed and we can
now draw a box around it. And we only look for FLs that are
significant. The significant ones are the ones that engulfed a FL to
its left. Otherwise it is not important.

Hi Guys.

Just back from a business trip, trying to recap your posts.

During these days I thought about our discussion here and I think I could risk to overcomplicate and over analyzing things.

So I thought I share here my latest considerations, of course ready to accept any comment and/or different point of view.

Actually what we learn overall in this great forum is to read Price Action, and take advantage from that Edge.

And what is Price Action ?

Or a Price Action Zone ?

It is Price moving in a way to "prepare" a later decision.

For this reason Price Action is what happens between two DP.

In a CP PAZ, for example, Price can decide to go back and fill it or shoot in the opposite direction.

Also in this case the two extremes of this zone will be important on return.

At those points Price will either bounce or show a new Decision: EG

The Engulf tells us that Price violated "Structure" and changed "Trend" until the next Structure level to be retested.

The next DP

It is like Trend Structure. Bullish, Bearish or Sideway.

A trend is not anymore such, as soon as its structure gets violated.

A PAZ is completed as soon as it achieves its next Limit (DP or FL) and confirms or negate the move to the next one.

That's my "Thinking about Price".

And Clouds are getting sharper to a clear Image.

With all the chats I'm in, I have lots of catching up to do, and I don't remember in which chat I said what!

I'm glad there's a lot of discussion in here, as I know where my journal is!

I want to answer a question I get asked a lot:

"In which timeframe do you trade?"

There's no need to trade timeframes.

Just trade high R instead, which could be on any scale.

If price is at a nice weekly SR kink, which is only a few pips wide, or it's at the MPL of a larger kink, await M1 PA.

If there's space in that TF to get >1R to the M1 approach kink, then
take the trade, closing enough at tg1 to cover your stop, then allow
price to either hit the weekly approach kink (watch PA there to see if
you should close all or allow to run) or your stop.

That's absolutely risk free trading!

posts.author: Edge
posts.text:
I tend to agree with GGJJ that any entry needs to be at a clean set of
 orders with the SL above the entire UFL or LFL being reacted to.

That being said, I also agree with Linos that the BSZ does not seem to
require PA (engulf into space) and the BSZ TG needs to be at the kink of
 the 2DT or 2DB which is often in the body of the flag.

The reason for this is because the other types of trades rely on a
UFL/LFL being engulfed into space and the TG is the opposing FL.

So based on this I would think the following statements may be correct about BSZ:

-	More frequent than the trades based on EG PA

-	Tend to have less R than trades based on EG PA and;

-	The win rate may be slightly lower than trades based on EG PA

Only my two cents. Usual caveats apply

posts.author: Atari
posts.text:
HCDE,

I recall IF answering another student about the same question you had on
 "I have a very very hard time finding space, engulf not hitting its
target.". Yes, we need to find space otherwise, there is no trade. If
it was easy to find space, then everyone would become a successful
trader overnight. The ITs will not make it easy and obvious.

Trading is based on your preference and your comfort zone and your
confidence in your analysis. There are master traders who take touch
trades and take confirmation trade. It all depends on the trade itself.
 First, I would suggest you get comfortable with confirmation trades
before jumping to touch trade. Confirmation trades will provide you
more winners and put money in the bank for you. It will also build
your confidence. Touch trading can be tricky, so you need to read the
market correctly.... . You need to know if the level it is reacting to
is the true supply..... you need to know how it reacted when it reached
that level....., for example did price impulsive move away from that
level and engulf an important FL to its left without hitting TG. If so,
 you have PA.. Now you want to see how price is retracing and
approaching your entry point.(in this example, I am describing a
QM)...... is it compressing, is it compressing and then a final
impulsive move to your entry level....These are the questions that you
need to answer. The 1/2 page on article on price reading in Marketpedia
speaks it all. So, I would recommend you reading it over and over again
 until you truly understand. If you have any question, then you can
post them and other students will help answer.

Here is a quote from IF. " The longer I trade, the fewer trades I
take. If it's not begging to be traded, I am not interested. There are
 lots of dead certain trades out there, each offering great returns.
These can easily be missed while sweating the outcome of marginal
trades."

direction. I keep my pairs to a maximum of 4. This helps me focus and
maximize my entry. Otherwise, I will end up missing the big trades.

posts.author: Edge
posts.text:
Hi Bobby,

I hope you dont mind. Here is my take on the BSZ. IF, can correct me. I
 may have posted this before so please forgive me for being repetitious.
 Lets take the below scenario for example.

I know its only a diagram (ignore the terrible R), but sometimes they
work better for the concepts before applying to the charts.

We have a BSZ, but we also have a engulf into space. The problem is
though we dont know if the engulf is reacting the OF from A. (eg: would
like to see A retested before the engulf). So for me in this case, there
 would be a opportunity for a BSZ trade, as I am not relying on PA.

the BSZ is a area for the ITs to get their liquidity. Its the FL where
we are looking to trade. not the BSZ itself. Its just another trap. the
BSZ itself is a indication the ITs are tricking and creating liquidity
for themselves before price turns We have to ask ourselves if we dont
have a opportunity for ITs to get their liquidity on the approach we
should be cautious.

The BSZ is often a quick scalp with lower R (not all the time).
Furthermore, because we are not relying on the EG but rather the trap
(ie: two or more highs/lows) it seems like a TT which may also have a
lower win rate than a PA trade. I also like to see clean orders in the
FL we are leaning on.

In regards to your point in your question to IF , for me I like to look
for a good FL (has to be a UFL/LFL for me and confluence with a LS),
having multiple highs/lows lining up prior to the FL (not within the FL
on that scale but before the FL in no mans land). entry at a nice set of
 orders within the FL, SL beyond whole FL and just ride it back to the
kink of the BSZ.

It may not directly go to your question but I hope it helps. IF/H/M you
know the deal, should I be wrong please give me a kick in the arse.

What you're doing now, is trying to force the sand through the neck of the sand timer. This can't work.

So, get away from it long enough for it to settle itself in your mind.

Don't look at a chart of forum post for a week, a month, three months if necessary (everybody's different).

posts.author: Manu
posts.text:
Ok, I will try too.

I see the symmetry as floors of a building where the price goes from one
 to another. Imagine that the price is a ball. A ball may bounce upward
on the floor or down on the ceiling of a floor. But this ball also has
the ability to cross the floor or ceiling if given circumstances.

The rule is that the ball will only bounce (if it does) on the floor or
ceiling of the floor where it is at the moment (not in the space between
 them wich is the floor itself), and if it crosses for example the
ceiling and goes upstairs, the inertia will take it to the roof of that
new floor (target). Then it could bounce there or cross that roof at
first touch and move to the next floor. That is, if the price comes from
 below, the ceiling of new floor to which it accedes will be the target

Let's see the chart:

The price (ball) reaches the roof of the first floor and does not
bounce, it crosses. We have left the first floor behind and we are
already on the second floor. What happens here? The price begins to
rebound on the roof and the floor several times until finally it crosses
 the ceiling and goes to the third floor. The price has already left the
 second floor and will not be able to cross it back until it reaches the
 roof of the third floor (target).What do we have on the second floor? A
 FLAG. Which are its limits? The floor and ceiling of the second floor.
Floors and ceilings are FLs and can be FTRs, S/R, etc, too. I supose
that at he left the ceilings and floors are respected, too.

What happens on the third floor? Reaches the ceiling and directly
crosses (line 3) to the fourth floor, so it must go to the ceilong of
that new floor (target). What happens on the fourth floor? The ball
(price) bounces a couple of times on ceiling and floor and crosses the
floor returning to the floor below (third floor).

As I said before, the price can only bounce off the floor and ceiling.
As it comes from the ceiling, where could it bounce? On the floor, which
 is in turn the second floor ceiling.

And so on.

So what conclusion can we draw from this symmetry?

The price will always bounce off the ceiling or floor and not anywhere
else inside the floor. Therefore, WE ONLY MUST PLAN THE TRADES AT FLOOR
OR CEILING OF THE FLOOR IN WHICH WE FIND US. OR WHAT IS THE SAME, IN THE
 FLs, FTR, etc.

The engulf of one floor with a Flag inside will shoe us intentions to continue in the direction of the engulf.

In the future, this structure of floors will be respected and the
importance of each floor depend on what you have in the past on that
floor

PD: It is possible that everything I have said is nothing but nonsense.
And i know that my english sometimes sucks, sorry for that.

posts.author: Edge
posts.text:
Clean orders are exactly that. Where there has been no retrace to pick
 them up. Be careful, in some instances what looks clean may not be. For
 example a big pole down which looks like it has left clean orders at a
decision above, may have retraced. So get all the info possible in LTFs

To think about clean orders, turn your mind to CP. True CP (not stacked)
 acts as a pole on the opposing move because any orders have been picked
 up (for reasons discussed all over RTM).

Also, a flag may look completed in one scale, but there are often more
MPLs on tiny scales. One must adjust analysis and expectations for this

Here is my take for old Task set by Ifmyante

When i was doing the task, I was lost, but then was thinking of boxes and the way ITs think to catch all stops

I am not sure if I am correct, but seems okay to me :)

My thinking process: Supply was strong move down, therefore to fill up rest of the orders, they need buyers.

In order to do so, they cannot move the market fast, otherwise everyone
will just buy and price shoots too far - REMEMBER: For ITs to buy they
need sellers and vice versa.

Therefore from my graph:

1. I as IT moved the price slowly back up to the supply (with CP) and added SELL orders throughout the CP.

2. As the price reached the previous H & S (QM) level, i let it
stall for a while making them believe I am adding more buy orders

at the same time Sellers see Double Top pattern and are ready to sell.

3. At the supply QM level, I remove my buy orders and price moves down making Sellers jumping on the wagon.

4. I suprise them and push the price back to FO level (There are now
greedy buyers on board, and Double top sellers on board + This last push
 up to FO also invites late buyers as they believe its the start of new
"trend")

I noticed, it was easier to make this chart than reading the chart from MT4 lol... I need more practise:DD

Here's a post from Zee's journal:

zee wrote: I really thought that this one was one very decent PA. Apparently not. Comments are welcome.

It really did look like good PA.

But it seems whoever's dropping the Yen through its range is in a big hurry to get there, and is breaking the rules in doing so.

We read PA, and use it extensively for our trading. But the market is
moved by people. Most of these people we see over and over again, making
 plays from the same book all week long.

Sometimes though, a new player will dump a ton of orders into the
market; more than the ITs are willing to cover, and a level will break.

Sometimes an IT will himself make a slip and accidentally break a level.

Sometimes an IT will break a level just to mess with us lot's brains.

These events are extremely rare, but they do happen.

If they didn't happen, we could go all in on every trade, and soon find ourselves as rich as the Rothschilds!

It's due to this risk of false PA that we only risk a small percent of our accounts on any trade or set of correlated trades.

Note: Should the ITs ever change their rulebook, don't worry. I'll have it reverse engineered in no time

PinkPanter, news releases works almost exactly the opposite way most
people imagine. The big spikes that happen right before and during a
news release are rarely caused by ITs dropping massive orders and then
reversing their orders with even more massive orders the other way.
What often happens is that some IT's (since ITs trade different time
frames too) remove their orders from the market. This causes a vacuum
of orderflow where price moves to find new equilibrium. When we are
talking about a spike to supply, there was more demand than supply once
IT pulled their orders. This allows the sharp move higher to strong
supply or an area with lots of retail buy stops (because IT takes
opposite of retail). Then price falls because of overwhelming supply.

Hi If,

[/quote]

Hello HCDE, first time poster here, so please I am not trying to sound patronizing at all,
 A 'range' is typically the distance from swing high to swing low, so
when we talk about range we need to be specific about what timeframes.
In the picture IF posted, when he talked about dealers (or IT) that
needs to fill a range, he most likely refer to a HTF range as depicted
in my drawing below. So imagine on a HTF scale, price has already
established a range from A to B. So when IT bring the price back to C,
the movement from B to C is called 'filling the range'. Likewise,
movement of C to D, and then from D back to E, are all called filling
the range.

Best regards

Astro

I got two similar guidance regarding scales today. One from HCDE and one from Boby:

HCDE: I think the weight of thing is linked to what we see on
chart, i mean if a LS is seen on M10 and not on H4, then it's kink is of
 no importance. But if that m10 ls KINK is aligned with a H4 LS, and has
 clean orders, it can be of vital importance. That's how i try to assess
 targets too, i ask myself: what LS are we reacting to? Is this a target
 and on what scale? is there order flow where we are reacting? If no,
isn't it, in some way, an engulf giving indications for the next moves?
Where is the origin of the move that brought us there?

Boby: So basically the scales are correlated in a way, between
 them. So, lets say we have a nice LS kink which is on h1 TF, if we
really want to trade it, we have to find which LS from LTF is correlated
 best with HTF LS, so we look on the daily for larger LS which align
with my h1 LS. In this way we can find running trades, and that can stop
 us from trading in the middle. Another way it could be to follow FLs.
Lets say a HTF FL breaks, so price can retrace to the next FL in the
same HTF scale before it can hit the target. In this way, any of lower
TF FLs are just middle levels. Of course, i can wait for first piece of
PA to occur (in much lower TF) and after that i have again a new scale
to work with, but i can't expect the whole HTF space to be filled, as a
reaction to an LTF FL.

Then one important hint from bro Staurum: On another issue, here is what i have on my trading plan: Look out for unvisited zone for:

Generally, unvisited zone marks a higher scale trade, and therefore
higher win/loss ratio + higher R. However, its rarity is what patience
must fight for.

Visited zone, on the other hand, marks a lower scale trade and is easily
 FO-ed by the higher scale PA. Not as high win/loss ratio + not as high R
 must be within expectation because the trades are not so rare and
therefore patience required is not as intense.

I feel by thinking about the guides above and practicing into the charts, we will understand about scales eventually.

I see where you're up to in your learning, and I know that you can make
it. But you'll need to give yourself a real, stress free, chance to do
so.

The mind does a lot of processing while you're engaged in menial tasks,
making a part time job a great advantage for anybody learning the
markets.

I feel for you brother. At the start of RTM, I made myself homeless,
leaving everything behind, and for the first six months I had to double
or triple my account every month just to make ends meet. So I know the
stress you're under.

I can't ask you to keep at it, but I can say that you have a great chance of success if you find a way to earn while you learn

There's a massive difference between trading to add to your wealth, and trading to survive.

NEEDING the wins by a certain date puts massive pressure on any trader.

We don't mind if it takes an extra month to earn a nice supercar, but we mind very much a month between meals.
