I wanted to get back to the first chart FIND THE DP OF THE BREAK
 which I started my journal with and I didn't want to share initially
because I was testing the theory but I can now see it's valid so I would
 like to elaborate. I remember when I was younger I used to be very
charitable and always share what I had but as I got older I got selfish
somehow. I do share but not as much as I remember when I was younger
always sharing anything I had with my friends. In sharing this I hope I
can help others see the light and increase me wanting to share with
others more in the true spirit of RTM.

We can see so many LS and so many kinks and so many FL on the chart but
do they all have unfilled orders? Salivan's FOF concepts got me thinking
 and here is something which I think everyone could easily use. To be
able to trade we need to think like the IT and we can see their
footprint is left on the chart. Salivan has shown order flow is the key
but how to see this in the charts? There are many ways but today I would
 like to share a simple method almost mechanical which will have you
taking trades in no time. Once you see this and understand why they are
made you can then trade very easily. I have seen many people who get
into analysis paralysis and get stuck and get disheartened. I hope this
can help some of you.

We need to remember the IT need to fill large orders and they cannot do
this in one go so they must hold price. We come to know this as BSZ but
what I would like to show you today is not how to trade beyond the stops
 in the bsz but to trade the DP of of the BSZ or the decision which the
IT made to break the BSZ.

Since we can assume BSZ has been created for IT to hunt stops so there
must be a decision point where the IT say ok now we have filled lots of
orders lets go. They break the BSZ and thus hit stops and fill more of
their orders. Now we know a key factor footprint which the IT have left
on the chart. Their DP to hit the BSZ and take stops. We can then safely
 assume there are some orders still left on the FTB to this DP.

You can find this on any scale. Just keep your targets to that scale.

PS: Salivan did mention that it was very easy for him to read the
markets before the election then things changed. I wouldn't be surprised
 if eventually the IT change their way and we have to research hours and
 hours again to find the key. But one thing is for certain. FOF will
always be the key. Learn to read the chart not as boxes and heads and
shoulders but as a breathing organism which moves and is attracted to
orders which are in the market. Find where the orders are and you will
find a trade.

Thanks RTM

Thanks Salivan

Thanks IF

posts.author: Enlightenme
posts.text:
Mukhcin wrote: a loss trade...i can't find a reason of FO. and is it and eng or FO...?

It seems like you got the direction right that it is going up.

FO areas are there to trick retailers. Just like what IF implied- when ITs want to sell, they need retailers to buy.

Not all FLs work and FTB is only for those FLs that work. I used to
think that breaking important areas create a strong bounce during FTB to
 the strong FL made. However, it doesn't seem to be the case. In my
opinion, the FL reliability doesn't depend on the importance of the area
 it broke, but on the importance of the area it is in. Of course, watch
for PA.

Try watching the RTMA lite videos and the other lengthy videos. They helped me a lot. :)

-EM

In Forex trading there is much less regulation than in equities for
example. So with fewer rules, the banks will use every tool at their
disposal to take our money or in this case not allow you into a trade
that will cost them money.

During every news release they have an excuse to widen the spread. The
more important the news the better the excuse they have. If you are
executing a long position, you need to be aware that these positions are
 even harder to catch because they normally widen the ask. They do this
 because our charts print based on the bid price and it is better to
hide their manipulation.

Here is a chart of today I picked. You can see the spread goes as high
as 6 pips at times with this broker. Granted this is daily rollover
when it gets this high. However the spread increases multiple times a
day---news releases, equity market openings, market closings, slower
times, faster times, etc, etc, etc.

Now here is another chart for you. This is a screenshot I took when I got 360
 pips of slippage on USDCAD. I, of course, contacted the broker and
their answer as always is that it is not them but the liquidity
providers. Don't be fooled.

* Be aware when trading around things like Central Bank Rate announcements.

* Beware trading around end of day rollover or even worse end of week.

* Understand the more "exotic" a pair the wider the spread can go
without warning. NZD normally has higher spread than EUR and in some
cases, IT will go absolutely nuts on the spread around things like end
of day rollover.

* Recognize that long trades at fantastic areas might need an extra pip or two to get filled.

posts.author: dengaima
posts.text:
PinkPanter wrote: i have been tricked a lot of times out of great position with this spread trick...

Please help me understand this bid/ask better...

I think in scenario 1 your trade is dead the moment ask price widens 30 pips

Scenario 2 will not execute the trade

Explanation: those price is not related to your condition but other party's condition.

Bid is someone willing to pay you (when you sell)

Ask is someone willing to offer to you (when you buy)

Simplified:

When you look for SL placement. Watch out for line closer to you.

Buy execute - look out for ask line hitting your SL

Sell execute - look out for bid line hitting your SL

When setting limit orders - watch the line which is further from you

For sell limits the bid line has to touch your limit line

For buy limit your ask line has to touch your limit line

In conclusion look for line which is disadvantageous to u.

Dengaima

posts.text:
Hey Gembel just thought Id throw this up as again, I notice Im looking at something very similar to what you are. For AU.

I know the term origin isnt used as widely around here anymore but for me it still seems to be a great way for me to systematically approach identifying the correct engulfs, poles etc. If price engulfs then it generally wants to move to the source of the move, kinda thing. So I also saw your "bullish intention? " as just that. It not only engulfed the origin of that move, in which case I would have just said tg met, but it engulfed the base too, or from a diff. perspective or scale, engulfed this FL you have highlighted in red. So Im hoping it can make it up to the next origin. If so, only question really is how deep will it retrace before then. Also gotta look at both sides, if it takes out the low of this next base then is that a signal for lower? Or could it just be a FO? Or maybe should be looking at what the base is a reaction to, and use that FL instead of the base its self to determine. I dont know, but just offering up my thoughts.

posts.text:
first of all i like to post the Price Reading Article here

it's a precious gift from RTM and a wise guide for trading

Price Reading

In order to be able to trade the markets, we need to be able to
understand why price is where it is, and where it will go to next. The
best indicator for all this is Price itself. It holds all the clues
you'll ever need to work the market out. We do our trading at levels
called Supply and Demand Zones, and we watch Price Action there to give
us signs as to the intentions of the big money.

 Here’s what we look for on the charts:

General: HTF. Know where price is coming from and going to, and the PA past and present in all the TFs, from the Monthly down.

Specific: At the zones you want to trade, look to:

Past.

Study the zone in all TFs, down to M1 ask yourself:

Where were the decisions made? Clean S/D? Mark these lines. No clean S/D? – compressed zone

Did price really shoot away form the zone, or did it cp away?

Did the zone itself react at the right place? Look beyond the zone
further into the past. See what it reacted to. Was there a better S/D
nearby that price wants to visit? This explains many fakeouts. Did price
 originally react to the RS of a Flag Limit? It can fakeout to true SD
of the FL.

Present:

Approach.

How is price returning to the zone?

Where’s the nearest flag in the TF you want to trade? This is your tg1 in this TF. Flags in the LTFs? What does PA tell you?

Has price tested the last flag on approach? (good sign)

Has price compressed into the zone in this TF or LTFs? (good sign)

Is there big news on the way? Has there just been big news?

Reaction.

In LTF, does price react violently to the first decision point? Does it quickly engulf the nearest S/D? (good sign)

Does price simply CP away? Maybe it wants to go to the next decision point

If the first decision point breaks, watch the signs on approach to the next, and, of course, reaction.

level ( where people put their stops instead of putting their entry )

posts.author: omidfxt
posts.text:
hey micka1

all the question you are asking are really important and deep!

they needs lots of time to be answered(and i'm not really enough experienced to answer all of them
 ) and lots of chart. so i just tried to answer them from my point of
view and know that they are not enough! and beg my pardon if i miss
understand some of your question while answering

about the first target, generally the answer is yes but it really
depends, for example if price engulfed the last FL on approach before
reaching our entry then the first target can be the next one and you can
 get more pips!

and about the origin for the target, it depend again! if origin be far
away it will be better to chose a closer FL for the first target and for
 the final target, yes origin can be a good target depends on the multi
time frame analysis and the engulfed that occurred in the chart

and yes MPLs can be the origin of the move too

Second engulfs can be really great when they happen into free space!
but depends on the situation, sometimes after the second engulfed you
don't have enough space to enter and it's possible that there will not
be a good retrace to enter with, and we have to be careful that second
engulfed haven't reached it's target!

about a FTR that got faked out, if you mean the QM lvl, and MPLs, we
have to always look for them in the FL! there are a lot of QM lvl shapes
 in the chart but the best ones are the ones that occurred in a FL!

about CPAZ, e.g when the last Demand in the CP got engulfed we can
expect that price goes through the CP zone and we have to make sure that
 priced cleared all the pockets of Demands while going up! but most of
the time the CPs aren't perfect, if it's in a proper zone, it we be
really nice to trade it

and the cp in your chart, if we consider the engulf of that FL that you
spotted, that will be a good sign for entering with the retrace

by the way your charts are really artistic

OK Guys

It is about 8 month that i am living in RTM and enjoyed every second of it. RTM really feel like home for me!

from the first moment i start RTM, i forgot every bullshit that i
studied before, candle sticks, trendlines, channels... and stop trading
 live and put all my time into learning RTM concepts

has been said there and a complete plan for your trading journey has
been told there

After doing homeworks for about 4-5 months! i went through the journals
and at the same time started trading on a demo account for two months
that i post it's result in the previous pages in my journal, that was a
turning point in my trading style and understanding!

market and become profitable at least for three months as IF said

)

A Note before you begin

To all new traders:

This is a business, a very hard business.Every day we stare into the
abyss, and the abyss stares right back into us.To make our living, we
must daily face the demons Fear and Greed, and win.

Most of us, upon beginning our journey in trading, blew account after
account , trying out any system which was advertised well enough. We
found out that the market could chew us up and spit us out without
giving us a thought. We certainly paid our dues to that which would
provide for us later.

We imagined that we'd get rich quick, and that just didn't happen so easily.

What we had to do was put away all those silly indicators that promised
to give us an edge, and just look at what the charts were showing us.It
took thousands of hours of hard work and dedication to become successful
 traders.

Eventually, we found that price has ways of telling you what it's going
to do next. We began to notice many different patterns and price
structures which indicate that price should move to here or there.

We were no longer looking for an "edge". We just saw the truth of the market - what it wanted to do next.

.

.

.

Begin trading in Demo

I know you're itching to make your millions right away. You will not.
You will not hit the ground running. You will hit the ground rolling and
 stumbling and not knowing where your feet are. Make all your initial
mistakes for free.

Become regularly profitable for three months before you trade
with real money. Every loser can have a winning streak and think he's
cracked the market. You will have winning streaks and losing streaks
along the way. This is part of the learning process. Imagine that you
need a trading license to trade live, and that you must be consistently
profitable for at least three months to earn that license.Don't create
any shortcuts or loopholes. Earn that license fairly and honestly, or
it'll cost you, I promise.

When you've earned your trading license, celebrate. Have a party if you
like. Award yourself the license, either physically or mentally. You'll
need that memory to cling to in the dark times ahead.

When you're ready to trade live, remember this:

Trading live is a world away from trading demo. The emotions you will
feel will be far removed from those you experienced in demo. Sure, you
are ready to read the market, but now is the time to master your
emotions. This may take time. Fear and greed can be as destructive as
those silly systems you left behind.

Successful traders don't just take money magically from the
markets. They take it from PEOPLE. They take it from the 95% of people
who try to trade and fail. Don't let them see YOUR money in the market
until you're one of them.

So as you read above IF advise us not to start trading Live till we become profitable at least for 3 months

Hey Guys

here is a brief explanation on how the market works and how the main player try to win the game

Nothing is new here, all had been said thorough RTM. Just want to share it with my friends as a remind:

Before you want to join the game you HAVE TO know who are your enemies and how they play the game!

Why you have to know them?

Just a simple logic:

Because they are the main players in the game and the ones who are changing the market conditions

Certainly they are in the market to make money for their investors and absolutely themselves!

So you can’t be a good player if you don’t know the games rules and what there are looking for!

As you know nobody isn’t in the market just for the sake of God!

All the players in this game are looking for MONEY!

The same reason you are here! Aren’t you? : )

Here we can specify Forex players:

(image resource;forextraderportal.com)

All the players above want to increase their capitals and made more money

So as a simple logic there isn’t such a condition for everyone to profit from the market

As In the real world if you want to sell something you have to find
someone to buy it from you and if there isn’t any buyers so your
property doesn’t have any value!

And if there are lots of buyers, there will be a completion between them
 to owe your property so the value of your property will raise and you
can sell it in a higher price!

It is the same in the market. It is all about supply and demand!

Ok. Let’s get back to the main players in the market

They are all in a competition and want to make money from the market

But between them there some BIG GUYS that can make more money and no ones is going to stop them!

Why? Simple because they have the money and certainly the power!

If they want they can smash everyone on their way!

And they do! Because they want it all!

So how can they do it?

Again simple! They cheat on other ones! And if they want the money they have to do it!!

Because for example if they want to sell loads of something they have to
 have loads of buyers for their sell orders. That simple!

Ok. Now we know who are they and what they want. Great!

Now let’s see how it’s possible for them to achieve their goals?

First of all let’s talk about one of the participators in the market:

Retail Traders!

Most of the time retail traders are known as individual traders that are
 ordinary people that are trying to make money from the market(and in
95% of the time they can’t!)

But I think we can call someone as a retail trader that is not a BIG GUYS!

An individual trader, an institute traders or even a bank trader that is not in the BIG GUYS band can be a retailer!!

Now we are familiar with the retailers that are an easy competitor for BIG GUYS!

What are the BGs(Big Guys)’s plan for them?

Simple again! They interest everyone into trading and teach them how to do it wrong!

Brokers are some of their best friends!

Brokers make the deal and profit from the spreads and commissions! Easy money for them !

So if they have enough customers they can make more money.

Ok. Simple work! Just try to advertise for trading and show it as simple as possible!

They try to provide sexy platforms and apps for trading and lots of artistic indicator!

You can interest everybody into trading just by a simple indicator and a beautiful trend line or channel!

They translate their false trading strategies that are prepared very
smart into many language and give them to you just for free! Yeah they
really love retailers in the deepest part of their hearts!

They show you: oh look at this beautiful channel. Every time price hit
one side, it will react there and will go to the other side. Also look
at that beautiful MACD, RSI, … indicator that is telling you when to
trade and when to exit!

So amazing. Who is enough silly not to start trading after seeing this!

Absolutely no one as most of us did! : )

So let’s start with the free education and after a short period of time
we can start trading and open a live account to make the millions that
we were dreaming all the times!

Ok a good and sexy plan!

But most of the retailers don’t know who are behind the sense that are playing the games!

Smart and experienced traders teams with millions in their asset on their trading desk!

They are there for retail trader’s money and will make them confused each time!

Retailers: Damn! my stop just got hit by a few pips and then price went in my direction!

Ok. That because the lake of my understanding. I will study more and
will do it again. There is a huge amount of money right there, I can’t
give up on it simply!

That is the story that will be repeat again and again and HAS TO be repeat to full the pocket of BGs and their friends!

Just simple as always!

...........................................................................................................................................................................................

So as an advantage of knowing the main players in the market and their goals:

We as Smart retailers : ) have to be aware of all the tricks that are played in the market

As RTM told us many times, we have to try to get into the mind of the
BGs and put their hats on our heads and look at the chart as ones does!

We have to think in terms of order flow. Where BGs can fill their orders?

Where they can trap others to provide opposite positions for them to fill their orders?

RTM showed us how to see the manipulation of hope and fear and think
about the retailer’s mindset. How to see the buildings of positions and
the real movement of price and the reasons behind them

If we study all the RTM concepts they are all saying that what are BGs
doing in the market and where they are looking for trapping other
retailers

RTM is telling us always looking for signs of what the BGs are doing at
 the significant areas and emphasize on it that if we don’t see what
they are doing, there will be no trade for us!

If you seek through RTM and all the Concepts and the trades IF and
masters took you can see it clearly what is going on the market and you
will understand how to READ THE MARKET properly

far from this community and want to share it with my friends

You can read more through RTM and some very limited sources in the Internet

Know your enemies and their intentions and don't let them fool you : )

Hi,

Here is what I see:

ORFL -Down to the left on a lower time frame:

We have a reaction (supply) and a reaction to the supply (Origin). Origin is tested and bounces price (ORFL).

Then, ORFL Down is itself engulfed and a new FL Box (red) is formed.

When the red FL Box it engulfed another FL Box is formed and we have a swap zone.

Like before, we have a reaction to a FL (the FL is neon green). There is
 also an engulf of a very small ORFL down, which occurs before the
larger reaction to the green FL. Just like before, price engulfs this
zone and another ORFL is formed. Test 1 to create supply:

After supply is formed by testing the ORFL Down, an opportunity to FO to
 MPL (deeper in to the ORFL) exists and price reacts accordingly. I
think this is why Omid went short at that level.

posts.author: hoeschec

samjardavid wrote: hi hoeschec ^_^

what the different between ORFL and FL? is ORFL more important than FL

Thank you in advance

David

Hi Samjardavid-

A FL is any FTR that holds price up or down whereas a ORFL is an origin up/down and a FL.

ORFL is often the target of longs/shorts, so they hold special
importance. Salivan discusses the concept of magnetic attraction vs.
repulsion and this is related specifically to ORFL's.

posts.author: Ifmyante
posts.text:
Every candle on the chart is part of a PAZ of one form or another and knowing where price is in relation to these zones gives us a massive edge on the markets. Up until now, we have been taught nearly everything we need to know to be successful traders, PAZs really are the last piece of the puzzle. So let’s get started! So what is a Price Action Zone? A PAZ is exactly what it says; it’s a zone on your charts that show a distinct type of Price Action! These distinct zones include poles, flags, stacked supply/demand and compression. Once we are able to accurately determine where these zones are, there is one rule. ONLYtrade the edges! One great type of PAZ is the space between two Failure to returns’ (FTR), which is the space in which a flag forms; let’s look into this a little further:

You can see in the above chart I have marked off 8 FTR’s as price climbed up, between each one of these FTR we have a PAZ. So we have 7 PAZs. Simple as. Once price breaks into a PAZ (engulfs a FTR) we know it wants to go to the other side of the zone (the next FTR). So let’s look what happens on the way back down.

FTR 8 gets engulfed, price has now gotten into PAZ 1. Price retraces

then goes to FTR 7

FTR 7 gets engulfed, price has now gotten into PAZ 2. Price retraces

then goes to FTR 6

FTR 6 gets engulfed, price has now gotten into PAZ 3. Price retraces

then goes to FTR 5

FTR 5 eventually gets engulfed and gets into PAZ 4 and follows

through to engulf FTR 4 and FTR 3 and gets into PAZ 6. Price retraces before going to FTR 2

FTR 2 gets engulfed (see insert 2). Price retraces then goes to FTR 1

Now that you know where price wants to go, it is your job to enter on a retrace to target the other side of the PAZ (the next FTR), and we already know how to do this don’t we? PA!

You can discuss the article HERE By Pedini

Hi, Hoto

I would draw these slightly differently, based on the post I made in the FTR PAZ thread. It would be great to have some feedback from those who've got this nailed.

rcmacf wrote: Here's how I am marking in the PAZs, based on my current understanding. I'm leaving out cpPAZ until I've got a handle on the FTR PAZ. I'm using the same chart area as above, so we've consistency. Peds, am I getting there?

1. First I mark in the FTRs I see. These I take to be an engulf (a new high in this case) showing intent to go higher, then the fail to go lower. It does not become a true FTR until price then moves higher than the initial higher high. So, for example, z does not qualify as an FTR as y is a few pips lower than x. (it is a cpPAZ edge, but I'm not going near those yet). I've used a little red ellipse to show the tips of the FTRs.

2. I then mark in the demand zones (or supply if moving down) which the FTRs represent. My indi marks those created above current price blue, and those below as pink). These are going to become the targets on the way down - the FTB to the FTR, essentially.

3. Then it's a case of watching what price does:

The engulf at 1 means expect price to go to 2 (engulf 1 also engulfs an FL to the left of the top elipse, and should have you primed and ready for point A to happen - it is ignored demand becoming supply - an SR flip).

The engulf at 3 means expect price to go to 4

The engulf at 5 means expect price to go to 6, whichever PAZ edge that leads to next. If you were sharp, you could maybe get in at B.

And see how the influence continues..

posts.author: Pedini
posts.text:
Hi Myst. There certainly is a lot to consider when looking for a good entry. Firstly your H1 and M15 level really join up to be the same, but from a broader view of your question I understand this may not also be the case. Unfortunately the question you have put forward does not have a specific answer. What I can tell you however is this...

Too many traders, even those who have picked a great entry get killed because they have an unrealistic target. One may pick a level on an M15 chart (which isn't aligned with a HTF level) and try to target a level on the H4 or D which is going to get the a zillion pips and to their surprise they get stopped out when they may have been able to take 20 or 30 pips if they were realistic and targeted a m15 zone instead. The ONLY thing that will tell us what level is going to bring us down through to another level after an engulf is PA alone.

Lets say price makes its way back up to your marked out M15/H1 level at 71ish (which also seems to have some nice history). Price starts to form some wicks which tells us selling is happening, and we manage to enter with PA at a nice QM. Now realistically price can very much make its way back down to the next ftr, which also happens to be the start of a compression PAZ. But, we have to ensure that PA is supporting the move down. If we drop from the m15 level and start forming some nice supply on the way to our target, then great, we can hold. But, if some supply gets engulfed north on the way down before the tg is reached we may want to exit at an appropriate level and bank some pips.

So to sum it up, we have to look for appropriate PA at each potential level to give us an opportunity to go short. If we don't get it at the first M15 zone, then the next level seems to be a nice cap and QM on the daily that we can wait for.

I can post some charts if need be, but I hope I have summed it up.

Peds

Fxyogi,

I feel it is important to clarify a few things here:

1: FTR is not an alternative to SD trading, no no!

It's enhancement!

2: the name "Failure to Return" does not stand for "failure to return to supply/demand". Far from it!!! What it means is "failure to return and make another HH or LL" or "Failure to continue in the original direction".

Thus, your comment regarding FTR C is irrelevant: FTR ALWAYS RETURNS TO SUPPLY/DEMAND, what's more, the existence of FTR itself proves that Suppy/ ´Demand is present. (see the diagram) If it was not, no FTR could be made, the price would simply continue in the original direction. Does it make sense? It think this is very important.

But not always the Suppy / demand is so apparent in the chart as in FTR C example

In the FTR C scenario, the price engulfed the last demand of

the down leg, but failed to continue in the direction of the down leg: there was strong demand for the instrument. The demand was much stronger than the supply. Who can be the source of such a big demand? Yeah, the big guys were hungry

Another interesting thing: there was an early indication that price would want to reverse... look at the FTB to FTR B... can u see it?

3: As far as I know, the term "FTR" is unique for RTM, however, the concept is universal. For example, some traders outside RTM call it "hook".

posts.author: Pedini
posts.text:
Hiya Fxyogi. From your diagram it really seems you are getting your head around the FTR quite nicely. Well done.

In reference to your questions,

1. Remember that a FTR is in itself supply or demand. So yes, to be considered a ftr it must first break a high or low or supply/demand.

2. Now this is an interesting question. Point A FTR does not necessarily have to be a test of another level, price may very well not make it to a level of supply/demand before it fails to return. But even if it does reach a supply or demand level it is still a FTR. If you read about and study how compression forms you will see that it is exactly that.

Supply/demand traders consider the second time back less probable, but we are moving much further than simple Supply/demand traders.

3. This is correct, but only to the next ftr. Also consider where price can retrace to before it advances to the next FTR, and also why.

Hope this is of some help.

Peds

Hi, Many times, kinks overlap indeed, leaving no space for us to see engulfs. But it's a matter of scale: Inside every kink there are lower scale kinks, and ITs tend to give up their intention by bouncing price in between these LTF kinks. And sometimes you can catch LTF engulfs or BSZ that can get you in.

LS = Left shoulder.

posts.author: homerus
posts.text:
Ifmyante wrote: Have you read anything by Red about the diamond?

Actually, does anybody know if it's been explained before? If not, does anybody care to explain it?

Sure, it can be found in the PIE thread on FF:

Diamonds often occur as an early sign of a reversal and the reason for
it is to trap as much retail money as possible, it tends to trap buyers
and sellers then resolves very quickly after it completes a cycle of
trapping retail.

A diamond represents caution above all else because there is no clear
defined momentum either way. But from a price structure point of view,
its difficult to hold any position, buy or sell for any period of time
or profit. Why diamonds occur near reversals is that the market wants to
 take out all buyers and sellers and then resolve quickly and the shape
of the diamond does that. Its a trend traders nightmare and a scalpers
or range traders ideal situation.

posts.author: sunnytrader1984
posts.text:
@Infest

as you said there are several ways to trade this setup and I in no ways
would argue to that, everybody who trades, trades in his own way.

Like Pedini said, for us, the H4 supply above was just a level, where we
 expected price to show us something to trade. So the price came in,
made a nice RBD, but this is not enough if it does not engulf the last
swing low. If it would have stopped above the last swing low, we would
not trade it, since there can still be HHs forming. An engulf of swing
low is the PA which says to us, it is relatively safe taking the trade,
given somebody who has the might to make an engulf is selling here.

Once we have an engulf at a significant level, all we need to do is find
 a nice place to leave your order and let it do its thing.

nothing comes with a guarantee, but sometimes it comes with a high probability!

Hope this is helpful!

posts.author: Pedini
posts.text:
Hey Hoto.

Your points 1, 2 and 3 are all part of the stacked demand. In general
when price gets into stacked demand, it normally wants to go through it
to the top or bottom level, in this case the bottom level. It is not the
 same as compression as compression takes out remaining orders while
stacked demand still have orders hiding away. But if you think about it
logically it will be more profitable to get to the cheapest or most
expensive level to trade from...

...you can see from base 1 that price takes off and comes back to
re-test the base, these orders have now been filled and it is this point
 I want to see broken to get into the stacked demand below. This happens
 as you can see at the circle, and the entry is simply a supply/QM
level.

You can see now that price returned to the last base in the stacked demand, which is also a flip zone and took off very nicely.

I hope this answers both your queries!

Peds

Ahhhh....sweet sweet eureka comes yet again...Thank you!

So yes PAZ is any price action or price structure on the chart that
shows all opposing levels on the chart have been taken out at some
point, and price should cut right through to the last untouched level.
Compression is the simplest to understand because the last sentence is
all compression is about. But PAZ could take on an infinite number of
looks as long as it shows the remaining orders in all opposing levels
have been filled.

But the PAZ can never include the most recent level because you would
not expect price to just cut right through it. So you mark all the
violated levels up to the most recent, then when the most recent gets
violated it shows that the buyers/sellers are no longer interested in
holding price up/down. Thats when you enter on what ever reaction that
most recent level caused.

posts.author: Pedini
posts.text:
Heya Cas,

When drawing Compression PAZ's which is what I drew up on my gold chart,
 you want to be absolutely sure that price is going to go to the other
end of the compression. The only way to do this is to make sure the last
 pocket of supply or demand has been engulfed. Until this happens, we
don't know compression is going to work and really it can go on forever
(just look at AUDNZD).

Looking at your lines now:

1 - This was a test of a flip level, it formed the drop base rally at 4,
 but there is still supply above us (so its not the edge of our PAZ)

2 - Again even if this level is broken, which it was, there still remains to be supply above that needs to break.

Finally price breaks into our PAZ at 3. This was the last of the supply
till the other side of the zone and that is why it is our PAZ level. You
 can see price then retraced tested out Drop Base Rally at 4 and
continued through the zone.

I hope this helps,

Peds

Hiya Pedini,

Please excuse me while I jump onto your journal!

I've seen it written elsewhere on RTM that 'FTR = FL', but you seem to
treat it differently, and in a way that chimes with how I've come to
think of it.

So, it seems to me that the FTR is just confirmation that the FL is
current, willing Supply / Demand, but this does not mean that the FTR is
 current, willing Supply / Demand in and of itself (whether it is or
isn't depends on the structure and location of the FTR to my mind).

It's this FTR confirmation of the FL which enables us to determine where
 PAZes are bounded, and where to look for EGs, which show us that
current, willing Supply / Demand has now been absorbed, so price will
only find more at the next confirmed level out (explaining why price
will likely move from one edge of a PAZ to another edge of the adjoining
 PAZ)... .

My conclusion is actually that 'FTR (usually) = FTB' - and thus the FL
has already been tested and Supply / Demand removed from it. Perhaps the
 subtle difference is a matter of how quickly the FL is tested after it
is formed?

Am I on the right track or wide of the mark?

Thanks in advance.

Spongy.

posts.author: Pedini

Hey guy, just got back from a weekend away, I read your comment on the
 weekend, but wasn't ready to put my mind from "Break mode" to "Chart
mode". Anyway, back into it, YIPEE!

Spongy - Going from your comment, and some of your articles you have put
 together, you really have a talent for tieing information together! As
for your question, in my mind this is how I see it (and it may be a
simplistic way of viewing it). A FTR is when a level is broken and price
 fails to get back to higher/lower prices, this failure can be a test of
 the broken level, or it may fall short, but it is still a FTR.

Now, as for your comment regarding a FTR testing and thus removing
supply/demand from a flag, again you have this correct IMO, but you may
be missing something. I remember when I first started on supply/demand
trading I used to watch Sam Seidens webinars. Now Mr Seiden is very
strict on teaching not trading a level that is a test of another level
(which in our case can be a FTR). To me this is nonsense, just think
about how compression forms for example, every time supply/demand is
tested in compression it is testing a test of another level, so these
levels work!

You also have the idea behind the PAZ down well. For me the FTR is more
important to engulf and then to look for a trade, rather than basing a
trade on the FTR itself (unless it was preceded by an engulf of another
FTR). This is all a little bit of a mouthful, I hope it's understood!

Hoto - I didn't mark out any CP because there was nothing important to
mark off, and as you see the trade was not based on cany CP. You are
spot on, those are the exact reasons I marked off those FTR levels

Hey guys, thanks so much for the questions, they are great. At the
moment, it is obvious that EU is in a trading range, and there have been
 some fake moves on either side and trapping people trading the range. I
 would personally choose to stay out till it resolves itself.

As for your questions, what I will do when I see an engulf is ask myself
 "does this engulf make sense?" By that I mean look at the history
around where price engulfed. Did it engulf into a DP or a key level? Did
 it engulf into supply/demand. Also, look where the source of the engulf
 came from, was it coming from a HTF supply/demand level or has it
failed yet to reach one? All these things should give you a heads up on a
 potential FO.

For example, if price is engulfing south, but price has yet to come off a
 significant level of supply, it makes sense to see a FO to help push
price to higher levels. Something that looks like it may be currently
happening on EU.

Anyway, I hope this gives some food for thought, it is past 2am, so
excuse my lack of a detailed information/charts, I will try to find some
 example to post when I am well rested.

 relationship with FTRs / DPs and so on. I'll give you some of the
opinion I've arrived at (please bear in mind that this is only my view

view; and it may be inaccurate or plain wrong. Caveat lector (because

Hiya Pedini,

The Engulf matters because it is usually a convincing show of force, but
 we also have to take into account what it Engulfs, how convincingly it
does so, what's beyond it, and what happens directly after. We can
Engulf an S / R level, Spike, or Supply / Demand area: to me, that last
one matters most as the first two are most likely reactions to it and
carry less import (in my eyes, but it depends on the situation). (Hint:
you may want to reflect deeply on this paragraph).

posts. The areas marked in grey are what I perceive to be real Supply

Sorry for butting into your journal here Pedini, but I'm itching to comment on this discussion.

Say you've taken a reversal trade and gotten in at the very bottom, and
the trade is hundreds of pips in profit, and you're now managing this
trade on the daily TF.

I believe that any trade you take subsequent to this on that pair should
 be taken with absolutely no regard for the original trade.

Say your MM has you risk 2% per trade, and your original trade had you
buy 1 lot, and you now find yourself with the right PA at the extreme of
 a very important daily level.

You should be able to take this trade according to your normal MM plan,
regardless of what other trades you have on the same pair. If it calls
for a purchase of 2 lots, then 2 lots is what you should buy, and you
should manage this trade completely independently.

Certainly it's hard initially to ignore the fact that you're now in for 3
 lots on the same pair, but you've got to look at it rationally, leaving
 fear out of the equation.

If this is a currency trade, imagine that the first trade is on
something else entirely - imagine you bought a lot of coffee if you
must.

Remember, our best trades are taken at extremes, and we know the
limitations of each trade we take, so we should take every trade on its
own merit.

Just a thought - have a great weekend :)

Supply and the Engulf of that pinbar only went deeper into that Supply

This is how I was studying it, hopefully it highlights the importance of the answers to those questions!

I have trouble believing in 'ancient' areas of Supply or Demand on longer time-frames. It's not that price doesn't turn at them sometimes,
 it's just that the orders which cause the reaction to the area are not
the remainder of those that created the original area - so if price
turns because of new orders, how important is the old area?

Too often I've sat waiting for a turn from an 'ancient' area, when none
has been forthcoming, and current PA has been telling me something
different (and that is not to say my reading of PA is any good
 ). To me, the importance and definition of areas decays over time
until they become either matters of convenience / coincidence, or traps
(for S / D traders!). So, with that in mind, I waited to see whether
price would react to the area, then looked for something in the shadow
of that reaction.

Also the Compression into the area might not indicate weakness, so I am
not anticipating a turn based on this leading confirmation: as there are
 fresh areas of Supply, I want to see them taken out first before I'm
convinced.

In the chart below, I've marked a couple of fresh Supply areas along
with the Demand area I was interested in. Ideally I wanted to see
proximal Supply get engulfed before the retrace - this didn't happen.

posts.author: Spongiform
posts.text:
Hello Pedini,

I know you only had three (maybe four) reasons for your choice, but here's my read ... . There are many similarities with other entries (which is good :) ), and some subtle differences.

 Warning: Spoiler!

 [ Click to expand ]

 [ Click to hide ]

W1 - the nature of that reaction to potential Demand, confirms it
 as a strong source of buyer interest - Pro Money. The level is placed
at the bottom of that reaction as there are confirmed orders around
here. There's still buying interest when price returns much later, but
it's not Pro Money interest - it's just the liquidity for Pro Money to
drive price down:

D1 - a close up on the break below that level. There's an EG or FO of
it, but we don't know which until we see what happens next. There isn't a
 new high after, so it's not FO. A further EG takes out Demand, then
price is driven down hard - FTR.

I don't have H4 history, but I would be happy enough picking that one
green candle as the basis of new Supply (note: I might just have easily
selected only the top wick and ignored the body. I included the body this time because it shows the point where late buyers were crushed). Also, my view (is this shared?) of FTRs is that they can
 be a source of Supply or Demand, or they just confirm its presence by
being reactions to it, so clipping the top of the FTR but placing the
Stop above highs or lows to its left covers both horses, so to speak:

H4 - because of the the way I marked Supply on D1, I actually see an
Entry, it could easily have been otherwise - it still misses the level
marked for the bottom of that reaction seen way back on W1. I've marked
what seem like reasonable TPs, but my view (for now) is that price is
hasn't finished going up yet, so I don't think TP2 is likely:

H4 - and just to be awkward (who me?
 ) I wouldn't actually have taken the trade as marked for two
reasons/beliefs: that price information integrity decays over time
because of anticipation and interpretation, so that the way price is
moved at these areas is very much a matter of convenience based on where
 current liquidity is, or where it can be induced, or which direction
it's pointing in; and that accuracy is not so important anyway, where
there are such differences in price feeds between brokers (a trader's
hit on one platform is a miss on another, candles and levels can vary so
 the candles and formations I see may not be the ones anyone else
sees... .). So I would have waited to see what happened in the area and
based my opportunity off of that, here's some conjecture:

compartmentalizing of trades on a smaller TF and being an avid follower

 for me to grasp. Like what determines you direction for the day, the
daily curve, 4 hr, 1 hr?? I feel the direction is half the battle
because when working with smaller TF entries, you will get entry signals
 all over the place and if you are in a zone that is on the wrong side
of the curve, you will eventually blow an account by entering on the 15
min or 5 min because you probably will get some sort of a reversal
signal being that these entry TFs are so nimble compared to their larger
 TF zone counterparts. I guess what I'm trying to ask is how do you
spot the plausible reversal zones on the larger TFs (4hr, daily,
weekly)? Do you just go for extremities (from engulf to engulf) or
from fresh zone to fresh zone?? There have been many times where I
have seen a RBR or DBD get completely blown through on the 4hr or daily
even if an entry signal was given on the smaller TF because the trend
was so strong. Do you just depend on original DBR and RBD for macro
trend REVERSAL spots?? I just like the Idea of knowing my direction for
 the day and only taking longs or shorts for days weeks until the trend
is over, thus staying out of the cop of counter trend movements. Happy
belated B Day btw.

I did not and don't make the decision to trade that FL when it is
created, nor do I any other FL. The price action after it is created is
very important. The main reason I took the trade is there was clearly
some untested orders and to make it even better there were a nice set of
 lows to fake below. It also looked like it could have been on the edge
of a potential range. This is why I was confident that price would
bounce. Once the bounce happened I was happy to sit and watch it for a
while to see where it went.

Your level circled in green will most likely hold some importance in a
lower timeframe, it doesn't look to amazing to me there though, however
it still has the potential to bounce price. Again, it depends how price
approaches it etc.

Major swap zone engulfed > a supply FTR created > then price

> so price was just going back to the demand FTR from where you
shorted.

Thank you so much again.

posts.author: prosenjitghosh
posts.text:
Hi Friends, I went through all the materials I found here in RTM, whether it is Marketpedia, Homework section or Journals, I found all of them to be extremely important and simple to learn, nevertheless to say, this is a Gem of a Community, where all the members are actively participating, sharing and learning together.

Well I believe, "Knowledge is the only thing, that increases by sharing". And happy to see that happening here, time and again.

And this is what is knocking in my head, to open my own "Journal" to carry on with the spirit of "Learning by sharing". So henceforth, I will post here, all the analysis I do or whatever doubts I have or something new which I come across, in terms of RTM style of Trading and Psychology.

And one request, please do pardon my bad English, as my Mother Language is Bengali.

Thanks and Regards, Prosenjit (PG)

posts.author: projectsagana
posts.text:
Here's a chart of USDJPY

I've been trying to figure out what are the "A Trade" set ups for me. This particular "A Trade" set up I've been studying has appeared on this h4 time frame. It's a bullish reversal trade set up. Price must be in down trend prior to this set up. Then price bases in a range for a moment, then rises for a leg up when supply and demand hit an imbalance state of price action. The leg up then makes a higher high breaking the down trend line. So a rally-base-rally demand zone have formed. I set up a long limit order on that demand zone with a stop loss just below it and an automatic 2:1 target. I just wait for the price to arrive to the zone and fill my order and let the market do its thing.

So that's what I saw on the Japanese Yen against the US Dollar over and over again on the 4h time frame.

My posts have been everywhere... what I mean, I would focus on one thing then move on to another topic with out completely mastering each topic. For some reason I also believe as I'm learning, I also don't need to know absolutely everything, but only to get an accurate idea to where the market is currently heading to make money. Ultimately as in a never ending learning experience I want to keep improving my chart reading skills and able to trade based on what I believe the market is about to do and PROFIT BIG MONEY CONSISTENTLY $$:) I learn tremendous amount of knowledge about the market in each posts that I make because it takes me to focus on price action and write it down what I see and let my self completely immerse in this money making puzzle.

While reading price history to figure out why price turned in such way is important. I also think it's essential to my learning curve to just simply follow the current market. To apply from all the lessons I learned about PA here in RTM about any pair's current price action. I may make wrong expectations about the market to where it will go next. I also may make right expectations about the market current direction. This way I will learn in real time rather than just reading price in hindsight.

So I read this article called Price Readingwww.readthemarket.com/index.php/price-reading and inspired to follow a single pair for now and do a reading session daily for 30 days and see where it would take me.

For the Daily, since I have a full time job, I will pick either the before I go to work or after I get home from work to do my daily updates. And that daily update will include the 4h or 60m chart or even go to the smaller time frames if needed to explain to my self the logic the market chose to be.

aus1way wrote: Also I was looking at this chart and wondering when does an FTR become an FTR and when is it a retrace or are retraces FTRs

Think about in a trending market. If the market wants to go up it doesn't just go straight up. You might see big long candles in the HTF but check in the LTF you'll have a bunch of pull backs or a retrace in price action.

To answer a part of your question FTRs are really just pull back in price action and to quote Les_Paul from the article "It is important to realise that FTRs are places where institutional traders open / close their positions."With that knowledge, not all pull backs are levels where IT's open and close positions to produce significant reaction. All pullbacks can be technically called a FTR level, but it could also not be tradable. We have to figure out which FTRs are the important one.

I'm still learning about these FTRs also and the best way to learn them is actually do the homework. Find homework of the FTRs and note which one produced significant reaction. Then compare them to the FTRs all over the charts. If you're having trouble defining which ones are FTR go back and read the article again.

There are 4 types of FTRs 1. FTRs after an engulf of major support/resistance line 2. FTRs after an engulf of minor support/resistance line 3. FTRs after an engulf of the opposite FTRs (these FTRs include FL. Yes FL's are sometimes FTR) 4. FTRs after a break into a CPAZ

aus1way, study this picture, read the article, and find some FTRs and label them exactly like these.

from the article, "Price action breaks the barrier (1) and retraces (2). It is irrelevant whether price action crosses the barrier again or not (as in examples (ii and iv above). At the extreme of the retrace a base is very often made (b)."

Thanks for being open with your emotions. Emotions play such an important part of trading. This state of mind of frustration just means that there's is still something that we have to incorporate into our reading and trading. It's just that we're hitting on a level that's been waiting to be broken and go to the next level. It's like if you ever played a video game and the bosses gets harder each level you advance. It's just a challenge for us to beat.

Or think of the price acting bullish, climbing upwards on a supply level and think that supply level as our challenge. Price wants to go up but that supply level is causing a reaction to bring it down. Okay, so first time visit might produce a significant reaction. It drops. A loss for the bulls. We are the bulls, wanting to climb higher. It tries to come back up again, the 2nd time. It reacts a little, but not too much of a loss. Then for the third visit, by the time gets there, that challenge gets consumed. Each visit to that challenge, that supply, and hopefully we learn from it, gets consumed until there's no more to consume at that particular challenge, the supply level. It engulfs it, breaks through a barrier and next the level is our next one to break.

I know this is a crazy metaphor, but the point is: Each of those challenge presented to us, over and over again, just like price visiting a level many times, gives us another opportunity to learn and make better decision. For the mistakes that we had made over and over again become so obvious that we learn from it and make better judgement on price next time.

A concept that's presented to us and we're still on the early stages of puzzling this market together. Or something that's missing that we're not aware of yet and that's needed to be put on our conscious level. I believe everything we need to win is at RTM and grateful for that! I also believe everything we need to win consistently comes from our lessons and experiences.

Astro, we will master this! Let alone, reading the articles, journals, and different posts at RTM and making winning and losing trades is a sign of success.

I learned this from milkeyway.

My understanding: ITs want to buy or sell. They have big money. Their orders are gigantic in size. When some of their orders get filled, prices move BIG TIME. Their executed partial orders are distinctly visible in the price charts. They want more money. They have a problem: They need more willing buyers/sellers to fill their orders. What do they do? Trick retail traders. One of the ways they do that is to feed on break out momentum traders.

ITs main concern: finding liquidity to fill their side.

I hope I am in the right direction when it comes to this.

posts.author: ShadowPit
posts.text:
I ponder the same questions PS, especially when I hit a long run of losses. Here's what I think in red.

projectsagana wrote: Why does sometimes current price action seems so clear and sometimes don't? In my opinion, before even placing a trade, it's about making sure you have a plan that identifies the bare minimum of variables such as; reversal possibilities, obstacles and targets in multiple time-frames. If you're forcing a trade for the sake of having something on, you probably haven't done the requisite preparation, and you will not make the right decisions when you need to on entry, trade management, or exit possibilities. Disaster!

Is this just a matter of state of mind? Like being in the zone? Look I am not a psychologist so take my words with a grain of salt, but being in the right state of mind is a direct consequence of being adequately prepared to trade, confidence stems from preparedness, and with confidence you establish a winning attitude. You're prepared by establishing 'best practice'. Best practice being, having a trading plan with a system you trust, recognising you're in a healthy mindset (not stressed), not allowing outside influences effect your judgement. Does this make sense?

I've definitely had moments when I see price happen ahead of time and were able to take advantage of that. Definitely, sometimes it'll happen naturally, and you won't even know it until after the fact and you have somehow magically added 20% to your account without batting an eyelid. It'll be different for everyone but it is worthwhile reflecting on your own personal habit and what you did right in correlation to how the market behaved during that time to understand how you can get yourself in that zone time and time again.

And others not so much. Hmmm... My goal is be able to read the market and see the ITs intentions clearly ALL THE TIME. Yep, yep and yep. Been there. Still end up there after ridiculous winning streaks. The self doubt creeps in and you trust your plan less, you deviate from your system, you turn into a loose cannon. Always do your analysis from the top down, HIGHER time frame. How often do look at a daily chart? I hope every day! One time-frame analysis will have you scurrying away into a corner when you watch FTR after FTR fail.

Anyone have this phase? You betcha!

P.S. If you haven't already, pick up all the psychological nuggets of wisdom from this fine gentleman's thread. WARREN

Hi PS, (prepare for many words - you asked for thought provoking) I wouldn't beat yourself up too much about the USDCAD trade. You took it out for a small profit! You will be better prepared next time I have no doubt.

With regards to your price read in your last post. The H1 stuff looks like textbook RTM to me with consideration to the HTF which I love. This helps me too buddy:)

For your D1 chart. Sure that is a valid FTR and expecting some sort of bounce is only sensible, AND there was a 100 pip long trade from it too! But, I think it's at this point when you're looking at a too good to be true daily level with compression approach and you're so zoomed out that it's actually time to start consulting the Weekly and Monthly charts for additional clues and PA you would expect to see.

When price falls as quickly as it came up you don't want to be caught trying to catch falling knives, check the weekly out, eeep! So you have to do something different from what the herd is doing (I am assuming they are trying to pick the bottom). When you are in the moment, put yourself in a neutral position, one engulf at a time, and instead of looking for reversal PA exclusively, look for the "how do I get it in on this bear move!" Okay so maybe a chart or two will explain this better..

Regarding your questions in orange on the chart, follow and check me here:

P = price breaks a low and forms a new LL R = price retraces to create potential FTR, then blows past P to confirm FTR O = price breaks a high and forms a HH J = price retraces to create potential FTR, then moves past O to confirm FTR E = price FTB's to FTR at J, then ENG's the top of the consolidation on its way to... C = price FTB's to FTR at R, then ENG's the bottom of the consolidation (J and E) T = target for a sell at C because that's HTF demand (from Feb.)

Think of FTR's as obstacles. Until price removes the obstacle (or gaps beyond it), it can't get to whatever is on the other side. The FTR at R is longer term than the one at J, so some refer to J as a "local FTR". But both are FTR's that have to be dealt with before price can move to the other side, and the way price deals with them is normally to bounce off of them and go back "from whence it came." I don't think an FTR matters much until price returns to it. If that's true, then R doesn't matter while price is at J. When price gets to E then J matters, and when price gets to C then R matters.

In a long-winded, roundabout way that answers your question about where price is coming from. In a longer term view, price is coming from R and while it's dilly-dallying around before it returns to R price is coming from E (which would be a shorter term view.) I think that's what they mean by this stuff being snowflake-like, or cyclic, or layered, or whatever other terms people use for "patterns within patterns" or "moves within moves."

Incidentally, did you notice that R was actually tradeable since it's the right shoulder of a QM? I just noticed it myself so being that I've been studying this chart to type this message, I think I need to redo some QM homework!

Back to boxes: the box that contains O, J, and E is a PAZ that marks the limits at the bottom at J and at the top at whatever FL/FTR caused price to stop moving up. It's marked with a "!" and was formed by breaking P (my MT4 is having issues pulling M1 data on this pair right now so I can't show it, sorry.) Once this obstacle (aka: FTR) that's limiting upward price movement is ENG'ed at the red line, then that obstacle marks the bottom of the next PAZ and price is held between the red line and the FTR at R until one of the 2 is ENG'ed.

Hopefully I'm not confusing the subject and that adds some insight or maybe it just tells you stuff you already know, but that's where my current understanding has me. I never really understood why PAZ's (especially FTR PAZ's) were so hyped, but I'm starting to understand and see the power they hold.

One thing that really helped me in the last couple of months was to make sure all of my trades had enough room for profit. I had to learn the hard way after suffering several losses that there is no need to force a trade when there is no free 'space' for price to move and at least reach a decent first target. Sure, sometimes price blows right through a zone but a good chunk of the time, orders have to get absorbed first. I would even say that space is the most important thing to look for in a possible trade. Observe some of the trades that the senior members have posted and look at how obvious a lot of their trades look. Most times you will notice, they look so appealing because they had enough room for profit. Also, scrub trough the PIE tread on FF and look at Red's charts. Pretty much all of his trades have clear room for profit and he usually takes off 2/3 of his position at the first major obstacle (usually an SR/ flip zone) and closes out the rest of the position at the source/ origin of the move.

Also, here is an acronym I developed that has helped me focus on the important things to look for in a trade. The acronym is STTAR and the breakdown is as follows:

SPACE: Make sure there is room for profit and enough space to get decent a RRR at your first target.

TIMING:Try to trade during the corresponding hot spots for your pair. In other words, try to time your trades during the major market opens for the corresponding pair you are trading (i.e. trade the Yen pairs during the Asian session, trade the Euro pairs during the London session etc...) You will also notice that a lot of fake outs and direction changes form during session changes (opens and closes) and news events..

TREND:The trade is either counter trend, trend following, or neutral (in the case of a ranging market). This matters a lot when it comes to how you want to manage the trade. In counter trend situations, I am much more willing to take full profit at my first target and be aggressive with my trailing stop. In trend following trades, I am open to holding on to my trades for more profit and I allow more lenience for pullbacks. I tend to treat ranging market trades like counter trend trades i.e. be aggressive with the stop trailing and profit taking.. Now of course the market is fractal and trends can be different on different TFs, but I tend to look at the HTFs for the ultimate gauge on what the trend is (4hr, daily, weekly....) But if you are a 1min scalper per say, then you could just use the 1hr charts as your trend curve etc...

APPROACH:Is price moving in a parabolic, steady, or compressed manner toward your trade zone. If it is moving parabolic toward your zone of interest, then sometimes the momentum is unsustainable. Other times, the overzealous momentum of a parabolic move can blow right through zones. IMHO, It is important to try to use confirmation trades when price is moving toward your zone of interest in a parabolic fashion. The good thing about parabolic approaches, is that they give you ample space/ room for profit if the LTF confirmation gives you the signal to take the trade. If price is moving in a healthy, steady manner toward your zone and especially if it is building a base right before the zone (remember the importance of 'room for profit'), this is another time to use caution when looking for a trade because the PA shows signs of a healthy trend. I also tend to wait for LTF confirmation in these scenarios. If price is compresses into your zone, then you can usually put on a limit order and let her rip IMO.

Reaction:Did your zone cause a LTF engulf and in what manner did it do so. Was it a fast powerful rejection, or a weak limp one. If the rejection was weak, perhaps price wants to go higher. Look our for reactions that occur before the bounds of the zone are reached. Institutions LOVE to use these as fake out levels to get cheap easy orders.

If you think about it, as long as these 5 principles all check out, then you have a very good chance of having a profitable trade. They don't all have to check out for every trade, but the more of them that do, the better chance your trade has of winning ( I personally recommend that at least 3 out of the 5 principles check out in every trade with the idea of 'space' being the constant that has to be present every time).

Sorry for the long explanations to my STTAR acronym as I'm sure you already know most of this information but I just wanted to show you something that has helped me quickly concentrate my mind on the important things to look for before taking a trade.

Hope this helps, SyT

One thing that really helped me in the last couple of months was to make sure all of my trades had enough room for profit. I had to learn the hard way after suffering several losses that there is no need to force a trade when there is no free 'space' for price to move and at least reach a decent first target. Sure, sometimes price blows right through a zone but a good chunk of the time, orders have to get absorbed first. I would even say that space is the most important thing to look for in a possible trade. Observe some of the trades that the senior members have posted and look at how obvious a lot of their trades look. Most times you will notice, they look so appealing because they had enough room for profit. Also, scrub trough the PIE tread on FF and look at Red's charts. Pretty much all of his trades have clear room for profit and he usually takes off 2/3 of his position at the first major obstacle (usually an SR/ flip zone) and closes out the rest of the position at the source/ origin of the move.

Also, here is an acronym I developed that has helped me focus on the important things to look for in a trade. The acronym is

and the breakdown is as

STTAR

follows:

Make sure there is room for profit and enough space to get decent a RRR

SPACE: at your first target.

Try to trade during the corresponding hot spots for your pair. In other

TIMING: words, try to time your trades during the major market opens for the corresponding pair you are trading (i.e. trade the Yen pairs during the Asian session, trade the Euro pairs during the London session etc...) You will also notice that a lot of fake outs and direction changes form during session changes (opens and closes) and news events..

The trade is either counter trend, trend following, or neutral (in the case

TREND: of a ranging market). This matters a lot when it comes to how you want to manage the trade. In counter trend situations, I am much more willing to take full profit at my first target and be aggressive with my trailing stop. In trend following trades, I am open to holding on to my trades for more profit and I allow more lenience for pullbacks. I tend to treat ranging market trades like counter trend trades i.e. be aggressive with the stop trailing and profit taking.. Now of course the market is fractal and trends can be different on different TFs, but I tend to look at the HTFs for the ultimate gauge on what the trend is (4hr, daily, weekly....) But if you are a 1min scalper per say, then you could just use the 1hr charts as your trend curve etc...

Is price moving in a parabolic, steady, or compressed manner

APPROACH: toward your trade zone. If it is moving parabolic toward your zone of interest, then sometimes the momentum is unsustainable. Other times, the overzealous momentum of a parabolic move can blow right through zones. IMHO, It is important to try to use confirmation trades when price is moving toward your zone of interest in a parabolic fashion. The good thing about parabolic approaches, is that they give you ample space/ room for profit if the LTF confirmation gives you the signal to take the trade. If price is moving in a healthy, steady manner toward your zone and especially if it is building a base right before the zone (remember the importance of 'room for profit'), this is another time to use caution when looking for a trade because the PA shows signs of a healthy trend. I also tend to wait for LTF confirmation in these scenarios. If price is compresses into your zone, then you can usually put on a limit order and let her rip IMO.

Did your zone cause a LTF engulf and in what manner did it do so. Was

Reaction: it a fast powerful rejection, or a weak limp one. If the rejection was weak, perhaps price wants to go higher. Look our for reactions that occur before the bounds of the zone are reached. Institutions LOVE to use these as fake out levels to get cheap easy orders.

If you think about it, as long as these 5 principles all check out, then you have a very good chance of having a profitable trade. They don't all have to check out for every trade, but the more of them that do, the better chance your trade has of winning ( I personally recommend that at least 3 out of the 5 principles check out in every trade with the idea of 'space' being the constant that has to be present every time).

Sorry for the long explanations to my STTAR acronym as I'm sure you already know most of this information but I just wanted to show you something that has helped me quickly concentrate my mind on the important things to look for before taking a trade.

Hope this helps, SyT

posts.author: gristar
posts.text:
You got stopped out because "ASK PRICE" touched that level. you may turn on your MT4 ask line by right clicking on your chart and go to properties. You will see a line slightly higher displayed on the price shown by your candle. Sometimes ask price is near to bid price which is the candle showing but sometimes it could be far. The different between ask and bid is what we call Spread. Spread is not constant all of the time. it may be widen by broker some times. when it is wide enough to hit your SL, it may look like what happened to your chart. You think the candle never touch the level so your SL should not be hit, but in fact SL got hit by ASK line,

when you Buy you use Ask price, when you Sell you use Bid price (which is your candle)

posts.text:
I finally have my own personal written trading plan on hard copy. It's meant to be simple and will be editing it through out my learning curve to see what works and what doesn't.

It's Raining Money Trading Plan

[/size]

I. Easy As 1-2-3 Plan 1. Identify Location of price 2. Identify Direction of price 3. Identify Entry in price

II. Four Locations of Price 1. Inside/Reaction of a SUPPLY level

- The direction of price is currently up, and here is where we will WAIT for

signals whether price will bounce down or engulf the level up

2. Inside/Reaction of a DEMAND level

- The direction of price is currently down, and here is where we will WAIT for

signals whether price will bounce up or engulf the level down

3. After an ENGULF of a resistance or supply level

- An engulfing of a supply level into a PAZ means price most likely wants to go

to the next higher level of supply and here is where we WAIT for signals whether price indeed wants to keep going up or it was a FO

4. After an ENGULF of a support or demand level

- An engulf of a demand level into a PAZ means price most likely wants to go

the next lower level of demand and here is where we will WAIT for signals whether price indeed wants to keep going down or it was a FO

III. Money Map Guide 1. HTF vs LTF - HTFs will be used for identifying location and direction of price. LTFs will be used for entry in price

Style of Trading: HTF/LTF

A. Position: Monthly as HTF, and Daily as LTF *B. Swing: Wkly as HTF, and 4h as LTF *C. "Intra-Swing": 4h as HTF, and 15m as LTF D. Daily: 60m as HTF, and 15m as LTF

*I will be using Swing and "Intra-Swing" Style of Trading

- HTF is ALWAYS more significant than LTF - HTF supply would most likely end LTF uptrends - HTF demand would most likely end LTF downtrends - LTF uptrends would most likely end at HTF supply - LTF downtrends would most likely end at HTF demand - AT ALL TIMES, ALWAYS BE AWARE OF WHERE PRICE IS IN THE HTF

2. Engulf to PAZ

- When price engulfs a level into a PAZ, it would most likely reach the next

opposing level

- When price engulfs a supply level into a PAZ, it would most likely reach the

next higher level of supply

- When price engulfs a demand level into a PAZ, it would most likely reach the

next lower level of demand

Engulf of SUPPLY into PAZ simplified illustration

Engulf of DEMAND into PAZ simplified illustration

IV. The "Make Me Rich" Set Ups

- The most important, must have signal of all of the Make Me Rich Set Ups is:

Engulf

- No Engulf = NO Trade. ALWAYS WAIT FOR THE ALL MIGHTY ENGULF!! - Minimum potential RR is 3:1, if RR is 3:1, take profit at 2.5 RR, if RR is 4:1,

take profit at 3.5 RR

- Always have a stop loss pre-determined when entering a trade - Always have a profit target pre-determined when entering a trade - Risk per Trade: 1% of account balance

1. Reversal FL/FTR Demand

2. Reversal FL/FTR Supply

3. Reversal Bullish QM

4. Reversal Bearish QM

V. Profit and Risk Management

Risk Per Trade: 1% of account balance Position Size Calculator: www.babypips.com/tools/forex-

calculators/positionsize.php

Target per Trade: Minimum of 3-to-1 potential RR Monthly Target: 8% of account balance Maximum Loss per Week: 4% Maximum Open Trades Simultaneously: 4 Trades

1st Edition: 2-16-15

From here I will be forward testing it by trading live on a demo account. The only way for me to graduate from a demo trader to a live trader is if I manage to get 8% increase for 3 consecutive months.

At the same time I am demo trading, I will also be using FX Tester 2 to help me more about my rules

Hey Guys,

I have the urge to let some steam out and come clean… I just feel like this is the right place to share since I know I am going to be sticking around until I either make it or make it:)

A little history about me,

I have been at this business for more years than I care to admit openly (cause you’ll guess my age

), let’s just say it’s been over a decade I am working on becoming

consistently successful in this path I have chosen for myself.

I had a career in a very demanding industry and through hard work I even managed to carve my own partnership until many years later I felt I wasn’t giving trading the attention it required so I closed shop and took it onto myself to make a living out of trading. I thought I would force myself to learn swimming or drown. That was 4 and half years ago… I had ups and downs as one would expect.

Like so many, I too have gone down the indicator avenue and back up again until coming back full circle. I have had a lot of success at times and when my confidence grew I lost almost all in just a few trades. Suddenly the system I had built for myself that had generated 330% ROE in 6 months (with almost no drawdown) cost me 275% in 7 trades. I’ll let you imagine what that did to my psyche… I then couldn’t look at a chart for months on end without getting panic attacks; I had anxiety, depression and sleepless nights coupled with nightmares of market crashes (or rallies for that matter) that sucked the life out of me while of course being against me.

The next phase was filled with research, learning Supply and Demand and of course after demoing for a few weeks, I jumped right back into live, losing the rest of my initial equity and much much more. It seemed every level I traded failed! It was as if there was this dark cloud of bad luck hanging over my head. Needless to say, I was devouring all Red’s material, followed PIE, then registered with AG until I came here because IF was anyway my favorite all along (this is no flattery, it’s true). I lurked for over a year in here absorbing the material and getting lost often along the way too; traded my new discovered knowledge only to lose more.

I think I am under pressure because I need to make a living out of this. I am not giving up, even though lately I had to move back in with my family because I could not sustain the expenses of my own place.

The reason for all the above is really because I caught myself lately looking into snake oil again. Also, I want this to be a new beginning for me through this journal. So I am holding myself accountable in front of all you good people on here.

That’s it for now; I have to get back to studying
