for bearish PA on the M5 chart within the entire M30 zone to signal you back in. (For what it's worth your analysis sent some pips my way, I took the trade.)

In summary Because I've crapped on a bit, some things to be mindful of: 1. The word 'fake' often comes with negative connotations and thus 'fakeout' can be harmful, be very careful of the language and terms you use to describe your trading as depending on how you have a term defined in your mind, it will affect how you take action and execute your trading plan. 2. An analysis of a chart in one moment of time will not always be relevant by the time you make the trade. A good analysis requires constant information gathering using multiple time frames and from pre-trade to post-trade.

"THE ART OF WAR"

HAIL TO THE RTM

HAIL TO IF AND ALL OTHER MEMBER OF THIS GLOBAL SOCIETY

Peace be upon you FOLKS

At first I prefer to write an introduction

Introduction

For two months, that I am here . In this period I have learned a lot
from you. I had not seen a gathering of this magnitude. Before I came
here I had fun playing with chart and drawing my analysis. Andicators
and all other painting tools .

But now I believe that a blind man could see the light if and only if it is touched. After pass the following topics

RBD,DBR

CP

SUPPLY AND DEMAND

FTR,FTB,…

I intend to continue my trading journey here . I will be starting what
an ENGULF means. But first I would like to infrastructure to topic.

Before we begin I would like to emphasize that I am a novice and this is
 just what I've seen in this two month. So all the topics that I write
can be misleading. But all my efforts is that I can prove things to
myself. I thank all those who have helped me in understanding. And at
the end, I apologize for the lack of English language.

The smallest member of this community

Salivan

First, I will address several questions.

1-What is the market?

2-Who will drive the market ?

3-What is their purpose?

4-Why RTM ?

5- What are our weapons ?

6-How a tool works?

7-Why it works?

Now I try to answer these questions in my point of view .

1-What is the market ?

I think the market is a jungle .there are the number of bull ,the bears,
 the dogs, the lambs and the pigs in this jungle that they fight to each
 other's.

2-who will drive the Market ?

In my idea the dogs .they called them Big Boys , Smart Money , IT s .

Dogs are loyal to their commitments. And I think all the things that one
 need in this jungle is loyalty to its commitments. So that They
eventually wins.

3-what is their purpose ?

What are their obligations ? They need to empty the pockets of others either bulls or bears .

4- why RTM ?

For me , because RTM showed me in what areas ,the moderator of this
jungle is waiting for it's prey to hunt them and it is not important if
they are bear or bull or lamb or pigs. Here, kill or be killed.

5-What are our weapons ?

There are a lot of armaments in this castle.

SUPPLY & DEMAND,RBD,DBR,CP,ENGULF,FO,3DERIVE,QUASIMODO,CAN-CAN,FLAGS and some others.

6-How a tool works ?

In the videos, Mr. IF has told us how a tool works and how we can use them,

also the masters wrote some articles for us, that I call all this collection, the art of war .

7-why it works ?

This is the most important part .because the I think it's more important why a tool work that what it works .

So that I start with RBD,DBR s.

What is RBD ,DBR ???

RALLY BASE DROP :

Generally We call it supply . it's The resistance against rising
prices.it Contains the worst buyers and also some decision points that
sellers exceeds buyers . so that if any decision made there that price
is too expensive we expect in future the big boys can grab some orders
from unsuspecting traders or the worst buyers here again . so that this
zone is full of DPs. I think all the market are DP s.in this case Some
decisions have been taken to reduce the price . but why they think price
 is here too expensive ??

Psychologically, people tend to repeat their decisions in life the
decisions that altered the course of prices in general are important to
us. So that if the price is reduced with these decisions we call this
area that the decision have been made in it, supply (RBD).and the same
applies to regional demand(DBR).some decision have been taken that price
 is too cheap so the big boys can grab some orders from the novice
traders like me in that area in future again.in this case some decision
have been taken to rally the price and support it.so This set of
decisions in that area, that the price is cheap cause a DBR for us that
we call it DEMAND area .

But the quality of development of these areas are important to us. How
and in what form they are formed is very important. Do they have a firm
decision or indecision has occurred in past ??these are also important .
 Another issue is approaching the prices to these areas.so that if price
 approaching to a fresh area as a compression we can expect that area to
 work again as before. But if price approaching the area Strictly we
should wait and use other weapons .

I think all the market is fear and greed. Those CPs represents the fear.
 And high volatility is indicate the greed . so that in greed we should
pay more attention to other weapons why the opponent does not fear
losing and very assertive in approaching our privacy. our privacy is our
 castle , where we already have seen fighters failure. If you look into
the real world you will see that the losers always fear at The places
where they have failed there . So this is a psychological reason. This
forest is a mirror of the behavior of its residents.

After a number of failed raid to break up the castle If they want to
break the barrier must gather more power so they go down to
reinvigoratewe, call it deep pullbacks. This is what we see in the real
world. Castle also been hitting so that it's too weak for the next
attack and we call this consumptions of the orders. Weakness or strength
 of the castle can be determined from something that we call it SUPPLY
& DEMAND. I want to say that I see the difference between SUPPLY
with RBD and DEMAND with DBR . I will explain the reason, In future.
Therefore the more attacking to a castle cause it weaker and in the next
 raid, it may be rejected by the stronger amount of attackers.

This how I read the story .

After that we have some other weapons to determine whether a castle resistance against the attacks or not ?

Something that called CP. Compression is a kind of fear. But sometimes
this is fear that gives courage. My fear is what gives me the courage.
Again, these two issues are related to underpin our castle .A new castle
 usually resistance against the fear of the attackers .

Retreat or recess of warriors in the way up toapproaching the castle is a
 sign that they fear . After reaching the Castle The first warrior who
fail ,break the morale of the fighters . On the other hand if the army
on the way forward reach to a coward Front ,Of course, it will be faster
 to defeat it .

now what is the difference between SUPPLY and RBD ?

Imagine we want to build a fortress. a fortress which contains many
castle that Each castle has a flag . in my idea even a strong fortress
on a loose ground cannot withstand the attacks .so that I consider
supply as a ground as the foundation of the fortress and consider the
fortress as RBD. vice versa for DEMAND and DBR too. In the RBD the upper
 castle in this case the extreme edge of the fortress is SUPPLY area
that resistance against the Attackers.

The question that must be asked here is that Why this Classifications are important for me ?

If attackers can infiltrate a castle after a while they vivify their
power then march in the same direction of the seepage to approach
another castle on their way . how much to be returning to shore power
depends on the strength of the fortress collapsed, that RTM call it as
ENGULF .

I have another question:

Who make this ENGULF ?

No one in particular , The only things that make penetration occurs are
the fort foundation strength and the strength of the invaders blows.

The question is whether the big boy makes an engulf or all attackers make it?

Or do engulf pre-made and big boy sees it and then decide for it ?

This question also are right and logical .

In my idea all these issues together, provides the ENGULF :

A.

The weakness of the land on which the castle was established on it . In
 this case SUPPLY & DEMAND (Combination of fortresses that collapsed
 earlier)

B.

Amount of fresh attackers and how long it takes to accumulating fresh power to continue their way .

C.

BIG BOYS (heroes) are also analysis the war and novices are do it too .

I will try to prove and also improve this story .in the next part of this article I will try to anatomize the topic engulf .

END OF PART 1.

Any comments would be really appreciated

The smallest member of this community

Salivan

THE ART OF WAR

PART2

In the previous section PART 1 I tried to tell clip of a battle.

A war in which fighters are trying to conquer the castles in the air.
Decisions should be taken to conquer a castle. Places where decisions
are taken are important for us. The think tanks! If you want to destroy a
 castle ,at first penetrate to the think tanks .

Before conquering a castle it should be breached. We as a trader there
is no matter if a fortress conquered by bulls or bears . We're just
looking to make a profit in this war and wherever a permeation occurs we
 accompany the fighters. So we want to be loyal to our rules, not the
rules of the war. In the meantime, there are signs to those who deal
with THE RTM ART OF WAR.

WHAT IS AN ENGULF ?

The most important question in RTM training camp. First of all I want to describe a hypothetical battle.

Suppose that an army is advancing to conquer the enemy positions. Enemy
positions include a number of castles that formed a fortress. To conquer
 a fortress its FLAG should be conquer. As soon as the flag of first
castle was removed we must ask ourselves a few questions.

1-

What is the position of the conquered castle?

2-

Where they come from and where are they now?

3-

Is there a nearby castle, which is already under attack?

4-

After the conquest of the castle and down the old flag, did the attackers have raised their flag?

5-

Where is the nearest room to think and also where is next think tank that should be conquered?

Answer all these questions will help us to be able to properly read the
map. And all this story is only to know that, the forces after pulling
down the enemy's flag ,retreat to rest and gather strength again to
reach the goal. The aim is to flag down the next summit.

Therefore , THE ENGULF is a sign that tell us in advance there is a goal that has not been realized.

In next part I try to make some images from the different battlefield.

END OF PART 2

WITH REGARDS

 SALIVAN

This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads regarding trading:

We're always looking for signs of what the big guys are doing at
significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing, there's no
trade

So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide their orders in
the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty sure of their
intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before the turn

If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just turn
immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them to
fill all the orders they must fill.

This is why we wait for an engulf. This shows their intention to reverse
 price. Then we watch them trying to hide their orders in the market on a
 retrace, ready to take price to the origin of the move

 IF

This is all there is to the market nothing more ,nothing less .

read this golden rule over and over again

BUT WHY ENG HAPPEN ???

ENG is a sign , ENG is an unrealized TARGET and ENG is a trick also.

here is an EX :

In the FL above we have an important DP to break prior barrier as supply
 zone. Those retailers who sold in point 2 with the SL above the SUPPLY
ZONE when their SL hit it make a buy limit order and the demand
increases (LQ increases) but it's not big enough for filling the smart
money's short orders. for example in point 2 we have 700k offers (the
supply consumed 3 times so that it's weaker than before, less sell order
 than before) then we need 1000k bid for increasing the price, and after
 increasing it, the hit SLs turn to buy limit orders and now we have
[(1000k-700k=300k)+buy limit orders + break out traders ],by this
algorithm the demand increases . And this growth of demand will continue
 till the supply exceeds demand again (BIG BOYS orders fill).

I point 1 some trick happened:

ITs sell at a lower price than before and also buy it to make confidence
 for those who are really glad (wow we bought price in the lower than
before, Celebrate!!!

But in fact that was a trick .and by this trick (selling the price in a lower price other smart moneys says:

WTF, one of our friends sold USD/JPY in a lower price, we must help him
in the upper side to short and forcing the price to the demand, now the
ITs are happy and celebrate!![For more note: pay attention that the FL
is not real demand (source) it is ignored supply] .

AND HOW they can grab some more orders from unsuspecting traders???

by hitting the sellers SL and encourage break out traders they can make
pools of LQ for their short orders .look at the zone in point 3.in the
zone 4 again we have the same scenario .

 failed yet to reach one? All these things should give you a heads up on

breakout traders are really getting trapped nearly everywhere.....they

 in the market...they were stopped out by a few pips and now market will
 leave without them....so they join because it looks so promising and
they dont want to miss this good trade because they were taken out by a
few pips...but of course price will turn there and will take out their
stops...and maybe invite them to open another position because now they
think market is going in the other direction....of course they will be
on the wrong side of the market again...this cycle repeats itself over
and over again...

posts.text:
Lately I had a man-cold, and for a while during that time I'd open the chart and feel I had no idea what I was looking at.

I knew I knew the market, but there was still something inside me telling me that I wouldn't be able to read it

This wasn't upsetting at all , because I knew full well this malady would pass and I'd be back on top of it again.

This can happen to anybody, due to illness, fatigue, fear of failure, fear of success, or any number of other causes.

For a student this can be very distressing and debilitating.

But it need not be terminal. The problem is not that one's read has
gone. The loss of the read is just a manifestation of another problem in
 life.

That's why, when we lose it, we must step away from the charts, and look within ourselves to find the unresolved issues.

Once we've faced and fixed them, we can get straight back to work in a
better state than if we never had the problem in the first place

I remember when I was learning the market, I'd have these EUREKA moments, which were wonderful!

I'd think to myself "I've got it! I've got it!" and imagine that now everything I did would be perfect from then on.

But it wasn't. I'd still not be right all the time. Soon I'd get another eureka moment, and think I had it again. But no.

There are a number of lessons which need to be learned, and each helps.
After all these lessons are learned, it still takes time for them all to
 fit together.

Once they do all come together, we don't think "EUREKA". Instead we sigh, and say "I'm ready".

IFMYANTE

ps.RTM not only taught me the market's behavior but also the life's behavior

posts.author: hndrk
posts.text:
Hello Salivan,

With 'average spread' I mean that if the spread on a pair stays around 1
 pip most of the time than I would call the average spread on that pair 1
 pip.

And with spread I mean the difference between the buy price and the sell price.

So if the average spread on a pair is one pip than for a buy limit I would add that to my entry point to ensure a fill.

Example: If my level is 1.00 and the average spread is 0.10 then my buy limit is at 1.10.

Thank you.

Hi kutumbaba

you are very welcome here

About Engulf , in fact our weapon in the war between sellers and buyers
is ENG as it's the intention of ITs to push price up/down . with out ENG
 trading will be so hard to find the correct direction of price , so
that if we want to know their intention in future we must pay attention
to their secret signal that they give to each other in past . in every
TF always we have an ENG bcz ENG in term of Order Flow is the only
reason for price movement . so Engulf of important S/D is an unrealized
goal for big guys .they use ENG to show what they want in future , every
 ENG has it's own target and in that target big guys again make an other
 decision to respect the target or break it . after break a target(ENG)
then new transaction of orders execute to hold price up/down in future .
 so generally with out ENG there is no ENG .

the question is this :

which engulfs are important ?

OK , just engulf of important S/D , all the supply are a reaction to a
better price as true supply and for demand Vice versa , demand is a
reaction to a true demand . our true transaction of orders is FL. FL is
the power of nations and price .reading the market in my idea is a
science but it's also an art to identify your enemy and the way that
they think about you . this war is about money as all the wars are about
 money .where money printed and where they used it to execute the orders
 is important for us . if you want to understand this i suggest you to
read RTM .

about second question :

after ENG where should we enter in the direction of ENG ?

OK, IMO , we trade in the direction of ENG like the the same as ITs in
those places that we have free order flow to push price in the direction
 of ENG. so that we should read the left orders , but how ?

with reading past , always past show you what will happen in future ,
but again how ? OK, those people who control our money , our future our
dreams and our life as our masters are the peoples who are very
sensitive and lazy to change their prior decision not only in the market
 but also in their life ,since 1761 up to now they are using the same
plan to play with hope and fear of nations before reaching their targets
 in all wars (financial, Geographical,historical and .... ) .

how to find free order flow ?

read past and wear ITs hat on your head and imagine you have billions of
 dollar to put in the market . imagine how you can make LQ by stop
hunting , imagine how much money is behind those places that we call
them interest area , imagine how many people scare and be happy with an
spike up or down . imagine how many peoples waiting for buy in demand
and sell in supply , so where do you turn price ?

exactly in a place that all retailers excited and close a winner trade and open a bad one. exactly in true supply and demand .

hope it helps you

regards

Salivan

posts.author: salivan
posts.text:
Ifmyante quotes

 If the signal is given by the market mover (an engulf into a new
zone), then price is very unlikely to break the extreme of the zone it
just came from. So, if you have the patience to wait at the last
remaining set of unfilled orders in the origin, you can be almost
certain that that price will be respected.

 There is absolute order in the market. Nothing at all there happens by
 chance. That's why it's so easy to read what's going to happen next.
There are rules which are strictly followed; so much so you'd imagine
it's all run by algorithms, up to the moment when the signal is decided
upon, and straight away thereafter. There is zero chaos in the market.
It's elegantly designed; a beauty to behold.

 Fakeouts are extremely easy to predict. Most SD traders still look
directly left, which is the big shortcoming of Supply/Demand trading.
It's further left again we should be looking.

 Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that
supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the
extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell
short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders. Extremely
 simple stuff.

 We always look to what S or D are reactions to, rather than just S or D themselves.

 Look for tricks being played on approach to a place where a trick was played, and you'll find where price will turn.

 If you can look beyond S/D, you'll see that the Flag Limit is the only
 true place to look for PA for a trade. Trade these levels and you're
taking gambling out of your method.

 All we can ever hope for is a bounce at these levels, unless we are
certain that this level is the deepest possible point of retrace after a
 previous engulf. Without that, we must watch PA as it develops, both
before and during the trade. Set and Forget trades can only be taken
once the signal is given and the target is clear.

 Being patient is absolutely vital for making giant trades. We must
wait for the very best possible places before we enter; the places where
 you'd expect great PA to react.

 If you're around to watch the PA unfold, it's rare your stop should
get hit. Price will so very often retrace enough for you to get out
without a loss. That's why I wait for the very best price to TT - it
tends to keep me in the black.

 I'm not even a part time trader now, so I miss nearly every piece of
action there is. If I ever open the charts and see a trade opp right in
front of me, I take it. However, I usually get between 10R and 25R per
trade. If I lose, it's usually no more than the spread and commission.
There are between 5 and 20 such confirmed trades available every day.

 First of all, we need to understand that time has no place in any read
 of the market. The only way to be completely sure of where a FL is, is
to be there when the break occurs, and mark the highs and lows as they
occur. Within a minute they can be obscured by a candle, but we'll know
exactly where they are. If we're not there to watch and mark, we must
use the full candle as a FL.

 If we've had an engulf and are getting in on a RT, we must always be
ready for a diamond to occur, especially if price hasn't yet hit MPL of
the zone the original bounce was a reaction to. So, if we're not going
to be around to watch PA, our stop must be beyond the original FL.

 Funny you should say that, as I teach to always and only trade within a
 flag. Sometimes the flag will already have developed, and sometimes the
 flag is to be made while you're in the trade. Either way, always trade
within a flag.

 Attune yourself to what the buggers are doing, and don't let them fool
 you. Just know they've got orders to fill at a level, watch them fill
some on approach (CP), see the momentum, and watch them come back to
fill more orders 'til they've had their fill.

 This perhaps should be the first thing that anybody ever reads
regarding trading: We're always looking for signs of what the big guys
are doing at significant areas, and if we don't see what they're doing,
there's no trade. So, on approach, if we see the big guys trying to hide
 their orders in the market, we see compression, and can feel pretty
sure of their intentions - to get in as many orders as they can before
the turn If we don't see this, we can be pretty sure that it won't just
turn immediately, as there usually won't be enough orders against them
to fill all the orders they must fill. This is why we wait for an
engulf. This shows their intention to reverse price. Then we watch them
trying to hide their orders in the market on a retrace, ready to take
price to the origin of the move.

 When we see decent CP coming into the base of a pole, we are very
often safe to touch trade the base. The safest thing to do however is to
 await the first engulf into the cp zone as confirmation.

 Very often a zone will break strongly and price will retrace but fail
to retouch it. This is still the FTR - the confirmation of a new trend
(do a study of how price reacts and how far it goes after hitting this
spot). So an FTR can be first time back, but doesn't need to be.

 During holidays, volume in the market is often greatly diminished.
This would lead some to imagine that price hardly moves. But. Say
someone decided to put a truckload of orders into the market. If there's
 nobody else in the market to oppose these orders, price can do nothing
but shoot away. So remember. Low Volume can = High Volatility.

 Until now I have been so unfocused on the charts that my exits have
been very sloppy. My trade plan now has a couple of variables, but
essentially I'll let price travel back to the other edge of the last PAZ
 in the TF I'm trading. If it engulfs, I'll exit on a RT or a break of
the next LTF FL. If it rejects, I'll let the trade run and await exit
PA.

 It's all about getting into the mind of the market makers and trading as they do. Nothing special.

 Most of my analysis comes in after the trade is entered. Before taking
 the trade, I do as you said - simple - it's really easy to find pockets
 of orders which will bounce price, and if they happen to be at great
htf levels, even better - there's the highest chance of them giving
maximum pips. What I do certainly looks like touch trading - picking
tops and bottoms, but what you said belies that. These are not tops and
bottoms, but retraces to the best price to re enter. Once I'm in though,
 I'm never guaranteed massive returns - sure price will bounce where I
enter, but I'm never complacent until I've seen the engulf. In fact, I'm
 never really complacent at all. If PA tells me to get out, I must get
out!

 Many might misconstrue us as pattern recognition traders - we're not.
Certainly while learning we look for recurring patterns in the market.
But once we understand them, what becomes most important is WHY the ITs
made them. It's paramount to understand that it's not enough for the ITs
 to simply move price. They must also get massive amounts of orders
filled in order to make maximum gains. They must also refrain from
giving other ITs false signals, which could ultimately cause chaos for
everybody. Think of these things as you study, and you'll be able to get
 into the mind of the market mover.

 Here are just a few targets for price, and the QM level is a big one.
Certainly we need to get PA for entry before or once it's hit. If it
breaks, then the same level can have the opposite effect on return.

 Once price engulfs a level, all that's important is how far it
retraces before hitting its target. While the pockets of orders remain
in this RT, it remains strong. If price totally compresses (picking up
all orders) forward from the tip of the RT, then we will look primarily
for the orders at the entrance to said CP.

 To the ITs, candle closes don't mean a damned thing, so please don't use them in your own analysis.

 A line is not the answer. Certainly, you may draw a line, but you must
 then go into the LTF to find a DBR/RBD on the right side of the LL/HH
swing which covers that line. That RBD/DBR will be your box. You can
scalp from each of these, knowing that it may only be a scalp. If you're
 simply setting a PO, then you must set your stop beyond the FL the
HH/LL is a reaction to.

 The usable engulf is the one which hasn't hit its target. Every engulf
 has a very specific target. Apply that statement to your charts and
eventually you'll see what I mean.

 Being only a sporadic trader (I really couldn't sit and watch the
charts all day anymore!), I tend to open the charts from time to time
and ask myself what's coming up in the next few minutes for me to take.
If I'm lucky, I'll open the charts when we're at an HTF level. If not,
I'll gladly take whatever high R M1 or whatever is there for the
picking. 30 pips with a 3 pip stop is exactly the same as 150 pips with a
 15. If there's nothing decent to take, I shut the charts.

 If I were asked where to trade, in one word, I'd say: Stops

 I'm way too disorganised to use limit orders! I just open the charts
from time to time, and if I see the ITs scaring the retailers into
closing good trades at a good level, I enter. I'll take off some of the
position at the first target, so if my stop gets taken I can profit
overall, then watch PA level by level. If price doesn't get into a big
zone quickly, I'll usually get bored and go flat, having made enough to
cover my next week's expenses. If I were truly meticulous, I'd treat my
exits the same as my entries, and trade up and down all day, but trading
 is usually way down on my to-do list.

 Certainly there's an awful lot to learn here. But if I were to
summarise what I think is most important, I'd say look to an engulf into
 free space that hasn't yet hit the origin (tg). Very often it will
retrace deeply before advancing to the origin. Learn to spot these, and
you'll be better equipped than most other traders out there.

 Price moves from PAZ to PAZ. The clear target for any trade after an
engulf is the other end of the PAZ in that TF. If you zoom out to HTFs,
you may find the TG is even further, but if not, stick to the TF you're
in.

 I just want to warn you though that watching candles is an absolute
waste of time. It distracts you from reading the story of price. The
chart is a page, and a candle is a word. A word in itself has little
meaning; it can be taken out of context. Sure, a sentence can be very
powerful, as can a group of candles. But to get a real sense of the
story, we need to view it all as a whole - be aware of how this
paragraph relates to one many chapters back, and get a sense of where
the story will lead in the future.

 In essence, we know that if price engulfs South, it wants to move down to the last engulf North.

 We want to read the story of price, and believe me, price has a story!
 You'll need to go further left to get your analysis right. Yes, you've
marked levels well, but what are those levels a reaction to? Without
knowing this, you're just gambling. So, look left, read the story, and
be better equipped to predict what'll come next.

 Ask yourself "Why did price shoot up from there?" You'll answer
"Because someone wanted to buy a lorryload, but there was nobody willing
 to sell at that price, so price shot up to find sellers." The next
question you'll ask yourself is "Will he have left orders to buy again
at that price?" The answer is usually "yes". Next question is "will
price reverse from there?" The answer is, "Well, it may well bounce form
 there, but we won't know if it'll reverse until an engulf tells us it's
 reversed"

 Of course, the extremes in one TF can be midrange in another TF, which
 is why it's vital to manage your adds in the lower TF until they break
into HTF trades.

 Okay! One giant clue: If something which should have been important got ignored, then it will be given great import on return.

 Personally, I love to dissect the HTF zone, in LTF, and look for a DBR
 or RBD within it, where price had broken out of a box and failed to get
 back in.

 Whipsaw engulfing - a fakeout followed by a quick return breaking the last zone. It's great PA.

 An excellent Supply or Demand zone is one where the future has already
 been written. Having done some study of the markets, we know that once
we have an engulf of a zone, price will want to go to the origin. So we
look to where the trend change was confirmed - FTR.

 You must study the zone which is being reacted to just as much as the reaction itself.

 Just consider the manipulation of hope and fear at turning points, and you'll have a very valuable eureka moment.

 When you begin to see the symmetry in the market, you're making one of the final steps in reading and predicting it.

 High R is High R, and these trades happen with great frequency. I
applaud this easy way of making good money. If you're at the MPL of an
HTF level, however, think about taking enough at LTF tg1 to cover the
HTF stop, and letting the trade run.

 A bit of simple advice, to avoid overtrading and impulse trading: Draw
 up the most important looking zones, and look for trades only there.

 We absolutely must have an hard stop, always. But if we don't have an
engulf before entry, we don't put it directly above the high or below
the low, where all the retail stops lie. Instead, we find a lovely LTF
RBD/DBR just beyond, and put it on the other side of that, so that we
have the best chance to get out at BE or in big profit from the usual
RT.

 There's no indication that a demand has been respected until the source above has been engulfed.

posts.author: salivan
posts.text:
this is the structure of Free Order Flow :

price reading article

In order to be able to trade the markets, we need to be able to
understand why price is where it is, and where it will go to next. The
best indicator for all this is Price itself. It holds all the clues
you'll ever need to work the market out. We do our trading at levels
called Supply and Demand Zones (Video), and we watch Price Action there
to give us signs as to the intentions of the big money.

Here’s what we look for on the charts:

General: HTF. Know where price is coming from and going to, and the PA past and present in all the TFs, from the Monthly down.

Specific: At the zones you want to trade, look to

Past. study the zone in all TFs, down to M1

ask yourself

Where were the decisions made? Clean S/D? Mark these lines. No clean S/D? – compressed zone

Did price really shoot away form the zone, or did it cp away?

Did the zone itself react at the right place? Look beyond the zone
further into the past. See what it reacted to. Was there a better S/D
nearby that price wants to visit? This explains many fakeouts. Did price
 originally react to the RS of a Flag Limit? It can fakeout to true SD
of the FL.

Present.

Approach.

How is price returning to the zone?

Where’s the nearest flag in the TF you want to trade? This is your tg1 in this TF. Flags in the LTFs? What does PA tell you?

Has price tested the last flag on approach? (good sign)

Has price compressed into the zone in this TF or LTFs? (good sign)

Is there big news on the way? Has there just been big news?

Reaction

In LTF, does price react violently to the first decision point? Does it quickly engulf the nearest S/D? (good sign)

Does price simply CP away? Maybe it wants to go to the next decision point

If the first decision point breaks, watch the signs on approach to the next, and, of course, reaction.

Chew this over for now. Apply it to your chart history. Apply it to
as many failed setups as successful ones. Millions of them if possible!
Capture and file them all. This will help make it instinctive

posts.text:
"Free Order Flow "

in order to read the market and understand every price movement in the
market we need to investigate the it in terms of true orders that
executed in the market .we know that FLs in the only true place in the
market that this sets of orders executed in . and also we know that this
 kind of orders executed after engulf of opposite orders .

so what we need again if we can see those orders ?

as i told before there are lots of FTRs in one TF but there are few FLs .
 but every of this FLs also has it's own value in terms of order flow ,
some are good for a bounce , some will be break with out any bounce and
some hold price .

how we can understand if those FLs have the orders to hold price or not ?

this is the most important question that we should ask every time we
look at the market .as we know ITs can not fill all their orders in one
place so they have to accumulation the orders to reach their targets .
but the places that they are going to start a new trend is FLs. in this
case they trade in monthly TF and start accumulation the orders in 1 min
 TF to their monthly target . so the targets are always important than
the entries , bcz if we understand the target we can understand also the
 whole story for price .

but what is FOF and what's it's rule in reading the market ?

Free Order Flow is the sets of orders that Clean and apply always in the
 market by pro moneys , they will create the scenarios by this to shake
out retailers and grab some more orders from unsuspected traders . as we
 know our target and entry are always FLs , so when they engulf a target
 in fact they are buying /selling in a higher/lower price so in it's
scale then are coming back to accumulation of orders and they want to be
 the only one that sell or buy in the market , but the question is this
how we can understand the ITs scenario in the price movement ?

this takes thousand of hours and full control in every scale to
understand what they are going to do next . as a basic we should
understand price reading article that is in the markepedia and also put
ITs hat in our head .

in order to understand this we should always ask this questions :

where price coming from ? a reached target or not ?determine your scale
that you want to trade . always look at HTF as it has the major map of
price movement and enter in lower TF as they create this map .

where is price now ? is it in S/D so it can fake to the extreme orders in to the true S/D .

and other parts in price reading article .

all my efforts here was to apply reading the market not drawing rectangles ,

if we want to understand FOF we should understand FLs scales,and
targets at first and we should understand big losses for ITs if they
don't take out some sets of orders , for example we want to trade daily
TF and we find a FL in daily TF to trade it , it's not guarantee that
they engulf a daily TF FL for showing us their intention for future ,
they can engulf a lower scale FL inside that daily FL but don't engulf
the daily FL , this is an other way for ITs to showing their intention ,
 that's why i always say try to read the orders .

look at the charts below :

so FOF has a big relationship with price reading article and targets for
 pro moneys . they always show their intention inside their targets .

how to be able to read FOF in the market :

if i want to write a proper way i can say without being able to read the
 market in terms of FLs and Orders and price reading article we can not
read FOF , and it's need massive focus to read it .

some clues :

basics :

1- understand the full concepts behind RTM stuff ( FTR,FL,QM,CP,CANCAN,CAPS,....)

PRO :

1-understand FL in terms of orders not rectangles .

2- understand scale and understand this , that orders are more important than the TFs .

3-understand this they need to left the targets for few pips around their higher scale targets for future .

4-what's CP ? it's a kind of deep RT after engulf . how a CP start to be play in price movment?

these whole pieces of puzzel can help you to understand FOF

understand price reading article as an Instinctive way .

more important than others , without putting thousands hours inside the
chart there is no way to understand it as it should be something
Instinctive.

hope it helps you .

regards

Salivan

FL can be found in Left Shoulder, R/S, PreCP, a break into CP.
Previously we are taught FL established on S/R. Sali does mark the FLs
on S/R, but he just picks the obvious ones that hold price. Swap FLs are
 also obvious.

FL1 = a break of 2May1996 low.

FL 2 = swap to FL1

FL 3 = swap to his "OrFL"

FL 4 = break of 97 Oct high, resulting in a very BIG FL.

FL 5 = self explanatory

FL 6 = break of 1992 high.

FL 7 = swap to FL6

FL 8 - swap to FL3 and also break of the big FL4.

 , so QM formation (assume we are in supply) is an south engulf of a FL and a RT to a FL to grab some more orders and then continue in the direction of engulf . in some cases that FL that price RT to is aligned with the QM LVL OR LS .

so it's not a rule that always price must RT to the exact QM LVL . the RT is to a FL .

hope it helps you.

regards

Salivan

Hi Salivan, hope all is well! Have you not been trading late? It's quiet in here...

As I did my homework tracking kinks/FLs, I found one observation and it
is to do with 'scale'. And I would like to seek your opinion on this.

Is it correct to conclude the following:

1) There are kinks of various size depending on the time scale we look
at. Hence a kink that is identified on a daily chart, is more likely to
be of larger size than a kink that is found on a 1-min chart.

2) However, the importance of a kink is not a function of its size and
the timeframe in which it is found. The importance of a kink depends on
what creates it. Hence a tiny 1-min kink, created by the break/engulf of
 a Daily SR, is more important than another 1-min kink created by the
break of a 1-hr SR.

3) Following the same logic as No. 2 above, a 1-min kink that breaks a
Daily FL is going to be more important than another 1-min kink that
breaks 1-hr FL.

So now, when I draw kink/FL, I classify them using the following two parameters:

(1) Which timeframe is this FL/kink found? For me the more invisible it is, the more powerful it is.

(2) What creates this kink? For me, kink created by breaking a HTF
levels (Daily/WK SR) is more important. And of course, a 1-min kink that
 is found at key locations (LS, Pre-CP) are also more important.

I was wondering what is your opinion on the above? Thank you very much.

AK

I think the difference between two depends on what's on the left - Has it hit it's target (FL) or has it engulfed the target.

If ENGULF, then most likely it would want the very last set of orders before moving on. In the diagram case

It can happen with

1. Making HH/HL, luring traders into buying, in expectation of price
rallying (in this case can get Trendline/MACD traders and retrace
buyers).

2. Setting resistance (Double top, triple top etc.) before the MPL (In
this case can get both seller stops and buyers + breakout traders)

3. Making CP (Traders are entering left and right as this can be seen as Triangle Flag forming)

4. QM turning into DM (Trapping Head & Shoulder traders and R/S traders)

I am not quite sure about ignored levels, but I think its something along this line:

After hitting target and is not retracing enough to hit opposing FL, thus level is ignored - Orders left

If Target hit and there is no intention to make a LL

then we can expect the FL is getting respected, therefore we wait for local FL to be engulfed and trade back up to previous UFL

I hope I atleast made some sense

Dengaima

Hi Salivan, I love what you're doing here! Let me share my thought on your Gold trade. Start with Daily chart:

So, around 8 September 2017, price broke into the compression zone, it
cleared two peaks inside the compression but could not break above the
3rd.

Now going into 1-min chart to see where these levels were broken:

The important engulf should be the one that broke FL-A. Next we zoom
into the area above FL-A to see how smaller-scaled FLs interact with
each other.

Here's where a bit of subjectivity comes in: Would you drew B or C as
the FL that held price up? Salivan used B, but remember, neither B or C
broke anything significant to the left, so I drew both as I can see
price reacting to both. So what happened to price next?

Well, FL-C was engulfed and this created FL-D. Price tried to break
below B but the first attempt was not successful, it bounced back up
towards the MPL of FL-D where it reloaded and then came down to engulf B
 successfully. It tried to engulf FL-A and again the first attempt was
not successful, it bounced up to FL-D again, reloaded, and then came
down and finally engulfed A. This tells us that FL-D is very strong
since it is the source of the engulf of FL-A. In the meantime, FL-E was
created after engulfing B and also the CPAZ inside A.

Next I tried to investigate why after engulfing B, price retraced to
point [1], was it because of a iQM level in area [3] as pointed out by
Salivan?

I looked at 10s chart below:

So now, imagine we were still on the 8 September, and the chart below is
 what we were seeing, with all the analysis above, I asked myself the
question: Where would I have planned the trade?

So while I think it is logical to place SL just above FL-E, I still need
 to establish a good entry level, and for this, I need to look into 10s
chart again to see if there is a clean DP at the MPL of E? What I saw
was a small scale QM, so a good level to short would be 1355.343?

posts.author: naascott
posts.text:
Here goes something! I can feel the confidence increasing as I keep making great calls on price action with what I have learned here What better way than to share them in an online journal where like-minded folks can see and comment.

Many thanks, RTM for making this site possible. I truly believe I have found home!

For a trading plan, here is one slightly modified to trade harmonic patterns, and will adjust where needed as learning progresses.

Desired TF's: H4, H1, 30, 15. While paying attention to higher TF S/D areas and LTF decision areas. RVR - 2:1 - 4:1 Max loss on any trade 59 pips Max loss P/day 3% Lot size micro: max 0.3 no higher until 59 successful trades called / logged. Weekend rule: trades must be +75 to hold otherwise closed. Entry rules: Distinguished PA as taught by RTM must be present. Clear S/D, DP's, & S/R areas taken into account in each set up. I am finding I like to look for trades around poles and flag limits, FTR's and FTB's. Trade mgmt: First rule - always accept risk as a loss before taking any trade. Second Rule - set break-even at earliest convenience. Third rule - TP targets. With my harmonic trade plan, first tp was at 2:1 (prz to B point). Here, I will try to target obvious DP's that line up with rvr, and get a feel for what works and will adjust accordingly. I will also gladly accept any guidance from anyone who offers it.

Looking forward to the journey!

For a start, I had been browsing over at trading view, which is a great place to create online charts, and up pops a notice that I should go long on the USDCAD - that a great "buy" was setting up. I immediately wanted to go take a look and see for myself. So I put on my RTM glasses and lo and behold I saw something totally different. Now perhaps the fella was seeing something more longer term, but what I saw was a great possible short setting up.

Here is a screen cap of the set up as it was happening: Note this is not make anyone look bad. But to me, it seems rather revealing of some of the stuff being taught out there I suppose.

I jumped into the 4 hour and placed an ellipse in the area where price was at, and then added an arrow down. I saw the engulfs and to me it seemed as though price wanted to go back to the origin of the 4hr supply area.

You look to be doing just fine. I've noted on your chart below what I look for in a QM.

Just keep digging into the different TFs in the charts to see why price turned at levels. Use CP, FLs/FTRs, swap etc in your analysis. Go painstakingly through a chart in M1, reading PA as you go. Look to see can you identify the special levels.

It is important to keep interacting with all the other traders who are learning and posting on the forum, by giving your own analysis. There are a great bunch of traders posting right now, and the forum has never been in better hands. Make sure you are part of it and move along with them.

posts.text:
Hi Scotty, Great vids

I hope you don't mind, but I' had a thought about your QM trade. The QM pattern that you've marked out...H-L-HH-LL-QM... would be a bearish QM. I'd be looking for that sequence at the top of a price swing, not after a fall. The bullish QM....L-H-LL-HH-QM..that I've marked is invalidated once the LL is broken (your L). and forms a Diamond (to shake out the QM buyers). Looking left you'll probably see that your LL was price the IT's really wanted to buy at... and munch up some nice QM buyers stops!

posts.text:
Haven't posted in a while, but I liked what I was seeing on the E/U

A quick look at the daily, and price is calling me to an FTR

Then, I jump down to LTF's and start looking for smaller FTR's and where price might want to show signs of reversal. I see a nice CP zone, a nice RN, then two smaller FTR's just above the RN. I then see what appears to be a small poke into the CP zone. Now it's getting interesting.

I think these type of set ups can be traded time and again with amazing accuracy.

Here is a little set of management rules that can be used in doing so:

1. If you see an approach to a daily FTR. 2. Mark off any clear compression zone as price approaches the FTR. 3. Locate all fresh, non tested FTR'S on lower time frame (5 min 1 min). Look for big RN's near area. 4. If you have two FTR's on the lower time frame in close proximity of the RN, place entry at RN and stop above no more than two FTR's. PIP risk could be 10-20 pips max or whatever % your account will allow. 5 Target other side of CP zone.

Great RVR!

I have embarked on primarily focusing on the last FTR's into the highest/lowest points of price structures (ie - QM's usually). Finding the origin of an engulf of these areas are often great places to TT with very little risk. For example, many of these from the 1 minute time frame can offer many times the reward of your risk. Testing in FXT2 with about 8 pips of risk as the max has been eye-opening.

Now think about that! Risking 8 pips, you could lose 7 out of 10 trades and still make money with a reward of 15.1. Actually, you could still make money with a 90% losing streak on 10 trades where you only won one trade with this kind of RR.

posts.author: naascott
posts.text:
I don't think it has ever been more clearer to me than what I saw in this particular area of price on the GU. How interesting this is becoming.

The seeming logical progression 1. Price gives a clue it wants to go higher by engulfing into a CP PAZ above its flag. 2. Price engulfs out of flag indicating it wants to also go lower. 3. The second engulf point seems pivotal in that it creates a key leg that has the RBR that is used to hold price up to create the FL that is used to create the "High and Low"

of our QM. 4. Price after retesting FL, moves on to create our higher High that contains two very important FL's - the one becoming the point or origin where price will offer up the completion of the QM. 5. Once the FL is engulfed, the RBR is then used one last time to allow price to come & create the lower low of the QM.

posts.text:
Some sweet PA just prior to Crude oil inventories this morning. My goal is to get so good that I can see this as it is happening. This, to me, is the real skill! Forward Sight Reading <<< we want this

1. An area of some last demand below near the top of what appears to be a cp paz, (which seem to of had a nice clear engulf).

2. Price comes off a local higher high and FTR's & stalls before dropping into it. 3. Price performs a quick engulf back up and then drops to demand. I mark that structure and look for price to hold. Sure enough it does, price then surges nicely not too long after - engulfing the FTR back up, 4. Price rises to new highs - engulfing a very nice level above - then falls back and swaps nicely with recently engulfed FTR (which is also swapping with the last FTR into the local higher high, by the way) 5. From this point some small clues are given, price RT's back and offers a HH (green rectangle). Price then RT's back and offers a HL (yellow rectangle) 6. We are now 30 minutes away from the inventories release. And it wasn't surprising to see price momo past our chop box / fake highs and into an area that held price up before reversal to new lows. (i.e. the key FL / origin of move down, MPL, or whatever you like to call it)

Lastly, it was not at all surprising to see price surge down once it got below our demand area. Thanks for reading

posts.author: ShadowPit
posts.text:
Having a journal of any sort is very personal. I have made my journal public here first and foremost, because I do not trust myself to keep an accurate record privately of my learning. Secondly I want to climb to the top of the RTM ladder!

I envision that I will update this first post to form a table of contents, an organised linked record as opposed to a linear read through. I am imagining coming back to visit regularly over the 12 months time to see a post littered with links to nuggets of discoveries I have made and documented in this journal.

Let's begin.

posts.author: ShadowPit
posts.text: H1/H4 - I noticed GJ had been compressing to a marked Support line now Resistance. M5 - I drop down as low as M5 to find price structure at this previous support line to find the pocket of potential supply. An FTR was found. Caution - Price has already visited this area. An FTB has been and gone. Trading to the right - Asian session sent price towards the FTR with a strong bullish candle. But price stalls, price consolidates and does not break higher. London Open is also unable to break higher, PA on the M30 chart I had been observing creates long upper wicks two times. I send my sell order to my broker.

Continuation: M5 - Price declines sharply, engulfing the lower time-frame support and forming a new FTR immediately after with momentum. Caution - Price bounces noticeably forming a V shape on this timeframe. I am always cautious about this type of approach. Trading to the right - Caution noted, price hasn't created new demand, nor is price reacting of 'fresh' demand on the HTFs I observe. Price actually stalls before the FTR and begins to curl over. Conclusion: TG1 & TG2 reached. Hindsight: This trade very quickly showed I could have doubled the trade reward by waiting longer. I can think of various tasks for my to-do list. This could be the catalyst to collect statistics on taking different type of trade exits. There is always a decision to be made at each stage of the trade. Entries. Active trade period. News events. Exits. Perhaps in this case I could have employed a trailing stop. Or waited for PA in the opposite direction. Sorry guys just thinking out loud here. Expectation vs Anticipation vs Doubt vs Cold Hard Statistics! <--- This is what I want to build. Sometimes I feel you can spend so much time trying to find that perfect entry and when you finally get it, it doesn't end there, your guard is a little down, and then you realise the tough battle to fight when it comes to exits. Maybe a little more. Maybe a little less.

juniormaiafx wrote: Just look that... is that right???

weekly). A decision needs to be made one way or the other. Unfortunately your analysis will not be a reliable indicator for price reversal..

If you think you feel ready to learn QMs, I would recommend you focus on finding QM's that happen on LTF. There are LOTS of them. The best QM's to learn from will be very obvious and have a form of symmetry about them. Please re-read the article and observe these things about QM price: 1. The location at which the pattern occurs 2. The symmetry of the pattern 3. The momentum of each engulf 4. The approach 5. The reaction 6. What causes the low to form, what causes the high to form, what causes the lower low to form, what causes the higher high to form? (and visa versa for the opposite setup) 7. How far does price go as a result of the setup?

After you do this, find in historical charts price patterns that look almost exactly like the examples. There's more than meets the eye.

What I think you really should do very thoroughly FIRST is to make sure you've done all your homework. Get comfortable identifying supply and demand, support, resistance, rbd, dbr, ftr, fl, dbd, rbr. Know all that stuff like the back of your hand.

While you're feeling confident you are now an expert at marking up your chart with supply/demand etc., be sure to look up the definition of the word engulf. Think about what it means in regards to trading. Dream about it daily! I do. Why does price engulf anything? What does that actually mean? Apply it to MULTIPLE time frames. One engulf may not be greater than the other. I want you to keep coming back to this forum for advice but please make sure you do the homework. Practice makes perfect. Good luck friend.

Hello Shadow Pit,

I have a logistical question about limit orders that I would like to ask you since you seem to be well versed in taking them. I have two charts of the USDCAD below. The first one is a daily chart. On the daily I noticed a solid break down of daily support at the blue dashed line. When I zoomed in to the 4hr chart, I noticed a clean, strong 4hr DP to push below the htf support line, and thus, I found it fitting to put a sell limit there with the TP at daily demand. (Note, the actual order is not pictured in the charts because it was right next to another pending order and looked messy, so I just used lines to represent the order..) Now I placed my sell limit before the area of daily demand was hit with the expectation of my 4hr DP being the thing that was going to drive price down to this htf demand area. Now here comes the tricky part..

The question that has plagued me for quite some time is should you leave a limit order in place after your TP line has been hit??? When I think about it logically, it seems that since the area of daily/ htf demand was hit, this could invalidate my sell limit since htf SD holds more weight that LTF levels (and rbr/ drd zones are more so trend continuation zones and don't usually cause reversals after htf levels have been hit). If this is to be the case, then I would expect my 4hr DP to get blown through and become a retest level for price to use so it can rise to the daily/ 4hr source of the move down to look for shorts (pictured in the second chart.) The other half of me still thinks that we should still get a nice bounce off my sell limit area since it was such a clean strong and untested area of supply. So how would you personally play this Shadow Pit?? The scenarios I see are to wait for ltf confirmation in the 4hr DP since my take profit at htf demand was hit before my order was triggered. Secondly, I could just take my order off and expect it to get blown through and retested on the way up to the daily source. Third, I could leave the order on as planed with the same TP. Last but not least, I could be more aggressive with my trailing stop/ profit taking once the position is triggered by the sell limit or ltf confirmation since the sell trigger initiated after htf demand was hit. Also, do you ever leave limit orders on if your take profit has been hit before the entry got triggered??

posts.author: ShadowPit
posts.text:
sylntthunder wrote: Hello Shadow Pit,

The question that has plagued me for quite some time is should you leave a limit order in place after your TP line has been hit???.... So how would you personally play this Shadow Pit??..... Also, do you ever leave limit orders on if your take profit has been hit before the entry got triggered??...

Hello SyT.

Firstly, good job on running through the various scenarios you could be making, but you're still wondering which scenario you choose will lead to profit? What I think you really should be asking is how do you know what trading decisions to make as well as the when and the why? A lot of this will come down to how disciplined and concious you are with your decision making and knowing (having the PROOF) if those decisions are profitable for you over a large sample size (You've forward tested the sh*t out of your decision making, you have tried various scenarios of the same trades and compared the results).

At the end of the day you will have to make one decision over another (trade or no trade, limit order or wait n see etc.) and what might be 'right' one day will be 'wrong' the next but one of your key objectives in trading should be to minimize risk so you've got the 'wrong' decisions covered that way at least! Remember.. you simply cannot 'WIN' every single trade regardless of how well prepared you were for all possible scenarios.

OK OK ok so I have rambled and I haven't told you anything you don't already know...guess what I probably can't actually help you for this one trade nor decide for you the most effective approach in the future. But here's the part where I make some suggestions anyway. Treat trading like a business right? This is one way to address the dilemma...gather PROOF that one decision is better than the other.

If you want to put in the real hard work, FORWARD test 100 trades similar to your USDCAD analysis and compare the stats (equity curve, expectancy etc.): 1. In the 1st account place the limit order, with SL and TP and leave it be. 2. In the 2nd account place a limit order...AFTER the REACTION validates the zone, with SL behind reaction pattern and TP with consideration to price structure of the APPROACH. 3. In the 3rd account duplicate scenario 1. but apply some trade management using the HTF. i.e. trail the stop, what is the reaction, how does this effect the outcome of my SL and TP placement, how is price behaving as it comes close to your sl or tp 4. In the 4th account duplicate scenario 2. but apply some trade management using the HTF. i.e. trail the stop, how does this effect the outcome of my SL and TP placement, how is price behaving as it comes close to your sl or tp 5. In the 5th account duplicate scenario 2 but instead use a market order where you can comfortably define your risk and reward 6. ADD all the scenarios you're interested in understanding how it effects your longer term performance

...I think you get the picture..You're testing combinations of decisions and seeing which ones are the most effective and which ones are useless!

By doing this, not only will you learn a thing or two about reading the market but you have now collected high quality reliable EVIDENCE, reflective of YOUR decision making and you will know where YOUR strengths and weaknesses are in regards to applying each scenario and you will know which scenarios you will want to continue forward with. Essentially, you're evolving your own trading decision tree/process map/flow chart. You're eliminating unreliable trading decisions and focusing your future attention on improving profitable decisions. Rinse and repeat. Eventually you will be 5 years deep in your career and all that hard work and the knowledge you have gained about your trading decisions will be called 'experience', and you will instinctively know what decisions to make and when.

Trading is a lot of hard work. Let's revisit your USDCAD dilemma, assuming it aligns with all the RTM teachings... except of course for the fact that you're committing to a trade decision before you've even witnessed the approach or the reaction. Maybe you just leave the limit order with SL & TP, maybe you are right and it's a perfect trade, but ask yourself, what does that really mean in the grand scheme of things, do I rule out all the other scenarios because this one time this strategy worked? Of course not, you want the BEST trade execution & trade management strategies that work for you, the only way to find that out is to measure them against each other, and choose what works for you.

I personally wouldn't have a limit order here anyway, because as you have established it has indeed invalidated the original analysis and price is now coming FROM a place of evident demand and the supply to stop its run is yet to be determined (this could be a rule in your trading plan like 'too much uncertainty for a limit order'). posts.text:
I'm glad you asked.

How many times have you watched price react to something and gone, 'oh boy I wish I traded that when I noticed it..'? To be honest I didn't think for too long when I executed, I saw a setup (H1 selling) and I dropped down to the LTF and participated with a limit order, with reasons based on probabilities (more likely vs less likely) and potential expectancy (is there room to run!?).

I suspect you are a little interested in some deeper thought process, so let's try and 'unpack' what I might have thought in the moment.

Let's highlight reasons to justify it. What did I see? What boxes did I mentally try and tick off for this setup?

1. You have price consolidation (range) 2. It is consolidating in a 'good' spot on the HTF 3. With a break in the anticipated direction and an accompanying pole 4. This pole engulfs the bottom or top of another consolidated area (an FTR, a FL, a DBR, RBD, etc) (not at the time of entry.) 5. The entry is placed at some sort of FL, FTR, DBD/RBR that formed near where the break of the consolidated area happened (a retest)

So we can very quickly assess that I ticked off 1, 3 & 5. There is no need to think twice about entry. But let's address your potential concerns with what I have just presented:

You might argue that with criteria 2 that price/reaction wasn't at a good spot because it hadn't actually traded in the HTF supply zone, but have you looked at a weekly or a monthly chart lately, which way is price going? Maybe that doesn't help so much, so let's be practical... draw a line through 1.4250 and look at it on the daily...zoom it out a little, let's not split hairs about 5-6 pips, this is a GOOD spot for LTF PA to form, previous support becomes resistance. I didn't speculate on this, price signaled its intention when it was ready to go and I had a place to define a setup, with setting the risk and places to look for profit pending future PA.

Which leads us onto your other concern...that demand below. Why didn't I wait for criteria 4 to happen before looking for entry? Well, I already spotted profit potential (room to run!) before it did engulf the next barrier, and the most recent momentum was down as the H1 printed.. You've got to remember I have a tiny 6 pip stop and the next potential barrier is 24 pips away. 4:1 instant potential. As we now know it went on to run to 100+ pips, I did not know that would happen but I participated in the moment knowing the potential that existed and I treated it one engulf at a time.

As for your long setup, I think you took a very reactive trade or an ill informed one, you haven't given enough consideration to the new information right in-front of you, it just engulfed the last printed H4 demand. Not your A+ setup...Price is telling you a story, use everything it offers you...

I want you to have a think about something else: Probabilities...Accepting loses....Risk Reward...You MUST have this in the back of your mind when you trade. I had accepted at entry that I could very quickly get taken out with the next M1 candle, there's always the chance of that happening, but I would have persevered and kept on trading similar setups if they came up, as long as the initial macro setup was still intact, or until price either made a higher high, or I have exceeded my attempts. I would gladly lose 4-5 trades at 6 pips for a shot at an immediate 4:1 or in this case 15:1. But in reality it's never going to get to that many loses on one setup, because by 2-3 losses I should know that I am wrong or wake up to the fact that I am failing some very basic entry discipline! Where as some traders will trade 30+ pip stops for one chance and sweat it out for a few hours to make a lazy 2:1 or 3:1, and they might have a perfectly legitimate reason to do so, such as not being around to baby sit trades..But I think that is a very hard and slow way to make money.

Hey mate,

I see it as one engulf that has happened in a moment in time and that simply isn't enough for me to want to just blindly hold to that ultimate target you have identified..

So for illustration purposes only and on one chart (H4) only. This is for a really simplistic view of how you can be pretty mechanical about how you might read the market on any given day

Area 1 of this chart is completely off limits unless Zone A is engulfed. Area 2 of this chart is completely off limits unless Zone B is engulfed. Area 3 (our target) of this chart is completely off limits unless Zone C is engulfed.

So with all that in mind you can pretty much conclude and create a single trade plan of action that to realise the Target price must first:... Engulf Zone B...AND... Engulf Zone C... AND.... NOT Engulf Zone A.. That's a lot of things that need to happen. AND the picture is going to bloody change on its way there (or on its way away!) AND price will create new zones within the same range! eep..It just takes a while for it all to sink in to our brains to act upon..so as they say...practice makes perfect:)

So hold up a second! The Day is still young and there will be new PA printed in 4 hours, 8 hours, 12, 16..20 that you will need to incorporate into your read of this price chart and add it to the plan!

AND you still need to include this same logic to multiple time frames to give yourself the best chances of reading intention correctly.. I guarantee that once you do this a few times over you will eventually realise that its not just a simple matter of saying ONE FL engulf on ONE timeframe has automatically opened up some overhead target (because if you resign yourself to that statement of truth you will ignore everything else that's in front of you that tells you the complete opposite, which is the ultimate thinking trap)...now...let us go have a look at Ifmyante's post hereand ponder why its just easier to take most of our profit at tg1 i.e. your immediate obstacles

Training your eye. That's what it boils down to. Many trials, many errors. It's just going to take time. So! Give yourself a break from time to time, the subconscious works in mysterious ways. Another way you can learn is to try trading without a stop (put an OH shit! stop for safety) for a while and exit manually where you would normally put your stop. This forces you to continue thinking about the market reaction at your predefined level and proactively make a decision on when to exit, when to hold, when to move your stop back in. It buys you time to think about what price is doing, observe HTF, observe correlations, what you might have missed, where it might be targeting, where else it could reverse, why you should or shouldn't stay in the trade and accept the bigger risk.

When you get it wrong and price blows straight through, that usually means you have missed one or two things completely. I've got a growing checklist that fires off in my mind when I'm observing charts, placing trades, deciding what to do next...it only takes a few extra seconds to stop, breathe and think... Does it make sense in the HTF? Does it make sense in the LTF? Where is price coming from/going to in the HTF/LTF? What has price just done on approach? Broken a range? Broken some other FL I ignored? Flagged? Compressed? Finding support/resistance on new price action? Is there evidence of momentum at this level? Is the level even fresh? Time of day? News? Is TG1 far away enough to make this worthwhile? Any correlations to support the strength/weakness of the currency?

You're good at this. Find out the reason why something failed, make note in your head and move on.

p.s. Have you visited the Price is Everything thread on FF? I find myself going back there every other month to view Reds and Dropped Onions posts through the lens of my new understandings. Observe how they read price, its very iterative, in the moment, baby sitting the trade at every turn. It's a great way to learn to apply your thinking on top of theirs.

p.p.s. The trading without a stop suggestion is purely to get you out of the routine of setting and forgetting and into the zone of continuous decision making and understanding the reaction and if its meeting your expectation or not. You can worry about the R:R stuff after you feel confident that you're reading price correctly and consistently.

Hello, I still feel like risk:reward and probabilities don't get enough attention on this forum.

Here's a story (queue violin): when I first got interested in trading, probably much like some of you did, I created spreadsheets which linearly took my meager account deposit from rags to riches in a matter of 50 excel rows! As it turned out, I am not the kind of trader who can string together an infinite amount of wins in a row. So a while ago I created a pretty basic spreadsheet using excels Random number generator, which would model a simple equity curve a little closer to my reality. Stumbled across it again today, made it presentable, thought I would share it. Alternatively, there are also a multitude of modelers when you google equity curve generators.

Discipline and patience; something I struggled with from the beginning and still do to some extent. Having something visual, whether it be a trading plan, wallpaper of an expensive car or house or a sexy randomised equity curve helps to remind me that this is a long term game, and that it is actually okay to be WRONG, and have a string of losses, and the importance of getting over losses quickly. It really is amazing what IRON DISCIPLINE will achieve.

Food for thought: How long would it realistically take you to execute 1,000 quality trades, and what could your equity curve look like after that type of sample size?

Reasons for aborting or refining strategy or creating new strategy a. If price breaks above orange zone strategy 1 is a failure. b. If price breaks below the red zone ellipse, strategy 2 is a failure, but strategy 3 may not have been executed. Strategy 4 would be to look for new supply/FL to form at the ellipse. c. etc.

What is the meaning of all this? Highlighting the importance of planning ahead of time. Whether you do this planning in your head, through a written personal journal or just plain marking up charts and questioning the logic; the fundamental point is to extract the most value and profit from trading RTM style, you must continuously evaluate a chart so that you can: - identify obsolete trade strategies and cull them - identify new opportunities that didn't previously exist

- cut your losses - hold onto your winners - reevaluate risk - win

We really do have a lot of control on how we profit from the market. If you can't control the final outcome over the distance a trade idea can go, at least control what you sacrifice as collateral should the trade idea not go according to plan. Sound. Risk. Management. Ever wondered why when people post their positive equity curves they don't go at a 45 degree angle? It's because it takes LOTS and LOTS of attempts at seemingly inconspicuous trade ideas with low risk, and potential for high reward. You will experience, lots of small losers/breakevens, lots of small wins, a few big wins. The few big wins are what will point your equity curve upward. /rant over

posts.author: ShadowPit
posts.text:
I am not too scientific about chart or trade selection as there are so many opportunities on every chart every day. When I first sit down I will click through around 20 pairs 1-by-1, pretty quickly, and eyeball the charts. Usually a chart will simply pop out to me before I get to the end of the 20 pairs and I'll drill deeper.

For example, in the chart above. It was a very common and obvious price setup which I am used to at a glance.: 1. There was a strong push down creating a pole. 2. In the middle of that sharp move down you can see the FL formed at the break of the low on the left. 3. You can observe clearly the price retracing and "engulfing" the FL to the left which forms the signal to go long at the decision point and/or QM level. 4. The only thing I had left to do was check that price was coming from a HTF demand and that was that. This is a very common setup that occurs within a few hours after high impact news events.

It ain't always that easy though, the majority of other trade setups I observe and take usually require far deeper investigation, they can often be more complex and not conforming to any specific price setup model like the one described above, they can also be time consuming to come to a decision on direction, and then require a lot of waiting for the right level, but this can all be managed with alerts, which I do use. But yeah, I hold no allegiance to any one pair or currency, but from my behaviour of scanning through 1-by-1 I usually end up trading the same pairs!

Unfortunately I don't really have any qualified advice for you. Given your fatigue, I might suggest you at least start small and note down 1-3 different setups you are comfortable with, like the one I have described above, and work on identifying those setups on 4 pairs only and pick those charts apart over the course of a week and reassess on the weekend whether you need more or not. It definitely helps to be well rested as well:)

posts.author: ShadowPit
posts.text:
Hello,

Firstly, I do not know where it will retrace to, nor do I create any expectations on where it will go. Secondly, that engulf you have marked off doesn't really tell you much, it also doesn't tell the same story on D1 charts, which suggests price has bounced from D1 demand. The area you have marked reversal, isn't very specific and thus I don't think it adds any value to your trading analysis. In regards to the fakeout you have marked, if you look on the daily its a perfect touch on a previous resistance area, so take from that what you will...Be careful with how you label things on your chart, you have labeled things on your chart which in combination give you conflicting bias on where to trade from and where to. Ok so onto what I think about the EURUSD:

EURUSD H4

EURUSD M15

If I were to short this chart the blue rectangle is where I would look for PA on the H4. ** I am interested in approach, because if price enters that area it will quite possibly engulf the FL with the green circle outline. If price creates demand when it breaks this FL I would be interested in seeing that demand engulfed before looking for short opportunities on the LTF. If I were to touch trade a short, I would be looking for price to approach the maroon area on the M15 chart. Ideally a compressed approach. Some things I would be cautious about if price reaches this area include what price looks like on the Weekly/Daily charts and if it is congruent with the LTF analysis, I would ask myself what this means for my trade targets and where I can logically take profit off or hold further. **Conversely if this area were to break I would look to find any long opportunities.

When you create some sort of a plan like the one above, you begin to anticipate where price will go (targets), and when your targets are correct more often than not, you begin to take trades in the opposite direction you're anticipating as price has not yet reached its target. So the other question you should be asking yourself is, how do I get in long, and where should I get out? It will ultimately come down to the other areas of your trading plan such as your profit objectives, risk management, how long you're willing to wait for price to reach your area, and how long you're willing to hold.
