Before I post again about the LQ gap I decided to give a brief about the mechanism of order flow.

When we look at the market watch window in our trading platform we'll see instrument's symbols and next to it two different prices, one is bid and another is ask or offer. These prices are offered to us through an online broker who is not just a broker but also a dealer.

Here is an explanation of the difference between a dealer and a broker from “Trading & Exchanges – By Larry Harris”

“Dealers and brokers help people trade. Dealers trade with their clients when their clients want to trade. The prices at which a dealer will buy and sell are the dealer's bid and ask prices. After they trade with their clients, dealers then try to trade out at a profit by selling what they have bought or by buying back what they have sold. In effect, clients pay dealers to take their trading problems. The dealers then try to solve them at a profit. Dealers profit by buying low and selling high. Successful dealers must be excellent traders.

Brokers are agents who arrange trades for their clients. They help their clients find traders who are willing to trade with them. They profit by charging commissions.”

Dealers are market makers and also known as market specialists, so they play a big role as a market participant beside other pro money, understand how they play and you'll play with them. Now we understand that online brokers act as brokers and dealers.

Back to the market watch window, the ask/offer shows the lowest offer price which the market is willing to sell at and for you to buy, the bid shows the highest bid price which the market is willing to buy at and for you to sell.

I’ve already explained in posts #
	82
 &
	83
 that there are two types of orders “market orders” and “limit orders”, in the below image I’m showing an example of an order book aka; DOM, Price Ladder, Level II. Bear in mind this is only for explanation purposes, in the currency and metals market there is no depth of market, it only applies to centralized markets such as futures, equities and commodities. Of course banks and dealers have their own order books but it only shows their clients orders. Back to the image, the offers column for sell limit orders, bids for buy limit orders and in middle is the price. I’ve taken eur/usd prices as an example, the orders are standard lots/contracts (i.e. 200K = 2 lots and 1M = 10 lots), the two prices highlighted in yellow presents the Bid/Ask prices which we see on our market watch (spread in this example is unrealistic and only to make it easier).

Anyone entering the market with market orders will be buying at 1.3010 and selling at 1.300. Now let’s say you place buy market orders of 500K (5 lots) what will happen?! Your orders will be executed at the lowest offer consuming the 200K at 1.3010 and a 300K out of 500K at 1.3020 and this price will be the new lowest offer with 200K limit orders, so as offers were consumed price moved up to 1.3020

Another scenario; you are placing a sell market orders of 1 million (10 lots) what is the outcome?! Your orders will be executed at the highest bid consuming the 400K at 1.3000, the 200K at 1.2980, the 300K at 1.2970 and a 100K out of 500K at 1.2950 and this will be the new highest bid with 400K limit orders, so as bids were consumed price moved down to 1.2950

This is how price moves up or down by consuming orders, and bigger orders generate buying/selling pressure (momentum) pushing price in its direction consuming smaller orders until it stops (slow down /stalls) at a new price where there are opposite bigger orders are placed.

One last thing, the stop loss pending orders considered as limit orders and when it’s executed it adds pressure in the opposite direction.

Hope it makes sense.

posts.author: FX.Sniffer
posts.text:
benhur wrote: I hope it is alright to ask you to elaborate more about "Liquidity Gaps"?

What is your definition for it, and how (and why) you expect of price reaction at this zone?

There is no easy way to answer this question as it requires a study of the market microstructure which explains how the exchange occurs in financial markets and the order flow process, but I’ll try my best to make it simple.

First of all, kindly refer to my first post
	here
 for some of the terms which in my opinion share the same meaning/definition.

Second, take a look at my previous post.

Now back to basics, we know that in a normal market there is a buyer for every seller and vice versa, this is considered a stable state of the market as it creates a balance between supply and demand and maintains a stable price value, and as the imbalance occurs in supply and demand the value of price increases or decreases. The balance state on chart is presented by a consolidation in price, and the imbalance is presented by a high volume/momentum candle (also known as a sign of Pro money / Institution’s buying or selling). If we zoom into the consolidation (LTF) we’ll find other states of balance and imbalance.

In post #
	90
 I tried to explain the orders execution of Pro money but not in an accurate way for the sake of simplicity but I fixed this in post #
	138
. So to recap, to have your orders executed at current price you need someone on the opposite side with the same number of orders otherwise price will move too much from your entry until it finds an opposite stack of orders. Retail traders have a big advantage over Pro money since their orders gets executed at current price, a benefit that Pro money doesn't have due to their mass orders which gets executed at different prices as the price moves away from their initial entry. Hence they tend to accumulate/distribute their orders through positioning, re-entering on retracements or even creating them as well as fakeouts.

By now you understand why the sign of pro money buying/selling is presented by a high momentum candles aka liquidity gaps, but if you didn’t then continue reading.

A liquidity gap means low liquidity! How?! You know that for every seller there is buyer and vice versa, but you also know that online brokers doesn't guarantee a non-slippage or a no requote during the time of volatile news due to low liquidity, and you can clearly see it on charts during such news when a long spike or a high momentum candle is created in seconds. A broker wouldn’t take the risk if you’re buying because they can't find you a seller unless they are willing to take the risk by selling to you as a dealer.

So how could we say it’s a low liquidity when price moves in a high volume?! Again, we know that high volume candles are signs of big money, institutions etc. entering the market or in control of the market pushing price in their direction...that is true. However, the liquidity in this case is being injected from one side only (the dominant side) hence the name liquidity gap and the equation “Volatility = High Volume + Low Liquidity”.

Now bear with me...The "normal or balanced state" of the market is to have a seller for every buyer thus maintaining an efficient change in price value, so when the market moves up or down either in consolidation or in a ladder steps behavior then it’s a “normal balanced state”, but if it moves up or down with a high volatility and momentum then its "abnormal or imbalanced state" and it’s a sign of domination from one side.

So what is the conclusion?! The dominant side (pro money) would want to collect their profits as soon as price reaches their targets which results in market returning to its previous state (rebalancing) on a wider scale and filling up the liquidity gaps.

I've answered the definition part in your question; now let’s answer the other part related to price reaction. I hope you were paying attention to the Fiber and Cable as I suggested in post #
	134
 and you can see the marked LQ gaps in the process of getting filled.

Look at the attached Gold daily chart and see the price behavior when it broke through a decision area/major key level of significance, creating a high momentum candle as a sign of one side in control bulls or bears and how they wanted to push it higher or lower, of course price will return to fill the LQ gaps but later in the future, not at the present time of the incident specially not when it starts creating a new DP/Supply/Demand as pro money position their entries. On the other hand you can notice larger high momentum candles (LQ gaps) gets filled the same day or next day but this happens when price fails to break through a major DP or key level and this is when pro money are accumulating/distributing (bottom and top side of the chart).

The market is in a constant state/phase shifting from normal to abnormal, balanced to imbalanced and back again, just the same as in ranging to trending and back again (refer to Wyckoff Market Theory), and every range contains the two phases if you zoom in, the same applies to the bottom consolidated area in chart.

Supply & Demand trading style is in harmony with order flow and it works according to this stuff. IMO if we learn how the market works from the beginning it would save us a lot of time in our journey.

Hope I made it clear and simple.

posts.author: FX.Sniffer
posts.text:
MCFly wrote: I'm not sure I like the explaination in the vids about why the gaps tend to get closed but in the end they mostly do.

Everyone points at S/D, Balance and Imbalance in a different way without explaining the real mechanics behind it.

Although in my previous posts I tried to make it clear why LQ gap gets filled but I’ll repeat it in a simple phrase;

In LTF LQ gaps gets filled because - When pro money enter with their big orders it moves the price away and against their entry price, therefore they await for price to return to their entry price to continue adding their orders.

In HTF LQ gaps get filled because – When pro money closes their buy orders they become sellers, and when they close their sell orders they become buyers.

Thank you.

Reading COT (Commitment of Traders) charts to identify the long term market sentiment;

COT charts are based on COT reports which are published by the CFTC each Friday on 19:30 GMT.

From outsource: There are several reasons why COT charts provide valuable information about changes in the position commitments of traders:

- Flips in the overall positioning may be an accurate trending indicator

- Extreme positioning has historically been accurate in identifying FX market reversals

- Changes in overall number of contracts can be used to determine strength of trend

The below chart shows the recent Commercial Traders Net (Hedgers, Exporters, Importers), Large Speculators Net (hedge funds, banks etc) and Small Traders Net.

What concern me are the Commercial and the Speculators, and the index values of 100 and Zero on the vertical axis. Knowing that when one is at 100 the other will be at Zero and vice versa.

So, let’s take a look at the euro COT chart and compare it with eur/usd chart.

Starting with old history from 5 Jun 2012, Com traders index was at 100 and Spec index at 0 and eur futures price 1.2446 (marked by a vertical dotted line on COT chart).

Present time on 29 Jan 2013, Com traders index at 0 and Spec traders index at 100, and eur futures price 1.3665

In below chart prices are marked by horizontal lines and dates marked by vertical lines. The first lower crossing on the left side at [1] represents the old history and the second higher crossing on the right side at [2] represents the present. The weekly chart for an overall view and daily is for a zoom in view.

Now, let’s start the analysis…..at [1] the Com were very long and Spec were very short, so what happened in price? It moved up above support level and into a decision area of supply followed by a move down to the 1.2446 value and bounced up retesting S/R level then back down into demand area from weekly TF where the stacked buy orders are, and price reversed in direction to rally up. Now open your eyes wide open and look at the level 1.2446 and see how it acted as an S/R flip level.

So why price didn’t reverse directly from 1.2446?? Simply because of positioning.

At [2] present time the Com are very short and Spec are very long, so what will happen? Currently we can see price bouncing down from 1.3665 to S/R level and two stacked decision areas of demand, but where are the stack sell orders on chart??! Yes at the higher decision area of stacked supply. So let’s see how it goes in the coming days.

posts.text:
Very important lesson for lots of traders, even the expierenced one's.

Gold is in a HTF down trend so what we want is to enter shorts as long as price prints lower lows. And this fact occured just a few days ago on April 4th. Accomplished by big momentum down candles, so in no way we want to look for possible longs here, maybe scalp one's but in no case any long setups. We let the big boys decide to print higher highs on HTF so that we can enter at the retest with the lowest risk, but trying to get the turning point just doesn't make lots of sense.

I'm also in this progress which gave me lots of "Aha-moments" and some very easy entries with ZERO risk and ZERO drawdown - because you go with the trend. So all you have to do is find where the big decisions were made from the big boys.

FX Sniffers last post contains all the information. Especially his first picture. "Engulfed previous low - engulfed previous low - engulfed previous low"... this should always be the first thing that comes in mind when looking for trading decisions. And on daily the level at 1589 (support line) that got engulfed by big momentum candles AND engulfing previous low makes up a more than perfect entry. I do not know how many traders took this trade at the 1589-level, but I am quite sure that many many of them just earned their money not even for this month, but also for the next - if they held it like FX Sniffer did.

Got a PM that better be answered in public...

The message was saying that in our early days of traditional S/D trading we used to look for candle engulfing pattern and on RTM here almost nobody uses it but the engulf of the zone is in play. So, I have a question: why don't you use the engulfing candle pattern and why do you treat the zone engulfing as more reliable?

My answer is:

I still look at candle engulf when I look for S/D clusters and I look at other candle patterns as well, but the engulfing of areas is more reliable because "Price Dynamics" is not just a simple candle pattern but "a study of price in motion in regards to the supply & demand order flow", in other words; "the history of price action/reaction and behavior in relation to the supply & demand".

Moreover, the candle engulf on HTF could be an engulf of a significant area on LTF, the areas could be decision points or highs and lows which are areas of significant interest and engulfing them means price wants to travel beyond that area, as well as bears or bulls on the other side are starting to weaken.

What if you’re looking at the line chart and you don’t have any candles?!

Think of candle engulfing as the basics of S/D, and the area engulfing as the advanced S/D.

3D VS. 3T

There is a difference between the 3 Drives and the 3 Touch aka 3 Taps, both are a result of distribution and accumulation.

3D falls under the compression category and is a reversal move.

3T falls under the trend following category and is a continuation move, but also could a compression when price returns to it and breaks the 3rd touch.

The below image explain the difference and the 3D has been explained by IF

. As for the 3T its simply a 3 touch of a trend-line.

In below image and on the left side is an example of a 3T into a down trend-line and the third touch was preceded by a lower low and formed a lower high, on the right side a 3T into an up trend-line and the third touch was preceded by a higher high then formed a higher low.

In IF's example you can see both patterns in his chart, a 3T followed by a 3D. For more on trend direction and the role of highs and lows refer to the

posts.text:
I’ve received an important pm that better be answered here, here is a part of it:

“Now before I met you guys here at RTM this year my view of what I can make in forex was different. I was considering 40% annual a good return. Now when my friend and I see your returns (yours, and others so on...) it's hard to believe this is possible. My friend looks at statistics and says that none of you guys are in Forbes 500 but with this % return all of you should be in there. Also claims that none of world best traders could average over 100% yearly. Well you get the point.

Now my friend has the point I agree, but also I spend days here and I see what you do and how. Well to make this shorter could you maybe shed some light for me?”

Now my feedback, I know why I’m not in Forbes. However, I had the same question regarding other traders (not necessarily in RTM) who shows their amazing consistent winners and makes you think that it’s so easy, and the issue that they don’t explain the reasons behind their entries and they never show you the bad trades. Some might learn something from their charts and others might not but in the end they could mislead you into a disaster. The internet is a double edged sword, anyone can post anything wether its false charts or demo results. Here in RTM we tried to avoid this by digging deep into the price action and teaching the reasons behind our entries and what is expected next, and we wish from whoever learns from our posts to carry on the torch and pass it over to new members.

So if you want my advice whatever results you see on the internet by others doesn’t mean anything, all you need is a method or to learn how to read the price and your results depends on you and your circumstances, if someone is showing unbelievable results it’s not necessarily fake or even true, and it doesn’t mean that you could achieve the same because by end of the day it all comes back to a certain factors.

1)	Your personality & your circumstances: in short you can call it “psychology”, human behavior is common and the proof is if you meet a group of traders and share your trading stories you’ll find that you all share a lot in common, the same mistakes, fears, greed etc. and only the elite who succeed in this business are the ones who succeed in controlling their feelings and bend the circumstances to their advantage. Each trader has different circumstances that could either help or add pressure, for example are you trading part time or full time and do you have enough savings or do you need every cent you can make from the market, does your family/GF/BF supports you or not and so on.

2)	Your startup capital: the amount of money in your balance plays a big role, the bigger accounts the better, of course rules are made to be broken and a trader can make thousands out of a hundred but also there are traders who wasted millions.

3)	Your money/risk management: this one is much related to 1 & 2 as a cause & effect. MM could vary depending on capital and the personality, bigger capital allows you to use bigger contracts and bad MM could demolish big accounts, solid MM ease psychological pressure and bad psychology destroy all MM rules, the examples are endless.

4)	Market state or condition: in some market conditions you can make huge profits, in others you can’t make a clear decision. For example if we consider you’re implementing a solid MM plan trading one instrument and everything is perfect the monthly ROI will never ever have the same result for the 12 month.

In fact all the above mentioned points are related and connected to each other as affects & effects.

So back to the Forbes list, I’ve never posted consistent profitable trades neither here nor anywhere else and never claimed that I achieve a certain monthly ROI, so this question is irrelevant to me but it could be asked to others if they claim or show such results. As for the yearly return % in general it depends on all the above points. In some of the live competitions traders have achieved more than a 100% ROI in one month, as for institutions, banks, hedge funds, regulated managed accounts etc their risk profiles are monitored & controlled by regulations so as their returns. Moreover, not all private independent traders show off or publish their ROI. Therefore, if you find anyone on the internet or anywhere else publishing their results without teaching then either they are scammers or showing off or looking for investors or selling something.

Here in RTM we had an objective to teach and maybe someday become a physical academy or even startup a fund management, this is why most of our posts are showing the why and how before or after and not just after the facts results.

So in short take the trading methods as it is or tweak it and ignore others results, don’t think about it, in the end your returns depends on YOU. I don’t guarantee that you’ll make a 100% yearly ROI or less or more because I don’t know you or your circumstances but I guarantee that you’ll save a lot of time in your journey.

Cheers,

posts.text:
Founders and members of RTM,

I’ve been in this market since 2003 and during all these years I’ve never been an active forum member or blogger, until the PIE thread back at FF has changed that for some time all the way to AG until our journals were taken from us then Ifmyante gathered our group and we all helped in founding RTM.

The idea of RTM was to create a global home for traders who share the same trading style based on a pure price action and we all have shared the same dream of developing this community to become a free school for new traders and in addition to a fee service to the elite or whoever want a special mentoring, as well as to start up a fund management service by creating our own capital corporation as you can see in the ladder page where I myself have created the organizational structure slides. We all had great ideas and each of us was unique with his/her own unique expertise and skills. However, speaking for myself the first few months spent in founding RTM and establishing the foundation of a trading group has caused me too much as a waste of time on something that requires a non-trader to work on. Since the end of 2011 and I’ve been a full-time trader and my life was great before RTM till it flipped over. Let me be clear here, I’m not blaming RTM for anything, actually I blame none but myself. However, I’ve learned a great lesson from that period of time and a true serious trader who depends a lot on his trading income shouldn’t be able to spend time on chatting, blogging, online communities, etc. unless in a certain special cases if the trader has a spare time, or has another source of income, or seeking a new source of income. Everyone in the cyber space has his/her own agenda and when agendas are gathered together they either meet or collide. My own agenda is to be the best I can be as a trader in regards to knowledge and experience (this has already been confirmed to me personally by the testimonial of an institutional trader and a market maker), and to make my first million out of trading which I failed to do this year. All I desire is to live on my profits from trading as much as I can squeeze out of it, no need to manage other’s money or to offer a commercial service because if I do so then I’m not the TRADER I’m seeking to be, I could be anything else like an analyst or a teacher or a scammer but not a TRADER. With my skills and a decent capital I can achieve what I desire so why should I waste time and efforts on anything else when I can spend it on family, friends, by the pool, or whatever!!!

However, as mentioned before if I have the spare time and it’s not going to affect me in any bad way or cause me trouble then maybe I would give sometime to blogging or whatever even though that I’ve learned one should keep his knowledge to himself, but depending on a human nature some are too generous or like to give something back.

My advice from an anonymous to every serious trader and it’s up to you to take it or leave it, seek the knowledge anywhere you can find it but don’t waste your time on anything more if you want to succeed as a trader. Trading requires a lot of mental awareness and sensibility so don’t let anything or anyone else disturb it. Stop wasting your time on child’s play and pay attention to the chart or read macro-economic or intermarket analysis or anything that will help you to develop and reach your extremes. Start reading between the lines and stop being spoon-fed. Don’t chase everything that is glowing in the dark or you could end up in a deep hole. Stop arguing about nonsense and let it be, take what works for you and create your own style, don’t mimic others and don’t let them affect you with their own styles, be unique and digest whatever you can, don’t try to absorb everything one-shot, take your time and step by step.

Having said that, I’ve decided to remove myself from any association with any website/group which I don’t solely own or have a full control over, including RTM and by doing so I’ve published my own articles in my own blog, and I don’t know if I will ever post over there or do any new activities but for the time being my work should be in the right place where it belongs. Therefore, I ‘m requesting RTM to remove my articles from the markepedia and any other work I’ve done for RTM except for this journal which I expect to remain here for the old time’s sake.

This shall be my last post here and any other public forum. Please don’t post any questions or send me any private messages which I’m not going to answer. Oh yeah, and I’m not asking anyone to follow me because I have nothing to offer and have no secret agenda.

RTM admins, founders and members I wish you all the best and many thanks to all of you and please forgive me for my faults and mistakes.

May you find peace.

FAREWELL.

FX.Sniffer

well maybe Price movement and candles could be the place where RTM

Weekend should be the best time to re-catch some lost coffee time and
re-pay sleep debts. Unfortunately, having watched lite course video no.1
 and also youtube video

"simple way to know where price will bounce", plus having read a post about MPL that i did (
	readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/hom...gnment-dbr-rbd#60256
), something just kept me awake and wondering despite my attempt to switch off and sleep.

"STOPS" is the X-Factor. This is the IT's "it" factor after all.

Salivan posted many charts in which he drew some silly cartoons
representing IT's face, and he would ask about how the ITs want to play
--the game--.

So, really, i could've spent a good time away from the charts enjoying
some nice cookies wife just made with all kids jumping all over and
hanging on like monkeys distracting me from whatever it is i'm tryin' to
 do. Nevertheless, curiosity just easily took over, felt like an
addiction to the mind, and is extremely hard to drift away once it's
taking its toll into thoughts.

Googling everything i could find about "stops hunting", "catching stop
losses", "retailer's stoplosses", "Market maker's tricks", etc. etc.
etc. There are just so many articles about all of them, but i choose to
keep these just because of personal preference:

	www.dukascopy.com/fxcomm/fx-article-cont...&action=read&id=3329

	www.dukascopy.com/fxcomm/fx-article-cont...&action=read&id=3346

There is one particular paragraph that i'm interested in. it's as follows:

"The learning path for most traders is to study charts, patterns,
indicators, and attach meaning to these patterns. This is nothing more
than a deception. Traders are driven to stare on the charts and their
patterns or are convinced to purchase highly sophisticated softwares and
 programs that are convenient and comfortable but never proven to profit
 consistently. This learning paths are designed and promoted by market
makers for the sole benefit of their business. There is nothing wrong
with reading charts and indicators as long as they contribute to
everyone's success in the long run. But it seems that more than 90% of
traders end up losing a lot of money over several years."

ABSOLUTELY CORRECT. Why? Because it pretty much summed up what i've been
 through over these last 13-14months, if i'm not mistaken, up until i
came to know and find RTM (not just its name, but the meaning of its
name) existed. Hopping here and there just to find what works, what
doesnot work, what is hit and misses, etc. etc. Well, sadly, even after
sometime learning RTM, i was still looking for patterns and attached
meaning to patterns, for example looking for QM or DM or CP patter, only
 to find later that because of my incomplete knowledge of RTM then i'm
just still in the "deception slump".

So much that i'm trying to learn from so many great people, i'm also
finding people who is trying to learn from me. and thanks to RTM's
suggestion, it's indeed the best way of learning. how do we know? just
imagine how we were in their shoes, or how we are going to be in other
people's shoes. learning from the more experienced and teaching the less
 experienced is actually having mentors on both side of the evils. it
ended up forcing us into reflecting our own mind and soul against
others, but reacting back to us.

Even though RTM here contains a lot of puzzles, the learners (including
me, still) just can't easily break away from poisonous bad habits, i.e.
"study charts, patterns, indicators, and attach meaning to these
patterns". We will sometimes be fooled into thinking,

*ok here is break, FTR, then there is CP approach, good, let's put a
pending limit order there and put stops behind the FTR; without even
thinking who is going to hunt these stops.

*ok i see a high, higher high, and lower low, that's it. QM!! ok...
let's put pending order here put stops on HH. at least i would get a
bounce or a scalp, ok i'll exit here and/or move stops if reach there.
All i need is just a few bounces everyday so i can watch my account
grow. I don't need anything else in RTM because reading is a hassle and i
 dont have time for that. lol... the reality is whether or not, without
complete understanding of RTM, we have good reasons for somebody else
NOT to hunt these stops.

I mean everyone, incl. me, after watching lite course videos recently
uploaded, will be all over the place trying to look for "left shoulders"
 and "QM" levels. if that so, we are not so much different from those
trolls learning QM MASTER CLASS from a person who didn't even complete
RTM years back.

Well, we could argue, "no we know about FL and a place where to look FL
zone". Really? how on earth can we understand FL without going through
the homeworks and also the other masters' journals, including IF's
journal. IF's journal especially contains lots of charts that, if we
realise, often force us to find the "other" zones in order to grasp
fully what he taught. It's just impossible to understand "Price Reading"
 without going though hardwork and out-of-count hours of messing around
with charts. Disclaimer: "All of these do NOT apply to the genius, which
 certainly i'm not one of."

*ok i find this good RBD/DBR and based on my homeworks so far, i can
spot which one is good RBD/DBR and which one is not, i'm sure this is a
good one, let's put a pending order here and stops just behind RBD/DBR;
without even thinking or doing the other homeworks about FL to even know
 whether or not those RBD/DBR is reacting to the right place.

*ok i find this FL is very well hidden and it's at a good place on S/R,
so should be good, so let's put a pending order there because my winning
 trades proved good on these set-ups; without even waiting for PA
confirmation, or worse, trying to be like the master traders or IF.

There are just countless, countless mistakes that we could have repeated
 even after we have studied RTM materials. why? because we will get
distracted with so many techniques and technical operations (as i called
 it), that we always forgot that the main focus, ideally, should be to
trade along with ITs. where is the place? answer: "STOPS". It's not
finished yet. Many times over and over, when explaining a chart or price
 movement, IF would not only simply walk us through the technicals, but
more importantly also, he explained and told the stories behind the
reasons, which are pretty much roamed around "Retailers' psychology".

Had a good talk yesterday in church with a very old friend. he was
working in one of the financial institutions back in Aust as a
constultant to a group of programmers tasked to design algorithms by the
 company's trading department. We both recognised that market makers /
the "biggies" as we call it are just very cunning and evil in driving
market into corners where stops and traps are actually being "pooled" at
 times.

It's almost like a recent youtube video that just stole my interest for a little while:

It basically told how dolphins are very smart in working together as a
group to corner their preys into a corner so that they can ALL have a
feast TOGETHER. The preys can't easily get away because the dolphins
(the big money) are the one herding the trend & direction. Of
course, not all preys will get "EATEN UP", because dolphins also have
limited stomach. well at least, they ARE FULL AND SATISFIED already.

Sunday lunch time. a good "Mie Goreng" awaits.

posts.author: staurum
posts.text:
Price is Fractal

I have poured a lot of thoughts, maybe too much that i ended up falling asleep as i read and watched about it. lol

A couple of good videos that i like:

I currently follow Mandelbrot:

"Fractal" is such a fascinating subject. I thought fractal is all about
structures, order, similar shapes. Instead, fractal is beyond that. It
also encompasses chaos and unstructured roughness. Many science has
applied fractal concept into explaining mother nature and modern
science. I wont be the one explaining. Life, age, time and space, all is
 indeed fractal.

From what i understand, Fractal has size, scaling factor and dimension.

A line has 1 dimension. A plain has 2 dimension. A box is 3-D.
Sierpinski mesh is 1.585-D. Britain's coastline dimension can be
calculated. Even any island's coastline can be calculated. How can
something so unorderly, chaotic, unstructured be considered fractal?
well sea surface is, just as much as the clouds in the sky. One
characteristic of fractal is a small part of it looks/represents/mimics
the whole of it. So as we zoom in to these matters, as small/little/tiny
 as they can be, they look/represent/mimic the whole of them.

Why is dimension needed? it has something to do with scaling factor. but, what about price chart?

I dont have the answer, but somehow my mind goes to (
	readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...gging?start=75#61669
) and what charvo said

"let's imagine price is drawing a tree, price has to firstly draw the
 trunk, then the branches, finally the leaves. on the other hand, when
the tree dies, the leaves fall first, then branch broken down, and
finally the trunk collapse. there's a fixed order. when you scrutinize a
 piece of a branch, you see the same order; when you oversee a forest,
it still follow the same order...... and relate these with timeframe,
that probably helps on topic of 'scale'."

What is a trunk to some branches could be just one of the branches to a
bigger trunk. The opposite could also be true: what is a branch to a
trunk could be the trunk for other branches and also some leaves. It
really depends on when and where the piece is located. [Funnily, RTM
teaching goes the same. In that, who is now a teacher to some students
could have been once a student among others to another teacher. In turn,
 who is now a student may well be a teacher for some other students. It
really depends on when and where the person is currently. That is how
market is best studied] Also, it is assumed that the tree stops growing
for some reason or is already fully grown. It may be another different
story if we know that the tree is still growing. It will also be another
 different story if we know that the tree is collapsing. Why need to
know if the tree is growing/collapsing? Because the scaling factor will
matter and we can better identify the positioning of a piece inside the
tree if we know the full story/picture of the tree. I just dont know yet
 how to turn this fully into charts/price.

After marking and drawing some charts into a set of messy print-outs
(after which my kids turned perfectly into a chaotic paper toss game), I
 realised that

a flag can turn into a flag limit in a higher scale;

a pole in a scale is just a small PAZ inside a flag;

poles and flags stacked in one direction makes a higher scale pole;

poles and flags zoned against each other makes a higher scale flag.

As Sali often repeated to me, price moves from FL to FL. Of course he
cant tell me in what scale, but he already directs me into the
direction, i.e. deeper study of FL which is the chain-link of everything
 else.

Again, my curiosity goes back to "Investigate flag completion and evaluate how price can move in order to complete a yet to be completed flag"

Of all scales and timeframes, we need to go to the highest. so yes,
weekly is great. but timeframe doesnot matter, what we need is to cover
the whole history, so you need to zoom out the timespan as wide as
possible.

Only after working in the highest/the widest, then we can work down on smaller scales within the limits found.

So i just want to focus on the first chart, as the rest just follows through.

Now, when you say "significant high", once price breaks that high, price
 made a no-return move. So the FTB/2TB/3TB/n-TB is tradable. However, as

necessary for us to RTM. I do hope you notice what i mean here. Another
is, (my mistake that i dont want anybody to follow), only mark a
zone/level according to what happens on its left, not according to what
happens to its right. By this, i mean for every turn, i was trying to
understand what FTR the turn is reacting to, and mark that FTR as FL.

posts.text:
It's about half a year already since i registered with RTM. there is
no words to express the gratitude feeling i feel. Looking back, oct 2015
 was the journey beginning. I knew a little bit about technical analysis
 as it was taught briefly inside a subject in my university study.
Little did i know, that everything about it was just a joke.

I still remember very very clearly, babypips.com and investopedia were
my starting places. i was completely overwhelmed by all the
subjects/materials, which i thought, i need to learn/master in order to
be a profitable trader.

I learned everything i could: steve nison's candlestick, basic elliot
wave, stochastics by G. Lane, MACD plays by A. Elder, Bollinger band,
RSI, Parabolic Sar by Wilder, Directional Index system by Wilder,
chart/bar patterns (HnS, wedge, cup & handle, etc. u name it),
trendlines, moving average lines, Keltner's channel, Average True Range
channel, Fibonacci's sequence, Harmonic patterns, and so on and so on
and so on. if someone ask anything about this, i'd be SO DAMNED HAPPY to
 teach them and coach them for free so that they become professional in
those areas. Gosh, the stupid phase of my life was just pretty much
worse than wasted.

Maybe i didnt finish learning all of them to combine them all into one
trading system, but after exhaustion i pretty much concluded "they were
all hits and misses".

Then i bumped into a person who claimed to be a successful pro trader
working for a bank for teenth of years trading commodities and forex.
Well, i was so happy, i thought ok i found the one who can truly tell me
 the truth about the market. then i was taken aback to the "stupid
phase" of my life by being told by him that not all indicators can be
used all the time in the market, indicators are used selectively
depending on the market circumstance. i thought "are u for real?". my
basic instinct was telling me "am i the stupid one here or is he? or is
there something he is not telling me?" anyway, let's give this guy some
benefit of my doubts.

consultations were on and off depending on how our time matches each
other. asking this guy a lot of questions and try to fit his words into
the charts only to find that everything is basically said in hindsight.
to consider these words, that i'm advised of, as wise words to the point
 of my frustration and confusion :: "should've could've would've" and
"maybe, if we 'r lucky, if indicator crosses, if signal shows up"; is
worse than an understatement.

everything is in hindsight that basically the move is explained because of the indicators. crazy fool, right?

i spent 6-8 months studying what his systems are ought to bring.
sometimes i'm given charts with so many charts. it's like a CCTV of 16
screens, each screen basically has a chart with one indicator, and the
others may have the chart with different set of indicators and some
screens are just indicator screen.

i'm advised to be able to trade and make good informed decisions,
everything must be considered. (hang on, i thought not all indicators
are to be used depending on different circumstances, albeit trending and
 ranging). how the hell was i going to make informed decisions, if i
couldnt decide first whether the market is trending or ranging. and then
 he said "oh depends on the timeframe u r looking at", then i was lost
(but now i'm found thanks to RTM lol).

a few weeks later, his analysis is found at talkingcash.blogspot.com

the whole site contained his analysis stories by (almost) daily. I
started to dissect everything on the chart for almost 1 month.

well let's take a look and carefully analyse the wordings:

In the daily charts, the short term directional indicators came up short just as it coasted the overbought zone.

of course it would, the price made it missed the overbought zone of the
oscillators, let alone stochastics. there is no way stochastic will tell
 the overboughtness before price moves.

In fact, it has cut and turned back lower now around the 73% level now.

ok, so now what? am i supposed to prepare to short? where to short? wait to cross 50% border down? i'm confused.

So for now, gold will feel a little weighty until it weathers this out.

what??!!??! so gold is going down, ok, but until what does weather out. i
 dont understand. what are we waiting for to weather out? well i've not
finished reading. let's move on.

If we are lucky, it might gold just dribbling and holding around the
1250’s level and once it is clear, puts it in a nice position to try
higher after the horizon clears again.

what does "lucky" mean? if 1250 hold, then we should buy there, shouldnt
 we? but where is stoploss? oh hang on the "once it is clear" confuses
me.

what needs to be cleared? the 73% stochastic reading? or the 1250?

which one is the horizon. *this guy is clearly in a la-la-land.*

The medium term trending indicators are starting to look kinky with one of the arms having a distinct crook in it.

i'm thinking, this could be the MACD lines, lol.. MACD can look kinky
and has one arm crooked, OF COURSE, because price just whipsawed it. but
 this sentence doesnt help anything to do with trading decision.

Although it has not yet soured, it shows that weakness has crept in
and if it is not corrected early on, the trend will decay over time.

so weakness has crept in = the bullishness has decreased.

here comes the stupid part:

If it is not corrected, trend will decay over time ==> this implies,
gold needs to breaks up, in order to continue the trend. isnt it a good
time to catch breakout traders?

another implication: if it is not corrected, it will go down. OF COURSE! even a 5-year-old can tell.

For today, to be really pushing it, gold needs to be closing below
1240 and very likely, the indicators would have cut lower by then.

GREAT! there u go, so wait to close below 1240, and we start selling. is
 this for real??? hahaha... i cant believe i was so naive to believe
these words.

The long term directional indicators continue to look perky and positive
 at the moment and yesterday’s move hardly weighed down on it at all.

Another la-la-land songs.

However, staying too low is not good for it and could coerce it into
cutting back into the channel and cancelling the newly confirmed, albeit
 not completely set in stone trend.

Really??????

The momentum/volatility indicators are took a dip in the last session
 and the early interest is evaporating as quickly as it condensed.

so which one caused it? the momentum/volatility indicator? or the price? how do we prevent it? magic crystal balls?

The positive bias have narrowed marginally and still some fight left
and if the 1250 hold, we could see a mini recovery towards the end of
the week.

ah ok,.. everything clicks. so buy near 1250, but close the trade if
price "closes" below 1240, so no stoploss, depending on the close below
1240. but hang on, i thought price needs to break up first? so buy 1250
or wait until 1263 breaks? i'm totally sold by now.

Interim supports are at 1246.50, 1238 & 1234 with minor supports at 1239.30, 1228 & 1219.40.

Interim resistances are at 1255.50, 1269.50 & 1289.50 with minor resistances are at 1268.30, 1277.30 & 1291.40.

The daily/weekly trend changer points are at 1231.35/1287.75.

Oh LOOK! scalping levels. very nice, but the whole analysis is based on the "dailies", meaning daily chart.

u see, isnt indicators fantastic?!?!?

Final rambling: thank Heaven i found what truly is the truth to read the market.

This is not for education purpose. i'm just sitting down enjoying a
traditional hot red-sugared ginger tea, on an almost torn apart
30-year-old wooden chair waiting for the birds to fly pass and chirp,
while waiting for the sun to set. Collecting thoughts is really good
exercise to maintain sanity.

Happy holiday, guys, from a country where one of its majestic governor
is condemned for a crime others committed so he can be sentenced to a
2-year prison life.

I think whats holding me back about the FLs and FTRs is that I'm only
looking at only a more localized picture of price movement, i.e. not
viewing where the FL/FTR is in relation to the overall picture of price
movement.

I've been thinking a lot about origins, targets and PAZs. I understand FLs are definitely the key/the limiter for each PAZs.

Our job is to find price movement that hasn't completed its journey to the target, and enter using proper PA on LTF on retrace.

If price has reached its target, then we wait for clear PA on where ITs
want to take price to. We never, for obvious reasons, trade a price
movement that has reached its target without a proper PA (engulf) that
points to the next target. So what I understand is that we should know
when an opposing FL is engulfed and an ORFL to be created first before
attempting to do trade anything.

Symmetry, I thought, is just a simple byproduct of ITs filling PAZs from

posts.author: staurum
posts.text:
I think this is a great reminder for everybody who's lost in price reading.

In his webinar, IF literally defines:

"how do you differentiate a fake engulf and a real engulf?"

"A fake engulf is just a BREAK of a LOW or an High, which hasNOT broken what they are actually a reaction to."

Some of the mistakes I made, as follows:

* treating an entry like an exit or vice versa. It is generally
true that we entry as if we're ready to exit from an opposite position
as if we have one, and vice versa: we exit as if we're ready to entry
for the next opposite swing. What is different though: an open position
will have several targets but one stoploss. in other words, an open
position will have several "happy exits" but one "suck toilet flush". on
 the contrary, It is definitely not correct for an open position to have
 one target but several stoplosses, in otherwords one "happy exit" but
several "toilet flush" points - this just does not work in trading.

what i simply mean here, a profitable position, when closed, does NOT
necessarily then interpret an entry for the opposite direction. This i
think, is just to satisfy our ego "to be correct" and our greed "to get
rich quick", oh and one more --> i need to be trading so i need to
click, click, click - entry, entry, entry. This will happen a lot when
there are so many temptations (even to an expression of "seductions", i
feel) when looking in LTF, for example 1m chart.

* watching approach and reaction. We need to be really really
careful when zoning our approaching flags and determining which is
reaction and which is non-reaction yet.

When price is going up towards our interest zone (flag limit zone at an
important barrier), we mark the flags price prints as it upwardly breaks
 the LTF barriers - this is what we call watching the approach. Only
after price has hit our interest zone, we need to see whether one or
more of the approaching flags we mark on LTF is engulfed, which then
allows us to even consider an entry, or not.

same in the opposite direction: when price is going down towards our
interest zone, we mark the flags price prints as it downwardly breaks
the LTF barriers. and only after the zone is hit, we need to see one or
more of the approaching flags is engulfed to consider an entry, or not.

Well, we need to be careful though, because it may not be as simple as that. These maybe related to "curve fitting":

- determining which zone, be it a whole flag or a miniflag inside it,
that needs to be engulfed, to allow us to consider an entry; will be so
obvious at times, but many times can be a little bit tricky.

- even after we find an engulf, our entry will sometimes be lost for
many reasons. this is when our "psychology" requires discipline.

- our interest zone "can be" broken and then price makes a giant retrace
 to the point of us thinking whether or not our zoning/analysis is
correct, let alone trade-able. again, this would be when our psychology
is being tested. we need to understand price is all about manipulation.
in order for price to move beyond, it needs to do the breaks and also
selfdoubts + confusions.

- another one, when price is going up towards our interest zone, we need
 to "carefully & critically" assess, whether or not the engulf (thus
 decision of direction) has already happened in one higher timescale up,
 therefore this upmove is "merely" a retrace back (not an approaching move) to some unpicked orders. In some occasions, our interest zone "may" be inside a bigger "interest zone" OR
 in "FRONT" of the "more important zone", and therefore whether or not
there is good approach and/or good reaction, price may fake-out beyond
our initial interest zone, thus we mistakenly conclude it as an engulf,
but then price shoots down even beyond our target had we been able to
trade it based on our initial analysis, or maybe after we conclude it as
 an engulf, we're ready to take an entry at the zone where we thought to
 be "origin of the move" and price shoots past it, we are left confused.
 Same applies for "when price is going down".

- last but not least (i might add some more): patience is truly a
virtue, knowing when not to trade is just as important as when to trade.
 nonetheless, neither is more important than self-mindmastery &
discipline Trading left & right, ups & downs is truly
beautiful, but i find that most often price just needs to structure
itself out just for us to take the profit out of it. Most people call it
 the set-ups. But it's just what price gives us. It structures itself,
leave some unpicked orders for us, dances around, and then we need to
"be sensitive" to its clue of invites (or traps).

Trying to trade when price hasnot finished its structures is kinda
similar to trying to taste some food in the kitchen that a chef hasnot
finished preparing. If we're as professional in food, then we know what
the finish-up should taste like, but the trouble comes when we are
arrogant and act as if we're more qualified to prepare the food and then
 starts making interventions.

I wish i can write this simpler. anyone is very much welcome to contributing.

When asked how to read the market, we are given the readthemarket.com
materials. We are excited, learn about it, putting all the puzzles
together with sleepless nights and self doubts. At mid journey or even
after learning almost all materials; funnily, we may still ask "so how
do we read the market using these?"

I think this happens a lot to some people who is looking for perfection,
 loss-proof working template/mechanism. Well peeps, this short video may
 help you as it has opened my mind eyes:

I used to be a perfectionist, but little did i know that I was more of a procrastinator than a perfectionist.

Every business has business plan. So is trading. Here are some examples I pulled up:

* Omidfx:
	readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...club?start=175#56499

* Edge:
	readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...es-journal-2-0#61591

* Michal238 :
	readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...-s-journal-2-0#60739

RTM should have one, but where is it? It's all in price reading article.
 Thanks also to our RTM founders, we are now guided by Markepedia
Roadmap & the "FAQ" article. Based on all these, we still need to
make our own "TRADING" business plan, dont we? well, how about
developing the price reading article to include markepedia roadmap. Now,
 our price reading article becomes longer than half a page long, but
more detailed and has psychology & money management aspects too.
Remember though: the plan is still very much gravitated towards PAR rule
 of thumb.

Then, based on our findings from our trades, screentime, homeworks; we can always add/remove/update the price reading article.

What's more interesting is to add IF's bits & pieces of lessons to
it, just to add some flavors. In addition to that, how about adding IF's
 quotes complied by Deenius:
	readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...-war?start=750#56612

Now our business plan starts looking like a manual, doesnt it? Please be
 careful not to make it too mechanical. Market is manipulated. Profits
are not exactly profits, neither are losses. It is all about transfer of
 wealth from the manipulated to the manipulator. So the manual just
helps us to understand price structures. How the ITs profit from price
moves is another side of the balance we need to interpret for ourselves.
 Having both mechanical & psychological sides balanced, we should be
 more sensitive towards "what may/will happen".

Having said that, every single one of us will have different business
plan, hence different practice and different trading style. no one is
ever the same. Yes, we all will look similar and often take same trades,
 but the process inside of us will never be exactly similar.

Let us not search for perfection, because perfection risks us to be a
procrastinator and focus too much on the results we desperately need to
achieve (just like the youtube video said); but instead, start building
the pieces slowly and patiently, enjoy the process, and what is much
more important, just like IF said: "feel more at home" with the charts.

Bro PinkPanter, i hope this post helps you and everyone in answering what you look for.

Best wishes,

by IF:

Fakeouts are extremely easy to predict. Most SD traders still look
directly left, which is the big shortcoming of Supply/Demand trading.
It's further left again we should be looking.

Say price is coming up to a supply. The only way we can be sure that
supply will hold price down is if that supply has already visited the
extreme set of orders in the flag limit to its left. If the supply fell
short of that, we can anticipate a FO to those extreme orders. Extremely
 simple stuff.

We always look to what S or D are reactions to, rather than just S or D themselves.

read (and thus our possible anticipative responses), and finally what
needs to happen to "increase possibility" of the zone (be it LFL or UFL)
 to be broken/engulfed long before price even touches it.

I've just been thinking, IF said something like this in the past: Every engulf has a target. a FL can only be a FL when it hits its target.

Then there's something said like: after a PA, price is going to the next FL before it can break the FL it reacts to.

In addition, we have from ignored article,

"Meaning, if price hits an area, reacts and does not hit the opposing
target, we can consider it an ignored area. Conversely, if price hits
the area and bounces back to the opposing first target then it cannot be
 considered ignored."

einrikr wrote: Would you be so kind to explain why you'd put the SL below the LL?

Hi Einrikr, putting the SL below the LL is the least you can do, have
you watched the Quasimodo video by Master IF? The rule says SL should be
 placed beyond the FL that the Quasimodo HH or LL is reacting to.

I have been monitoring EURUSD too, if you look at the following chart:

The first question I was asking myself was at point 1: Why did price
stop dropping right there? It looked like it's in the middle of nowhere.
 To answer that I went to look inside the long bullish candle at point
2. And I saw this kink on 1 min Chart:

Now going back to 15 min chart, extending this kink to the right, voila! Isn't that beautiful?

So now, as we look closer at Point 1, on 5 mins chart:

So now, imagine you were there, on September 14, 08:25 AM (EST), US RED NEWS coming in less than 5 mins:

- CPI m/m

- Core CPI m/m

- Unemployment Claim

To be honest, news can be very unpredictable, and my personal
risk-appetite may just persuade me to stay out of any trade before any
red news.

I could understand why you want to try your luck at setting a BUY LIMIT
Pending Order at Zone A, as it is untested. The question is, where do
you place your stop loss? You can place it just below zone A, or just
below the LL, or below the FL zone B that the Quasimodo was reacting to.

What I was trying to ask MasterTrader Staurum is, the choice of the SL
placement, is that a results of his technical analysis of the chart
(i.e. there are rules that he used to arrive at this decision), or it is
 a personal preference, or it's experience?

Thanks and best regards

AK

Sunday afternoon cookies & tea:

Again, i'm having a mind dumping exercise, while being grateful of all
the goods and the bads giving colour to our life. just like what Mark
Gungor said in:

we, boys, tend to go into our "nothing" box, just chill and think about
absolutely nothing. Well thinking about it, dat s not entirely true.
Even when someone is having a cup of coffee, or tea, or laying down on a
 sand sunbathing by the sea, or even smoking alone on a balcony; our
mind chatter, even without our slightest effort, just goes on and on
with incredibly many things revolving around our head as if there are
thousands of youtube videos or TV broadcasts roaming around making
noises all at the same time.

However, believe it or not, many if not most breakthrough ideas generate this way.

anyway, not wanting to brag too long, just a tip: when doing any
homework or analysis, try to voice-speak, i.e. talk to ourselves with
our own voice. Just thinking in mind or whispering inside head often
gets distracted. By listening to my own voice, I can sometimes develop
two or three personalities that debate one against another. It's very
very stupid, i know; so when i'm doing this, i can't let anyone near me,
 else become jokes.

but, to me, mostly something good comes out of it and makes my learning full of critiques and what-if scenarios.

Remember Rome is not built in a day and there are just too many ways to reach there?

Take a deep, long recovery rest for the battles ahead are long and hard,
 but we all have what we need here, don't stop believing.

posts.author: staurum
posts.text:
The honour is mine!

I have never imagined that I would end up here and found the only one
truthful material on learning about "the wickedness of the financial
world" here. A lot of the philosophies behind the materials are so much
related to many aspects of my daily life. It might be my opinion only,
but thinking about reading the market day after day, i've come to look
at the world from a very different pair of eyeglasses, i.e. most of the
things we see or believe are manipulated.

Most does not mean all, so it is our humanly duty to grasp which ones are true.

I thank you, Chief, for granting me the star. It was a true surprise for
 me that my work is recognised to be of help to members here.

The first paragraph in
	readthemarket.com/index.php/en/lb-topmen...ote-before-you-begin
 could not be truer. Basic human traits are just not suited for trading.

I personally know some members here who I regard are true traders, not
only in technical but also in psychology and attitude. They have gone
through hell of trading, depression after depression, road blocks after
road blocks, with so little help, let alone encouragement; but they kept
 at it anyway. Decoding the market mechanism was their primary focus.
Fame and recognition is certainly the last. These "silent" members have
learnt so much about the market, and guided me that humility is the most
 important of all. When you posted
	readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/jou...gloo?start=150#66436
, i thought you critiqued me silently. Thank you for that post, though. It was just on time.

They also know what you've shared with us is invaluable, if not
irreplaceable. If i were to be you, I would rigorously select who &
who I want to even think about sharing this knowledge with. Even so, I
would require a huge amount of contribution or compensation for the
knowledge gained, & i'll make sure they pay.

We don't really know why, on earth, as a human, you would ever ever
share these away. For me, personally, even a priest, monk, or any
perceived-to-be-alhonest person would never do it, unless they've gone
beyond any limit of human wisdom already.

Anywayl, i've learnt a lot from them, and therefore must say these people deserve the star way way more than I do.

Traders helping traders is still alive here. I still remember the times
when I asked Salivan hundreds of questions, though at the time he
answered it perfectly (as i just realised now
 ), back then I was still not satisfied. I also remember the
dissatisfaction and the hunger of learning gave me some sort of anger
and frustration so much that my stupid emotion was trying to blame RTM
for all the incompetences I had at that time.

As time passed, things just really really really slowly come closer
piece by piece. It was HARDLY instant, but rather took a loonng time - I
 can feel some nods from the members

At one point in time, during a read, I realised that everything that
Salivan did not answer me directly has all this time been in Art-of-War
journal. It s right there in front of me, but yet the dissatisfactory
& hungry emotion I had just blocked my stupid brain from clearly
simply seeing it. I was looking up to him so much that I did not realise
 he was trying to help me, but the true obstacle is me myself and i.
Popped up a pathetic laugh, then, from my face. So, thank you bro
Salivan, thank you for sharing your hardwork, i really appreciate it.

Most of all, thank you, IF, for sharing the spirit of RTM. I honestly
don't feel i'm it, but i truly feel i've been shared one of it. THANK
YOU

I'm given a spare time, so i feel this is best used to dump some mind poos off the bottleneck of my head into my own journal.

A person is only limited by his belief, his imagination. What he sees,
he believes. What he is told, he is suggested. What he is used to,
outside of the norm will feel aliens. Sense of comfort restrains
potential expansion & growth. Diligence inside the known looks
great, however only a few ever questions: does it? A search outside the
boundaries is critiqued and labeled dangerous. Sounds like programming,
does it. People with same programme in mind go together and herd, and
this is contagious.

I, for one, was a person who tend to continue searching for new things,
new answers, new solutions while not realising in doing so there is a
high risk that i'm also letting go the precious things i'm holding. Is
it diligent? is it lazy? Is it pathetic? Is it purposeful? or is it
simply greed? Trying to have everything so that we have every
options/alternatives/answers possible in our hands. Knowing when to
continue expanding and developing is not more important than knowing
when to stop and simply look within. Piano teaches me to self-practice,
but more importantly self-discover the bodily and mind responses i never
 knew before. Health cannot be discovered, investigated, nor bought; it
simply needs to be earned and requires us to work to "deserve" it. So
are other many important things. Often, ignorance still wins.

Everyone has different tenacity in life. The efforts are different, and
sometimes distinguishable. The results are also often (but not always)
different and distinct. Tenacity to make things work is also different
from tenacity to find reasons why things don't work. Great inventors, in
 my view, didnt have much time to elaborate their unsuccessful findings;
 but rather tried to save their lifetime to just find what does work.

One of great learning way is to question everything. Radical honesty, as
 Ray Daiio put it, really is the best way to effective efficient
improvement. One finding to the next finding, one hypothesis to the next
 hypothesis. Testing everything. Working at everything. So time
consuming, so energy draining. Mistakes repeated one after another until
 we stop them. Following and replicating others without personally
investigated reasons is the biggest sin anyone easily commits. Humans
since childhood are so indoctrinated with word "Faith & Belief".
Even the government, social media, giant corporations want all humans in
 the world to stay in the "Faith & Belief" world. Please wake up and
 listen, It is good only for children and the naive. Mature adults
holding this philosophy without personally working to prove it are
simply lazy and will be lost so easily, or worse: "slaughtered,
harvested off".

Time is almost up. Until next "mind-dumping session" time....

Big thanks to IF as always, one of the only few human beings who is way too nice in this world.

posts.author: staurum
posts.text:
Just wanna share a little perspective on this holiday time, in which i got a chance to revisit our education home. To those who have run so far but feel that we've hit a giant unsolvable wall in a maze.

Maybe it's a good idea to start a chart with basic Supply & Demand brain. Do we remember that RTM all initiated there? (from HTF to lower TFs as many as we wish).

Initially we would trade the S/D zones blindly, right? let's move on. Markepedia says: "The truth is; supply/demand are often reactions to the Flag Limit (a RBD or DBR after a break of a high or low)". This is all we need to know, the rest would be personal homework. We can ask yourself a whole bunch of questions, but structure our questions like we would structure a maze.

For example:

"That zone simply looks like a supply/demand zone, but is it really? is it a reaction or a break just before retrace?"

"let's say it's a reaction, then which flag limit that zone reacts to?.... hang on, a flag limit was initially just an FTR that met its target, let us look to the left and see where/whatzone that flag limit seeks to target?.... mm... which zone that flag limit fails to return to? and in that zone, is there clean orders? that could be the target of a break of this flag limit?" "now looking at the target of that flag limit, where was this target actually targeting towards? (remember that the target of an engulf is just an opposite engulf? - this would bring us further into some loops/series of questions again... so this would be the expansion of the maze) " "ok, let's go back, if this supply/demand is a reaction, has the reaction reached its target? if not yet, then we might have a trade opp. if not, then no good opp, but is there an unfilled orders in the zone it is reaction to? if so, what would we do?" "Let's say it's a break of a zone to the left, then we would not try to look to trade this zone, but where is the next zone that this break is targeting towards? If this is a break, where price *should return to*, and where are the clean orders that may ping-pong price to reach its tg." let's go back and re-ask: "ok this supply/demand zone does not look like a reaction, nor a break - seems to happen in the middle of nowhere." or "mm... this supply/demand zone looks like a break of this zone but a reaction of that zone"... this would bring us into another size of maze of questions. Also, maybe we can ask something like "ok where was price departing from before reaching this supply/demand zone? is that departure zone a reaction or a break?" and so on and so on. Do we remember a saying "price travels from supply to demand and vice versa"? well here in RTM we are trying to be that Supply/Demand or Spike low/high.

Just remember the origins of our thought process, because we will very easily lose ourselves into solving some branch areas of the maze but forgot the structure of the original maze we were coming from.

To me, personally, RTM is not a puzzle. Puzzle is limited, but i dont think a knowledge is limited. Instead, i personally "feel", RTM is a growing maze of knowledge. RTM creates the centre of it and it is up to us to "expand our map of understanding price action". RTM gives us a starting platform of thought for our own journey to understand the market. RTM is not a destination whereby all knowledge is complete and finished already. It truly is not. We may feel stuck or getting nowhere, but we need to ask ourselves if it is because RTM stops guiding us into the further dark zone of the maze, or maybe if it is because we are just too afraid to expand ourselves more due to fear of being wrong or fear of getting lost.

This sort of process, in my opinion, can't be literally orchestrated in a forum, let alone in an open group chat (otherwise, RTM will turn into tradingview.com forums, where the blinds are leading the deafs but they are all quacking each other to exhaustion). Trading is very much correlated to working on ourselves. Each individual of us has different brain and therefore different maze of thoughts. i am in a stupid ridiculous need to dump some mind poos and i can't find a better place than in this mistakes-ful journal of mine.

Let's get on with it.

It's quite a common sense, generally publicly accepted, that price moves because of orders executed. This is a necessary and sufficient premise. If price moves because of some sort of magic hand, holy grail patterns, dark secret indicators or even a ghost, it *could be* a necessary premise, but how sufficient it is to be true rises too many works to deduce.

Orders, the culprit, to be executed are none other than limit orders, stop orders, and market orders, regardless of them being entries or exits. Of course, there will be combinations like OCOs, etc, but I deem them unnecessary. Another necessary & sufficient premise is that price moves (ups or downs) because one-sided orders overpower/overconsume the other-sided orders.

My, doubtful, assumptions are that: While no matter how hard players try their best to hide their cards, the house always know, but the house itself will always hide their hands. The players can not and will not beat the house. The house may passively let the players to win from time to time, or actively catch the bets (the orders) by overpowering the players. Shifting it a little into vocabulary of orders: The house never leaves resting orders, i.e. limit orders and stop orders, to be seen by everybody else. Therefore, it is likely that the players leave the resting orders, although it is also possible for them to execute at-market orders, it is common sense that the house (the one having hidden their hands) moves price by executing its at-market orders against the opposite orders. Thinking about orders: Limit orders cannot exist without stop(loss) orders. Stop(entry) orders, however, do not need limit orders, but will likely have its own stop(loss) orders too. Limit orders are commonly placed in front of a H/L of some sort, and therefore stops behind that H/L. It is my own guess that these limit orders belong to S&D players, S/R players, or perhaps Trendline players. Stop(entry) orders are usually placed beyond (or, on a break) of a H/L of some sort, and usually stops behind the opposite L/H. Again, it is my own guess that these stops belong to Break-Out players, or trend-following players. The volume of orders on execution at a level at any given time, will decide the move and also the extent of the move. Search "order flow" or "market auction theory" on youtube. plenty of examples. basics of supply & demand concept. The volume of orders ultimately depend upon the decision AND the capacity (or capital/investment limit) of the *betters*.

It is always the house's choice, depending on its own interest and intent, to either let the resting orders to be executed without intervention (i call it "pass the bet"

on purpose), or catch the resting orders by executing its at-market orders (i call it "call the bet") to fill its book. One thing I absolutely believe is that the house *survives* by feeding off *Large Sums of Orders*, and it never loses to the players.

In regards to H/L: this is very subjective concept. In a very simple way: A Level is considered a High, if price travels from it to break the previous relative lows. Vice versa, A Level is considered a Low, if price travels from it to break the previous relative highs. How do we classify them? I personally think that the more important question is how do we compare their *sexiness*? Well, perhaps the more distant the H/L travels from its previous L/H before the break, the more attractive and the more obvious it is to the players (but not necessarily the house). Obvious H/L levels are commonly basis levels from which the players (S&D traders, BreakOut traders, Trendline traders, Fibo-ers, Indicator traders, Wave traders, etc.) analyse the charts and place their trades. It is my wild, unconfirmed guess that the more obvious it is, the more attractive the sum of orders are to be executed "around" there. In order for H/L to exist, there must be reversals and breaks. The reasons behind the reversals and the breaks are still homeworks.

How are they related to each other? No idea yet. How do we take advantage in the trading? Still in progress.

Is the market driven by emotions (fear & greed)? It maybe necessary, but when and where it is a sufficient premise, remains work in progress.

On another dimension of talk: It is my own adopted-from-rtm personal belief that the ITs work their way down from HTF to LTF. hence, my own wild guess is: a winner in lower scale can be a loser in a higher scale, but a winner in a higher scale will always be a winner on a lower scale. a loser in lower scale will always be a loser in higher scale, though a loser in higher scale can be a winner in lower scale.

I could be very wrong in any, some, or the whole of these writings. (until my next stupid mind-dumping session)

Just wanna share a little perspective on this holiday time, in which i got a chance to revisit our education home.

To those who have run so far but feel that we've hit a giant unsolvable wall in a maze.

Maybe it's a good idea to start a chart with basic Supply & Demand
brain. Do we remember that RTM all initiated there? (from HTF to lower
TFs as many as we wish).

Initially we would trade the S/D zones blindly, right? let's move on.

Markepedia says: "The truth is; supply/demand are often reactions to the Flag Limit (a RBD or DBR after a break of a high or low)".
 This is all we need to know, the rest would be personal homework. We
can ask yourself a whole bunch of questions, but structure our questions
 like we would structure a maze.

For example:

"That zone simply looks like a supply/demand zone, but is it really? is it a reaction or a break just before retrace?"

"let's say it's a reaction, then which flag limit that zone reacts
to?.... hang on, a flag limit was initially just an FTR that met its
target, let us look to the left and see where/whatzone that flag limit
seeks to target?.... mm... which zone that flag limit fails to return
to? and in that zone, is there clean orders? that could be the target of
 a break of this flag limit?"

"now looking at the target of that flag limit, where was this target
actually targeting towards? (remember that the target of an engulf is
just an opposite engulf? - this would bring us further into some
loops/series of questions again... so this would be the expansion of the
 maze) "

"ok, let's go back, if this supply/demand is a reaction, has the
reaction reached its target? if not yet, then we might have a trade opp.
 if not, then no good opp, but is there an unfilled orders in the zone
it is reaction to? if so, what would we do?"

"Let's say it's a break of a zone to the left, then we would not try to
look to trade this zone, but where is the next zone that this break is
targeting towards? If this is a break, where price *should return to*,
and where are the clean orders that may ping-pong price to reach its
tg."

let's go back and re-ask: "ok this supply/demand zone does not look like
 a reaction, nor a break - seems to happen in the middle of nowhere." or
 "mm... this supply/demand zone looks like a break of this zone but a
reaction of that zone"... this would bring us into another size of maze
of questions.

Also, maybe we can ask something like "ok where was price departing from
 before reaching this supply/demand zone? is that departure zone a
reaction or a break?" and so on and so on. Do we remember a saying
"price travels from supply to demand and vice versa"? well here in RTM
we are trying to be that Supply/Demand or Spike low/high.

Just remember the origins of our thought process, because we will very
easily lose ourselves into solving some branch areas of the maze but
forgot the structure of the original maze we were coming from.

To me, personally, RTM is not a puzzle. Puzzle is limited, but i dont
think a knowledge is limited. Instead, i personally "feel", RTM is a
growing maze of knowledge. RTM creates the centre of it and it is up to
us to "expand our map of understanding price action". RTM gives us a
starting platform of thought for our own journey to understand the
market. RTM is not a destination whereby all knowledge is complete and
finished already. It truly is not. We may feel stuck or getting nowhere,
 but we need to ask ourselves if it is because RTM stops guiding us
into the further dark zone of the maze, or maybe if it is because we are
 just too afraid to expand ourselves more due to fear of being wrong or
 fear of getting lost.

This sort of process, in my opinion, can't be literally orchestrated in a
 forum, let alone in an open group chat (otherwise, RTM will turn into
tradingview.com forums, where the blinds are leading the deafs but they
are all quacking each other to exhaustion). Trading is very much
correlated to working on ourselves. Each individual of us has different
brain and therefore different maze of thoughts. We would be "typically
similar" but will never be the same with each other.

May we all have a good, enjoyable rest time in this short holiday. on a
side note, remember that the celebration of this holiday originates from
 some very evil events. The blankets are so divine and holy, but most
humans are naively lured into unconsciously, by default, celebrating the
 things very undeserving.
